chapters.title: Chapter 401
paragraphs: A single word, almost a groan, slipped between my lips.
“...Lei Fei?”
Wei Fenghu’s only nephew through his sister. An S-rank Hunter secretly trained by China.
And a hero who had vanished alongside a thousand Hunters from the Public Security Armed Forces Department on the day the Monster Wave erupted.
*If you happen to meet that child, Mr. Jin...would you be able to bring him back?*
The old general’s desperate request echoed in my ears. That was probably why my body suddenly froze.
—You wicked human! Get a grip! He is no longer human. He is a fallen monster!
The Skeleton Warlord was stating the obvious.
Among the monsters I had defeated so far were Hunters and civilians resurrected as undead. Lei Fei was merely one of them.
The being before me was no longer an S-rank Hunter who had died carrying out his mission. He was a Death Knight Lord leading a monster army.
But...
*Something’s different.*
Crack, crack, crack!
—Kgh, k-khgh. Kraaah!
His body trembled in tiny spasms, groans escaping him at irregular intervals.
Each time the red glow in his eyes flickered like a traffic light, stark-white irises and pupils appeared beneath it—unmistakably human.
I had never heard of or seen an undead react this way. They had lost all sense and reason, driven solely by the instinct to slaughter.
*What if—just maybe—his transformation into an undead isn’t complete?*
If that was true...what was I supposed to do?
Right now, a single blow would end the battle and allow me to console the souls of the victims.
But what would I be killing? A hero who had given his life to protect others, or a Death Knight Lord who had led a monster army through countless massacres and acts of destruction?
“Fuck...”
My hesitation was brief.
There was no helping it. The die had been cast, and he and I had already crossed the point of no return. He wasn’t an opponent I could subdue with half measures. I had to end this now.
*Rest easy.*
Lei Fei. Death Knight Lord. Whoever he was, he would finally find peace.
My Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist, unleashed at full power at the eighth level, would end it without pain.
Fwoosh! Whoooooosh!
My fist, engulfed in blue flames, shot forward to bring everything to an end.
At that moment—
—My. Lord!
A chilling voice slipped between dark-red lips. The flickering glow in his eyes suddenly steadied, and tangible mana erupted from him.
Crackle! KRAAAANG!
Flames and darkness collided.
The two tremendous forces crashed into each other and exploded in an enormous shock wave.
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
The deafening blast left my ears ringing. The tremendous recoil hurled me backward, but I flipped in midair and righted myself.
The ground and the monster remains caught in the explosion had been blown to pieces.
Through the pale smoke blanketing the devastated area for hundreds of meters, a being wrapped in darkness approached.
—I am that person’s most loyal servant.
Sssssss.
Darkness rose from the ruined earth—the death energy held within the fallen monsters.
—I am the supreme commander who leads the legion of the dead.
Whoooooosh!
The swirling darkness rushed toward him and was drawn into his body. His half-destroyed armor repaired itself, his broken bones rejoined, and the red glow in his eyes blazed fiercely.
As he recovered, his power grew.
Now filled with even greater mana, the being slowly raised his sword.
—By my lord’s command, I shall fulfill my duty.
He was wrong.
His duty had been to serve as humanity’s shield and guardian. But the hero who had given his life for others had lost his memories and been corrupted by the Arch Lich.
**System** Lv. 140 Death Knight Lord
Lei Fei no longer existed.
The being approaching me was nothing but a monster.
In that case...
“I have a duty to fulfill too.”
The instant I murmured those words—
Whoosh!
A sword shedding mana came down toward my head.
Slash!
One handspan.
That was the distance by which death missed me.
Mana honed sharper than ever grazed my arm and sliced into the ground. There was no deafening crash, no spray of debris. More than ten meters of earth simply split apart like cheesecake.
Slice!
At the chilling sound, I thrust out my hand.
The searing heat of the Flame Divine Palm collided with the blade, which had already changed course.
KRAANG!
A tremendous shock wave exploded outward from between us. Through the swirling dust, I saw the red glow of his eyes burning brightly.
“Eat this.”
The Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist shot forward like a cannonball.
The bastard’s eyes flew wide as he drove his knee upward. My flame-wreathed fist collided with his knee, wrapped in darkness.
KRAAANG!
The world shook.
The tremendous recoil hurled me backward, and the outer wall of a building rapidly filled my vision.
I twisted my body in midair. The tips of my feet touched solid concrete.
*Flamefire Path.*
I channeled internal energy into both legs.
Concentrate.
Explode.
Crack. Boom!
The outer wall received all the force and speed loaded into my toes and burst apart.
I shot forward like a streak of flame. The Death Knight Lord was only just regaining his balance when I appeared in the air above his head.
*Inventory open. Summon.*
A sturdy spear shaft filled my hand. The energy coursing through my body surged down to my fingertips and into the spearhead.
Blue hellfire bloomed in midair, becoming a fire dragon’s claw as it slashed downward.
Fire Dragon Divine Spear, Second Form.
*Heavenly Strike.*
Whoooooooom—
Ultra-high heat burned the air.
The Death Knight Lord raised his sword toward the spear plunging down like a lightning bolt, his mana swelling as if about to detonate.
KRAANG!
The spearhead shattered, and a blue-black flash filled my vision.
Cracks spread like a spiderweb around the bastard, who had taken the full force carried by the spearhead. The next moment, the ground within a radius of more than a hundred meters sank inward.
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
The collapse opened a gigantic sinkhole.
Monsters caught in the aftermath of the battle shrieked as they plunged hundreds of meters into the depths.
The Death Knight Lord used a falling ogre as a foothold and shot back toward the surface. Then he looked up at me.
At me, standing high in the sky.
*Stepping on Empty Air.*
Another supernatural feat granted only to those who had reached the Supreme Peak realm.
Feeling the immense drain on my internal energy, I stepped on empty air and shot upward. Before my feet could touch the ground, mana lashed toward my side like a whip.
*Inventory open. Summon.*
Clang!
I managed to block the attack, but the spearhead shattered into countless fragments.
White Flame had already been hurled away as a javelin. Even if the weapons stored in my inventory were of usable quality, in a battle like this they were nothing more than disposable weapons.
But the story changed when I had dozens—hundreds—of them.
*Inventory open. Summon.*
Whoooooosh! Clang!
*Summon.*
Crack!
With every exchange of blows, a spear shaft bent and a spearhead broke.
I didn’t care.
Every sense in my body was honed to a silent edge, telling me exactly what was happening and what would come next.
*Summon. Summon.*
I crossed the spears in my hands and swung them like streaks of light.
Crack!
One shattered against his sword, but the other slammed into his side.
Boom!
As the earth-shaking impact drove him backward, I stepped forward.
One step.
That was all it took to appear before the Death Knight Lord. I advanced faster than he could retreat.
Blazing Flame Divine Spear, First Form.
*Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.*
Whoooooosh! Thrust!
A new spear, already drawn from my inventory, pierced the pitch-black armor and drove into the area around his knee.
The restored armor was tougher than before, but even the mana it had absorbed could not stop the Force coating the spearhead.
*He can’t feel pain, but he should still feel the impact.*
Contrary to my expectations, however, the Death Knight Lord did not waver.
Slice!
He severed the spear with his mana-coated sword. Instead of retreating, he charged straight at me.
Slash!
Space split open, and every hair on my body stood on end.
I thought I had turned my head in time, but a thread-thin streak of mana grazed beneath my earlobe and sliced halfway through it.
Ssshhh!
Blood spurted from the wound along with a sharp, stinging pain.
Feeling it run down my neck, I thrust my palm toward his face.
Flames surged, and the Flame Divine Palm was about to erupt—
KRAANG!
My eyes widened amid the resounding boom.
The palm that should have blown his head off had been stopped by a pitch-black gauntlet.
*What the hell?*
I wasn’t surprised that he had blocked the attack.
The Death Knight Lord’s movement was still clumsy, but what he had just used was a type of palm technique I recognized.
More specifically, it had taken the form of the Flame Divine Palm.
*This bastard...he’s copying my martial arts.*
As I stared into his unwavering red eyes, a thought flashed through my mind.
*An S-rank Hunter secretly trained by China.*
I had forgotten for a moment.
The being before me, now reduced to a monster, had once been a genius chosen from among 1.2 billion people—a secret weapon China had intended to keep hidden until the very end.
*Impressive. Truly impressive.*
I admired him inwardly.
At the same time, I became certain of one thing.
*You can’t beat me.*
If he was the man chosen from among 1.2 billion people, then I was one of a kind among nearly seven billion.
The blood I had spilled traveling between the modern world and Murim, and my countless brushes with death, had made me who I was.
“Let’s...end this.”
I stepped forward as the quiet words left my mouth.
My mind was calmer than ever, and my five senses were razor-sharp.
Fwit!
I tilted my head, and the mana the Death Knight Lord unleashed in an explosive burst narrowly missed me.
Feeling the Scorching Yang Qi filling my entire body, I drove out my fist.
KRAANG!
An earth-shaking boom rang out, and his body shuddered.
He hurriedly tried to block by imitating a grappling technique, but the Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist broke through his clumsy defense and slammed into his chest.
*More.*
Whoosh, boom!
*More. More. More.*
I repeated the words in my head as my hands and feet struck without pause.
Every blow laden with Force crashed against his sword or found an opening, battering him without end.
And it wasn’t only the spears summoned from my inventory.
My fists, legs, elbows—everything that made up my body was both weapon and shield.
Crack! Slice!
His wrist was severed along with the gauntlet, and the once-mighty mana flickered like a candle flame.
The Death Knight Lord’s armor slowly disintegrated, unable to withstand my physical power, which far surpassed human limits, and my internal energy, vast as the sea.
KRAANG!
We each struck without bothering to defend.
A System notification informed me that the Fire Dragon Armor’s durability had fallen, while the armor covering his body shattered like glass.
Clatter.
His bare flesh was finally exposed.
Dark patches of lividity mottled his pale skin.
The red glow in the dead man’s eyes flared more fiercely than ever, as though heralding the end.
—I am, I am...!
But his cry went unfinished.
Thrust!
A translucent spearhead punched through his pale skin and burst from his chest.
I had pulled White Flame back to me with Seizing an Object Through Empty Space.
Looking at him, I answered.
“That’s enough...rest now.”

chapters.title: Chapter 402
paragraphs: Thrust!
*What is this?*
It was hot, yet cool.
Sensing those two contradictory sensations, the Black Knight looked down at the transparent spearhead protruding through his chest.
He slowly raised his head. His gaze settled on the young human before him, whose expression he could not read.
“Enough...rest now.”
There was neither mockery for the defeated nor a victor’s joy in his voice. It sounded bitter and, in a way, wistful.
Those words filled the Black Knight’s mind.
*Rest.*
Then, in the next moment—
Crack!
The Black Knight heard everything binding him shatter.
The jet-black armor that had barely retained its shape broke into hundreds, then thousands of fragments, and the mighty mana within him faltered.
But the greatest change was taking place inside his mind.
*That’s...*
In a world that had slowed to a crawl, he saw a small, worn child’s shoe through the scattering fragments of armor.
At the same time, countless memories flashed through his mind.
“I want to become a Hunter.”
A young boy speaking of his dream.
“I’m proud of you. Thank you for growing up so well.”
“Thank you, Uncle. No...Father.”
A young man who had become both a proud nephew and a son.
“Is anyone there?”
“Welcome!”
On a day when everything had been perfect—the scent, the temperature, the weather—a man met a woman and fell in love.
“Will you marry me?”
The young boy who had wanted to become a Hunter became someone’s husband.
“Waaah! Waaah!”
“T-This child...”
“Congratulations on becoming a father, honey.”
At last, he became the father of a child.
“Dada! Momma!”
“Hahaha! That’s right! We’re your daddy and mommy!”
How could he ever forget those moments, when he had been happier than anyone else in the world?
A single tear rolled down his bloodless, pale cheek.
It swept away the dark clouds filling his mind. It was the tear of a dead man who had finally remembered who he was.
*Ah...ahhh...*
Only now did he know. Only now did he understand.
He reached out and grabbed the small shoe.
The nameless child crying in its parents’ arms overlapped with the image of his daughter smiling brightly as she saw him off on the morning he died.
“Daddy! Come back soon!”
“Have a safe trip. Be careful.”

He seemed to remember kissing his wife on the forehead and rubbing his face against his daughter’s cheek. He had hugged her as she laughed and complained that his beard was scratchy, then walked out the front door.
Leaving behind the same words he always did.
“I’ll be back.”
But he never kept that promise.
A few hours later, a disaster unlike any seen since the Great Cataclysm began. He fought with every ounce of strength he possessed until, at last, he came face-to-face with a certain being.
“How noble. Human, what is your name?”
The red glow burning in his eyes vanished as if it had been washed away.
The man with cloudy, gray-white eyes was no longer the Black Knight or the Death Knight Lord.
“Lei Fei. That is my name.”
Freed from his long darkness, he raised his head.
The setting sun shining through the clouds cast a reddish hue over his pale skin.
The System notification rang out just as I reached forward to deliver the final blow.
Ding.
**System Information about the target has changed. - The changed information is displayed through **Qi Sense**. **Lv. 120 Lei Fei**
The unexpected development stopped me cold.
The gray-white eyes of the Death Knight Lord—or rather, Lei Fei—slowly shifted from the sky toward me. The voice that slipped between his lips was hollow and lonely.
“It feels like I’ve just had a terrible nightmare. No, I almost wish it had been a nightmare.”
I had never heard of or seen anything like this before. After staring at him in silence, I spoke.
“Have you come back to your senses?”
“Yes. Only now, at last.”
Lei Fei looked down at his hands. They were pale and rotting, with parts of the flesh and bone missing after our fierce battle.
They were also soaked in red blood.
Human blood.
“What have I done?”
The man who had sacrificed his life for humanity had become the commander of a monster army and slaughtered humans.
I could not even begin to imagine how he felt after realizing that terrible truth.
“Lei Fei.”
I wanted to tell him. *It wasn’t your will. The Arch Lich’s magic had seized control of your mind.*
But Lei Fei shook his head.
“You don’t have to say it. I already know what you’re trying to tell me. But...”
Lei Fei gestured toward his body and continued.
“I don’t think I have much time left.”
Everything he said was true. The tough undead body that neither steel nor bullets had been able to pierce was slowly—very slowly—falling apart.
And, paradoxically, what was sustaining Lei Fei now was the mana that still remained within his body.
“It’s ridiculous. I became one of the undead and killed humans, yet I’m holding on with that very power.”
After muttering hollowly, he spoke to me.
“May I ask one favor?”
“...Please, go ahead.”
I thought Lei Fei wanted Erasure. I assumed he wished to find rest and escape from all his pain.
But the words that slipped from his lips were nothing like what I expected.
“Help me fulfill my mission.”
“I swore an oath on the day I became a Hunter. I swore that I would fight monsters until the moment my life ended. That oath still stands.”
Lei Fei had already fulfilled his mission. He had charged forward bravely and shattered magnificently.
When he fought humanity as the Death Knight Lord, he had been acting on the Arch Lich’s will, not his own.
And yet he wanted to fight again. Though his life had already ended, he stood tall once more and reaffirmed his mission.
That was why I had to ask.
“Why? Why go this far?”
Lei Fei smiled faintly.
“What a foolish question.”
“What?”
“Why did you come running here alone, knowing that countless monsters and dangers awaited you? Why am I trying to fight until the very end? What’s the difference?”
“You already know the answer. That is all.”
I already knew the answer.
The moment I heard those words, a shiver ran down my spine.
Lei Fei looked at me as I stood speechless, then raised a hand and gestured around us.
The countless monsters still remaining on the battlefield were reflected in his eyes, which had already lost the light of life.
“This...will be my final battle.”
Schlk!
Lei Fei pulled White Flame from his chest and handed it to me, then raised his sword.
Instead of the dazzling aura blade that symbolized an S-rank Hunter, ominous dark mana coiled around the blade and surged upward.
But the one wielding that power was not the Death Knight Lord.
It was a Hunter burning through his final mission.
“I’d like to fight alongside them. But will they allow me?”
Anyone who heard those words without knowing the circumstances would have dismissed them as random nonsense.
But I understood what Lei Fei meant. Lowering White Flame’s spearhead at an angle, I answered.
“They’ll be glad. If they’re the people I know.”
“...You think the same way I do.”
A red light flickered in Lei Fei’s gray-white eyes.
The mana he had dragged forth with all his strength seeped across the battlefield. Then a thunderous cry burst from his lips.
“Public Security Armed Forces Department—!”
And in the next moment—
Rustle. Rattle, rattle.

At the call of the Death Knight Lord—or rather, the head of the Public Security Armed Forces Department—the hundreds of Hunters who had fallen across the battlefield rose to their feet. Returned from death, they gripped their weapons and assembled in one place.
Lei Fei and I stood at their head.
“You take the lead. The living must finish this fight.”
As though bewitched, I stepped forward.
The monster army, thrown into confusion by the unexpected turn of events, finally gathered with savage roars.
They came for the commander who had become their enemy.
And for me, standing at the front.
Step. Step.
I walked forward, slowly but firmly.
Tap. Tap-tap.
Then I gradually picked up speed.
Lei Fei and the hundreds of Public Security Armed Forces Department Hunters resurrected as undead followed behind me.
It did not take long for the ripples to become a wave and crash over the enemy.
And at the entrance to what would be our final battle, Lei Fei shouted at the top of his lungs.
“Wipe them all out!”
It was the same cry that had echoed through the footage.
The Five-Starred Red Flag—their symbol and their pride—shone in the setting sun upon their battered, filthy armor.
With my chest throbbing, I became a streak of light and shot toward the monsters.
Whoooooosh! KRA-DOOM!
Crunch!
How many had I brought down by now?
Hundreds? A thousand?
Slash! Boom!
I had no idea. Like a man possessed, I kept moving forward. I smashed, cut, stabbed, and blew apart everything that stood in my way.
Whoooooosh!
—Kuaaaargh!
—Kraaah!
Blue hellfire surged upward in pillars, and monsters engulfed in flames that would not go out screamed.
Then, when I could no longer hear anything, I suddenly stopped.
“Hah, huff.”
I was out of breath. My mouth felt rough and dry, as if I had chewed and swallowed a handful of sand.
The fatigue I had briefly forgotten came crashing back over me as I looked around.
Across the vast expanse of land, not a single monster remained standing.
Neither the ogres and Trolls that had bellowed their savage cries nor the Wyverns and Gargoyles that had circled overhead.
And...
Thud. Thump!
The Public Security Armed Forces Department Hunters resurrected as undead began to fall as well.
Having fulfilled their final mission, they collapsed one after another like puppets whose strings had been cut.
As I watched them with an emotion I could not put into words, I realized what their collapse meant.
“...Lei Fei!”
He sat in the middle of the silent battlefield. One arm had been severed and his side torn open, yet he waited for me with a peaceful expression.
“You came at just the right time.”
I did not know why, but those simple words made something surge up inside my chest.
We had not even known each other for ten years, yet a curse slipped from my lips before I could stop it.
“Damn it...”
“Don’t swear so much. I saw you on television, and it seems to be a habit. Women won’t like that, and it’s not good for children’s education.”
Lei Fei let out a quiet laugh. He already knew who I was.
“Is that really the problem right now? There has to be some way...”
—There is no such way, you treacherous human.
The Skeleton Warlord’s voice was deeper and more subdued than usual.
Lei Fei stared at him, eyes widening.
“A monster?”
—I am the commander. You are a foolish but somewhat remarkable human.
“A monster, then. I have no idea what’s going on, but...yes, if you’re Jin Taekyung, I’m sure you’ll handle it somehow.”
Lei Fei nodded and raised his head toward the sky. His slowly blinking gray-white eyes reflected the sky, now stained entirely red.
“Could you pass along one message?”
I did not ask the foolish question, *To whom?*
I already knew.
“Tell them I love them. And tell them I’m sorry I couldn’t come home.”
It was the final message a dead man left for his family.
My chest churning, I answered.
“...I will.”
“Thank you. You’re a good person.”
Lei Fei smiled faintly and tapped my shoulder with his one remaining hand.
With a dry, crumbling sound, his fingers broke apart into dust. Soon, his arm, his leg, his chest...
At the very end, one last sentence slipped between his lips.
“Go west. End this war.”
Whoooooosh.
The wind blew. The hero, reduced to a handful of dust, scattered into the air.
As I stared blankly at the sight, dozens of planes appeared in my field of vision, flying toward us in formation.

“I want to become a Hunter.”
A young boy speaking of his dream.

Thank you for growing up so well.”
“Thank you, Uncle.

A young man who had become both a proud nephew and a son.
“Is anyone there?”
“Welcome!”
On a day when everything had been perfect—the scent, the temperature, the weather—a man met a woman and fell in love.
“Will you marry me?”
The young boy who had wanted to become a Hunter became someone’s husband.
“Waaah!
Waaah!”
“T-This child...”
“Congratulations on becoming a father, honey.”
At last, he became the father of a child.
“Dada!
Momma!”
“Hahaha!
That’s right!
We’re your daddy and mommy!”
How could he ever forget those moments, when he had been happier than anyone else in the world?
A single tear rolled down his bloodless, pale cheek.
It swept away the dark clouds filling his mind.
It was the tear of a dead man who had finally remembered who he was.
*Ah...ahhh...*
Only now did he know.
Only now did he understand.
He reached out and grabbed the small shoe.
The nameless child crying in its parents’ arms overlapped with the image of his daughter smiling brightly as she saw him off on the morning he died.
“Daddy!
Come back soon!”
“Have a safe trip.
Be careful.”
He seemed to remember kissing his wife on the forehead and rubbing his face against his daughter’s cheek.
He had hugged her as she laughed and complained that his beard was scratchy, then walked out the front door.
Leaving behind the same words he always did.
“I’ll be back.”
But he never kept that promise.
A few hours later, a disaster unlike any seen since the Great Cataclysm began.
He fought with every ounce of strength he possessed until, at last, he came face-to-face with a certain being.
“How noble.
Human, what is your name?”
The red glow burning in his eyes vanished as if it had been washed away.
The man with cloudy, gray-white eyes was no longer the Black Knight or the Death Knight Lord.
“Lei Fei.
That is my name.”
Freed from his long darkness, he raised his head.
The setting sun shining through the clouds cast a reddish hue over his pale skin.
The System notification rang out just as I reached forward to deliver the final blow.
Ding.
**System Information about the target has changed. - The changed information is displayed through **Qi Sense**. **Lv.

The unexpected development stopped me cold.
The gray-white eyes of the Death Knight Lord—or rather, Lei Fei—slowly shifted from the sky toward me.
The voice that slipped between his lips was hollow and lonely.
“It feels like I’ve just had a terrible nightmare.
No, I almost wish it had been a nightmare.”
I had never heard of or seen anything like this before.
After staring at him in silence, I spoke.
“Have you come back to your senses?”
“Yes.
Only now, at last.”
Lei Fei looked down at his hands.
They were pale and rotting, with parts of the flesh and bone missing after our fierce battle.
They were also soaked in red blood.
Human blood.
“What have I done?”
The man who had sacrificed his life for humanity had become the commander of a monster army and slaughtered humans.
I could not even begin to imagine how he felt after realizing that terrible truth.
“Lei Fei.”
I wanted to tell him. *It wasn’t your will.
The Arch Lich’s magic had seized control of your mind.*
But Lei Fei shook his head.
“You don’t have to say it.
I already know what you’re trying to tell me.
But...”
Lei Fei gestured toward his body and continued.
“I don’t think I have much time left.”
Everything he said was true.
The tough undead body that neither steel nor bullets had been able to pierce was slowly—very slowly—falling apart.
And, paradoxically, what was sustaining Lei Fei now was the mana that still remained within his body.
“It’s ridiculous.
I became one of the undead and killed humans, yet I’m holding on with that very power.”
After muttering hollowly, he spoke to me.
“May I ask one favor?”
“...Please, go ahead.”
I thought Lei Fei wanted Erasure.
I assumed he wished to find rest and escape from all his pain.
But the words that slipped from his lips were nothing like what I expected.
“Help me fulfill my mission.”
“I swore an oath on the day I became a Hunter.
I swore that I would fight monsters until the moment my life ended.
That oath still stands.”
Lei Fei had already fulfilled his mission.
He had charged forward bravely and shattered magnificently.
When he fought humanity as the Death Knight Lord, he had been acting on the Arch Lich’s will, not his own.
And yet he wanted to fight again.
Though his life had already ended, he stood tall once more and reaffirmed his mission.
That was why I had to ask.
“Why?
Why go this far?”
Lei Fei smiled faintly.
“What a foolish question.”
“What?”
“Why did you come running here alone, knowing that countless monsters and dangers awaited you?
Why am I trying to fight until the very end?
What’s the difference?”
“You already know the answer.
That is all.”
I already knew the answer.
The moment I heard those words, a shiver ran down my spine.
Lei Fei looked at me as I stood speechless, then raised a hand and gestured around us.
The countless monsters still remaining on the battlefield were reflected in his eyes, which had already lost the light of life.

Schlk!

But the one wielding that power was not the Death Knight Lord.
It was a Hunter burning through his final mission.
“I’d like to fight alongside them.

Anyone who heard those words without knowing the circumstances would have dismissed them as random nonsense.
But I understood what Lei Fei meant.
Lowering White Flame’s spearhead at an angle, I answered.

If they’re the people I know.”

paragraphs: The twenty-odd military transport planes and the fighter jets escorting them ran into trouble before they could even land.
“W-What the...”
“We can’t find a landing site!”
Below them lay a small city reduced entirely to ruins.
The buildings packed tightly together had collapsed like dominoes, and flames rose from here and there.
But what frightened the pilots most was the horrific sight visible even from far above.
Schoolyards, convenience stores, government offices... In a place where peaceful daily life had vanished, mountains of corpses and rivers of red blood filled the void.
A vision of hell painted by the monster army.
As the pilots trembled with indescribable terror at the lifeless ground below, a voice rang out.
“Land.”
“C-Commander-in-Chief, but...”
“No buts. You will land. That is an order.”
The pilot took one look at the middle-aged man’s stony face and realized he had no choice.
He was a soldier, and the man before him was the de facto commander-in-chief directing this war.
Disobeying General Wei Fenghu—the Minister of National Defense under the Central Military Commission and Chairman Xiao’s most trusted confidant—would have been madness.
Then Wei Fenghu spoke again, and the pilot decided that disobedience might actually be the less insane option.
“Head for the general hospital the Western Front has been using as its temporary headquarters.”
“What? But that’s...”
“According to the last communication we received, that was where the fiercest fighting took place. It may still be going on.”
“I know that as well as you do. We may already be too late. But we have to go. If even one person is still alive, we must help them and fight alongside them.”
Wei Fenghu continued, his eyes grave.
“Take the controls. And land first.”

It was extraordinary enough that the commander-in-chief had come all the way here himself. Now he was ordering his plane to land first. With monsters potentially still in the area, the risk was enormous.
*Damn it.*
The pilot squeezed his eyes shut and switched on the radio. His trembling voice soon spread across the communications network to every aircraft.
“VIP-777 to all aircraft. I repeat, VIP-777 to all aircraft...”
As he listened to his orders being relayed, Wei Fenghu slowly drew a deep breath.
The parachute strapped to his body in case of an emergency felt as heavy as a massive boulder.
*Is it because this is my first real battle in more than thirty years? I’m trembling.*
And Wei Fenghu was not the only one.
All four thousand Hunters aboard the twenty-odd military transports carried fears of their own.
Some probably wanted to run away that very instant. Others were suppressing their fear and desperately trying to stoke their will to fight.

No one knew who would die in the battle about to begin. Wei Fenghu was no exception. The reason he had risked coming to the fiercest part of the battlefield despite being the commander-in-chief was simple: the morale of his soldiers.
*A commander who sends only his subordinates to their deaths has no right to command.*
That had been Wei Fenghu’s lifelong principle, and Lei Fei—his nephew and as good as a son to him—had respected him for it.
The sudden memory of that beloved face sent an ache through the old general’s heart.
“...I miss you.”
Wei Fenghu murmured quietly.
It had already been fifteen days since Lei Fei had gone missing. But he had not let go of hope. Neither had Lei Fei’s wife and daughter, who had been moved to a safe place.
*Today, I saw someone who reminded me of you.*

A young man who was still only in his twenties. He had achieved an incredible military feat in a distant foreign land, and when he heard that the Western Front was in danger, he had left without hesitation.
He had even laughed while attempting a teleport with a survival rate of only ten percent.
“Ten percent sounds pretty good.”
“It’s probably a thousand times higher than the odds of crossing dimensions.”
When Magic Johnson relayed those words, Wei Fenghu had immediately mobilized the command headquarters’ forces and assembled the squadron.
He had been deeply moved by the courage shown by Jin Taekyung, a young foreigner, and the sight of him had brought his missing nephew to mind.
*You would have done the same, wouldn’t you?*
Just as Wei Fenghu’s lips curved into a faint smile after asking the silent question, a cry rang out.
“H-How can this be...!”
“C-Commander-in-Chief!”
Wei Fenghu raised his head at their urgent shouts and looked out the window.
As the ground drew closer, a sea of corpses and blood came into view, more horrific than any battlefield he had ever witnessed.
Corpses and blood. Blood and corpses...

The general hospital serving as the Western Front’s temporary headquarters lay in ruins, its twisted steel framework exposed. A gigantic sinkhole gaped like the entrance to hell, and dozens of craters carved into the ground brimmed with red and green blood.
Monster and human corpses lay tangled together in numbers too vast to count.
Thousands?
No. Well over ten thousand.
“My God...”
“W-Who did this?”
A land of death raked by disaster.
The pilots stared speechlessly at the devastated ground until Wei Fenghu’s shout jolted them back to their senses.
“Lower our altitude! Quickly!”
“Yes, sir!”
The threat from the monsters had vanished, but they could not afford to let their guard down.
The pilot maneuvered the aircraft more carefully than ever, his entire body drenched in cold sweat as he attempted the landing.
Krrrrrrk, boom!
The aircraft shuddered violently several times. At last, when the transport successfully landed, the first person to step out was none other than Wei Fenghu.
Tat-tat-tat!
The two hundred Hunters aboard the transport quickly poured out behind him.
Their reactions fell into two categories.
“This is fucking insane...”
Shock at a sight beyond anything they had imagined.
“Urk... Urrrgh!”
Nausea from the stench of blood filling the air and the dismembered corpses strewn everywhere.
And through it all, one question filled every mind.
*Who did this?*
They had even forgotten they were supposed to search for survivors. Wei Fenghu and everyone else stood frozen like statues.
Then—
Splash. Splash.
Footsteps echoed across the silent battlefield.
Two hundred pairs of eyes turned toward a lone figure crossing the field, wading through pools of blood.
The man was drenched in green blood from head to toe. Wei Fenghu stared at him and groaned out a name.
“Mr. Jin...?”
It was definitely him.
Though he looked like a man made of blood, Wei Fenghu recognized him.
Jin Taekyung had survived a Teleport spell with only a ten-percent survival rate, overturned a hopeless battle, and lived.
His seemingly endless steps finally came to a halt before Wei Fenghu.
Splash.
Jin Taekyung brushed back the hair clotted together with the monsters’ sticky blood. After a long silence, he spoke his first words.
“The battle is over. There are... no monsters left alive.”
That unbelievable declaration sent a shudder through everyone present.
According to the Western Front’s final transmission, the monster army had numbered a staggering ten thousand.
And that was not all. A Death Knight Lord believed to be one of the Arch Lich’s closest servants had personally entered the battle, making this the most overwhelming offensive of the five fronts.
By contrast, barely a thousand Hunters had stood against them. The remaining People’s Liberation Army troops might as well have been made of paper.
*Not only did he win that battle—he annihilated a monster army of ten thousand.*
It was a battle that would have been impossible without one man.
And a victory made possible because that one man had been there.
An S-rank Hunter was said to be a strategic weapon capable of overturning an entire battlefield in an instant. But since the Great Cataclysm, who had ever accomplished something like this?
The two hundred Hunters gazed at the young man before them in awe.
But Wei Fenghu was different.
The old general stared at Jin Taekyung with grief and fear in his eyes.
No—not at Jin Taekyung himself.
At the sword in his hand.
Wei Fenghu knew that sword all too well, which only made the pain in his heart worse.
He knew what its presence meant.
“Did you... meet him?”
After a brief silence, Jin Taekyung answered.
“He asked me to pass along his love.”
“He also said he was sorry.”
Wei Fenghu clenched his teeth against the sob rising in his throat. Through his tear-clouded vision, he heard one final sentence.
“He was the best Hunter I’ve ever seen.”
That was all.
Plip, plip. Tears rolled down Wei Fenghu’s wrinkled face.
A breeze blew from somewhere and gently wrapped around him.
Rank, achievements, whether someone was a Hunter or not—none of it mattered.
The fact that he had sacrificed himself for someone else was enough to make him worthy of being called a hero.
That was why Lei Fei would remain in my memory for a long time.
A man resurrected as an undead who died as a human.
He had fulfilled his mission to the very end. He was a true Hunter and a true hero.
The countless others who had died here today were no different.
And neither were the two people who had yet to regain consciousness.
*The healer said they wouldn’t wake up until they’d recovered from their exhaustion.*
Remembering what the healer who had stopped by earlier had told me, I looked at Team Leader Choi and Xiao Shen, both sunk in a deep sleep.
Thanks to the Top-Grade Potion, their injuries had vanished as if they had never existed. But the fatigue accumulated in their bodies and minds was a separate matter.
*Even I occasionally pass out, and I level up.*
The two of them had fought bravely to the very end.
They had held on to their weapons even while enduring the pain of having their limbs severed.
“Heroes... heroes, huh.”
I muttered under my breath and looked at the sword lying beside me.
The sword left behind by that very hero. His keepsake.
Wei Fenghu had wept without end as he returned it to me despite my repeated refusal.
“He would have wanted you to keep it too, Mr. Jin.”
*Really, Lei Fei?*
I ran my fingers over the blade as I asked a question that would never receive an answer.
It was a magnificent sword, its chilling edge apparent at a glance.
*Item appraisal.*
Ding.

**System Item Window Hero’s Soul Type:** Sword **Grade:** Supreme Peak **Restriction:** Those worthy of being called heroes **Description:** Extremely hard and sharp. The final soul of a noble hero dwells within it, and those who meet its qualifications can draw out even greater power.
*Hero’s Soul?*
It was a fitting name for Lei Fei, but the sword was certainly strange.
Its Supreme Peak Grade made sense, considering it had survived that fierce battle without so much as a hairline crack. The restriction, however, was unique.
*Only someone with an upright character can use it?*
Hmm. Might as well put it to the test.
Without hesitation, I gripped the hilt and slashed downward through the air.
Whoosh!
Better than I expected.
The weight and balance were perfect, and I liked how its edge seemed sharp enough to split the wind itself. The System notification that immediately followed was the icing on the cake.
Ding.

**System Hero’s Soul** has recognized you as someone of upright character. Hero’s Power** has manifested. All stats have increased slightly, and fatigue has been reduced. You may draw out even greater power under certain circumstances.
I had no idea what those certain circumstances were, but apparently this wasn’t one of them. The increase in my stats was so tiny I couldn’t feel it at all.
It was like adding a single bucket of water to a lake.
*Still, it would be perfect for judging someone’s character.*
A character-testing sword.
From now on, I would test everyone who approached me with Hero’s Soul. If the sword accepted them, I’d keep them close. If it didn’t, I’d cut them down, root and branch—snip...
Crackle!
A powerful electric current suddenly shot through my hand, and I dropped the sword.
“What the hell?”
As bewilderment washed over me, a sharp alarm sounded and a System message appeared in the air.
Beep!
**System You have harbored an evil intention! Hero’s Soul** has rejected you! - The effect of **Hero’s Power** has disappeared!
Come on. It was just a passing thought.
I looked down at the fallen sword and let out a short laugh. It suddenly occurred to me that perhaps a little of Lei Fei’s soul really did linger within it.
Wait. If that was true...
“Are you listening?”
After a brief silence, the Skeleton Warlord, currently stored inside my Inventory, answered.
“I wanted to ask you something.”
“...If your question concerns whether that sword is an Ego Sword, the answer is no. Only the faintest trace of a soul remains within it. The human you are thinking of has already ceased to exist.”
He usually had a screw loose, but he was still a Named Monster and the commander of an army of the dead.
He had absorbed some of the magical power scattered during Lei Fei’s Erasure and grown even stronger, so there was a good chance he was right.
That aside...
“Is something wrong?”
“Hmm?”
“You’ve seemed gloomy for a while.”
Even as I said it, I wondered if the question made any sense. Why was I asking an undead monster why he seemed gloomy? Weren’t they gloomy by nature?
*The problem is, he doesn’t usually act like this.*
But then the Skeleton Warlord suddenly spoke.
“A thought occurred to me.”
“What thought?”
“What kind of being was I in the past?”
“I have no memories at all. Although the human named Lei Fei has ceased to exist, this commander was secretly envious of him. At least he learned who he was.”
I hadn’t expected him to be thinking about something like that.
After considering it for a moment, I spoke in a warm voice.
“Then should I erase you too?”
“What? You said you were envious.”
“N-No, that isn’t what I meant...”
The Skeleton Warlord’s frantic explanation was cut short by a knock and a polite voice from beyond the door.
“Mr. Jin. Comrade Minister of State would like to see you.”
It seemed it was already time.
“Yes. I’ll be right there.”
I took one last look at the two sleeping figures, then rose from my seat. As I did, I murmured the words I hadn’t managed to say earlier.
“Well, if you ask me, you were probably a pretty decent guy.”
“...Huh? Were you talking to this commander?”
“No. Just talking to myself.”
“Ahem. Right?”
But the sudden brightness in the Skeleton Warlord’s previously dejected voice was definitely not my imagination.
I let out a quiet laugh and left the room.

sentences.text: The twenty-odd military transport planes and the fighter jets escorting them ran into trouble before they could even land.
“W-What the...”
“We can’t find a landing site!”
Below them lay a small city reduced entirely to ruins.
The buildings packed tightly together had collapsed like dominoes, and flames rose from here and there.
But what frightened the pilots most was the horrific sight visible even from far above.
Schoolyards, convenience stores, government offices...
In a place where peaceful daily life had vanished, mountains of corpses and rivers of red blood filled the void.
A vision of hell painted by the monster army.
As the pilots trembled with indescribable terror at the lifeless ground below, a voice rang out.
“Land.”
“C-Commander-in-Chief, but...”
“No buts.
You will land.
That is an order.”
The pilot took one look at the middle-aged man’s stony face and realized he had no choice.
He was a soldier, and the man before him was the de facto commander-in-chief directing this war.
Disobeying General Wei Fenghu—the Minister of National Defense under the Central Military Commission and Chairman Xiao’s most trusted confidant—would have been madness.
Then Wei Fenghu spoke again, and the pilot decided that disobedience might actually be the less insane option.
“Head for the general hospital the Western Front has been using as its temporary headquarters.”
“What?
But that’s...”
“According to the last communication we received, that was where the fiercest fighting took place.
It may still be going on.”
“I know that as well as you do.
We may already be too late.
But we have to go.
If even one person is still alive, we must help them and fight alongside them.”
Wei Fenghu continued, his eyes grave.
“Take the controls.
And land first.”
It was extraordinary enough that the commander-in-chief had come all the way here himself.
Now he was ordering his plane to land first.
With monsters potentially still in the area, the risk was enormous.
*Damn it.*
The pilot squeezed his eyes shut and switched on the radio.
His trembling voice soon spread across the communications network to every aircraft.
“VIP-777 to all aircraft.
I repeat, VIP-777 to all aircraft...”
As he listened to his orders being relayed, Wei Fenghu slowly drew a deep breath.
The parachute strapped to his body in case of an emergency felt as heavy as a massive boulder.
*Is it because this is my first real battle in more than thirty years?
I’m trembling.*
And Wei Fenghu was not the only one.
All four thousand Hunters aboard the twenty-odd military transports carried fears of their own.
Some probably wanted to run away that very instant.
Others were suppressing their fear and desperately trying to stoke their will to fight.
No one knew who would die in the battle about to begin.
Wei Fenghu was no exception.
The reason he had risked coming to the fiercest part of the battlefield despite being the commander-in-chief was simple: the morale of his soldiers.
*A commander who sends only his subordinates to their deaths has no right to command.*
That had been Wei Fenghu’s lifelong principle, and Lei Fei—his nephew and as good as a son to him—had respected him for it.
The sudden memory of that beloved face sent an ache through the old general’s heart.
“...I miss you.”
Wei Fenghu murmured quietly.
It had already been fifteen days since Lei Fei had gone missing.
But he had not let go of hope.
Neither had Lei Fei’s wife and daughter, who had been moved to a safe place.
*Today, I saw someone who reminded me of you.*
A young man who was still only in his twenties.
He had achieved an incredible military feat in a distant foreign land, and when he heard that the Western Front was in danger, he had left without hesitation.
He had even laughed while attempting a teleport with a survival rate of only ten percent.
“Ten percent sounds pretty good.”
“It’s probably a thousand times higher than the odds of crossing dimensions.”
When Magic Johnson relayed those words, Wei Fenghu had immediately mobilized the command headquarters’ forces and assembled the squadron.
He had been deeply moved by the courage shown by Jin Taekyung, a young foreigner, and the sight of him had brought his missing nephew to mind.
*You would have done the same, wouldn’t you?*
Just as Wei Fenghu’s lips curved into a faint smile after asking the silent question, a cry rang out.
“H-How can this be...!”
“C-Commander-in-Chief!”
Wei Fenghu raised his head at their urgent shouts and looked out the window.
As the ground drew closer, a sea of corpses and blood came into view, more horrific than any battlefield he had ever witnessed.
Corpses and blood.
Blood and corpses...
The general hospital serving as the Western Front’s temporary headquarters lay in ruins, its twisted steel framework exposed.
A gigantic sinkhole gaped like the entrance to hell, and dozens of craters carved into the ground brimmed with red and green blood.
Monster and human corpses lay tangled together in numbers too vast to count.
Thousands?
No.
Well over ten thousand.
“My God...”
“W-Who did this?”
A land of death raked by disaster.
The pilots stared speechlessly at the devastated ground until Wei Fenghu’s shout jolted them back to their senses.
“Lower our altitude!
Quickly!”
“Yes, sir!”
The threat from the monsters had vanished, but they could not afford to let their guard down.
The pilot maneuvered the aircraft more carefully than ever, his entire body drenched in cold sweat as he attempted the landing.
Krrrrrrk, boom!
The aircraft shuddered violently several times.
At last, when the transport successfully landed, the first person to step out was none other than Wei Fenghu.
Tat-tat-tat!
The two hundred Hunters aboard the transport quickly poured out behind him.
Their reactions fell into two categories.
“This is fucking insane...”
Shock at a sight beyond anything they had imagined.
“Urk...
Urrrgh!”
Nausea from the stench of blood filling the air and the dismembered corpses strewn everywhere.
And through it all, one question filled every mind.
*Who did this?*
They had even forgotten they were supposed to search for survivors.
Wei Fenghu and everyone else stood frozen like statues.
Then—
Splash.
Splash.
Footsteps echoed across the silent battlefield.
Two hundred pairs of eyes turned toward a lone figure crossing the field, wading through pools of blood.
The man was drenched in green blood from head to toe.
Wei Fenghu stared at him and groaned out a name.
“Mr.
It was definitely him.
Though he looked like a man made of blood, Wei Fenghu recognized him.
Jin Taekyung had survived a Teleport spell with only a ten-percent survival rate, overturned a hopeless battle, and lived.
His seemingly endless steps finally came to a halt before Wei Fenghu.
Splash.
Jin Taekyung brushed back the hair clotted together with the monsters’ sticky blood.
After a long silence, he spoke his first words.
“The battle is over.
There are... no monsters left alive.”
That unbelievable declaration sent a shudder through everyone present.
According to the Western Front’s final transmission, the monster army had numbered a staggering ten thousand.
And that was not all.
A Death Knight Lord believed to be one of the Arch Lich’s closest servants had personally entered the battle, making this the most overwhelming offensive of the five fronts.
By contrast, barely a thousand Hunters had stood against them.
The remaining People’s Liberation Army troops might as well have been made of paper.
*Not only did he win that battle—he annihilated a monster army of ten thousand.*
It was a battle that would have been impossible without one man.
And a victory made possible because that one man had been there.
An S-rank Hunter was said to be a strategic weapon capable of overturning an entire battlefield in an instant.
But since the Great Cataclysm, who had ever accomplished something like this?
The two hundred Hunters gazed at the young man before them in awe.
But Wei Fenghu was different.
The old general stared at Jin Taekyung with grief and fear in his eyes.
No—not at Jin Taekyung himself.
At the sword in his hand.
Wei Fenghu knew that sword all too well, which only made the pain in his heart worse.
He knew what its presence meant.
“Did you... meet him?”
After a brief silence, Jin Taekyung answered.
“He asked me to pass along his love.”
“He also said he was sorry.”
Wei Fenghu clenched his teeth against the sob rising in his throat.
Through his tear-clouded vision, he heard one final sentence.
“He was the best Hunter I’ve ever seen.”
That was all.
Plip, plip.
Tears rolled down Wei Fenghu’s wrinkled face.
A breeze blew from somewhere and gently wrapped around him.
Rank, achievements, whether someone was a Hunter or not—none of it mattered.
The fact that he had sacrificed himself for someone else was enough to make him worthy of being called a hero.
That was why Lei Fei would remain in my memory for a long time.
A man resurrected as an undead who died as a human.
He had fulfilled his mission to the very end.
He was a true Hunter and a true hero.
The countless others who had died here today were no different.
And neither were the two people who had yet to regain consciousness.
*The healer said they wouldn’t wake up until they’d recovered from their exhaustion.*
Remembering what the healer who had stopped by earlier had told me, I looked at Team Leader Choi and Xiao Shen, both sunk in a deep sleep.
Thanks to the Top-Grade Potion, their injuries had vanished as if they had never existed.
But the fatigue accumulated in their bodies and minds was a separate matter.
*Even I occasionally pass out, and I level up.*
The two of them had fought bravely to the very end.
They had held on to their weapons even while enduring the pain of having their limbs severed.
“Heroes... heroes, huh.”
I muttered under my breath and looked at the sword lying beside me.
The sword left behind by that very hero.
His keepsake.
Wei Fenghu had wept without end as he returned it to me despite my repeated refusal.
“He would have wanted you to keep it too, Mr.
Jin.”
*Really, Lei Fei?*
I ran my fingers over the blade as I asked a question that would never receive an answer.
It was a magnificent sword, its chilling edge apparent at a glance.
*Item appraisal.*
Ding.
**System Item Window Hero’s Soul Type:** Sword **Grade:** Supreme Peak **Restriction:** Those worthy of being called heroes **Description:** Extremely hard and sharp.
The final soul of a noble hero dwells within it, and those who meet its qualifications can draw out even greater power.
*Hero’s Soul?*
It was a fitting name for Lei Fei, but the sword was certainly strange.
Its Supreme Peak Grade made sense, considering it had survived that fierce battle without so much as a hairline crack.
The restriction, however, was unique.
*Only someone with an upright character can use it?*
Hmm.
Might as well put it to the test.
Without hesitation, I gripped the hilt and slashed downward through the air.
Whoosh!
Better than I expected.
The weight and balance were perfect, and I liked how its edge seemed sharp enough to split the wind itself.
The System notification that immediately followed was the icing on the cake.
Ding.
**System Hero’s Soul** has recognized you as someone of upright character.
Hero’s Power** has manifested.
All stats have increased slightly, and fatigue has been reduced.
You may draw out even greater power under certain circumstances.
I had no idea what those certain circumstances were, but apparently this wasn’t one of them.
The increase in my stats was so tiny I couldn’t feel it at all.
It was like adding a single bucket of water to a lake.
*Still, it would be perfect for judging someone’s character.*
A character-testing sword.
From now on, I would test everyone who approached me with Hero’s Soul.
If the sword accepted them, I’d keep them close.
If it didn’t, I’d cut them down, root and branch—snip...
Crackle!
A powerful electric current suddenly shot through my hand, and I dropped the sword.
“What the hell?”
As bewilderment washed over me, a sharp alarm sounded and a System message appeared in the air.
Beep!
**System You have harbored an evil intention!
Hero’s Soul** has rejected you! - The effect of **Hero’s Power** has disappeared!
Come on.
It was just a passing thought.
I looked down at the fallen sword and let out a short laugh.
It suddenly occurred to me that perhaps a little of Lei Fei’s soul really did linger within it.
Wait.
If that was true...
“Are you listening?”
After a brief silence, the Skeleton Warlord, currently stored inside my Inventory, answered.
“I wanted to ask you something.”
“...If your question concerns whether that sword is an Ego Sword, the answer is no.
Only the faintest trace of a soul remains within it.
The human you are thinking of has already ceased to exist.”
He usually had a screw loose, but he was still a Named Monster and the commander of an army of the dead.
He had absorbed some of the magical power scattered during Lei Fei’s Erasure and grown even stronger, so there was a good chance he was right.
That aside...
“Is something wrong?”
“Hmm?”
“You’ve seemed gloomy for a while.”
Even as I said it, I wondered if the question made any sense.
Why was I asking an undead monster why he seemed gloomy?
Weren’t they gloomy by nature?
*The problem is, he doesn’t usually act like this.*
But then the Skeleton Warlord suddenly spoke.
“A thought occurred to me.”
“What thought?”
“What kind of being was I in the past?”
“I have no memories at all.
Although the human named Lei Fei has ceased to exist, this commander was secretly envious of him.
At least he learned who he was.”
I hadn’t expected him to be thinking about something like that.
After considering it for a moment, I spoke in a warm voice.
“Then should I erase you too?”
“What?
You said you were envious.”
“N-No, that isn’t what I meant...”
The Skeleton Warlord’s frantic explanation was cut short by a knock and a polite voice from beyond the door.
“Mr.
Jin.
Comrade Minister of State would like to see you.”
It seemed it was already time.
“Yes.
I’ll be right there.”
I took one last look at the two sleeping figures, then rose from my seat.
As I did, I murmured the words I hadn’t managed to say earlier.
“Well, if you ask me, you were probably a pretty decent guy.”
Were you talking to this commander?”
“No.
Just talking to myself.”
“Ahem.
Right?”
But the sudden brightness in the Skeleton Warlord’s previously dejected voice was definitely not my imagination.
I let out a quiet laugh and left the room.

chapters.title: Chapter 404
paragraphs: “Whew.”
Night had fallen, pitch-black.
The moment he returned, the young man threw off his equipment and dropped heavily into a seat. As he struggled to catch his breath, a middle-aged man approached and handed him a drink.
“You look exhausted. Drink this.”
The two men had bonded somewhat on the way here over their shared status as Hunters drafted from Shanxi Province.
The young man recognized the familiar face and eyed the can in the middle-aged man’s hand, then muttered dubiously.
“Did this come from the supplies? I don’t think I’ve seen this drink before.”
“It came in with the foreign relief supplies. It’s not from our country.”
“Hmm. Got anything carbonated?”
“If you don’t want it, forget it.”
The middle-aged man began to withdraw his hand, but the young man quickly grabbed it and spoke with a solemn expression.
“Sir. Have I ever told you that canned ration drinks are my favorite thing in the world?”
“No.”
“Then you’re about to learn.”
“Good. That’s the spirit.”
“I’ll enjoy it.”
Click.
The young man opened the can and took a sip. His expression changed subtly, but before he could say anything, the middle-aged man asked him a question.
“You’re coming back from searching Sector Three, aren’t you?”
“...Urk. Yes.”
“Must’ve been rough.”
The young man answered with a shrug. His bare upper body was drenched in cold sweat that had yet to dry, and green blood was splattered across his cheek.
“Monster blood. Did you get into a fight?”
“No. I was passing a building when a damn Gargoyle corpse fell. Must’ve been caught on the roof.”
“That must’ve caused quite a commotion.”
“Do you even have to ask? The rookies with only a year or two under their belts started puking and pissing themselves the moment they got covered in blood.”
“And you?”
“I may not look it, but I’ve been a Hunter for seven years. I didn’t even blink.”
The middle-aged man’s gaze slowly drifted toward a particular part of the young man’s body. He stared at the faint stain on his navy-blue pants, then nodded.
“Hmm. I see.”
“...It’s sweat.”
“I didn’t say anything. But looking at you is somehow making my eyes sweat.”
“...Actually, I did piss a little. Is it obvious?”
“Yep.”
“Damn it.”
The middle-aged man silently watched him swear and tip back the can, then abruptly asked, “Did you find any survivors?”
“So it was the same on your side.”
The young man’s expression stiffened the instant the words left the man’s mouth. The middle-aged man let out a sigh.
He had already taken part in one search himself.
It had been a truly nightmarish experience.
Everywhere he looked, bodies torn apart by monsters lay piled high, and the horrific stench made his head feel as if it would split open.
Neither of them would ever forget what they had seen that day.
“...I can’t even imagine how fierce the battle must’ve been.”
“You don’t need to. Whatever you imagine, it was worse.”

The four thousand Hunters who had come here with Minister of National Defense Wei Fenghu had been divided according to their units and sent to search the small city. Every piece of search equipment they used kept producing the same result.
No survivors.

Aside from the three thousand People’s Liberation Army soldiers who had fled in terror at the start of the battle, everyone lay cold and dead. No one yet knew how many of the cowardly deserters scattered across the region had survived.
“At this rate, we can’t even call it a casualty count. A death toll would be more accurate...”
“Watch what you say. We don’t know that yet.”
“Mm. I’m sorry. I spoke carelessly.”
“As long as you understand. And...”
The middle-aged man cut off the young man’s thoughtless remark and continued.
“Casualty count is the right term. There are survivors.”
The young man remembered the three people he had momentarily forgotten—the three who had survived this gruesome hell.
“You mean the regimental commander of the Public Security Armed Forces Department? That young fellow?”
“That’s right. The young man from Korea survived too.”
“And then there’s...”
The first two had certainly acted heroically, but compared to the last survivor, they were no more than fireflies before the sun.
The young man swallowed hard, and the middle-aged man finished for him.
“Yes, that man. No—that person survived too.”
Unmistakable awe filled his voice. He felt no discomfort referring to someone far younger than himself as “that person,” because he knew just how extraordinary the man’s achievements had been.
“Can you believe it? That a single Hunter could be that strong?”
He was a seasoned Hunter himself. That meant he could at least vaguely imagine what sort of monsters S-rank Hunters were.
But Jin Taekyung’s feats had been so incredible that it was hard to believe they were the work of a Hunter—or even a human being.
“It was a monster army nearly ten thousand strong. There were two Death Knights, and even a Death Knight Lord said to be as strong as an S-rank Hunter, if not stronger.”
The middle-aged man rattled on, his voice brimming with excitement.
“And how many allied Hunters were there? A mere thousand. The People’s Liberation Army was there too, but even they...”
“Nearly half of them fled when the front line collapsed. The rest fought bravely, but the monsters slaughtered them. I heard about it too.”
“How many Hunters do you think were left when Jin Taekyung arrived? A thousand? No, I’d stake my life that fewer than half were still alive!”
Had he witnessed the situation when Jin Taekyung arrived, the shock might have sent him into cardiac arrest.
Even this man, who revered Jin so deeply, had never imagined that Jin Taekyung had faced the monster army alone.
“He led hundreds of exhausted, wounded Hunters and annihilated a monster army more than ten times their size! Do you think that makes any sense?”
The young man gave him a deeply skeptical look.
“I don’t think it does.”
“Exactly. But that person did it!”
“Uh, sir. Sorry to rain on your parade, but none of that has actually been confirmed yet, has it?”
“What?”
“I think Jin Taekyung...”
“Not Jin Taekyung. Mr. Jin!”
The middle-aged man’s eyes bulged as he barked the correction. The young man flinched and cleared his throat.
“Ahem. I mean, I admit that Mr. Jin is incredibly strong, but I can’t help thinking the story might be a little exaggerated.”
“Exaggerated? You saw the marks left on the battlefield and you can still say that? If it wasn’t Mr. Jin, then who...”
“Come on, don’t get so worked up. Try looking at this objectively. If everything you’re saying is true, then Mr. Jin is stronger than Faye Chen or Wu Heixing.”
“I have no interest in ranking them, but judging by their accomplishments during this Monster Wave, Mr. Jin clearly comes first. So?”

“Faye Chen may be from Hong Kong, but she’s a hero who accomplished countless great feats during the Great Cataclysm. And for all the trouble Wu Heixing causes, he’s still a true genius born of Zhonghua. Jin Taekyung surpassing both of them? That crosses the line.”
The middle-aged man stared at him with equal parts disbelief and contempt.
“You’re the one who crossed the line.”
“What?”
“Is that really all you have to say? You shout that Zhonghua is number one, then belittle the hero who won us a great victory and saved our people?”
The young man’s face twisted.

“Since you brought it up, Jin Taekyung only saved two people today. No, one of them was Korean, so he only saved one of our people. And that man was perfectly fine, without a single wound. He fought to protect his own countrymen, that’s all. You don’t seriously think he used a Top-Grade Potion, do you?”
“There’s no point talking to you. Instead of praising him, this is how you repay him? I wonder what Mr. Jin would say if he heard...”
The middle-aged man shook his head and rose from his seat.
At that moment, a voice spoke behind them.
“Maybe he would’ve said you were a fucking asshole who wasn’t worth helping.”
The two men spun around in shock at the voice that had approached without a sound.
Before them stood a man whose face they knew well from television and the media.
“Hic.”
The young man stared up at someone a full head taller than him and began to hiccup.
“J-J-J-J-J-Jin!”
The middle-aged man stuttered as though he were buffering.
Jin Taekyung regarded the two of them with a friendly smile.
“Young man, stop hiccupping unless you want to become a good Chinese person. And you, sir, stop the earthquake—unless you’re planning to bring down the Arch Lich with a massive one.”
“Hic—gulp.”
“A-Are you really him?”
Jin Taekyung nodded slightly.
“I was going to keep walking, but then I heard something particularly irritating.”
“...Th-That...”
Jin Taekyung turned to the source of that irritating noise, who had stopped hiccupping and begun trembling like a leaf.
“How old are you?”
“I-I’m twenty-nine.”
“You’re older than me. I’ll speak casually.”
“...What?”
“What?”
“N-Nothing.”
The young man had no grounds to complain even if Jin Taekyung cursed him out, let alone spoke casually to him.
He had only ever seen Jin Taekyung from a distance or in passing. Now that he realized Jin had heard everything he had said, his hands and feet began to tingle, and his vision went white.
“I-I’m sorry.”
“You don’t need to apologize. That’s how talking behind someone’s back works. I understand.”
“Th-Thank you.”
Just as Jin Taekyung’s gentle smile began to melt the young man’s heart, he continued.
“Nothing to thank me for. Talking shit is fun while you’re doing it, but when you get caught, you’re fucked.”
“There should be someone behind me right now. See him?”
Slowly—very slowly—the young man shifted his gaze.
Sure enough, a little over ten meters away, a middle-aged man with the face of a demon was radiating a terrifying aura in his direction.
“They say he’s an A-rank Hunter with the Central Military Commission. He must have found your story very interesting, because he keeps bowing to me. Run over and put a pain-relief patch on him.”
“Y-Yes, sir!”
The young man answered with a shriek and dashed over, only to let out a real scream when a mana-infused kick caught him in the shin.
Jin Taekyung laughed quietly at the sight and started to leave, then suddenly stopped.
“Ah, there’s one thing you’re mistaken about.”
“M-Me?”
The middle-aged man, still half-dazed, snapped back to his senses.
“I’m sorry, but what would that be?”
“I didn’t do it alone.”
“What?”
“Everyone fought like hell. By the time I got there, the battle was almost over. Make sure you tell the others that too.”
“Is that really true?”
“Of course. Oh, do you have a family?”
“Yes. Three daughters and five sons...”
“You’re quite the patriot. In a few years, you’ll have enough for a soccer team.”
Jin Taekyung thought for a moment, then abruptly asked, “You’re not assigned to a combat unit, are you?”
“...You could tell right away.”
The middle-aged man lowered his head in embarrassment.
“As you can see, I’m an E-rank Hunter, so I was excluded from combat. I’ll probably be assigned to tally the casualties.”
“Then could I ask you one favor?”
“It would be my honor, Mr. Jin.”
“Please add one person to the list of the dead. You won’t find his body, so I’m asking you to make a special exception.”
“What is his name?”
“Lei Fei. Lei Fei.”
Those were Jin Taekyung’s final words to him.
The middle-aged man remained rooted in place, staring after Jin for a long time before finally releasing the breath he had been holding.
He felt certain that Jin Taekyung’s expression the last time he saw him would remain etched in his memory for a long time.
*What was that look in his eyes...?*
The resolve to see something through, no matter what.
The middle-aged man, who had been singing Jin Taekyung’s praises moments before, picked up the can the young man had left behind and took a swallow to wet his throat.
Then he grimaced at its indescribable flavor.
“Ptooey!”
Burdian?
It seemed to be a Korean drink, but it tasted god-awful.
“You’re here, Mr. Jin.”
Wei Fenghu was not the only one waiting for me.
Five monitors stood inside the conference room, each displaying a seated S-rank Hunter.
I spoke calmly.
“Let’s go end this war.”
At long last, it was time to eliminate the culprit behind all of this.
