Neither of them would ever forget what they had seen that day.
“...I can’t even imagine how fierce the battle must’ve been.”
“You don’t need to.
Whatever you imagine, it was worse.”
The four thousand Hunters who had come here with Minister of National Defense Wei Fenghu had been divided according to their units and sent to search the small city.
Every piece of search equipment they used kept producing the same result.
No survivors.
Aside from the three thousand People’s Liberation Army soldiers who had fled in terror at the start of the battle, everyone lay cold and dead.
No one yet knew how many of the cowardly deserters scattered across the region had survived.
“At this rate, we can’t even call it a casualty count.
A death toll would be more accurate...”
“Watch what you say.
We don’t know that yet.”
“Mm.
I’m sorry.
I spoke carelessly.”
“As long as you understand.
And...”
The middle-aged man cut off the young man’s thoughtless remark and continued.
“Casualty count is the right term.
There are survivors.”
The young man remembered the three people he had momentarily forgotten—the three who had survived this gruesome hell.
“You mean the regimental commander of the Public Security Armed Forces Department?
That young fellow?”
“That’s right.
The young man from Korea survived too.”
“And then there’s...”
The first two had certainly acted heroically, but compared to the last survivor, they were no more than fireflies before the sun.
The young man swallowed hard, and the middle-aged man finished for him.
“Yes, that man.
No—that person survived too.”
Unmistakable awe filled his voice.
He felt no discomfort referring to someone far younger than himself as “that person,” because he knew just how extraordinary the man’s achievements had been.
“Can you believe it?
That a single Hunter could be that strong?”
He was a seasoned Hunter himself.
That meant he could at least vaguely imagine what sort of monsters S-rank Hunters were.
But Jin Taekyung’s feats had been so incredible that it was hard to believe they were the work of a Hunter—or even a human being.
“It was a monster army nearly ten thousand strong.
There were two Death Knights, and even a Death Knight Lord said to be as strong as an S-rank Hunter, if not stronger.”
The middle-aged man rattled on, his voice brimming with excitement.
“And how many allied Hunters were there?
A mere thousand.
The People’s Liberation Army was there too, but even they...”
“Nearly half of them fled when the front line collapsed.
The rest fought bravely, but the monsters slaughtered them.
I heard about it too.”
“How many Hunters do you think were left when Jin Taekyung arrived?
A thousand?
No, I’d stake my life that fewer than half were still alive!”
Had he witnessed the situation when Jin Taekyung arrived, the shock might have sent him into cardiac arrest.
Even this man, who revered Jin so deeply, had never imagined that Jin Taekyung had faced the monster army alone.
“He led hundreds of exhausted, wounded Hunters and annihilated a monster army more than ten times their size!
Do you think that makes any sense?”
The young man gave him a deeply skeptical look.
“I don’t think it does.”
“Exactly.
But that person did it!”
“Uh, sir.
Sorry to rain on your parade, but none of that has actually been confirmed yet, has it?”
“What?”
“I think Jin Taekyung...”
“Not Jin Taekyung.
Mr.
Jin!”
The middle-aged man’s eyes bulged as he barked the correction.
The young man flinched and cleared his throat.
“Ahem.
I mean, I admit that Mr.
Jin is incredibly strong, but I can’t help thinking the story might be a little exaggerated.”
“Exaggerated?
You saw the marks left on the battlefield and you can still say that?
If it wasn’t Mr.
Jin, then who...”
“Come on, don’t get so worked up.
Try looking at this objectively.
If everything you’re saying is true, then Mr.
Jin is stronger than Faye Chen or Wu Heixing.”
“I have no interest in ranking them, but judging by their accomplishments during this Monster Wave, Mr.
Jin clearly comes first.
So?”
“Faye Chen may be from Hong Kong, but she’s a hero who accomplished countless great feats during the Great Cataclysm.
And for all the trouble Wu Heixing causes, he’s still a true genius born of Zhonghua.
Jin Taekyung surpassing both of them?
That crosses the line.”
The middle-aged man stared at him with equal parts disbelief and contempt.
“You’re the one who crossed the line.”
“What?”
“Is that really all you have to say?
You shout that Zhonghua is number one, then belittle the hero who won us a great victory and saved our people?”
The young man’s face twisted.
“Since you brought it up, Jin Taekyung only saved two people today.
No, one of them was Korean, so he only saved one of our people.
And that man was perfectly fine, without a single wound.
He fought to protect his own countrymen, that’s all.
You don’t seriously think he used a Top-Grade Potion, do you?”
“There’s no point talking to you.
Instead of praising him, this is how you repay him?
I wonder what Mr.
Jin would say if he heard...”
The middle-aged man shook his head and rose from his seat.
At that moment, a voice spoke behind them.
“Maybe he would’ve said you were a fucking asshole who wasn’t worth helping.”
The two men spun around in shock at the voice that had approached without a sound.
Before them stood a man whose face they knew well from television and the media.
“Hic.”
The young man stared up at someone a full head taller than him and began to hiccup.
“J-J-J-J-J-Jin!”
The middle-aged man stuttered as though he were buffering.
Jin Taekyung regarded the two of them with a friendly smile.
“Young man, stop hiccupping unless you want to become a good Chinese person.
And you, sir, stop the earthquake—unless you’re planning to bring down the Arch Lich with a massive one.”
“Hic—gulp.”
“A-Are you really him?”
Jin Taekyung nodded slightly.
“I was going to keep walking, but then I heard something particularly irritating.”
“...Th-That...”
Jin Taekyung turned to the source of that irritating noise, who had stopped hiccupping and begun trembling like a leaf.
“How old are you?”
“I-I’m twenty-nine.”
“You’re older than me.
I’ll speak casually.”
“...What?”
“What?”
“N-Nothing.”
The young man had no grounds to complain even if Jin Taekyung cursed him out, let alone spoke casually to him.
He had only ever seen Jin Taekyung from a distance or in passing.
Now that he realized Jin had heard everything he had said, his hands and feet began to tingle, and his vision went white.
“I-I’m sorry.”
“You don’t need to apologize.
That’s how talking behind someone’s back works.
I understand.”
“Th-Thank you.”
Just as Jin Taekyung’s gentle smile began to melt the young man’s heart, he continued.
“Nothing to thank me for.
Talking shit is fun while you’re doing it, but when you get caught, you’re fucked.”
“There should be someone behind me right now.
See him?”
Slowly—very slowly—the young man shifted his gaze.
Sure enough, a little over ten meters away, a middle-aged man with the face of a demon was radiating a terrifying aura in his direction.
“They say he’s an A-rank Hunter with the Central Military Commission.
He must have found your story very interesting, because he keeps bowing to me.
Run over and put a pain-relief patch on him.”
“Y-Yes, sir!”
The young man answered with a shriek and dashed over, only to let out a real scream when a mana-infused kick caught him in the shin.
Jin Taekyung laughed quietly at the sight and started to leave, then suddenly stopped.
“Ah, there’s one thing you’re mistaken about.”
“M-Me?”
The middle-aged man, still half-dazed, snapped back to his senses.
“I’m sorry, but what would that be?”
“I didn’t do it alone.”
“What?”
“Everyone fought like hell.
By the time I got there, the battle was almost over.
Make sure you tell the others that too.”
“Is that really true?”
“Of course.
Oh, do you have a family?”
“Yes.
Three daughters and five sons...”
“You’re quite the patriot.
In a few years, you’ll have enough for a soccer team.”
Jin Taekyung thought for a moment, then abruptly asked, “You’re not assigned to a combat unit, are you?”
“...You could tell right away.”
The middle-aged man lowered his head in embarrassment.
“As you can see, I’m an E-rank Hunter, so I was excluded from combat.
I’ll probably be assigned to tally the casualties.”
“Then could I ask you one favor?”
“It would be my honor, Mr.
Jin.”
“Please add one person to the list of the dead.
You won’t find his body, so I’m asking you to make a special exception.”
“What is his name?”
“Lei Fei.
Lei Fei.”
Those were Jin Taekyung’s final words to him.
The middle-aged man remained rooted in place, staring after Jin for a long time before finally releasing the breath he had been holding.
He felt certain that Jin Taekyung’s expression the last time he saw him would remain etched in his memory for a long time.
*What was that look in his eyes...?*
The resolve to see something through, no matter what.
The middle-aged man, who had been singing Jin Taekyung’s praises moments before, picked up the can the young man had left behind and took a swallow to wet his throat.
Then he grimaced at its indescribable flavor.
“Ptooey!”
Burdian?
It seemed to be a Korean drink, but it tasted god-awful.
“You’re here, Mr.
Jin.”
Wei Fenghu was not the only one waiting for me.
Five monitors stood inside the conference room, each displaying a seated S-rank Hunter.
I spoke calmly.
“Let’s go end this war.”
At long last, it was time to eliminate the culprit behind all of this.

chapters.title: Chapter 405
paragraphs: “The operation will commence tomorrow at 06:30. Every front is to carry out its assigned orders without fail.”
Pop.
With those final words from Wei Fenghu, the Minister of National Defense, the meeting ended.
Lee Jungryong, Vice Guild Master of Ares Guild, leaned back in his chair and stared at the five monitors that had gone dark.
*Things are moving quickly. Far more quickly than I expected.*
This was not a war that would end easily, nor was it a war that should end so easily.

China was both a Hunter powerhouse with an enormous number of Hunters and a closed-off country. It was also one of the few countries where Ares Guild, which had extended its reach across the world through its mercenary business, had failed to establish a proper foothold.
That was why Lee Jungryong did not want China to remain stable. The more damage China suffered, the wider the cracks he could exploit.
More than a million casualties? Hundreds of trillions of won in property damage?
What did any of that matter? This Monster Wave might have been a disaster for some, but for Lee Jungryong, it was an opportunity.
But...
*Once again, Jin Taekyung is the problem.*
Lee Jungryong raised a finger and slowly tapped the table.
He had always known that the world did not move according to plan, but lately, whenever Jin Taekyung blocked his path at every turn, the same thought kept surfacing.
*He’s dangerous.*
The interest Lee Jungryong had felt when he first learned of Jin Taekyung’s existence had long since vanished without a trace.
If a child who had barely reached an adult’s waist suddenly shot up within a few months and met that adult’s gaze head-on, the adult could not help but be unsettled.
And what if the child was still growing?
*He’ll only become more dangerous.*
If the Arch Lich’s rampage had been an opportunity for Lee Jungryong, it had given Jin Taekyung wings.
The man had achieved incredible feats in battle and now stood in the global spotlight.
Another war had produced a new hero, just like the heroes born amid the chaos of the Great Cataclysm.
*People fear the strong even as they envy them, but heroes are worshiped.*
Lee Jungryong knew that better than anyone. And if this war ended because of Jin Taekyung’s exploits—if that happened—then...
Crack.
The tip of his finger, infused with aura, had already bored through the solid wood and reduced it to powder.
Lee Jungryong silently looked down at the table, its center punched clean through.
For now, it was only a small hole. But if it continued to grow, it would soon become impossible to control. He had to fill it before the table collapsed.
“Send in the Head of Security.”
At Lee Jungryong’s quiet order, someone waiting outside the door left to carry it out.
Before long, the door opened and a familiar figure stepped inside.
“You called for me?”
Jin Taekyung was not the only one who had changed in such a short time.
Go Jun, Lee Jungryong’s right hand and Head of Security, had changed a great deal as well.

A dark light lay deep in his eyes, and his voice had grown dry. A few people who knew the circumstances whispered that after losing to Jin Taekyung, his already hard expression had turned even gloomier.
Lee Jungryong disagreed.
“You look well.”
“I’ve made a little progress.”
“Too much modesty is unbecoming. You accomplished a great deal on today’s battlefield as well. You deserve the praise.”
“...Thank you.”
The monster army’s sudden assault on five fronts had left enormous casualties, but the northern front under Lee Jungryong’s command had been the sole exception.

The Ares Guild elites, who had conserved their strength by hanging back in previous battles, slaughtered the monster army. Go Jun had also single-handedly killed two Death Knights that had served as the monsters’ leaders.
“What were our losses?”
“Eleven severely injured and forty-six lightly injured. No deaths. The severely injured will need more time to recover, but the others have already been fully healed.”
The more than four thousand casualties among the other Hunters and soldiers did not enter their calculations.
Lee Jungryong asked, and Go Jun answered. To the two of them, only Ares Guild counted as allies.
“It’s unfortunate about the commander, though. To die such an untimely death. He was quite a tough man...”
As Lee Jungryong trailed off, a gloomy light flickered in the depths of Go Jun’s eyes.
“I’m sorry. I tried to stop them with everything I had, but there were simply too many monsters.”
“It couldn’t be helped. Did you recover the body?”
“It was too badly mangled, so we had no choice but to cremate him. The staff officers who died with him were treated the same way.”
“Well done. Ah, you know Lieutenant General Wang Ochun has been appointed the new commander, don’t you?”
“Yes. I was just on my way back from meeting him.”
Only a handful of people, including Lee Jungryong, knew that Lieutenant General Wang Ochun and Go Jun had met before.
For several years, the two had occasionally shared meals at secluded safe houses. Each time, the trunk of Lieutenant General Wang Ochun’s sedan grew heavier.
“What did he have to say?”
“He said he looked forward to working with me.”
A faint smile touched Lee Jungryong’s lips.
“Of course. You’re comrades who will be fighting together.”
By now, Wang Ochun was probably delighted to have been entrusted with such an important post. He had no idea that this entire chain of events was anything but simple good fortune.
Nor did he know that his tough predecessor, now reduced to a handful of ashes, had been preparing a report on Ares Guild’s lackluster performance in battle.
“Watch over him carefully. We can’t afford to lose our commander twice, can we?”
“Understood.”
Anything could happen on a battlefield.
A commander on poor terms with someone might be torn to pieces by monsters, while a corrupt general with a fondness for money might be appointed in his place.
Now in a considerably better mood, Lee Jungryong continued.
“You’ll have a hard time starting tomorrow, so get plenty of rest tonight.”
“What do you mean by that...?”
“We’ve been ordered to advance with all possible speed and sweep away the remaining monsters.”
“Mobile warfare, then. Was that order issued to every front?”
Lee Jungryong nodded.

Beginning tomorrow morning, the five fronts, including the northern front, would commence mobile warfare. Within a few days, they would cut off the monster army’s retreat and tighten an encirclement around it.
“They must have taken considerable losses as well, but their numbers will still be formidable.”

“What do you think this country has more of than anything else? Even now, hundreds of transport planes are carrying Hunters in from all across China. Even low-ranking Hunters will make useful arrow fodder.”
Lee Jungryong spoke calmly, then continued.
“Focus on minimizing the Guild’s losses. Just in case...”
His gaze deepened as it settled on the table.
“There may come a time when you have to fill a hole.”
“...I’ll keep that in mind.”
The meaning was unclear, but to Go Jun, Lee Jungryong was both a revered Master and as good as a god.
Without questioning him, Go Jun silently nodded. Then he suddenly realized that he had forgotten to ask something important.
“Where is our final destination?”
Instead of answering, Lee Jungryong raised a hand and pointed at the map of Sichuan Province that covered the wall.
Pshk!
A blast of wind shot from his fingertip and pierced one section of the map. Go Jun’s gaze fell on the place-name written beside the hole.
Suining City.
The place where this entire catastrophe had begun.
The Arch Lich was there.
At dawn the next day, everyone who woke found themselves divided into two groups.
Those who were leaving and those who were staying.
Naturally, I belonged to the former group, while Team Leader Choi and Xiao Shen belonged to the latter.
Only when our departure was imminent did the two of them finally regain consciousness—and immediately start protesting the fact that they were being left behind.
“Mr. Jin. I’m perfectly fine.”
“I’m perfectly fine, hyung!”
“I can fight.”
“I’m confident I can fight harder than anyone!”
*...What is this, an echo?*
As I looked at Team Leader Choi and Xiao Shen shouting with stiff expressions, I had no choice but to make them an offer.
“Hmm. If you can last ten minutes against me, I’ll take you along.”
“Is that what you call an offer, you shameless, wicked human?”
*Shameless, my ass.*
If anything, those two were the shameless ones. They could barely run properly, yet they wanted me to take them onto a battlefield.
It was good that they were burning with fighting spirit, but heading into battle in their current condition was a surefire way to get themselves killed.
*And what kind of undead talks about conscience?*
*Why, I oughta...*
After making that threat in my head, I addressed the two thoroughly dejected men.

“For now, focus on recovering. If you spend the next few days getting your feel back and your stamina returns, you might be deployed to the front then. That goes for you too, Shen—not just Team Leader Choi.”
“Hmm.”
“Hmmmm.”
They still did not look happy, but at least they seemed somewhat resigned.
Both of them knew what condition their bodies were in. They could not keep insisting forever.
“Then I’d better get going... Ah.”
I had forgotten something.
Pretending to rummage through my bag enchanted with space-expansion magic, I pulled out the item I had stored in my Inventory and held it toward Xiao Shen.
“Here.”
Xiao Shen blinked.
“...Hyung?”
“What are you waiting for? Take it. My arm’s going to fall off.”
Xiao Shen reflexively accepted it and stared at me in confusion.
“What is this?”
“A gift. Someone I know entrusted it to me, but I think you should have it.”
“A sword this fine?”
“Why? You don’t want it?”
“No, that’s not it. I’m just not sure I should accept something like this...”
Xiao Shen hurriedly waved his hands, then gazed almost dreamily at Hero’s Soul as he gripped its hilt.
Its weight distribution and balance were close to perfect, and the transparent blade gleamed with unmistakable sharpness.
He swallowed hard.
“Can I really accept this?”
“I’m not giving it to you for no reason. I’m giving it to you because you qualify.”
“I qualify...?”
“That’s right.”
The courage he had shown in the last battle. His sacrifice for someone else.
That was enough.
Besides, I had been using a spear for years. If I kept the sword, it would only rot away in my Inventory.
Xiao Shen, another Chinese member of the Public Security Armed Forces Department, was a more fitting owner than I was.
*And since nothing happened when he grabbed the hilt, I guess the sword has accepted him too.*
The Skeleton Warlord grumbled quietly.
“This commander is good with a sword too... This commander likes swords...”
*Huh? What was that?*
It was hard to hear the words of a loser who had secretly grabbed Hero’s Soul from my Inventory at dawn and screamed.
“...Hmph, forget it. A cheap sword like that is unworthy of this commander!”
*What is he talking about? Someone who wants it more than you is sitting quietly right here.*
Since I was thinking about it anyway, I discreetly glanced at Team Leader Choi.
Truthfully, I had agonized until the very end over whether to give Hero’s Soul to Xiao Shen or Team Leader Choi.
Team Leader Choi was human too, after all. He might have felt hurt.
But apparently, all that concern had been for nothing.
“Congratulations, Regimental Commander Shen. That is truly an excellent sword.”
At Team Leader Choi’s sincere congratulations, Xiao Shen finally came to his senses and looked back and forth between him and Hero’s Soul.
Conflict flickered in his eyes, but a bright smile soon spread across his face.
“I don’t think I’m the one this sword belongs to.”
“Mr. Choi, would you accept this sword in my place?”
I had not expected that.
Still...
*That’s nice to see.*
Team Leader Choi politely refused in his confusion, but Xiao Shen had already made up his mind, and his resolve proved stronger.
As I watched the two of them pass the sword back and forth, I quietly slipped out of the ward and started walking.
Before I closed the door, Team Leader Choi’s voice reached my ears.
“Of all the swords I’ve ever seen, I like this one the most.”
Right. Then that settled it.
I strode through the ranks of the troops who had already assembled.
The wall of people parted before me amid looks of awe.

If you can last ten minutes against me, I’ll take you along.”
“Is that what you call an offer, you shameless, wicked human?”
*Shameless, my ass.*
If anything, those two were the shameless ones.
They could barely run properly, yet they wanted me to take them onto a battlefield.
It was good that they were burning with fighting spirit, but heading into battle in their current condition was a surefire way to get themselves killed.
*And what kind of undead talks about conscience?*
*Why, I oughta...*
After making that threat in my head, I addressed the two thoroughly dejected men.
“For now, focus on recovering.
If you spend the next few days getting your feel back and your stamina returns, you might be deployed to the front then.
That goes for you too, Shen—not just Team Leader Choi.”
“Hmm.”
“Hmmmm.”
They still did not look happy, but at least they seemed somewhat resigned.
Both of them knew what condition their bodies were in.
They could not keep insisting forever.
“Then I’d better get going...
Ah.”
I had forgotten something.
Pretending to rummage through my bag enchanted with space-expansion magic, I pulled out the item I had stored in my Inventory and held it toward Xiao Shen.
“Here.”
Xiao Shen blinked.
“...Hyung?”
“What are you waiting for?
Take it.
My arm’s going to fall off.”
Xiao Shen reflexively accepted it and stared at me in confusion.
“What is this?”
“A gift.
Someone I know entrusted it to me, but I think you should have it.”
“A sword this fine?”
“Why?
You don’t want it?”
“No, that’s not it.
I’m just not sure I should accept something like this...”
Xiao Shen hurriedly waved his hands, then gazed almost dreamily at Hero’s Soul as he gripped its hilt.
Its weight distribution and balance were close to perfect, and the transparent blade gleamed with unmistakable sharpness.
He swallowed hard.
“Can I really accept this?”
“I’m not giving it to you for no reason.
I’m giving it to you because you qualify.”
“I qualify...?”
“That’s right.”
The courage he had shown in the last battle.
His sacrifice for someone else.
That was enough.
Besides, I had been using a spear for years.
If I kept the sword, it would only rot away in my Inventory.
Xiao Shen, another Chinese member of the Public Security Armed Forces Department, was a more fitting owner than I was.
*And since nothing happened when he grabbed the hilt, I guess the sword has accepted him too.*
The Skeleton Warlord grumbled quietly.
“This commander is good with a sword too...
This commander likes swords...”
*Huh?
What was that?*
It was hard to hear the words of a loser who had secretly grabbed Hero’s Soul from my Inventory at dawn and screamed.
“...Hmph, forget it.
A cheap sword like that is unworthy of this commander!”
*What is he talking about?
Someone who wants it more than you is sitting quietly right here.*
Since I was thinking about it anyway, I discreetly glanced at Team Leader Choi.
Truthfully, I had agonized until the very end over whether to give Hero’s Soul to Xiao Shen or Team Leader Choi.
Team Leader Choi was human too, after all.
He might have felt hurt.
But apparently, all that concern had been for nothing.
“Congratulations, Regimental Commander Shen.
That is truly an excellent sword.”
At Team Leader Choi’s sincere congratulations, Xiao Shen finally came to his senses and looked back and forth between him and Hero’s Soul.
Conflict flickered in his eyes, but a bright smile soon spread across his face.
“I don’t think I’m the one this sword belongs to.”
“Mr.
Choi, would you accept this sword in my place?”
I had not expected that.
Still...
*That’s nice to see.*
Team Leader Choi politely refused in his confusion, but Xiao Shen had already made up his mind, and his resolve proved stronger.
As I watched the two of them pass the sword back and forth, I quietly slipped out of the ward and started walking.
Before I closed the door, Team Leader Choi’s voice reached my ears.
“Of all the swords I’ve ever seen, I like this one the most.”
Right.
Then that settled it.
I strode through the ranks of the troops who had already assembled.
The wall of people parted before me amid looks of awe.

paragraphs: The age of the Great Cataclysm, which began with the descent of the Demon King Asmodeus, had been grim and chaotic. But humanity survived the crisis, swiftly repaired the damage, and built a civilization even more advanced than before.
Still, for some people, certain things mattered more than mana-stone elevators or healing potions.
“The internet got faster.”
The man who muttered those words in a reverent voice adjusted his glasses.
It was 11:30 a.m. Behind him, the ramen he had just dropped into the pot bubbled away, while cold rice and sour kimchi waited on the table.

Everything was ready. In exactly three minutes, he would add one—no, two—A-grade jumbo eggs he had agonized over buying during a supermarket sale. Then, after two more minutes, the perfect lunch would be complete.
And until then, the boredom would be solved by the marvelous modern civilization known as the smartphone.
“Let’s seeee, today’s news...”
Humming, the man skimmed the screen of his smartphone.
The main page of *Hunter University*, a massive online forum he frequented, had been updated with new top posts ranked by popularity.

1. **[Victory report after victory report—is the monster army already as good as shattered? The UN Security Council issues an official statement: “Humanity is strong. But the war is not over yet. We must not let our guard down until the very end.”]**
2. **[The Miracle of Sichuan Province. Jin Taekyung stood at the center of it all.]**
3. **[National prestige rises by the day as a new hero is born. K-pop and kimchi sales skyrocket.]**
4. **[Scheduled Korea-US summit to proceed... President Doramp makes a startling statement at an official event: “Is this Jin Taekyung’s country? He’s my idol.”]**
5. **[Ares Guild continues its string of victories. Truly living up to its reputation.]**
6. **[Chinese Chairman Xiao Yang: “Every one of them is a hero.”]**
7. **[Maesaeng-i.com Translation: Overseas netizens react to the current situation. “Who the hell is this ‘Lady of the House’ Koreans keep killing every chance they get?”]**

8. **[Japanese Prime Minister Maigumi Shinjiro: “The Monster Wave must be handled in a Fun, Cool, and Sexy manner.” When a reporter asked what that meant, he grinned and replied, “Explaining it wouldn’t be sexy.”]**
9. **[Russian President Furin: “To me, Shinjiro is like quantum mechanics. No matter how much I look at him, I can’t understand him.”]**

10. **[Web-novel author becomes a prophet: exclusive interview with Zerobic. “How do I feel right now? I’m still stunned. Since we’re on the subject, I’ll be taking a break today.” During the interview, his enraged editor burst in and injured him badly enough to require twelve weeks of treatment, resulting in an unexpected hiatus. Though bleeding, Zerobic smiled and said he was happy to be able to rest. His editor, Mr. Lee, wept. “He isn’t human.”]**
“Wow. This place is going absolutely nuts. Absolutely nuts.”
A smile tugged at the muttering man’s lips. No matter how far he scrolled, everything was about Jin Taekyung.
There seemed to be a few strange articles mixed in here and there, but simply reading them filled him with pride.
The comment section was already on the verge of exploding.

└ The activity here is insane lately. I’ve been on Hunter University since elementary school, but I’ve never seen it this heated before;; └ The truly insane one is Jin Taekyung. He carved through a monster army ten thousand strong all by himself. It still makes no sense when I think about it. How the hell did he do that? └ He’s amazing, but let’s get the facts straight. It wasn’t ten thousand, just a few thousand. └ LMAOOOO isn’t that still completely insane? └ For realᄏᄏᄏᄏ You’re the kind of bastard who’d get a goblin’s poison stinger in the ass and yell, “Ow, please let go gently!” Aren’t you the same guy who used an aura blade with your keyboard last time?

└ But at this point, Jin Taekyung doesn’t seem like an ordinary S-rank Hunter. Are all the other S-rank Hunters like that too? └ Even during the Great Cataclysm, feats on this level were rare. Cheon Taemin doesn’t count because he was just on another level entirely... But if you look at the records from the Great Cataclysm, Lee Jungryong probably accomplished something similar too. └ Hmm. So he still isn’t at Lee Jungryong’s level? Disappointing. └ ?? Do you think Lee Jungryong is some old man hanging around a spring on the neighborhood hill? Cheon Taemin may have overshadowed him, but judging by his achievements, martial power, and influence, he’s still one of the top figures in the entire world. └ 222. You only have to look at what happened a week ago. He wiped out the monster army with the fewest casualties across all five fronts. Jin Taekyung is incredible, but Lee Jungryong and Ares Guild are fucking amazing too. The northern front is actually advancing a little faster right now. └ Comments like this make me nervous for no reason. I’m worried that a bunch of idiots will show up again and start going wild with the versus arguments. └ They’ve been IP-banned to hell, so it should be fine. But at this point, isn’t the whole incident basically over? They’re crushing the monsters with mobile warfare right now. └ Undefeated for an entire week ᄃᄃᄃ; └ The Arch Lich must be panicking too. He put everything into that surprise attack a week ago and still got completely wrecked. The Death Knight Lord is dead, and the survivors who ran away are being harvested right now. They’re screwed.

└ At this point, shouldn’t the Arch Lich be making a move? He’s so quiet that it feels strange. └ I had the same thought, so I sent him a KakaoTalk message yesterday to see how he was doing. └ ? To whom? └ The Arch Lich. He said he was busy with his promotion match. Apparently, he was excited because winning this game would get him to Gold. └ The guy above is fucking insane. └ Zerobic is even more insane. Why the hell is that bastard suddenly taking a break? You’re supposed to row while the tide is in. This is ridiculous. └ Stop talking bullshit. The important thing is that if things continue like this, we can suppress this Monster Wave without suffering any more major losses. Let’s pray that the situation ends soon and observe a moment of silence for the victims. └ Hmm... I don’t like China, but I agree with this. Idiots and normal people coexist in every country. Good luck to all the Hunters and soldiers. └ Fighting.
The netizens were generally in high spirits.

The Monster Wave, which had initially been taken with deadly seriousness, had now become fodder for national pride. Even in the comments mourning the dead and cheering on those fighting, there was hope instead of fear.
*Then again, we have been hearing a lot of good news lately.*
The man nodded. It was only natural. According to the battlefield reports from the UN Security Council, there was no doubt that the tide had already turned decisively.

A week ago, the surprise attack launched simultaneously against all five fronts had caused enormous damage. But reinforcements far exceeding the number of casualties had been dispatched, and victory after victory had followed.
*At this rate, it might be over in a few days.*
Their momentum was unstoppable, like splitting bamboo. The Western Front under Jin Taekyung and the northern front led by Lee Jungryong stood out the most.
*The little punk. I was so worried about him at first, but he’s doing even better than I expected.*
After a moment’s hesitation, the man logged into the site and left a comment.

└ **Jin Taekyung’s Roommate:** Is this really the same loser Jin Taekyung? The real Jin Taekyung is a legend. I used to eat ramen with him all the time back in the day, and now he’s become an S-rank Hunter, a king-like existence, and the world’s strongest legendary hero. Looking at Jin Taekyung now honestly brings tears to my eyes...
Replies began springing up like weeds the instant he posted it.
The man gazed down at his phone with a pleased expression.
Then Seong Jinho suddenly realized he had forgotten something important.
“No! My ramen!”
“Man, I could really go for some ramen.”
At my mutter, Team Leader Choi, who stood beside me, asked, “Out of nowhere?”
Having finished recovering, he had rejoined us at the front aboard a jet last night.
“Yeah. Weird, isn’t it?”
“Considering the situation, you seem even more impressive, Mr. Jin.”
Slash!
Hero’s Soul flashed through the air, slicing through both the Lizardman’s weapon and its body.
Green blood gushed out, accompanied by a stench that stabbed straight into my nose. My appetite vanished in an instant as I launched myself forward.
Fwoooosh! Boom!
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
Terrible heat engulfed dozens of Lizardmen and burst into flames. The monsters recoiling at the sight already looked like routed soldiers.
Reading the flow of battle, Xiao Shen charged to the front and shouted.
“Charge! Charge!”
“Waaaaaah!”
“Blade of the wind, descend upon this place! Wind Cutter!”
Shwish-shwish-shwish-shwish!
Clang! Slash!
—Kueeeek!
—Kiruk, krk!
Overwhelmed by the human offensive pouring down like a wave, the monsters were helplessly driven back.
Their numbers were roughly even, but the monsters were no match for us in either morale or the quality of their forces.
Once the front line collapsed like a sandcastle, several terrified monsters turned and fled.
*And collapse happens in an instant.*
Fear was contagious.
When one fled, ten followed. After that came an uncontrollable rout.
Sure enough, my prediction proved correct, and cries of certain victory soon rang out.
“Pursue them! Don’t let a single one survive!”
“Get the speed buffs up!”
“Ranged units! Ready—fire!”
Shwish-shwish! Boom!
The Hunters, their momentum at its peak, began slaughtering the monsters fleeing without even maintaining formation.
It did not take long for the six-lane asphalt road, which would have been packed with cars only a month ago, to become buried beneath monster corpses.
“We won again.”
After the battle, I was checking my equipment when Team Leader Choi approached me. I shrugged.
“For someone delivering good news, you don’t look very happy.”
“That’s strange. I was just thinking the same thing while looking at you, Mr. Jin.”
Apparently, we had been thinking along the same lines.
Just as he said, I felt no joy at all despite our victory.
I had first noticed this same sense of unease on the second day after we launched our mobile campaign for the full-scale counterattack.
“What do you think, Team Leader Choi?”
“What exactly are you asking about? The sharp decline in both the number and quality of the monsters? Or the dozens of victories you’ve won over the past week?”
“Both.”
“You’re probably thinking exactly what I am. The current state of the war is certainly encouraging, but... something doesn’t feel right.”
Team Leader Choi looked toward the celebrating people.
Smiles spread across exhausted faces, each one filled with the hope that the war would soon end and they could return to the arms of their loved ones.

“It’s not that I can’t understand how this happened. There were so many high-level monsters during the early stages of the war. If they lost their elite forces, it would explain the current situation. But...”
“The Arch Lich. That bastard wouldn’t make things this easy for us. Would he, Team Leader Choi?”
Team Leader Choi nodded slightly.
“Does command share our suspicions?”
“Probably. I don’t know about the other S-rank Hunters, but Minister of National Defense Wei Fenghu understood the situation perfectly.”
“That’s a relief, but...”
Team Leader Choi trailed off. Once again, he had probably arrived at the same thought I had.
We were practically at our destination, Suining City.
The Arch Lich had not shown himself even once throughout the entire war. What the hell was he doing right now?
“Hmm. He should be greasing his bones about now. Becoming a magnificent undead requires proper maintenance, you know.”
*Shut up already.*
Whoooosh.
A vast space.
The darkness swirling within it was drawn toward a single point.
As the pitch-black darkness vanished, the light of the setting sun streamed through shattered windows and fell upon a solitary being.
“Come, Adversary.”
The voice was as cold as the winter wind.
Having gathered his magical power, the Arch Lich’s eyes gleamed.

chapters.title: Chapter 407
paragraphs: Daniel Inoue was Japanese American.
A former Navy SEAL, he had awakened as an A-rank Hunter at the age of thirty. After leaving the military, he joined a private military company, where he put his abilities to excellent use.
Mercenary work suited Inoue well enough. He had to spend half of every year in conflict zones across the Middle East and Africa, but the pay was enormous, and he got long stretches of time off.
He had joined the response to the Monster Wave in China for much the same reason.
“Hey, ninja. What are you thinking about?”
At his comrade’s sudden question, Inoue narrowed his eyes.
“Shut up, Sam. Aren’t you sick of that damn ninja crap yet?”
“What’s the big deal? You should be used to it by now.”
“That’s exactly why I’m sick of it. Try being called a ninja or samurai since you were seven. It’ll drive you insane.”
“Why? Sounds pretty good to me.”
“You damn Yankee bastard.”
“I’ll take that as a compliment. I’m a Yankees fan.”
The small white man snickered at Inoue’s grumbling.
“Just accept it already. At this point, it’s fate. Even your abilities are totally ninja-like.”
“...Damn it.”
Inoue muttered a quiet curse.
Just as his comrade had said, the ability he had received upon awakening was perfectly suited to stealth.
Thanks to it, he had become a specialist in espionage and targeted assassinations. Unfortunately, it had also cemented his image as a ninja.
“I heard your girlfriend’s pregnant. How about naming the baby Naruto?”
Inoue raised his middle finger at his relentlessly annoying comrade.
“If you name your son Sasuke, I’ll think about it.”
“Oh, not bad.”
Quiet snickers escaped from the people around them.
The atmosphere, stiff and tense only moments ago, began to loosen. Inoue and his comrade exchanged faint smiles.
The two had been close friends and partners for years. Their exchange had been little more than a skit meant to ease the tension before the mission began.
*Too much tension only makes people commit one mistake after another.*
That was true in battle, but even more so during an intelligence operation like this one.

They were entering unknown territory where neither communications nor magic could be used. Worse, their opponent was not some stupid, brutal rebel leader, but the Arch Lich that had unleashed an unprecedented Monster Wave.
*No matter how favorable the war is going, we can’t afford to let our guard down.*
Having reminded himself of that, Inoue addressed the twenty intelligence operatives.

“Listen up. From this point on, we’ll infiltrate in pairs. Use hand signals to communicate, and fire your signal flare in an emergency. You’ve all memorized your destinations and routes down to the last detail, right?”
“Yes.”
“Good. Then... we meet back here in three hours. Dismissed.”

At Inoue’s words announcing the start of the operation, the intelligence operatives nodded and scattered in every direction. Watching them disappear silently and swiftly, his partner Sam jerked his chin toward the path ahead.
“Should we get moving too, ninja?”
“Yeah, you carefree Yankee bastard.”
“Don’t be like that. You’re the best at this. Three hours from now, you’ll be on your way back after finding out what color underwear the Arch Lich is wearing.”
“...I really hope so.”
Inoue let out a quiet sigh and stepped forward. The pale fog blanketing Suining City clung damply to his entire body.
The advance of the five fronts, which had seemed unstoppable, finally came to a halt.
We were two hundred kilometers from Suining City, where the Arch Lich was located. While we rested and reorganized, a welcome face came to visit.
“Hey, Korean friends. How have you been?”
I sensed a considerable wave of qi nearby, and sure enough, it was him. I bumped fists with Magic Johnson and answered.
“Pretty well.”
“Jin. My lovable Miracle Boy. I missed you.”
“Sorry, but could you leave out the ‘lovable’ part?”
“Then I’ll call you Crazy Boy. You did pull off something crazy, after all.”
Magic Johnson grinned and added,
“And incredibly heroic. The same goes for Choi here.”
Team Leader Choi, who had been carefully polishing Hero's Soul, inclined his head.
“It’s good to see you again, Mr. Johnson.”
“Choi, don’t be like that. You’re making things stiff.”
“The atmosphere, of course.”
Magic Johnson threw back his head and laughed.
At this point, it was obvious he enjoyed watching our reactions. He was surprisingly playful for such a huge man.
Well, by now, we knew that everything was a joke whenever we met Magic Johnson.
Even Team Leader Choi, who always did Kegel exercises whenever he met him, gave a quiet laugh before asking,
“But what brings you here?”
“An emergency summons from headquarters. It’s an important matter.”
I frowned and muttered,
“This feels like déjà vu. Haven’t we seen this setup before?”
“Don’t worry, Jin. Nothing like last time will happen.”
By “last time,” he meant our main camp getting completely wrecked while the S-rank Hunters were away.
Well, the distance between the fronts had narrowed now. Even if everyone gathered together, we were practically close enough to touch noses if we fell over, so it should be fine.
*If they aren’t handling this over communications, it must be that important.*

As the Allied Forces continued winning and the monsters retreated, the Arch Lich’s territory had shrunk all the way back to Suining City. At our current location, both communications and magic worked smoothly.
“Do you know what we’re gathering for?”
“No. But I can guarantee it won’t be pleasant. I’ll stake my life on it.”
Please. Don’t stake your life on something like that. Give us a little more hope.
But Magic Johnson, as confident as ever, held out his hands to Team Leader Choi and me.
“Anyway, everyone else is already there. You two are the last guests.”
“Then please take us there, Mr. Johnson.”
Team Leader Choi took his hand without hesitation. Having already experienced Magic Johnson’s teleportation once, I nervously grabbed his fingers.
“Please drive safely—Gyaaaaaaaah!”
Whoooosh!
With the sensation of my entire body being crushed like a soda can, I was flung into a new space.
“Gyaaaaaaa...”
Damn it. Of all places, it had to be here.
A dozen pairs of eyes stared at me in silence. Under the dumbfounded gazes of the S-rank Hunters and senior Chinese generals, I stopped screaming and quietly slipped into an empty seat.
“Are we not starting the meeting?”
After a moment at a loss for words, Minister of National Defense Wei Fenghu finally spoke.
“...Then let us begin the meeting.”
The meeting that followed focused on a single subject: the information brought back by the intelligence team’s sole survivor.

“Daniel Inoue, who was in charge of the intelligence team, escaped from Suining City after eight hours—far beyond the scheduled operation time—and reported discovering a monster army numbering around thirty thousand.”
Thirty thousand...
It was an enormous force, but still well within the range we had expected.
The Arch Lich’s monster army had suffered its first defeat a week ago and had been retreating helplessly ever since, sustaining tremendous losses along the way.
“Judging by your expression, Minister, that isn’t all.”
Few people present could speak so casually to Minister Wei Fenghu.
Lee Jungryong was one of them. Whatever his personal feelings toward me, he had more than earned that right.
“Mr. Lee is correct. Thirty thousand is only the estimate based on what Inoue personally witnessed. The true number...”
“Could be twice that. Perhaps even more.”
“That is correct.”
Low groans rose from around the room. We had expected the enemy to be holding forces in reserve for the final battle, but not that many.
Wei Fenghu continued solemnly.
“However, most of the monsters are likely to be mid- or low-level. That is our one small consolation.”
“The same is true of our forces, Wei Fenghu.”
At the remark from Faye Chen, who had been silently sipping from a liquor glass, Prince Felix nodded.
“She is right. More troops than expected have joined our side, but we still cannot be certain of victory.”
“Damn it. Those monsters never end, no matter how many we kill.”
I couldn’t help snorting at Wu Heixing’s grumbling.
“Why are you laughing?”
“Because it’s funny, you idiot.”
“What?”

“Anyone listening would think you’d been fighting your ass off. You’re the bastard who tried to take a detour during the monster army’s attack a week ago because you thought arriving early might be dangerous.”
His expression was a sight to behold.
He must have thought no one knew, but word of Wu Heixing’s disgrace had already spread across every front.
“I know you’ve had a rough time too, but don’t whine in front of me or anyone else. Just looking at you is starting to piss me off.”
“What are you, self-employed? Why do you keep going *iik*?”
Wu Heixing’s face turned bright red. His body twitched as though he might charge at me at any moment, but that was as far as he could go.
The bitter memory of defeat lingered.
A hothouse flower that had spent its whole life being treated like royalty was bound to wither in a cold wind.
Of course, there were flowers of an entirely different sort.
Like Team Leader Choi, who was sitting beside me.
“That’s enough, both of you.”
At Team Leader Choi’s calm intervention, Wu Heixing glared at him.
“Are you ordering me around?”
“If that’s how you took it, I’m sorry to hear that, Wu Heixing.”
Team Leader Choi did not so much as blink at Wu Heixing’s threatening aura. Wu Heixing shot to his feet.
No, he tried to.
“Sit.”
My aura struck like an awl, and his body locked in place.
The other S-rank Hunters turned startled eyes toward me.
I glanced at Lee Jungryong’s deeply sunken gaze before continuing.
“Just so there’s no misunderstanding, yes, that was an order.”
“You, you...!”
“Sit. I won’t say it again.”
Whoooosh!
A wave of aura surged toward him, and Wu Heixing’s lower lip trembled.
Perhaps he would have counted as a genius even in Murim.
No, he definitely would have. Becoming an S-rank Hunter in his thirties would have been impossible without that level of talent.
*But he was only half the package.*
Awakening was an unearned windfall. Like a lottery winner, he had received extraordinary abilities and mana the moment he turned twenty.
And he was supposed to build up internal energy like a Murim practitioner and master martial arts at the Supreme Peak level?
*Well...*
Learning martial arts might make up for his technical shortcomings, but there was no doubt he would fall by the wayside long before he ever reached that point.
Compared to his talent, his effort and will were Third Rate.
“Enough.”
Lee Jungryong’s gentle baritone broke the tension.
The old snake, still looking like a handsome middle-aged man despite being well past sixty, watched me with a smile.
“I thought only your skills had improved, but your killing intent has grown stronger too.”
I met his eyes impassively.
“Rolling around in all sorts of places tends to put an edge on you.”
“I heard the Western Front was particularly fierce.”
“That’s not wrong. Want to come see the Western Front?”
“I must politely decline. If it was fierce enough that only three people survived, I think I’ll pass.”
“The older I get, the more cowardly I become. Ho ho.”
The blood in my veins turned cold.
That horrific battlefield flashed before my eyes, and before I knew it, a faint smile had formed on my lips.
“What are you trying to say?”
“Let’s think about something more productive than turning on our allies. Planning for the final battle would be a good place to start. Jin Taekyung, what do you think?”
I quietly tapped the armrest of my chair.
My insides twisted, but Lee Jungryong’s words had struck at the heart of the matter.
He was right. The battle bearing down on us was practically at our doorstep. That was what we needed to deal with now.
Then one thought came to me.
“A suicide squad.”
“A suicide squad?”
Everyone’s eyes turned toward me. Some nodded in agreement, while others looked uneasy.
But both reason and instinct told me this was our best chance to win while minimizing our losses.
“We gather our very best and cut off the head.”
Once the Arch Lich is destroyed, the undead army will collapse.

chapters.title: Chapter 408
paragraphs: “A suicide squad.”
The moment those words left Jin Taekyung’s mouth, Wu Heixing forgot his rising anger and nearly shouted.
*You crazy bangzi bastard!*
A suicide squad.
Wasn’t that exactly what it meant—to charge in prepared to die?
Even if they somehow broke through the monster army without knowing its exact numbers, the real monster—the Arch Lich—would be waiting behind it. The mere thought made Wu Heixing’s hair stand on end.
*This... this is insane.*
Wu Heixing didn’t care how many casualties they suffered.
China was a Great Nation with a population of over a billion, after all. Even if a hundred thousand or a million people vanished, they would amount to no more than a handful.
In fact, if that damn bangzi took the vanguard of the suicide squad and died a glorious death, Wu Heixing would happily raise both hands in celebration.
But...
“Let’s gather our very best and take out the head.”
That meant Wu Heixing himself would be included in the suicide squad. And he had no intention of taking even the slightest risk.
“Cut that ridiculous bullshit—”
Unable to hold back any longer, Wu Heixing shot to his feet and opened his mouth.
“Oh, that’s an excellent idea.”
Wu Heixing stared wide-eyed, unable to continue.
He had never imagined that Lee Jungryong would side with Jin Taekyung.
Not just anyone, but Lee Jungryong himself.
“W-What did you just say?”
“I said it was an excellent idea.”
Lee Jungryong continued with a gentle smile.

“We need to end this battle as quickly as possible. The Arch Lich is likely creating new undead even now. If the S-rank Hunters lead the advance and destroy it, the monster army—made up mostly of undead—will collapse, reducing our casualties.”
“M-Mr. Lee.”
“I imagine you agree with me. Just like everyone else here. Isn’t that right, Mr. Wu?”
“Everyone else? What are you talking about?”
Only then did Wu Heixing look around in confusion.
Not only Wei Fenghu and the other high-ranking Chinese generals, but also Faye Chen, Magic Johnson, and even Prince Felix were nodding slightly as they exchanged opinions.
“Hmm. Certainly...”
“Even if we reinforce our forces, the Arch Lich will do the same. The longer we drag this out, the larger the battle will become.”
“What if we select A-rank Hunters and other veterans, deploy them to one side, and have the S-rank Hunters lead the breakthrough?”
“It would be dangerous, but the plan has a real chance of success.”
“No matter how powerful a Named Monster the Arch Lich may be, we should have a good chance if the S-rank Hunters attack it together.”
Wu Heixing’s face went white as the conversation reached his ears.
*Have these people lost their minds?*
They were actually looking favorably upon this insane operation. They must have all gone mad.
Even Lee Jungryong, whom Wu Heixing had trusted, had sided with Jin Taekyung for some reason.
Desperate to avoid being included in the suicide squad, Wu Heixing hurriedly turned toward Jin Taekyung.
“W-Wait! If all the S-rank Hunters leave, wouldn’t that create a massive hole in our forces?”
“Gasp.”
Jin Taekyung sucked in a startled breath and looked at Wu Heixing in surprise.
“Wow. You do use your brain once in a while.”
“You’re right. We should probably leave a few people behind.”
*That damn bangzi.*
But this was no time to get angry. Wu Heixing suppressed his surging fury and continued.
“R-Right. So, to prepare for any unforeseen circumstances, I—”
Jin Taekyung abruptly cut him off and turned toward Magic Johnson.
“It seems like you should stay behind. What do you think, Johnson?”
“Me?”
What kind of situation was this? Wu Heixing desperately tried to intervene.
“M-Magic Johnson? Wouldn’t it be better to have at least one mage come with us?”
“Of course that would be good. It would—but...”
Jin Taekyung gave Wu Heixing a pleasant smile.
“What about the rear?”
“Huh?”
“What happens if the Arch Lich teleports behind our lines and attacks us from the rear? Are you going to stop it?”

“No matter how powerful the Arch Lich is, it won’t be able to pull something like that if a grand mage stays behind to interfere with its magic. And Magic Johnson’s wide-area magic could turn the tide of the battle.”
Every word made perfect sense. Wu Heixing’s mouth snapped shut, and Jin Taekyung clicked his tongue.
“Think before you run your mouth. Stop watching those ‘watch your rear’ GIFs on the internet and start thinking about the rear in an actual war.”
Ignoring Wu Heixing, who had frozen like a statue, Jin Taekyung asked Magic Johnson,
“What do you think?”
“You’re right, Jin. So I’m the only one staying behind?”
Defense Minister Wei Fenghu, who had been silently observing the situation, suddenly spoke.

“The Arch Lich must have held a large number of high-level monsters in reserve for the final battle. Far more than the number of A-rank Hunters on our side. We will need at least two more S-rank Hunters to maintain an evenly matched battlefield.”
It wasn’t over yet. Two spots still remained.
Finding a glimmer of hope, Wu Heixing cleared his throat.
“Then I suppose I have no choice but to stay—”
“If the others have no objections, I would first like to exclude Prince Felix.”
“What?”
“I’m sorry, but I cannot explain the details. There is a complicated issue involved.”

Felix was not merely an S-rank Hunter. He was a member of the royal family and practically a symbol of the United Kingdom. Nor was he some insignificant member of a distant branch. He was third in line to the throne.
Everyone present understood that the “complicated issue” Wei Fenghu could not explain was a diplomatic problem with the United Kingdom.
“Well, his father is the King of the United Kingdom, so I suppose that’s possible. Then the prince is out.”
At Jin Taekyung’s words, Prince Felix spoke with an uncomfortable expression.
“I hope you understand that this is not my choice. However, I have been bound to the royal family since birth, and I cannot disobey my royal father’s command—”
“It’s fine. I don’t care. I’d actually prefer it this way, since it would leave a bad taste in my mouth if the United Kingdom’s fourth in line to the throne got hurt during the operation I proposed.”
“Third! And show proper respect when speaking to me.”
“Oh, right. Congratulations on the bronze medal. Then, does anyone object to His Highness Prince Felix, that living hotbed of entrenched privilege, sitting this one out thanks to his connections?”
Wu Heixing started to raise his hand without thinking, only to stop when Faye Chen and Lee Jungryong answered.
“I don’t mind.”
“I agree.”
Jin Taekyung nodded and fixed Wu Heixing with a long stare.
“What about you?”
“M-Me?”
“When the only guy left asks that, what am I supposed to tell him? Tinky Winky, Dipsy, or Po. Pick one.”
There was no way out.
Magic Johnson and Prince Felix were foreigners, and both had legitimate reasons to remain behind. Even Faye Chen and Lee Jungryong had agreed.
Wu Heixing squeezed his eyes shut, opened them again, and muttered,
“...Agreed.”
“Answer properly. If you say it like that, how the hell am I supposed to know whether you mean agreement or *Donguibogam*? Are you Heo Jun?”
“I... agree.”
“Okay.”
It happened at Quick Attack speed.
One spot still remained, but Wu Heixing felt a sense of foreboding.
And it didn’t take long for that foreboding to become certainty.
“I would like Faye Chen to fill the final position.”
But what had thrown Wu Heixing into confusion was that it wasn’t Jin Taekyung who had blocked his last escape route.
It was Lee Jungryong.
*What in the world is that old man thinking?*
Wu Heixing vividly remembered the conversation he had shared with Lee Jungryong on the day Jin Taekyung had trampled him into the ground.
*He clearly suggested that we join forces. And now he’s stabbing me in the back like this?*
Faye Chen glanced at Wu Heixing as he ground his teeth, then tipped back her liquor glass.
“Well, Mr. Lee, I’m not the sort who enjoys danger. But wouldn’t our odds of success be higher if we left that brat behind instead of me?”
“No, Faye Chen. You will do more to reduce casualties by remaining behind.”
“You don’t know that kid. Just looking at him makes even someone who never had any patriotism develop some.”
“Don’t worry. I’ll be here.”
His tone was calm but filled with certainty.
Only Lee Jungryong could say such a thing with such confidence.
The old hero’s gaze, carrying an assurance no one present could deny, settled on one person.
“And Jin Taekyung. You’ll be there too, won’t you?”
His eyes were deep and unreadable.
Jin Taekyung silently met Lee Jungryong’s gaze before answering.
“Our dear Vice Guild Master certainly has a talent for making the obvious sound complicated.”
“May I take that to mean you will also be joining the suicide squad?”
“Of course.”
“Brave. Heroic, even. In that case, I’ll yield the vanguard to you.”
“Great. Does that mean I get to leave behind a famous quote like Louis Armstrong? Something like, ‘This is one small step for a man, but for monsters, it’s the Heavenly Demon’s Reign.’”
“That’s rather crude for a quote destined for the history books. And you have the name wrong. It wasn’t Louis Armstrong. It was Neil Armstrong.”
“You’re certainly well educated. Still, your academic credentials have nothing on the length of my tissue roll.”
The people around them developed pounding headaches trying to follow Jin Taekyung’s answers, while Wu Heixing fell into despair.
Until barely a month ago, he had been enjoying a lavish yacht party surrounded by dozens of beautiful women.
Now he had been assigned to a suicide squad prepared to die.
And then, in the very next moment—
—Do you think I betrayed you?
—Accept it. I promise there will be no danger.
As the Sound Transmission pierced his ears, Wu Heixing slowly raised his head.
Lee Jungryong was looking at him with a gentle smile as he continued speaking.
“He’ll carry out his assigned duty well. I guarantee it.”
Jin Taekyung slowly tapped the armrest of his chair as he replied,
“I’m looking forward to seeing just how brilliantly he carries out his duty.”
The rather lengthy meeting came to an end.

The suicide squad would be led by S-rank Hunters, with high-level A-rank Hunters and veteran B-rank Hunters making up the rest. The command staff would be working around the clock to select its members.
The Skeleton Warlord had remained silent throughout the meeting. But the moment we returned to the tent assigned to me on the Western Front, it solemnly declared,
“This commander will sit out this battle.”
“Yeah, fuck off.”
“At least ask why, you treacherous human.”
“Fine. Why?”
“As the commander of an undead army, this commander is reluctant to fight his own kind.”
I answered with a dumbfounded expression.
“What the fuck are you talking about? Who’s been sucking the energy out of his own kind to nourish himself this whole time?”
“Let’s be honest. If you said you just didn’t want to go because you were scared of the Arch Lich, would I curse at you?”
“You would.”
“You son of a—... Oh.”
The Skeleton Warlord’s distrust of me deepened even further as it spoke.
“In any case, this commander no longer wishes to take part in this war. Honor the promise you made that day.”
“The promise I made that day?”
“Have you ever seen such a treacherous human? Didn’t you promise that, in exchange for protecting two humans, you would grant any request I made?”
“Oh.”
It had been a while since I’d been left speechless.
I had definitely made that promise. Normally, I would have brushed it off by pretending to have amnesia, but this time I couldn’t ignore it in good conscience.
“Fine. What’s your wish?”
The Skeleton Warlord shouted as though it had been waiting for the question.
“Give me freedom!”
“Freedom?”
“That is correct. You, treacherous human, have insulted and abused this commander all this time! No fewer than 408 times!”
“...Did you come from an animal rights group or something?”
“Honor your promise! This commander shall finally find freedom!”
Freedom.
My head was already cluttered with thoughts of Lee Jungryong, so a wish like that hadn’t even occurred to me.
After thinking for a moment, I answered.
“Fine. I’ll give you freedom.”
“Ooh! Ooooooh!”
“Goodbye, then.”
“Huh?”
Without hesitation, I pulled the Skeleton Warlord’s skull from my Inventory and threw it outside the tent.
Into the middle of the thousands of Hunters swarming around outside.
Clack!
The sound of it hitting something rang out, and the area around the tent erupted into chaos. Shouts came from every direction, followed by the thunderous roar of exploding magic.
“Monster! Monster attack!”
“Kill it!”
Boom! Kaboom!
How much time passed?
Five minutes? Ten?
Rustle, rustle.
The bottom edge of the tent suddenly began to shift. Then a black, glossy skull rolled in and stopped at my feet.
“Oh, look who it is.”
“What brings the Skeleton Warlord, proud owner of a free spirit, here?”
“You... human...”
A red glow flickered pitifully within the skull’s empty eye sockets.
Was I imagining it, or was an undead actually whimpering?
The Skeleton Warlord continued in a tearful voice.
“Can I... take back my wish?”
“Oh, of course.”
I continued in the chipper tone of a customer-service representative.
“But you know wish coupons can’t be exchanged or refunded, right?”
“Come here, Golgoli.”
Hop.
The Skeleton Warlord feebly jumped into my arms.

“Cut that ridiculous bullshit—”
Unable to hold back any longer, Wu Heixing shot to his feet and opened his mouth.
“Oh, that’s an excellent idea.”

“W-What did you just say?”
“I said it was an excellent idea.”
Lee Jungryong continued with a gentle smile.
“We need to end this battle as quickly as possible.

If the S-rank Hunters lead the advance and destroy it, the monster army—made up mostly of undead—will collapse, reducing our casualties.”
“M-Mr.
Lee.”
“I imagine you agree with me.
Just like everyone else here.
Isn’t that right, Mr.
Wu?”
“Everyone else?
What are you talking about?”
Only then did Wu Heixing look around in confusion.
Not only Wei Fenghu and the other high-ranking Chinese generals, but also Faye Chen, Magic Johnson, and even Prince Felix were nodding slightly as they exchanged opinions.
“Hmm.

“Even if we reinforce our forces, the Arch Lich will do the same.

“What if we select A-rank Hunters and other veterans, deploy them to one side, and have the S-rank Hunters lead the breakthrough?”
“It would be dangerous, but the plan has a real chance of success.”

Wu Heixing’s face went white as the conversation reached his ears.

They were actually looking favorably upon this insane operation.
They must have all gone mad.
Even Lee Jungryong, whom Wu Heixing had trusted, had sided with Jin Taekyung for some reason.
Desperate to avoid being included in the suicide squad, Wu Heixing hurriedly turned toward Jin Taekyung.
“W-Wait!
If all the S-rank Hunters leave, wouldn’t that create a massive hole in our forces?”
“Gasp.”
Jin Taekyung sucked in a startled breath and looked at Wu Heixing in surprise.
“Wow.
You do use your brain once in a while.”
“You’re right.
We should probably leave a few people behind.”
*That damn bangzi.*
But this was no time to get angry.
Wu Heixing suppressed his surging fury and continued.
“R-Right.
So, to prepare for any unforeseen circumstances, I—”
Jin Taekyung abruptly cut him off and turned toward Magic Johnson.
“It seems like you should stay behind.
What do you think, Johnson?”
“Me?”
What kind of situation was this?
Wu Heixing desperately tried to intervene.
“M-Magic Johnson?
Wouldn’t it be better to have at least one mage come with us?”
“Of course that would be good.
It would—but...”
Jin Taekyung gave Wu Heixing a pleasant smile.
“What about the rear?”
“Huh?”
“What happens if the Arch Lich teleports behind our lines and attacks us from the rear?
Are you going to stop it?”
“No matter how powerful the Arch Lich is, it won’t be able to pull something like that if a grand mage stays behind to interfere with its magic.
And Magic Johnson’s wide-area magic could turn the tide of the battle.”
Every word made perfect sense.
Wu Heixing’s mouth snapped shut, and Jin Taekyung clicked his tongue.
“Think before you run your mouth.
Stop watching those ‘watch your rear’ GIFs on the internet and start thinking about the rear in an actual war.”
Ignoring Wu Heixing, who had frozen like a statue, Jin Taekyung asked Magic Johnson,
“What do you think?”
“You’re right, Jin.
So I’m the only one staying behind?”
Defense Minister Wei Fenghu, who had been silently observing the situation, suddenly spoke.
“The Arch Lich must have held a large number of high-level monsters in reserve for the final battle.
Far more than the number of A-rank Hunters on our side.
We will need at least two more S-rank Hunters to maintain an evenly matched battlefield.”
It wasn’t over yet.
Two spots still remained.
Finding a glimmer of hope, Wu Heixing cleared his throat.
“Then I suppose I have no choice but to stay—”
“If the others have no objections, I would first like to exclude Prince Felix.”
“What?”
“I’m sorry, but I cannot explain the details.
There is a complicated issue involved.”
Felix was not merely an S-rank Hunter.
He was a member of the royal family and practically a symbol of the United Kingdom.
Nor was he some insignificant member of a distant branch.
He was third in line to the throne.
Everyone present understood that the “complicated issue” Wei Fenghu could not explain was a diplomatic problem with the United Kingdom.
“Well, his father is the King of the United Kingdom, so I suppose that’s possible.
Then the prince is out.”
At Jin Taekyung’s words, Prince Felix spoke with an uncomfortable expression.
“I hope you understand that this is not my choice.
However, I have been bound to the royal family since birth, and I cannot disobey my royal father’s command—”
“It’s fine.
I don’t care.
I’d actually prefer it this way, since it would leave a bad taste in my mouth if the United Kingdom’s fourth in line to the throne got hurt during the operation I proposed.”

And show proper respect when speaking to me.”
“Oh, right.

“I agree.”

“What about you?”
“M-Me?”

Tinky Winky, Dipsy, or Po.
Pick one.”
There was no way out.
Magic Johnson and Prince Felix were foreigners, and both had legitimate reasons to remain behind.
Even Faye Chen and Lee Jungryong had agreed.

“Answer properly.

Are you Heo Jun?”
