chapters.title: Chapter 409
paragraphs: An unannounced visitor arrived before dawn had fully broken.
He stepped carefully into the tent and met my eyes as I sat cross-legged.
“You were already awake.”
“As you can see.”
I shrugged at Team Leader Choi.
“I haven’t been sleeping much lately.”
More accurately, I needed less sleep.
With stamina that had surpassed human limits and formidable internal energy amounting to three jiazi, I could blow away most fatigue by circulating my qi.
“Were you practicing the Mana Cultivation Method—or rather, the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique?”
“Yeah, something like that.”
To be exact, I was practicing the Fire Gate Divine Technique, the secret cultivation technique of the Fire Gate Clan. But I couldn’t tell him every last detail.
“I should have come later.”
“No, it’s fine.”
“Didn’t you say that cultivation must never be interrupted? That stopping midway could cause qi deviation...”
“Oh, that applies to you, Team Leader Choi. I’m fine. We’re on different levels.”
*Warning: your fact attack may hurt someone.*
For a moment, I could practically see the public-service announcement flashing across Team Leader Choi’s face.
He gave me a sour look, then slowly shook his head.
“I can’t argue with the truth.”
“Still, you’re learning incredibly fast. I mean that sincerely, so have a little more confidence.”
I did mean it. As befitted a descendant of Cheon Taemin, the hero who had achieved an indomitable feat in human history, Team Leader Choi possessed extraordinary natural martial talent.
For some reason, he also had a considerable amount of qi stored within his body, so his progress in martial arts was astonishingly fast.
In short, he was a talent with all the groundwork already laid.
*If he’d learned martial arts from childhood like Wu Heixing... he’d probably be an S-rank Hunter by now.*
Team Leader Choi’s expression softened slightly, and he nodded.
“How do I compare to Jin Taekyung?”
“Are you kidding? Of course I learned faster.”
*Who are you trying to compare yourself to?*
Team Leader Choi might have grown up under Lee Jungryong’s watchful eye, constantly held in check, but our lives had been fundamentally different.
Even after obtaining the System, I’d nearly died several times. Damn it, I’d been through hell.
“Anyway, what brings you here this early?”
“Something has been troubling me, so I came despite the imposition.”
“Something troubling you?”
“Yes.”
“Why? Did Johnson confess his love to you?”
“That doesn’t concern me. I know it’s simply Mr. Johnson’s way of showing affection. This is about Guild business.”
“Guild business... Did bad news come from Korea?”
At my worried question, Team Leader Choi shook his head.
“No. I’m worried because one of our Guild members seems to be heading into danger.”
“Oh.”
So that was what he meant. Once I caught on, I let out a quiet laugh.
“I know who you mean. Tall and handsome, right? With an absolutely wonderful personality.”
“I can’t speak to the first two, but his personality certainly is something else. In several ways.”
“Hmm. Then I don’t think we’re talking about the same person.”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
Team Leader Choi, who had been trading jokes with me until then, lowered his voice.
“You know what I mean.”
“Do I?”
“This operation is dangerous.”
“Team Leader Choi, don’t you trust me?”
“How could I not? You’re one of the people I trust most in this world.”
Team Leader Choi fixed me with a grave stare.
“And you’re about to carry out a dangerous operation with some of the people I trust least.”
Two names immediately came to mind.
Lee Jungryong and Wu Heixing. Men bound to me by bitter history—and comrades who would soon have to entrust their backs to one another.
I scratched my chin and answered.
“‘People I can’t trust.’ I can’t think of a more fitting description.”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung...”
“Team Leader Choi?”
He closed his mouth before he could continue. I quietly raised a hand and pointed toward the tent flap.
“As you know, I haven’t finished cultivating yet.”
“The battle will begin before the day is over. Clear your mind and prepare for the fight ahead.”
Team Leader Choi stared at me, conflicted and unable to speak. At last, he heaved a deep sigh and rose from his seat.
“I’ll see you shortly.”
“Sure. I won’t see you out.”
I felt his presence gradually fade as he left the tent.
The Skeleton Warlord, who had been moping ever since his wish coupon was refunded, immediately spoke in a hopeful voice.
—A very intelligent human. It is not too late. Why not heed that human’s advice?
“You’re really working hard at this.”
—If you insist on going, go alone! Why must you take this commander with you?
“Dying alone would be lonely.”
—Whaaaaaat?!
“I’m joking. It’s just our best option.”
—You call breaking through a massive monster army to confront the Arch Lich our best option? Are you an evil human, or simply insane?
Listen to the way this undead bastard talks.
I considered punishing him, then unfolded my legs and reclined diagonally across the bed.
“It’s a dangerous operation, sure, but we’ve got a good chance. Stop complaining.”
—And what if we get there and it does not work?
“Then we fight with everything we’ve got. That’ll give us a chance.”
The Skeleton Warlord muttered with the voice of one who had attained enlightenment.
—Miraculous logic indeed. To think this commander is stuck with such a madman.
“And yet you’re still here.”
—Still here? You mean I cannot leave!
“You’re hilarious. When was it that you came back on your own feet? Ah, never mind. Not feet—your skull.”
—Vicious humans seeking this commander’s life are everywhere! What else was I supposed to do?
I let out a quiet laugh at the Skeleton Warlord’s aggrieved protest.
*Don't be such a coward.*
I had plenty to say, but decided to save it for later. That was something he needed to realize on his own.
—You laughed! You just laughed!
“When?”
I played dumb and changed the subject.
“Anyway, the key is taking down the Arch Lich. Once the head is gone, the body can’t move.”
—Dullahans can.
That was true.
For a moment, the answer made perfect sense. Then I realized how ridiculous it was and pulled the Skeleton Warlord from my Inventory.
“No, seriously. This bastard has been asking for it.”
—C-Calm down, human. I said nothing untrue.
“Right. Dullahans can move without their heads. Let’s see what happens to the Skeleton Warlord.”
*Crack!*
I flicked his forehead with lightning speed, and the Skeleton Warlord shrieked.
—Agh! A crack! There’s a crack between my brows! I’m telling you, there’s really a crack!
“I held back, so what the hell are you talking about... Oh. There really is one.”
Maybe I should have hit him more gently. A tiny crack had appeared in the glossy black skull, its surface gleaming smoothly.
When I lightly touched the sliver of bone raised by the impact, the Skeleton Warlord screamed.
—My bone! My bone!
“Fine, I get it. Stop screaming.”
—My bones have been getting increasingly itchy and sensitive lately, and I was already worried, but this madman went and... Sob.
*What, does he have dry skin?*
At this rate, he would start an iTube channel and rack up a million subscribers as an undead beauty streamer.
*This bastard might not even be a monster...*
The more I saw of him, the stranger he seemed.
I stared at the Skeleton Warlord in disbelief, then suddenly threw open one side of the tent. The sun was slowly lifting its head in the east.
It signaled the beginning of a new day—and the battle soon to come.
Located in the central Sichuan Basin, Suining City encompassed two urban districts, three counties, and more than five thousand square kilometers of land.
Since ancient times, it had been known as the heart of central Sichuan Province, renowned for its refined culture, tranquil scenery, and thriving agriculture, industry, and commerce.
But all of that was now a thing of the past.
Caw! Cawww!
Countless crows wheeled through the overcast sky before descending upon the corpses strewn across the ground. There were no squabbles between the flocks over their prey.
Hundreds of bodies lay scattered across the land, and the crows filled their bellies by pecking at the rotting flesh of what had once been human beings.
For humanity, it was a calamity beyond compare.
For the crows, it was an age of peace and plenty.
Their peaceful feast did not last long.
Rumble. Rrrrumble.
A deafening roar and tremors rose from the ground. The crows cried out irritably and took flight as one.
Several black feathers drifted through the air, caught the wind, and sailed across the vast basin.
Countless marching feet and the metal wheels of tanks crushed the feathers as they fluttered down.
Boom. Boom. Boom.
A human army filled the horizon.
The tower shields held by the tank-class Hunters at the forefront scraped against the ground. Behind them, thousands of Hunters advanced in ordered ranks.
A pair of tightly pressed lips showed beneath a helmet pulled low.
Thousands of people, gripped by the invisible specter of war, marched onward in silence.
Toward the distant city shrouded in pale mist.
Toward the battle that awaited them, and the glorious victory beyond it.
Then a man at the center of the formation suddenly spoke.
“Fuck, look at that fog. Doesn’t it look like something out of one of those disaster movies where monsters show up? Anyone seen that one?”
Jin Taekyung’s colorful profanity came out of nowhere amid the solemn atmosphere, drawing snorts of laughter from all around him.
“Pfft.”
“Kff.”
“What? Am I the only one who’s seen it? That masterpiece?”
As Jin Taekyung shrugged, a voice answered from his right.
“I’ve seen it.”
“Really? That’s unexpected, Team Leader Choi.”
“What is?”
“You seem like the type who’d only watch musicals or orchestral performances. Things like that.”
The Hunters who glanced at Choi Minwoo bit their lips to hold back their laughter.
Before they knew it, their rigid bodies had relaxed and their breathing had steadied. The tension weighing on them eased considerably.
All the while, the two men continued their conversation.
“I occasionally watch movies to unwind. I enjoyed the one you mentioned too, Mr. Jin.”
“Oh, then you know the final twist.”
“Of course. Personally, I found it quite unfortunate.”
“Exactly. I had the same thought while I was watching.”
Jin Taekyung continued slowly.
“They could’ve survived if they hadn’t given up at the very end. They should’ve kept fighting with everything they had, no matter what it took. That sort of thing.”
His voice was low, but it carried unmistakable strength.
Infused with profound internal energy, it reverberated through the air and reached every ear.
And the thousands of Hunters and soldiers of the Western Front realized something.
Perhaps Jin Taekyung’s words had been meant for them.
“By now, the other fronts are probably surrounding Suining City just like we are, right?”
“They’ll have it completely encircled.”
“And the battle will begin soon.”
“We will win.”
Jin Taekyung laughed aloud at Xiao Shen’s resolute answer.
“Yeah. We have to. But...”
Jin Taekyung’s laughter abruptly stopped. The next moment, the playful light in his eyes vanished, replaced by a deeply sunken gaze.
The vast basin was reflected in his icy gaze.
“Looks like they have other ideas.”
Tap. Tap-tap-tap.
Grrrk...
Corpses slowly rose to their feet.
Skeletons.
Mist slid across the basin, carrying with it the growls of the monsters lurking within.
“Starting now...”
Jin Taekyung drew a deep breath.
“It begins.”

sentences.text: An unannounced visitor arrived before dawn had fully broken.
He stepped carefully into the tent and met my eyes as I sat cross-legged.
“You were already awake.”
“As you can see.”
I shrugged at Team Leader Choi.
“I haven’t been sleeping much lately.”
More accurately, I needed less sleep.
With stamina that had surpassed human limits and formidable internal energy amounting to three jiazi, I could blow away most fatigue by circulating my qi.
“Were you practicing the Mana Cultivation Method—or rather, the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique?”
“Yeah, something like that.”
To be exact, I was practicing the Fire Gate Divine Technique, the secret cultivation technique of the Fire Gate Clan.
But I couldn’t tell him every last detail.
“I should have come later.”
“No, it’s fine.”
“Didn’t you say that cultivation must never be interrupted?
That stopping midway could cause qi deviation...”
“Oh, that applies to you, Team Leader Choi.
I’m fine.
We’re on different levels.”
*Warning: your fact attack may hurt someone.*
For a moment, I could practically see the public-service announcement flashing across Team Leader Choi’s face.
He gave me a sour look, then slowly shook his head.
“I can’t argue with the truth.”
“Still, you’re learning incredibly fast.
I mean that sincerely, so have a little more confidence.”
I did mean it.
As befitted a descendant of Cheon Taemin, the hero who had achieved an indomitable feat in human history, Team Leader Choi possessed extraordinary natural martial talent.
For some reason, he also had a considerable amount of qi stored within his body, so his progress in martial arts was astonishingly fast.
In short, he was a talent with all the groundwork already laid.
*If he’d learned martial arts from childhood like Wu Heixing... he’d probably be an S-rank Hunter by now.*
Team Leader Choi’s expression softened slightly, and he nodded.
“How do I compare to Jin Taekyung?”
“Are you kidding?
Of course I learned faster.”
*Who are you trying to compare yourself to?*
Team Leader Choi might have grown up under Lee Jungryong’s watchful eye, constantly held in check, but our lives had been fundamentally different.
Even after obtaining the System, I’d nearly died several times.
Damn it, I’d been through hell.
“Anyway, what brings you here this early?”
“Something has been troubling me, so I came despite the imposition.”
“Something troubling you?”
“Yes.”
“Why?
Did Johnson confess his love to you?”
“That doesn’t concern me.
I know it’s simply Mr.
Johnson’s way of showing affection.
This is about Guild business.”
“Guild business...
Did bad news come from Korea?”
At my worried question, Team Leader Choi shook his head.
“No.
I’m worried because one of our Guild members seems to be heading into danger.”
“Oh.”
So that was what he meant.
Once I caught on, I let out a quiet laugh.
“I know who you mean.
Tall and handsome, right?
With an absolutely wonderful personality.”
“I can’t speak to the first two, but his personality certainly is something else.
In several ways.”
“Hmm.
Then I don’t think we’re talking about the same person.”
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung.”
Team Leader Choi, who had been trading jokes with me until then, lowered his voice.
“You know what I mean.”
“Do I?”
“This operation is dangerous.”
“Team Leader Choi, don’t you trust me?”
“How could I not?
You’re one of the people I trust most in this world.”
Team Leader Choi fixed me with a grave stare.
“And you’re about to carry out a dangerous operation with some of the people I trust least.”
Two names immediately came to mind.
Lee Jungryong and Wu Heixing.
Men bound to me by bitter history—and comrades who would soon have to entrust their backs to one another.
I scratched my chin and answered.
“‘People I can’t trust.’ I can’t think of a more fitting description.”
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung...”
“Team Leader Choi?”
He closed his mouth before he could continue.
I quietly raised a hand and pointed toward the tent flap.
“As you know, I haven’t finished cultivating yet.”
“The battle will begin before the day is over.
Clear your mind and prepare for the fight ahead.”
Team Leader Choi stared at me, conflicted and unable to speak.
At last, he heaved a deep sigh and rose from his seat.
“I’ll see you shortly.”
“Sure.
I won’t see you out.”
I felt his presence gradually fade as he left the tent.
The Skeleton Warlord, who had been moping ever since his wish coupon was refunded, immediately spoke in a hopeful voice.
—A very intelligent human.
It is not too late.
Why not heed that human’s advice?
“You’re really working hard at this.”
—If you insist on going, go alone!
Why must you take this commander with you?
“Dying alone would be lonely.”
—Whaaaaaat?!
“I’m joking.
It’s just our best option.”
—You call breaking through a massive monster army to confront the Arch Lich our best option?
Are you an evil human, or simply insane?
Listen to the way this undead bastard talks.
I considered punishing him, then unfolded my legs and reclined diagonally across the bed.
“It’s a dangerous operation, sure, but we’ve got a good chance.
Stop complaining.”
—And what if we get there and it does not work?
“Then we fight with everything we’ve got.
That’ll give us a chance.”
The Skeleton Warlord muttered with the voice of one who had attained enlightenment.
—Miraculous logic indeed.
To think this commander is stuck with such a madman.
“And yet you’re still here.”
—Still here?
You mean I cannot leave!
“You’re hilarious.
When was it that you came back on your own feet?
Ah, never mind.
Not feet—your skull.”
—Vicious humans seeking this commander’s life are everywhere!
What else was I supposed to do?
I let out a quiet laugh at the Skeleton Warlord’s aggrieved protest.
*Don't be such a coward.*
I had plenty to say, but decided to save it for later.
That was something he needed to realize on his own.
—You laughed!
You just laughed!
“When?”
I played dumb and changed the subject.
“Anyway, the key is taking down the Arch Lich.
Once the head is gone, the body can’t move.”
—Dullahans can.
That was true.
For a moment, the answer made perfect sense.
Then I realized how ridiculous it was and pulled the Skeleton Warlord from my Inventory.
“No, seriously.
This bastard has been asking for it.”
—C-Calm down, human.
I said nothing untrue.
“Right.
Dullahans can move without their heads.
Let’s see what happens to the Skeleton Warlord.”
*Crack!*
I flicked his forehead with lightning speed, and the Skeleton Warlord shrieked.
—Agh!
A crack!
There’s a crack between my brows!
I’m telling you, there’s really a crack!
“I held back, so what the hell are you talking about...
Oh.
There really is one.”
Maybe I should have hit him more gently.
A tiny crack had appeared in the glossy black skull, its surface gleaming smoothly.
When I lightly touched the sliver of bone raised by the impact, the Skeleton Warlord screamed.
—My bone!
My bone!
“Fine, I get it.
Stop screaming.”
—My bones have been getting increasingly itchy and sensitive lately, and I was already worried, but this madman went and...
Sob.
*What, does he have dry skin?*
At this rate, he would start an iTube channel and rack up a million subscribers as an undead beauty streamer.
*This bastard might not even be a monster...*

chapters.title: Chapter 410
paragraphs: *Has it been over thirty years?*
Lee Jungryong muttered to himself.
The stench of countless monsters and the reek of blood drifted in on the wind. It was the smell of a battlefield, stirring memories of long ago.
*Yes. It truly has been a long time.*

With a shrewd gaze that seemed at odds with his appearance, he watched the fog slowly draw nearer. The pale fog, where thousands of monsters were presumably lurking, radiated an ominous feeling simply by being there.
Most of the troops were shaken, but to Lee Jungryong—a living witness to the Great Cataclysm—it was an all-too-familiar sight.
“How old are you?”
At Lee Jungryong’s sudden question, Go Jun, the Head of Security standing one step behind him, answered.
“Thirty-five.”
“That’s a good age. Looking back, I was the same. Every day brought another brush with death, but I had dreams back then.”
Lee Jungryong gazed into the distance.
For a moment, he seemed to glimpse his younger self somewhere far away—a young man driven by the will to survive and the ambition to become the best.
But more than thirty years later, the man standing here was nearing seventy.
“Sometimes, doubt creeps in. I find myself wondering whether everything I’ve built might come crashing down.”
“I have not the slightest doubt.”
“Why not?”
Go Jun’s lips moved.
“Because you are here, Master.”
Lee Jungryong gave a quiet laugh.
“And what would you do if I fell?”
“I can say with certainty that will never happen.”
“There was a time when I thought the same of someone else. He was stronger than anyone, an insurmountable wall I could never overcome even if I devoted my entire life to trying.”
“He was the beginning and end of the Great Cataclysm. He was everything. Humanity’s savior, no different from a new god. But even he was only human.”
The hero who had achieved immortal feats had not shown himself for many years, and only a handful of people knew the secret surrounding him.
As one of those few, Lee Jungryong continued in a low voice.
“Nothing is eternal, and nothing is certain. I’ve found myself thinking that more and more lately.”
“...Is this because of Jin Taekyung?”
“When a crack begins, collapse comes in an instant. That bastard is the crack itself.”
“Then we must seal it before everything collapses.”
Lee Jungryong watched the fog slide across the desolate plain. When he spoke, his voice was gentle, but a blade lay hidden beneath it.
“Are you ready?”
“I will obey.”
Go Jun bowed deeply and drew his sword.
*Shing! Clatter!*
Hundreds, then thousands, of weapons were drawn behind him at once.
The Ares Guild’s elites, honed through countless raids and training exercises, stood alongside the Chinese Hunters. The light gleaming from their weapons rippled like waves.
“Please give the command.”
Lee Jungryong slowly began to walk.
There was no place here for soldiers or firearms. This was a battle solely between the superhumans known as Hunters and the monsters—and Lee Jungryong would reign as the god of the battlefield.
“Let’s go.”
With that single word, Lee Jungryong shot forward like the wind. The fog filling the plain split apart on both sides along the path of his sword.
*Kraaash!*
*Splurt!*
Drenched in horribly foul-smelling green blood, the young man barely managed to keep from gagging.
No, that was not quite right.
It would be more accurate to say he was not even given the chance.
*Whoosh! Boom!*
The upper section of his Tower Shield shattered, and a sharp fragment grazed the tip of his nose. Blood spurted out, and the scent of it pierced his nostrils.
It helped drown out the terrible stench, but directly before him, an undead ogre that looked freshly dead was raising a massive iron club.
“Grrrraaaaah!”
*Whoooooosh.*
The terrifying sound of it tearing through the air was enough to make his hair stand on end.
The young man gritted his teeth and bent his knees, shielding his head with his mana-infused Tower Shield.
*Boom!*
The tremendous impact tore through his entire body. His ears rang, his head reeled, and his arm hurt as though it had been broken.
*No. Maybe it’s already broken.*
But a broken arm barely even counted as a problem right now.
Not when a ferociously roaring, five-meter-tall monster was swinging an iron club as large as a grown man like a pinwheel.
*Boom! Boom! Boom!*
Under the relentless assault, the young man screamed, his voice edging toward tears.
“You turtle-dicked bastard! Why are you so strong?!”
The young man was a veteran B-rank Hunter. Naturally, he had fought ogres before.
As befitted A-rank monsters, ogres possessed tremendous strength and stamina, but they had never been this strong.
They definitely hadn’t been...
*Boom!*
The young man stared blankly as the high-strength Tower Shield he had bought for a fortune at the beginning of the year shattered after only five blows.
*What the hell... Did all these things take drugs or something?*
They were far too strong.
As he watched the iron club rise once more through the pale fog, the young man sensed that his end had come.
At the same time, one name flashed through his mind.
*Jin Taekyung.*
This was all that bastard’s fault.
If Jin Taekyung had simply pretended not to know him and walked past that day, some big shot would never have kicked him in the shins, and he would not have been drafted as a frontline tank.
Then he would not be about to die like this.
*Whoooooosh!*
Dodging was unthinkable. He did not even have the courage to look straight at the iron club hurtling toward him, filling his entire field of vision.
The young man squeezed his eyes shut and let out an involuntary scream.
“Jin Taekyung, you bangzi bastard!”
And then, in the next instant—
*Slash! Rattle-rattle-rattle!*
His vision went pitch-black. A cool breeze brushed across his entire body, and something poured down like a sudden shower.
Soon, a voice pierced his ears.
“What did you just call me?”
The young man’s eyes flew open. Green blood was scattering through the air in droplets. The enormous body of the undead ogre, now missing its head, was slowly toppling over.
And there was the face of a man scowling deeply.
“You’re that bastard from last time. Burdian.”
*Whoosh! Splurt!*
He had not seen it. There had been no way he could.
The man reached out, and a streak of light—probably a dagger—pierced three or four monsters. They crumpled like puppets with their strings cut.
An answer escaped the young man’s lips before he could think.
“Uh, no, I’m not.”
“No, my ass, you fucking bastard.”
*Slash! Bang!*
“You looked like you were in danger, so I saved you, and you call me a bangzi? You’d better survive. I’m going to make you run bread for me until you die of old age.”
*Slash! Sssshk!*
*Is this a dream?*
Every time the young man blinked, the monsters around him fell like bundles of straw.
Blue flames erupted, and whenever the air split with a shriek, an area that had been so densely packed there was nowhere to step was swept clean.
It all began at one man’s fingertips, and none of it looked like something a human being could have done.
The young man stared at him in a daze.
“Are you... perhaps a god?”
After a moment of silence, Jin Taekyung asked in return,
“Are you perhaps... a fucking idiot?”
*Rrrrummmble!*
Blue flames swept across the earth. Steel melted, and monsters engulfed in the blaze screamed in agony.
After wiping out dozens of monsters with a single sweep, Jin Taekyung glanced at the young man.
“Hey.”
“Yes? Yes?”
“Survive. I’m going to make you run bread for me.”
“Excuse me?”
“I’m not joking. If you die, I’ll kill you myself.”
“Oh, and take this.”
*Whoosh! Crack!*
Something shot toward the young man like a ray of light, struck him in the forehead, and shattered.
Before he could react, translucent liquid drenched him, and Jin Taekyung’s low voice reached his ears.
“You’ll be fine now, so get back to fighting. Don’t go picking fights with ogres unless you want to get yourself killed. Stick to the weaker ones. Got it?”
*Hissss.*
The liquid—no, the potion—seeped into him with a faint warmth.
The young man felt the wounds covering his body close and his broken arm mend. He nodded blankly.
“Yes. Yes.”
“Then I’m off.”
“P-Please be careful, sir.”
Forgetting that he was in the middle of a battlefield, the young man bowed deeply at the waist.
When he raised his head again, Jin Taekyung was gone, and a group was rushing past him.
*Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh! Slash!*
More than two hundred Hunters raced forward without hesitation along the path Jin Taekyung had opened, swinging their weapons.
Two figures at the forefront stood out above all the rest.
“Their formation has collapsed! Charge!”
One was a handsome man spouting incomprehensible Korean. The other was a remarkably young-looking Hunter.
They moved like the wind, their blades wreathed in dazzling aura as they cut the monsters apart.
*The suicide squad.*
He had heard about them. A number of S-rank Hunters, including Jin Taekyung, would lead the suicide squads from each front in a charge against the Arch Lich.
Only yesterday, he had thought it was impossible nonsense...
*Amazing.*
*Could I become like that too?*
As the young man gazed blankly at the scene, his chest suddenly grew hot. Some unknown strength surged up from within him, and he could not contain it.
He raised his half-destroyed Tower Shield and charged toward the nearest monster.
“Yaaaaaaaah!”
“Grrrraaaaah!”
*Whoosh! Boom!*
Damn it. It was an ogre.
The young man stared at his now completely shattered Tower Shield, turned on his heel, and ran.
*Orcs. Where are the orcs?!*
*Thud!*
*That did it.*
The impact against my knuckles told me all I needed to know. As certainty flashed through my mind, the head of the Lycanthrope lunging teeth-first for the back of my neck exploded.
**System Ding!* - You defeated Lv. 92 Darkened Lycanthrope! - You gained a small amount of EXP!
A Lycanthrope at level ninety-something?
I already knew Level was not an absolute measure, but the monsters gathered on this battlefield were clearly different from the ones I had encountered in Gates.
*They’re stronger.*
Their Levels were slightly higher, and they were superior in Agility and raw strength as well.
If it had been one or two monsters, I might have brushed it off. But everything from F-rank goblins to A-rank monsters was like this. You would have to be an idiot not to realize something was wrong.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung!”
“Hyung!”
I turned at the urgent shouts behind me and saw monsters packing the path I had opened, leaving no gaps between them.
The suicide squad was fighting desperately against them.
“Get the hell out of here. All of you.”
*Boom-boom-boom-boom!*
To the monsters, I was something they could neither stop nor evade.
Dozens of fist shadows shot out like cannonballs and rained down upon their heads.
Some were reduced to bloody pulp and hurled into the distance. Others simply crumpled where they stood.
I charged into the space that had momentarily been emptied.
*Slash-slash-slash!*
A spearhead wreathed in Force tore through bone and flesh, carving through everything around me. As the monsters fell, System notifications rang out without pause.

**System Ding! Ding! Ding!* - You defeated Lv. 55 Darkened Orc Warrior! - You gained an extremely small amount of EXP! - You defeated Lv. 83 Darkened Lizard Mage! - You gained an extremely small amount of EXP...
Then came a cheerful chime I had not heard in a long time.
**System Ding! Level Up! The effects of leveling up relieve fatigue and heal some injuries! - You obtained 10 points! - Your physical condition is at its peak!
I could feel it.
My steadily draining internal energy filled to the brim, and the fatigue accumulated throughout my body vanished as if it had been washed away.
But there was something more important.
“Team Leader Choi! Xiao Shen!”
“Yes!”
“What is it?”
I shouted loudly enough for my voice to shake the entire battlefield.
“The fog! Get as far outside its range as you can!”
This was not merely unpleasant, clammy fog. It was a kind of Magic wielded by the Arch Lich.
It strengthened the monsters within its range—or rather, made them *Darkened*.
*Damn Magic.*
At that very moment, as I glared at the mysterious fog filling the area around me—
*Kraaaa-boom!*
A thunderous roar, as if the sky itself had split apart, echoed across heaven and earth.

“Grrrraaaaah!”
*Whoooooosh.*
The terrifying sound of it tearing through the air was enough to make his hair stand on end.
The young man gritted his teeth and bent his knees, shielding his head with his mana-infused Tower Shield.
*Boom!*
The tremendous impact tore through his entire body.
His ears rang, his head reeled, and his arm hurt as though it had been broken.
*No.
Maybe it’s already broken.*
But a broken arm barely even counted as a problem right now.
Not when a ferociously roaring, five-meter-tall monster was swinging an iron club as large as a grown man like a pinwheel.
*Boom!
Boom!
Boom!*
Under the relentless assault, the young man screamed, his voice edging toward tears.
“You turtle-dicked bastard!
Why are you so strong?!”
The young man was a veteran B-rank Hunter.
Naturally, he had fought ogres before.
As befitted A-rank monsters, ogres possessed tremendous strength and stamina, but they had never been this strong.
They definitely hadn’t been...
*Boom!*
The young man stared blankly as the high-strength Tower Shield he had bought for a fortune at the beginning of the year shattered after only five blows.
*What the hell...
Did all these things take drugs or something?*
They were far too strong.
As he watched the iron club rise once more through the pale fog, the young man sensed that his end had come.
At the same time, one name flashed through his mind.
*Jin Taekyung.*
This was all that bastard’s fault.
If Jin Taekyung had simply pretended not to know him and walked past that day, some big shot would never have kicked him in the shins, and he would not have been drafted as a frontline tank.
Then he would not be about to die like this.
*Whoooooosh!*
Dodging was unthinkable.
He did not even have the courage to look straight at the iron club hurtling toward him, filling his entire field of vision.
The young man squeezed his eyes shut and let out an involuntary scream.
“Jin Taekyung, you bangzi bastard!”
And then, in the next instant—
*Slash!
Rattle-rattle-rattle!*
His vision went pitch-black.
A cool breeze brushed across his entire body, and something poured down like a sudden shower.
Soon, a voice pierced his ears.
“What did you just call me?”
The young man’s eyes flew open.
Green blood was scattering through the air in droplets.
The enormous body of the undead ogre, now missing its head, was slowly toppling over.
And there was the face of a man scowling deeply.
“You’re that bastard from last time.
Burdian.”
*Whoosh!
Splurt!*
He had not seen it.
There had been no way he could.
The man reached out, and a streak of light—probably a dagger—pierced three or four monsters.
They crumpled like puppets with their strings cut.
An answer escaped the young man’s lips before he could think.
“Uh, no, I’m not.”
“No, my ass, you fucking bastard.”
*Slash!
Bang!*
“You looked like you were in danger, so I saved you, and you call me a bangzi?
You’d better survive.
I’m going to make you run bread for me until you die of old age.”
*Slash!
Sssshk!*
*Is this a dream?*
Every time the young man blinked, the monsters around him fell like bundles of straw.
Blue flames erupted, and whenever the air split with a shriek, an area that had been so densely packed there was nowhere to step was swept clean.
It all began at one man’s fingertips, and none of it looked like something a human being could have done.
The young man stared at him in a daze.
“Are you... perhaps a god?”
After a moment of silence, Jin Taekyung asked in return,
“Are you perhaps... a fucking idiot?”
*Rrrrummmble!*
Blue flames swept across the earth.
Steel melted, and monsters engulfed in the blaze screamed in agony.
After wiping out dozens of monsters with a single sweep, Jin Taekyung glanced at the young man.
“Hey.”
“Yes?
Yes?”
“Survive.
I’m going to make you run bread for me.”
“Excuse me?”
“I’m not joking.
If you die, I’ll kill you myself.”
“Oh, and take this.”
*Whoosh!
Crack!*
Something shot toward the young man like a ray of light, struck him in the forehead, and shattered.
Before he could react, translucent liquid drenched him, and Jin Taekyung’s low voice reached his ears.
“You’ll be fine now, so get back to fighting.
Don’t go picking fights with ogres unless you want to get yourself killed.
Stick to the weaker ones.
Got it?”
*Hissss.*
The liquid—no, the potion—seeped into him with a faint warmth.
The young man felt the wounds covering his body close and his broken arm mend.
He nodded blankly.
“Yes.
Yes.”
“Then I’m off.”
“P-Please be careful, sir.”
Forgetting that he was in the middle of a battlefield, the young man bowed deeply at the waist.
When he raised his head again, Jin Taekyung was gone, and a group was rushing past him.
*Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh!
Slash!*
More than two hundred Hunters raced forward without hesitation along the path Jin Taekyung had opened, swinging their weapons.
Two figures at the forefront stood out above all the rest.
“Their formation has collapsed!
Charge!”
One was a handsome man spouting incomprehensible Korean.
The other was a remarkably young-looking Hunter.
They moved like the wind, their blades wreathed in dazzling aura as they cut the monsters apart.
*The suicide squad.*
He had heard about them.
A number of S-rank Hunters, including Jin Taekyung, would lead the suicide squads from each front in a charge against the Arch Lich.
Only yesterday, he had thought it was impossible nonsense...
*Amazing.*
*Could I become like that too?*
As the young man gazed blankly at the scene, his chest suddenly grew hot.
Some unknown strength surged up from within him, and he could not contain it.
He raised his half-destroyed Tower Shield and charged toward the nearest monster.
“Yaaaaaaaah!”
“Grrrraaaaah!”
*Whoosh!
Boom!*
Damn it.
It was an ogre.
The young man stared at his now completely shattered Tower Shield, turned on his heel, and ran.
*Orcs.
Where are the orcs?!*
*Thud!*
*That did it.*
The impact against my knuckles told me all I needed to know.
As certainty flashed through my mind, the head of the Lycanthrope lunging teeth-first for the back of my neck exploded.
**System Ding!* - You defeated Lv.
92 Darkened Lycanthrope! - You gained a small amount of EXP!
A Lycanthrope at level ninety-something?
I already knew Level was not an absolute measure, but the monsters gathered on this battlefield were clearly different from the ones I had encountered in Gates.
*They’re stronger.*
Their Levels were slightly higher, and they were superior in Agility and raw strength as well.
If it had been one or two monsters, I might have brushed it off.
But everything from F-rank goblins to A-rank monsters was like this.
You would have to be an idiot not to realize something was wrong.
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung!”
“Hyung!”
I turned at the urgent shouts behind me and saw monsters packing the path I had opened, leaving no gaps between them.
The suicide squad was fighting desperately against them.
“Get the hell out of here.
All of you.”
*Boom-boom-boom-boom!*
To the monsters, I was something they could neither stop nor evade.
Dozens of fist shadows shot out like cannonballs and rained down upon their heads.
Some were reduced to bloody pulp and hurled into the distance.
Others simply crumpled where they stood.
I charged into the space that had momentarily been emptied.
*Slash-slash-slash!*
A spearhead wreathed in Force tore through bone and flesh, carving through everything around me.
As the monsters fell, System notifications rang out without pause.
**System Ding!
Ding!
Ding!* - You defeated Lv.
55 Darkened Orc Warrior! - You gained an extremely small amount of EXP! - You defeated Lv.
83 Darkened Lizard Mage! - You gained an extremely small amount of EXP...
Then came a cheerful chime I had not heard in a long time.
**System Ding!
Level Up!
The effects of leveling up relieve fatigue and heal some injuries! - You obtained 10 points! - Your physical condition is at its peak!
I could feel it.
My steadily draining internal energy filled to the brim, and the fatigue accumulated throughout my body vanished as if it had been washed away.
But there was something more important.
“Team Leader Choi!
Xiao Shen!”
“Yes!”
“What is it?”
I shouted loudly enough for my voice to shake the entire battlefield.
“The fog!
Get as far outside its range as you can!”
This was not merely unpleasant, clammy fog.
It was a kind of Magic wielded by the Arch Lich.
It strengthened the monsters within its range—or rather, made them *Darkened*.
*Damn Magic.*
At that very moment, as I glared at the mysterious fog filling the area around me—
*Kraaaa-boom!*
A thunderous roar, as if the sky itself had split apart, echoed across heaven and earth.

chapters.title: Chapter 411
paragraphs: For a moment, it felt as though the world had stopped.
My instincts reacted before my brain could process the situation.

The breathing of the people around me and the monsters’ howls receded into the distance, as if they were coming from several kilometers away. My senses, sharper than ever, took in every detail around me.
*Fwoooosh.*
Droplets of blood, dirt, and dust drifted slowly through the air. Fog hung close enough to grasp if I reached out my hand.
And then...
*Qi.*
I could feel it—the immense movement of qi surrounding an area several hundred meters in every direction. As a red alarm began blaring in my head, I kicked off the ground and shot upward.
“Get clear—!”
*Kraaa-boooom!*
A flash of light was followed by a tremendous roar that shook heaven and earth. From more than ten meters in the air, I looked down over the battlefield.
The area within a radius of several hundred meters, centered on the spot where I had been standing only a few seconds earlier, had been devastated.
Through the lingering fog and billowing dust, I could see green blood coating the ground and monster corpses blown to pieces.
*A Magic Trap.*
Fighting an enemy who refused to show himself meant preparing for anything.
*There’s no compassion in war.*
The countless wars recorded throughout human history had served as witness, prosecutor, and judge.
Even humans committed all kinds of horrific atrocities against one another during war. Expecting compassion from monsters that weren’t even human was laughable.
That was why vigilance was an essential virtue in war. It reduced the chances of falling into an enemy’s trap and minimized casualties.
Just like now.
*Tap.*
I landed lightly and reached out my hand.
*Bang!*
Compressed air burst outward, scattering the dust clouds.
Familiar faces finally emerged from among the blood and corpses covering the ground.
“Team Leader Choi.”
Team Leader Choi took a deep breath and nodded. Behind him stood more than two hundred members of the suicide squad, their faces pale with terror.
“A few people are injured...but everyone made it.”
“That’s a relief.”
“It was an unbelievably powerful trap. Without this, most of us—including me—would probably have died.”
*Shk. Wooooong.*
Team Leader Choi reached out and touched the transparent barrier spread out before him.
It covered every member of the suicide squad—a Barrier spell painstakingly inscribed into a scroll by one of the three greatest mages among billions of people.
“When the battle is over, I should find Mr. Johnson first. His magic saved our lives.”
“Are you planning to thank him with a kiss?”
“At this point, there’s nothing I wouldn’t do.”
Xiao Shen exhaled the breath he had been holding and joined in.
“I’d be willing to go even further. This is truly...”
Unable to finish, he looked around.
The explosion had been that tremendous. By even the roughest estimate, more than a thousand monsters had been killed or rendered incapable of fighting.
A trap that had not distinguished friend from foe. The Arch Lich had thrown countless subordinates into it as kindling to catch me and the suicide squad.
*Look at this bastard...*
I had expected as much to some extent, but the Arch Lich’s cunning and boldness went beyond anything I had imagined.
If my signal had been even slightly late, or if I had not volunteered to be bait while breaking through the path ahead, every member of the suicide squad would have been buried here.
*Just like that day.*
A memory I would never forget. A tragedy that could never be allowed to happen again.
I turned and spoke.
“Keep your distance and follow me. Our objective isn’t to fight the monsters. It’s to break through them.”
The suicide squad answered with a thunderous shout.
The monster army, thrown into chaos after suddenly losing so many of its own in the explosion, hesitated and began to retreat.
A crisis had become an opportunity. We couldn’t let this momentum slip away.
“Charge!”
I unleashed an azure dragon’s roar infused with internal energy and shot forward.
*Slash!*
The head of a retreating monster flew into the air.
The two hundred members of the suicide squad drove into the gap left in the monster army like an awl. The main force behind them surged forward like a wave.
“Waaaaaaaaah!”
A deafening roar shook the battlefield.
Green blood spread through the fog.
And far above, a flock of crows circled as they watched the battlefield below.
The being sitting atop a throne of white bones, as if asleep, suddenly opened his eyes.
Intense light flared within his empty eye sockets, and a low murmur escaped him.
“Not bad.”
The Arch Lich had hundreds of eyes and ears.
Even now, the Familiars he had stationed throughout the battlefield were taking in every detail without missing a thing.
The humans and monsters locked in fierce combat.
And the group of humans rapidly breaking through the battlefield.
*The suicide squad. That was what they called them, wasn’t it?*
The Arch Lich suddenly recalled something.
An ancient, long-moldering memory. One he had been unable to forget despite spending what felt like eternity submerged in the River of Death.
No. One he could never forget.
*The Adversary.*
How could he forget?
The single human who had stood at the center of everything. The suicide squad that had risked death to charge alongside the Adversary.
*That bastard was the one who drove a sword into my body.*
The Arch Lich looked down at his body of pitch-black bone.
In the past, he had not been some lowly existence like an undead. He had been a noble and mighty being, trusted by a king and commanding countless monsters.
But on the day of the final battle, he too had fallen alongside his king.
At the hands of a mere human, no less.
“But...where is the Adversary?”
The Arch Lich’s voice was filled with doubt.
He had surveyed every front through his Familiars, yet the Adversary, who should have appeared, was nowhere to be seen. He had found several humans from his memories, but that was all.
*Could it be?*
The Arch Lich’s eyes flared violently as he realized something.
It was impossible to believe.
But what if—what if the Adversary had died?
What if the Adversary had met the fate of a mortal?
“Kha...khahahaha!”
His body, rigid as a statue, began to shake.
The laughter infused with magical power made the ground tremble and the air quiver.
Sensing the change in their master’s mood, the guards dropped to the ground and prostrated themselves.
“My lord.”
“Why do you laugh so?”
The guards were an impressive sight. Death Knights, each comparable to a Named Monster, stood alongside Liches with robes pulled low over their heads. Altogether, they numbered twenty.
They were creations made to fight the Adversary.
But now, the Arch Lich had changed his mind.
After laughing with delight, the Arch Lich finally spoke.
“Listen, my faithful servants.”
“Give us your command.”
The Arch Lich rose from his seat and looked down upon his loyal retainers. A chilling voice soon echoed through the space.
“Go to the battlefield. Trample those insignificant humans and wipe them out.”
The twenty Death Knights and Liches bowed without the slightest hesitation.
The Arch Lich was the lord of every undead present. There could be no hesitation in obeying his commands.
“We shall carry out our lord’s command.”
They answered in unison and departed in different directions.
The space was empty once more.
Still chuckling to himself, the Arch Lich sat upon his skeletal throne and focused his mind.
He was surveying the battlefield through the eyes and ears of his countless Familiars when he suddenly paused.
“But...what in the world is that human?”
The pitch-black eyes of a crow soaring overhead reflected a young human cutting through monsters amid sprays of blood.
It was a face absent from the Arch Lich’s memories of the past, though he had already seen him through his Familiars several days earlier.
“That’s the human who defeated the Death Knight Lord.”
The Death Knight Lord, created from Lei Fei, was the finest of all the Arch Lich’s creations.

Although Lei Fei’s powerful soul had prevented the Arch Lich from subjugating him completely, there could be no doubting his strength. The Arch Lich had personally bestowed a portion of his own power upon him.
And yet, because of that insignificant human, he had lost his greatest fighting force and wasted precious magical power.
“He irritates me. I should dispose of him properly while I have the chance.”
Having decided to eliminate him, the Arch Lich sent out a thought.
Half of the guards heading toward the various fronts changed direction at their lord’s order.
*Kra-d-d-d-d-k!*
Wind, weapons, and the bodies of monsters harder than stone.
Everything caught in the spearhead’s path was cut apart.
Heads flew into the air, and thick limbs spun through the sky.

A Troll that was still breathing was chopped to pieces before it had a chance to regenerate. An ogre that had become undead while still half-rotten staggered, only for a sword that came flying a moment later to take off its upper body.
*Slash! Slash! Slash!*
After cutting down three or four monsters in an instant with Hero’s Soul, Team Leader Choi shouted to me.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung! The monster assault is too strong!”
He was right. Once we broke through the front line, the number of monsters decreased, but those that remained were far stronger.
*I knew it would be like this.*
The monsters at the front, used as kindling for the Magic Trap meant to catch us, had mostly been mid- or low-level.
The Arch Lich had placed his elites in the rear and used the other monsters as both bait and meat shields.
*To wear us down.*
On top of that, the fog had grown even thicker, making the battle more difficult.
The monsters becoming stronger under its influence was bad enough, but in fog this thick, visibility was limited and sound didn’t carry properly.
That naturally favored monsters, whose senses were sharper than those of humans.
Of course...
*I’m the exception.*
*Whoooosh! Bang!*
My spear lashed out with all my strength, skewering six or seven monsters like meat on a skewer.
Xiao Shen and the Hunters in the suicide squad, having escaped the crisis, gave me grateful looks.
“Everyone, group up around me!”
“But we only have a few magic scrolls left. If another Magic Trap activates...”
“No time to explain! Stop talking and move!”
Team Leader Choi and Xiao Shen nodded at my shout and advanced with the suicide squad.
I understood their concern, but we had already survived three Magic Traps, and this was the rear where the Arch Lich had gathered his elites. The chances of another trap being triggered were slim.
“Focus on defense instead of attacking. Advance!”
The battle itself had become more difficult, but the reduced chance of suddenly stumbling into another trap took a weight off my mind.
I could get myself out of danger easily enough, but the other members of the suicide squad might not survive.
*Our final destination is just ahead. Minimize casualties, then join up with Lee Jungryong and Wu Heixing.*
*Slash! Kra-d-d-d-d-k!*
I was at the front, cutting a path through the monsters and beginning to feel fatigue build up, when—
“All. Of. You. Fall. Back!”
“Human. By my lord’s command, I shall take your life.”
The curtain of monsters split apart to the left and right like the parting of the Red Sea.
I stared blankly, my mouth hanging open, as the beings behind it revealed themselves.
**System Lv. 120 Darkened Lich Lv. 115 Darkened Death Knight**
There were ten of them, all hovering around Level 120.
For a moment, I could barely breathe. My hands and feet began to tremble.
Team Leader Choi shouted at me in a voice filled with despair.
“We have to retreat right now!”
“T-Team Leader Choi.”
“Get a grip, Mr. Jin Taekyung!”
“The lunchboxes are here.”
“If we keep going like this, we’ll be wiped out...huh?”
With trembling eyes, I stared at the ten monsters.
No—the ten lunchboxes.
“The lunchbox delivery is here.”
Put those question marks away, you bastards.
*One Annihilation, coming up.*

The Arch Lich had placed his elites in the rear and used the other monsters as both bait and meat shields.
*To wear us down.*
On top of that, the fog had grown even thicker, making the battle more difficult.
The monsters becoming stronger under its influence was bad enough, but in fog this thick, visibility was limited and sound didn’t carry properly.
That naturally favored monsters, whose senses were sharper than those of humans.
Of course...
*I’m the exception.*
*Whoooosh!
Bang!*
My spear lashed out with all my strength, skewering six or seven monsters like meat on a skewer.
Xiao Shen and the Hunters in the suicide squad, having escaped the crisis, gave me grateful looks.
“Everyone, group up around me!”
“But we only have a few magic scrolls left.
If another Magic Trap activates...”
“No time to explain!
Stop talking and move!”
Team Leader Choi and Xiao Shen nodded at my shout and advanced with the suicide squad.
I understood their concern, but we had already survived three Magic Traps, and this was the rear where the Arch Lich had gathered his elites.
The chances of another trap being triggered were slim.
“Focus on defense instead of attacking.
Advance!”
The battle itself had become more difficult, but the reduced chance of suddenly stumbling into another trap took a weight off my mind.
I could get myself out of danger easily enough, but the other members of the suicide squad might not survive.
*Our final destination is just ahead.
Minimize casualties, then join up with Lee Jungryong and Wu Heixing.*
*Slash!
Kra-d-d-d-d-k!*
I was at the front, cutting a path through the monsters and beginning to feel fatigue build up, when—
“All.
Of.
You.
Fall.
Back!”
“Human.
By my lord’s command, I shall take your life.”
The curtain of monsters split apart to the left and right like the parting of the Red Sea.
I stared blankly, my mouth hanging open, as the beings behind it revealed themselves.
**System Lv.
120 Darkened Lich Lv.
115 Darkened Death Knight**
There were ten of them, all hovering around Level 120.
For a moment, I could barely breathe.
My hands and feet began to tremble.
Team Leader Choi shouted at me in a voice filled with despair.
“We have to retreat right now!”
“T-Team Leader Choi.”
“Get a grip, Mr.
Jin Taekyung!”
“The lunchboxes are here.”
“If we keep going like this, we’ll be wiped out...huh?”
With trembling eyes, I stared at the ten monsters.
No—the ten lunchboxes.
“The lunchbox delivery is here.”
Put those question marks away, you bastards.
*One Annihilation, coming up.*

chapters.title: Chapter 412
paragraphs: *Flap, flap.*
A crow landed on an ancient tree in the middle of the battlefield, its eyes flashing brightly.
The Arch Lich had perched his Familiar in a spot with an excellent view and was watching the situation unfold with considerable pleasure.
*What will you do, human?*
One person was reflected in the crow’s endlessly gleaming black eyes.
An open mouth. Hands trembling slightly.
The sight of Jin Taekyung made the Arch Lich wonder.
*Was the Death Knight Lord truly defeated by such a cowardly human?*
The Death Knight Lord may have had a few flaws, but he was unquestionably a masterpiece for the ages.
The Arch Lich had been unable to resist coveting Lei Fei, an excellent material with a noble spirit and formidable martial power.

That was why he had personally granted him a portion of the magical power that formed the very source of his strength. Thanks to that gift, Lei Fei had become a being who transcended the limits of an ordinary Death Knight.
There was no way the Death Knight Lord could have fallen to a mere coward.
*What exactly happened?*
That day, the Arch Lich had not watched Jin Taekyung and Lei Fei’s battle to the end. No—he had not thought there was any need to.
By the time the young human arrived, the human army had already been wiped out. The situation on another front had seemed far more important than watching a foregone conclusion play out.
By the time he belatedly sensed the erasure of his precious retainer and sent a Familiar, everything was already over.
All the Arch Lich had seen was Jin Taekyung standing with several thousand humans who had appeared out of nowhere—and the monster army, annihilated to the last.
*That human clearly couldn’t have done it alone. Was he simply lucky?*
But his luck ended here.
As many as ten Death Knights and Liches possessed the strength of an entire legion, if not more.
*And unlike last time, he has no one capable of helping him.*
There was only one path left for that human now.
He would helplessly watch his companions die, then fall himself.
That was the only possible ending—and the punishment the Arch Lich had chosen for him.
*Cawww!*
The crow, sharing its master’s mood, let out a grating cry.
Step. Step.
At that very moment, the human approaching his retainers without fear came to a halt.
Then he raised a trembling hand toward the Death Knights and Liches radiating immense magical power.
*Does he intend to surrender?*
The Arch Lich had thought he was merely a coward. He had not expected him to be this stupid as well.
If he believed surrender would persuade the Arch Lich to spare him, he was gravely mistaken—
“One, two, three, four...”
The Arch Lich found himself flustered for the first time in ages.
First, because fluent Demon Realm language had flowed from Jin Taekyung’s mouth.
Second, because he had no idea what Jin Taekyung was doing.
*What in the world is he up to?*
He did not have to wonder for long.
“...Nine, ten.”
As soon as he finished speaking, a droplet of saliva fell from Jin Taekyung’s chin with a soft *plop*.
He wiped his mouth with his sleeve, a satisfied smile spreading across his face.
“The plating is a work of art. Seriously. I hereby award it three Jin-shelin stars.”
Neither the Arch Lich nor his faithful retainers understood what *plating* or *Jin-shelin* meant.
But they understood what Jin Taekyung’s next action meant.
*Gooooooong.*
The spearhead had already been drawn far back, too fast for the eye to follow. A terrifying torrent of qi gathered around it.
At that sight, the Arch Lich felt a shock as though his cold, hardened heart had dropped into his stomach.
A bone-deep chill swept through him, and his thought burst forth.
*Dodge—!*
But the spear shot forward faster than the thought could reach his retainers.
*Woooooong!*
The wind tore apart.
*Kraaaaaaaaaash!*
Space split open.
Within an instant divided into ever smaller slivers of time, a massive vortex wreathed in blue flames swallowed everything.
Countless monsters. Death Knights and Liches.
Even the flock of crows perched in an ancient tree nearby, watching it all unfold.
*Fwoooooosh!*
A blinding flash engulfed everyone’s vision.
*Whoooooosh.*
A wind that had come from somewhere seeped through my entire body.
It was a wind only I could feel—and the arrival of new power.
*Yes. That’s the stuff.*
I smiled at the empty space beyond the slowly fading light.
That was where the Death Knights, Liches, and countless other monsters had been standing.
Everything had been cleanly erased, leaving the air filled with System notifications.
*Ding. Ding. Ding...*

**System You defeated **Lv. 115 Darkened Death Knight**! - You defeated **Lv. 120 Darkened Lich**! - You defeated **Lv. 122 Darkened Death Knight**! - ... - You have defeated too many monsters! - You have gained a massive amount of EXP and Fame! - Level Up! - Level Up! - Level Up! - You have accomplished an exceptional feat! - As a Reward for your achievement, you have obtained the Title **One Against a Thousand**! - Due to the effect of the Title **One Against a Thousand**, all Stats rise by a set amount when facing multiple enemies, and fatigue consumption is greatly reduced! During battle, enemies will be intimidated, while allies’ morale rises dramatically! - Because you have accomplished an exceptional feat, a massive amount of EXP and additional Rewards will be granted! - Level Up! - A new stat, **Intimidation**, has been created! - Due to the effect of the Title **One Against a Thousand**, **Intimidation** has increased significantly! - Enemies who face you will feel fear and terror!
I closed my eyes and savored the lingering rush the System had given me.
A symphony of System notifications chimed without pause.
So this was what the bells of heaven sounded like.

Four Level Ups had completely washed away the fatigue from One Annihilation. I had gained a Title that would be exceptionally effective on a massive battlefield like this, along with a new stat called Intimidation.
*What a rush. It never gets old. The System is the best.*
If every day were like this, I could die without regrets.
“Is that true? Oh! Ohhh...!”
That fucking bastard.
The Skeleton Warlord’s mood-killing remark made me open my eyes. The first thing I saw was a sea of humans and monsters frozen like statues.
“...Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“H-Hyung.”
Team Leader Choi and Xiao Shen stared at me in a daze.
And it wasn’t just those two.
All two hundred or so members of the suicide squad looked the same.
Their eyes and voices held unmistakable awe as they gazed at me.
“Good heavens.”
“W-What in the world just happened?”
“There were ten Death Knights and Liches. Right there! I saw them with my own eyes!”
Yeah. They had been there.
But now they weren’t.
“Goddamn! Holy shit! What the fuck is this? Fucking! Fucking kimchi! Jesus kimchi!”
“Eeeh, eeeeeh? Nani? Naiii?!”
Since some of the Hunters had been sent by mercenary companies or the UN, their reactions varied by nationality.
I spoke to Team Leader Choi, who still seemed incapable of forming a sentence.
“Why are you so surprised? It’s not like you’ve never seen it before.”
“Was that what you used last time, when you defeated the Black Drake...?”
“That’s right.”
Team Leader Choi, who had seen One Annihilation once or twice before, swallowed hard.
“...I don’t remember it being this powerful.”
“I was holding back then.”
That was obviously a lie.
The truth was, even I was so stunned by what I had just done that I had no idea what to say.

The first and only time I had used One Annihilation after reaching the Supreme Peak realm was during my battle with the Western Heaven Demon Lord. I had been so exhausted that I lost consciousness immediately afterward.
*I didn’t know it would be this powerful either.*
There had been ten Death Knights and Liches, each one close to Named level.
I had thought killing six or seven of them would count as a success.

After all, monsters at Level 100 or above gave a considerable amount of EXP. With all the other small fry thrown in, there would be enough to level up, so I’d figured there was no way I’d collapse from exhaustion and make a spectacle of myself.
*...But this is even more than I expected.*
A double-edged sword.
No—a double-edged spear.
But it was undeniably one hell of a powerful strike.
It had blown away not only the hundreds of elite monsters packed tightly together, but all ten Death Knights and Liches as well.
That left a massive gap in the monster army surrounding the suicide squad and me, and the monsters themselves were visibly confused.
*I’d be an idiot to waste an opportunity like this.*
I raised my spear without hesitation.

The unexpected turn of events had temporarily brought both sides to a halt. But if the monster army recovered and surrounded the badly outnumbered suicide squad again, there was no telling what would happen.
“What are you waiting for, you bastards?”
“Huh?”
“What?”
“Eeeeeh?”
My shout, charged with internal energy, jolted everyone back to their senses.
There was no time for honorifics or any of that.
Right now, only one thing mattered.
“Wipe out everything in your path!”
*Ding.*

**System Due to the effect of the Title **One Against a Thousand**, the morale of your allies has risen dramatically! Those who follow your command will form a strong bond and fight even more effectively! - Due to the effect of the Title **One Against a Thousand**, the enemy has become greatly intimidated! - Due to the Title **One Against a Thousand**, the effect of **Intimidation** has increased! - Under the influence of **Intimidation**, the enemy feels fear and backs away!
The System messages described exactly what was happening.
The monsters still alive after witnessing the divine might I had displayed slowly retreated. Even the undead monsters, which had already lost their minds, were intimidated and flinched.
As for us?
“Charge!”
*Whoosh! Kra-d-d-d-d-k!*
With a thunderous shout, I leaped into the gap created by One Annihilation and swung my spear in every direction.
The roughly two hundred members of the suicide squad surged forward as one, roaring loudly enough to make my ears ring.
“Waaaaaaaaah!”
“Follow Mr. Jin! Wipe them all out!”
“Fucking! Fucking Jin Genghis Khan! Jesus Kimchiman!”
“Eeeeeeeh?!”
*Splat! Shraaaaaak!*
Green blood sprayed through the air, and undead bones shattered into pieces.
*Slash!*
I cleanly split the upper body of a Troll trying to turn its back and flee.
The Skeleton Warlord shouted at me furiously.
“Wicked human! Over there! Kill that one!”
“What? Who?”
“Kill that strange human who keeps going ‘eeeeeeh’!”
“Or I’ll kill him myself! If he does it one more time, I swear I’ll kill him!”
“Yeah, okay.”
I’d been hearing it too, and it was starting to piss me off.
“Ghk!”
The Arch Lich let out a strangled groan.
As if having the Link with his Familiar forcibly severed were not enough, all ten of his guards had been erased in a single blow.
Unlike ordinary monsters, they were retainers imbued with his own power. The Arch Lich could not escape the backlash.
“This is madness. How could a mere human...”
The Arch Lich gathered his disrupted magical power, then stopped short.
*A mere human?*
No. That was wrong.
Humans were certainly insignificant beings, but they could never be underestimated.
The Arch Lich had already learned that lesson through bitter experience.
*Could that guy...?*
At the ominous possibility that flashed through his mind, the light in the Arch Lich’s eyes blazed fiercely.

chapters.title: Chapter 413
paragraphs: *Fwoooosh! Kraaaash!*
A massive greatsword smashed into the ground. Wu Heixing’s body shot upward like lightning, having dodged the attack by exactly half a span.
*Shnk!*
His blade drove up beneath the ogre’s jaw and burst out through the crown of its head.
A precise strike, without a single wasted motion.
Wu Heixing wrenched his sword free, stepped off the falling ogre’s shoulder, and dropped into the horde of monsters.
The sword in his hand traced countless lines through the air.
*The Twelve Blood Net Sword.*
Some condemned the Cultural Revolution, which lasted from 1966 to 1976, as an atrocity that outraged heaven and humanity. For others, however, it had been the opportunity of a lifetime.

Wu Heixing’s grandfather, a longtime political associate of Mao Zedong, had risen spectacularly and embezzled an astronomical fortune. Using his son—a member of the Red Guards—as a stepping stone, he had smuggled away all manner of cultural artifacts and ancient books.
The Twelve Blood Net Sword Wu Heixing had learned was one of the countless ancient books his grandfather had acquired at the time.
*Shreeeeek!*
A net of twelve strands spread out, covering more than ten meters in every direction.
The net of red aura sliced through skin and flesh and cleaved bone. Dozens of high-tier monsters fell apart in pieces.
It was power worthy of an S-rank Hunter.
Thoroughly emboldened, Wu Heixing shouted.
“Red Guard Gang! What are you doing? Sweep them all away, you bastards!”
“Yes, sir!”
His mana-infused roar shook the battlefield.
The roughly three hundred elite Hunters of the Red Guard Gang, founded by Wu Heixing’s family and raised as their private army, charged into every opening without hesitation.
*Shreeeek! Splurt!*
*Whoosh! Slash!*
—Krrk, khrrrk!
“Aaaaargh!”
The screams of humans and monsters mingled with sprays of blood on every side.
The Red Guard Gang Hunters whom Wu Heixing had held in reserve until the very end were unquestionably strong. But their enemies were high-tier monsters as well.
The elite monsters positioned in the rear darted through the thick fog as they fought the Hunters. Regardless of the difference in level, the monsters outnumbered them three or four to one.
And yet...
“You filthy, stinking bastards dare!”
*Stab-stab-stab!*
The presence of an S-rank Hunter like Wu Heixing was enough to turn the unfavorable battle around.
He might have drawn widespread criticism for his debauched behavior and foul temperament, but he was still a genius who had grown up with every possible advantage.

Besides, unlike when he had first been deployed to the front lines, Wu Heixing had become more experienced. After passing through battlefields where death ran rampant, his skills had advanced by another step.
*I can do this! I’m Wu Heixing!*
Exhilaration surged from deep within his chest as he swung his sword without pause.
His enemy was a monster army numbering in the tens of thousands. He had been afraid at first, but somehow he had made it this far.
Whenever he suffered even a minor injury or began to tire, he gulped down expensive potions like water. When necessary, he had used the Red Guard Gang Hunters as shields to withdraw.
And now, not a single monster could stop his red aura blade.
*I’ll make sure no one ever looks down on me again. Lei Fei. That fucking bangzi bastard. No one!*
That was the moment Wu Heixing ground his teeth at the humiliating memory.
*Fwoooooosh! Boom!*
A spear flew in at blinding speed, skewering three or four Hunters like meat on a skewer before burying itself deep in the ground.
A three-meter-long lance—something rarely seen on a battlefield like this.
Wu Heixing whipped his head around to find the attacker, and his eyes flew wide.
“Death Knight!”
*Thud-thud-thud-thud!*
The figure riding a skeletal horse across the battlefield was unmistakably a Death Knight.
And there were two of them, not one.
The second Death Knight raised its lance from horseback.
“Everyone, watch—!”
*Fwoooooosh! Boom!*
Before Wu Heixing could finish his warning, the second lance tore through the air and pierced six or seven Hunters clustered together.
Even the finest armor could not stop the strike. Arms and legs flew into the air, and bodies missing their upper halves collapsed with heavy thuds.
The sudden appearance of the Death Knights.
Then, as the Red Guard Gang’s Hunters froze at the horrifying sight unfolding before their eyes—
—D-a-r-k. V-i-n-e!
An eerie voice like metal scraping against metal rang out, and the ground began to change.
*Crack! Kra-d-d-d-d-k!*
The solid ground split apart like a spiderweb, and black vines surged up through the cracks.
Filled with magical power, they moved like living creatures. Some seized human arms and legs, while others wormed through gaps left exposed by armor and pierced their victims.
*Shrrrrk! Stab-stab!*
“Kyaaaaargh!”
“Black magic! It’s black magic!”
“Don’t panic! Cut the vines! Get out of the area now!”
Screams and shouts rang out everywhere.
*Crack.*
Wu Heixing tore the black vines coiling around him from the ground like scallion roots and flung them aside, biting down hard on his lip.
It was not the deaths of his Hunters that troubled him.
He understood what this entire series of events meant.
“Lich...!”
Wu Heixing’s guess was correct.
High above their heads, a death mage riding atop the head of a giant Wyvern that prowled through the gray sky raised a staff made of skulls and bones and pointed it at the ground.
—C-o-n-f-u-s-i-n-g!
*Whoooooosh!*
With that eerie cry, magical power poured down like dark storm clouds and engulfed the entire area.
The Hunters struggling to escape the black vines suddenly writhed as hallucinations and phantom voices seized them. They became easy prey for the monsters lurking around them.
—Sssssss!
—Gwoooooar!
*Smash! Kra-d-d-d-d-k!*
“Krrk, khk!”
“P-Please, save me!”
“Mother! You can’t die, Mother!”
Some fell with a final scream.
Others continued to howl even as they died, unable to escape the hallucinations and phantom voices.
But there were also those whose powerful wills allowed them to break free of the spell.
“You have to go!”
“Young Master!”
Despite the shouts of the A-rank Hunters surrounding him, Wu Heixing’s face had gone as white as a sheet.
Only one question circled through his mind.
*What—what the hell am I supposed to do?*
The Lich was in the sky, while two Death Knights were rapidly approaching from the ground.
Could they retreat?
If they did, where would they go? How would they get there?
Wu Heixing might have been able to face the two Death Knights alone, but what about the Lich’s magic and the countless monsters surrounding the area so tightly that not even water could pass through?
No matter how hard he thought, he could find no answer.
*This...this fucking situation...*
*Crack.*
Wu Heixing was grinding his teeth hard enough to crack them when—
*Fwoooosh! Bang!*
With the sharp crack of compressed air exploding, a streak of light shot up from the distant ground and sliced through the sky.
The next moment, the headless body of the Wyvern began to plummet.
“This...”
Wu Heixing muttered the word like a groan.
Everyone forgot the situation around them and looked up at the sky.
Before their eyes, the Wyvern’s body plummeted faster and faster, while a heap of black bones—the being that had once been called a Lich—tumbled down after it.
“...That’s impossible.”
The Lich was dead.
Killed in a single strike.
Someone had pierced through dozens of layers of defensive magic and accurately intercepted a target in midair?
Even an S-rank Hunter could not easily guarantee such a feat.
Wu Heixing had never seen an attack so fast or so powerful.
But for someone else, it was as natural as breathing.
The man who had been quietly watching what he had done from a short distance away suddenly opened his mouth.
“It’s been a long time since I threw a spear. I’m certainly not as good as I used to be.”
The man standing behind him like an iron tower answered in a stiff tone.
“It was an excellent throw.”
“Hmm. No, it wasn’t. I seem to have grown rusty. Proof that I’m getting old, I suppose.”
“That cannot be.”
At the Head of Security’s usual flat response, Lee Jungryong smiled gently.
“I saw Death Knights.”
Go Jun nodded without a word.
“Yes. Two of them.”
“Do you think Wu Heixing can stop them?”
“If you mean the Death Knights, he should be able to defeat them without much difficulty.”
Go Jun added in a low voice.
“If there were no monsters around them.”
“So under the present circumstances, it will be difficult.”
“The black magic has dissipated, but they have already suffered considerable losses, and there are far too many monsters.”
“Then they’ll have to struggle with everything they have.”
“It will be a fierce and difficult battle.”
“My, my. Then I suppose we should help them.”
“Would it not be better to watch a little longer?”
Lee Jungryong widened his eyes in feigned surprise.
“Why?”
Go Jun had been taught by Lee Jungryong since childhood. He knew that each of these moments was a test from his Master.
He also knew what answer was expected of him.
“Would they not be more grateful if we helped them when the situation was more precarious?”
Only then did the Master smile in satisfaction at his Disciple’s answer. Even his manner of speaking changed.
“Yes. That’s exactly it.”
“The Red Guard Gang has been a nuisance for some time.”
“They’re amusing bastards. They shout about the people and communism, then form a private army of Hunters behind everyone’s backs.”
“But the Crown Prince Party supporting the Red Guard Gang is friendly toward us, is it not?”
“That is precisely why the Red Guard Gang must disappear. They have always avoided the sunlight by sitting in the shade of that tree. Once the tree is uprooted, what choice will they have?”
“They’ll have to find another tree or buy themselves a parasol.”
“We will become their new tree. If that happens, even more opportunities will open up.”
Go Jun nodded, then suddenly spoke.
“May I ask one more question?”
“Go ahead.”
“The reason you brought Wu Heixing into this operation... Does it have something to do with Jin Taekyung?”
The question had been troubling Go Jun for some time.
Even if Wu Heixing was an S-rank Hunter, why bring along an idiot like him?
*That man is immensely powerful. Even if Master is using Wu Heixing, what use could he possibly be?*
Sometimes, this happened.
Just when Go Jun thought he had grown accustomed to his Master’s thoughts and actions, he would find himself unable to understand Lee Jungryong’s true intentions.
And whenever that happened, Lee Jungryong would always wear an inscrutable smile.
Just like now.
“Team Leader Seok.”
Both his tone and the atmosphere changed.
Returning to his role as Ares Guild’s Head of Security, Go Jun bowed deeply.
“Yes, Vice Guild Master.”
“It seems the time has come for you to step in. What do you think?”
Go Jun raised his head and looked past Lee Jungryong’s shoulder at the fierce battle.
The carefully selected elites of the Red Guard Gang were dying to the monsters, while Wu Heixing had just finished taking down one of the two Death Knights.
“I’ll be going, then.”
“Do be careful not to get hurt.”
Go Jun answered with a brief bow, then led the waiting Ares Guild members toward the battlefield.
They did not shout as they charged the monsters, but the force they radiated was more than enough to overwhelm everything before them.
*Kra-d-d-d-d-k! Slash!*
Lee Jungryong watched in satisfaction as one flank of the monster army collapsed in an instant.
Then he suddenly caught the smell of blood carried on the wind.
The wind was blowing from the west.
It was the signal that the man he had been waiting for had arrived.
“Right on time.”
Lee Jungryong murmured under his breath and looked toward the distant horizon.
As he raised his qi, his senses sharpened like a razor, and a man’s shout reached his ears.
—Fuck, kill them all! And that bastard who’s been going ‘Eeeeeeh’ this whole time—if he does it one more time, I’m counting him as a monster. Got it?
Lee Jungryong let out a low chuckle and extended his hand.
Then he clenched his fist toward Jin Taekyung, who was somewhere out there.
