chapters.title: Chapter 414
paragraphs: Some faces are never a welcome sight, no matter how many times you see them. For me, Lee Jungryong and Wu Heixing fell squarely into that category.
Even so, I spoke first because Wu Heixing looked almost presentable today.
“Fancy seeing you here. I thought I’d never see you again.”
At my cheerful greeting, the battered Wu Heixing shot me a venomous glare.
“Shut up.”
“Say one more word, and on my grandfather’s honor, I’ll tear you limb from limb.”
*Is he some Chinese version of Kindaichi or something?* I could never understand why people like him treated their late grandfathers’ honor like a credit card.
I put on a serious face.
“Were you and your grandfather not on good terms?”
“What?”
“No, think about it. Why stake your grandfather’s honor on something impossible? You’d be much better off staking it on you getting torn limb from limb...”
“You fucking bastard!”
Wu Heixing sprang to his feet with an enraged shout, but Lee Jungryong raised a hand to stop him.
“That’s enough.”
“Mr. Lee! But this bastard...”
“Fighting among ourselves before the final battle will do us nothing but harm. Calm down.”
*Crunch.*
Wu Heixing ground his teeth as if he meant to break them, then glared at me.
“Understood. Since you insist, Mr. Lee, I’ll let it end here.”
“A wise decision.”
*Was he really the type to back down so obediently?*
As I studied Lee Jungryong’s gentle smile, I turned my head slightly.
A brief glance from Team Leader Choi told me plenty.
“What about you, Jin Taekyung?”
I looked away from Team Leader Choi and gave a casual shrug.
“When an elder speaks, you have to listen.”
“I didn’t know you cared about things like that.”
“You have to respect your elders, don’t you?”
At my calm, unruffled answer, Lee Jungryong gave a hearty laugh whose meaning I could not decipher. Wu Heixing glared at me as if he wanted to kill me all over again.
“Respect your elders? Spare me that ridiculous bullshit. Then what about me? I’m seven years older than you.”
“If you don’t want to write your will, start by making your eyes look nicer.”
“You turtle-dicked son of a...!”
“Quit your bullshit.”
Wu Heixing’s second outburst died in his throat.
I fixed him with a cold stare and continued.
“If you still have enough energy to lose your temper over something this trivial, go check on the friends you brought with you.”
“They risked their lives to follow you this far. They’re not consumables you can use once and throw away.”
I made no attempt to hide my contempt.
Barely fifty Hunters remained around Wu Heixing.
According to the report from headquarters, his suicide squad had set out five hundred strong. Most of them must have died or fallen behind.
“Losses? Sure, that happens. We’re in the middle of a battle. But...”
Wu Heixing’s armor might have been drenched in blood, but it was otherwise completely intact. Even as his comrades died around him, he had fought while protecting himself.
“Got anything to say, you fucking idiot?”
A line from an old superhero movie I had watched as a kid came to mind.
*With great power comes great responsibility.*
And that didn’t apply only to people bitten by radioactive spiders.

If someone could produce an aura blade instead of spiderwebs—if he had used that power to amass tremendous wealth and fame and cover up the crimes he had committed—then he had to bear at least some responsibility.
That was what I believed.
“You might be S-rank, but you’re no Hunter. So from now on, when you introduce yourself, don’t call yourself one. Just say, ‘I’m Wu Heixing, the lucky S-rank.’ Got it?”
Wu Heixing’s clenched fists trembled, but Lee Jungryong answered in his place.
“He did his best.”
“Judging by his armor, I doubt it. He could wipe that down right now and list it on Junggonara as used equipment.”
“Wearing sturdy, high-quality armor is hardly grounds for criticism.”
“I noticed this last time too, but you go out of your way to defend him. Does that bastard have some kind of dirt on you?”
“Everyone has weaknesses. I simply happen to be quite good at hiding mine.”
“You should have your computer checked. Who knows? Maybe Chinese hackers are sharing videos of the Vice Guild Master watching porn in a group chat.”
“I’ll keep that in mind.”
*He really is a formidable opponent.*
Lee Jungryong smiled without the slightest sign of agitation, but the man standing behind him reacted differently.
I waved at the man radiating a faint killing intent.
“Well, look who it is. Team Leader Seok. Isn’t that our Go Jun?”
Lee Jungryong’s Head of Security and Disciple.
I distinctly remembered beating him half to death before we left for China, but the man standing before me looked not only fine, but even more solid than before.
His gaze alone had grown deeper and more profound. I could tell at a glance that his abilities had advanced significantly.
*And he’s learned some patience.*
Go Jun was the most loyal of all the loyal hounds Lee Jungryong had raised.
In the past, he would have rushed at me without hesitation. But this time, he had gathered up his killing intent until not a trace remained and chosen silence instead of drawing his weapon.
Lee Jungryong regarded his Disciple with satisfaction before speaking.
“We’ve reached the Arch Lich’s doorstep. According to the coordinates, only twenty kilometers remain.”
I swept back my blood-sticky hair.
“Probably the longest and fiercest twenty kilometers on Earth.”
“Indeed. The Arch Lich has kept a considerable force in reserve.”
“How many?”
“An estimated fifty thousand.”
The moment those words left his mouth, a groan escaped from the members of the suicide squad who had been listening intently to our conversation.
The suicide squads led by Lee Jungryong, Wu Heixing, and me numbered only around five hundred in total.
The mere estimate was enough to fill them with despair. To reach the Arch Lich, we would have to break through an army a hundred times our size.
Perhaps that was why someone shouted in a frightened voice.
“We should retreat while we still can!”
As if a dam had burst, cries rose from the other Hunters.
“Fuck!”
“There are too many monsters!”
“We’ll all be wiped out if we keep this up!”
“I came here to defeat the Arch Lich, not to die a meaningless death!”
Even the roughly two hundred members of the Western Front’s suicide squad, who had made it this far with almost no losses, were no exception.
Yet amid the fear spreading like wildfire, two people remained unshaken.
Xiao Shen, who watched me with unwavering trust, and...
“There’s a possibility.”
Team Leader Choi had gone beyond simply trusting me. He had independently deduced one possible explanation for the situation. He continued in a calm voice.
“An estimated fifty thousand is far beyond the High Command’s prediction.”
“Then shouldn’t we obviously retreat?”
Team Leader Choi immediately shook his head at the shout from one of the suicide squad members.
“The number of monsters we faced was also lower than expected.”
“Huh?”
“There were certainly many of them, but the monster forces we encountered on the front lines were not as overwhelming as we anticipated.”
“Then...”

“The Arch Lich may have been guarding against precisely this situation. Rather than commit all its forces to the front lines, it kept an army of fifty thousand in reserve as a final move it could use under any circumstances.”
The faces of the Hunters watching Team Leader Choi stiffened—not because they fully understood what he meant, but because the ground beneath their feet had begun to shake with increasing force.
*Grk. Gr-r-r-r-rk.*
The rumbling could be felt from dozens of kilometers away. Everyone’s body trembled with it.

A ruined road stretched ahead, vast plains spreading out on either side. Beyond the dense fog filling the landscape, the roars and footsteps of tens of thousands of monsters merged into a faint, distant thunder.
“Grooooooar!”
“This is insane...”
“Run. We have to run. We can’t win this.”
People began to edge backward.
The only exception was the Ares Guild members, who stood firm without wavering. In front of them, Lee Jungryong watched Team Leader Choi with interest.
“So?”
Their gazes met. I saw Team Leader Choi’s grip tighten around **Hero’s Soul**.
“Although the High Command’s prediction was wrong, the front lines must have had forces to spare because the Arch Lich did not launch an all-out attack.”
“Even so, our forces were still insufficient compared to the enemy’s.”
“That is exactly why certain people were left behind—to make up the difference.”
*Grk. Gr-r-r-rk.*
The vibrations and roars grew stronger. Amid the anxious, agitated murmuring, Team Leader Choi’s mana-charged voice pierced everyone’s ears.
“Those capable of overturning the course of a battle in an instant. S-rank Hunters, each of whom is called a one-person army.”
At that exact moment—
*Fwoooooosh!*
A dazzling mass of light erupted above our heads.
Amid the brilliant radiance, the air split apart as if sliced by a razor-sharp sword. Three people descended through the opening, stepping on the empty air as though walking down a staircase.
“When I was a child, my great-grandmother would often sit me on her lap and tell me that royalty must fulfill the duties befitting their station. Commoners like you would not understand, of course.”
I let out a snort and bowed at the waist. He was usually annoying beyond belief, but this time I had no choice but to play along.
“His Highness Prince Felix.”
“It is pleasing to hear those words from your lips, Jin, Hunter of the Orient.”
At Prince Felix’s lofty, self-important manner, the beautiful woman beside him clicked her tongue.
“Can’t you do something about him? Gag him, at least.”
“I think we should indulge him today, big sis.”
“Oh my.”
Faye Chen’s eyes widened at my answer, then she broke into a bright smile.
“That’s nice to hear. Coming all this way was worth it after all. Don’t you agree?”
The last of the three laughed heartily at Faye Chen’s question.
“Does that mean I can expect something too? What do you think, Jin?”
“What, should I kiss you?”
“Oh, that wouldn’t be bad. But I’ll politely decline. I’m already married to my beloved Fred, and we have five adopted children.”
*Fwoosh. Thump.*
Magic Johnson glided down through the air and patted my shoulder with a palm as large as a pot lid.
“Jin, you brave little rascal. How did you ever think of attempting such a dangerous Teleport? I nearly gave up several times.”
“But you still did it, Johnson.”
“The odds were different. This time, there was only a ten percent chance of failure. You’re at least eighty percent braver than I am.”
Courage didn’t come in sizes.
Simply by risking death to come here, they had proved themselves worthy of being called the greatest Hunters in the world.
The people who had received these unexpected reinforcements stared at them with wide, disbelieving eyes.
“F-Faye Chen?”
“Prince Felix and Magic Johnson are here too!”
“They’re S-rank Hunters! S-rank Hunters came to help us!”
“I love you, Johnson! Fucking nice gay!”
But that wasn’t the end.
*Boom. Boom. Boom.*
Another vibration came through the ground, different from the one we had felt moments earlier.
It heralded the arrival of an enormous army marching in step. Far away, countless figures emerged as a line of dots stretching across the distant horizon.
“Did you think we came charging in without a plan?”
Faye Chen grinned.
“Ten thousand troops from the Western and Eastern Fronts combined. That should at least buy enough time for you to escape.”
A dazed voice slipped from someone’s lips.
“Now we can survive...”
A voice answered him.
“No.”
Team Leader Choi raised **Hero’s Soul** high.
Even through the dense fog, its transparent blade shone beautifully.
“We’re going to win.”
*I believed it too.*

sentences.text: Some faces are never a welcome sight, no matter how many times you see them.
For me, Lee Jungryong and Wu Heixing fell squarely into that category.
Even so, I spoke first because Wu Heixing looked almost presentable today.
“Fancy seeing you here.
I thought I’d never see you again.”
At my cheerful greeting, the battered Wu Heixing shot me a venomous glare.
“Shut up.”
“Say one more word, and on my grandfather’s honor, I’ll tear you limb from limb.”
*Is he some Chinese version of Kindaichi or something?* I could never understand why people like him treated their late grandfathers’ honor like a credit card.
I put on a serious face.
“Were you and your grandfather not on good terms?”
“What?”
“No, think about it.
Why stake your grandfather’s honor on something impossible?
You’d be much better off staking it on you getting torn limb from limb...”
“You fucking bastard!”
Wu Heixing sprang to his feet with an enraged shout, but Lee Jungryong raised a hand to stop him.
“That’s enough.”
“Mr.
Lee!
But this bastard...”
“Fighting among ourselves before the final battle will do us nothing but harm.
Calm down.”
*Crunch.*
Wu Heixing ground his teeth as if he meant to break them, then glared at me.
“Understood.
Since you insist, Mr.
Lee, I’ll let it end here.”
“A wise decision.”
*Was he really the type to back down so obediently?*
As I studied Lee Jungryong’s gentle smile, I turned my head slightly.
A brief glance from Team Leader Choi told me plenty.
“What about you, Jin Taekyung?”
I looked away from Team Leader Choi and gave a casual shrug.
“When an elder speaks, you have to listen.”
“I didn’t know you cared about things like that.”
“You have to respect your elders, don’t you?”
At my calm, unruffled answer, Lee Jungryong gave a hearty laugh whose meaning I could not decipher.
Wu Heixing glared at me as if he wanted to kill me all over again.
“Respect your elders?
Spare me that ridiculous bullshit.
Then what about me?
I’m seven years older than you.”
“If you don’t want to write your will, start by making your eyes look nicer.”
“You turtle-dicked son of a...!”
“Quit your bullshit.”
Wu Heixing’s second outburst died in his throat.
I fixed him with a cold stare and continued.
“If you still have enough energy to lose your temper over something this trivial, go check on the friends you brought with you.”
“They risked their lives to follow you this far.
They’re not consumables you can use once and throw away.”
I made no attempt to hide my contempt.
Barely fifty Hunters remained around Wu Heixing.
According to the report from headquarters, his suicide squad had set out five hundred strong.
Most of them must have died or fallen behind.
“Losses?
Sure, that happens.
We’re in the middle of a battle.
But...”
Wu Heixing’s armor might have been drenched in blood, but it was otherwise completely intact.
Even as his comrades died around him, he had fought while protecting himself.
“Got anything to say, you fucking idiot?”
A line from an old superhero movie I had watched as a kid came to mind.
*With great power comes great responsibility.*
And that didn’t apply only to people bitten by radioactive spiders.

If someone could produce an aura blade instead of spiderwebs—if he had used that power to amass tremendous wealth and fame and cover up the crimes he had committed—then he had to bear at least some responsibility.
That was what I believed.
“You might be S-rank, but you’re no Hunter.
So from now on, when you introduce yourself, don’t call yourself one.
Just say, ‘I’m Wu Heixing, the lucky S-rank.’ Got it?”
Wu Heixing’s clenched fists trembled, but Lee Jungryong answered in his place.
“He did his best.”
“Judging by his armor, I doubt it.
He could wipe that down right now and list it on Junggonara as used equipment.”
“Wearing sturdy, high-quality armor is hardly grounds for criticism.”
“I noticed this last time too, but you go out of your way to defend him.
Does that bastard have some kind of dirt on you?”
“Everyone has weaknesses.
I simply happen to be quite good at hiding mine.”
“You should have your computer checked.
Who knows?
Maybe Chinese hackers are sharing videos of the Vice Guild Master watching porn in a group chat.”
“I’ll keep that in mind.”
*He really is a formidable opponent.*
Lee Jungryong smiled without the slightest sign of agitation, but the man standing behind him reacted differently.
I waved at the man radiating a faint killing intent.
“Well, look who it is.
Team Leader Seok.
Isn’t that our Go Jun?”
Lee Jungryong’s Head of Security and Disciple.
I distinctly remembered beating him half to death before we left for China, but the man standing before me looked not only fine, but even more solid than before.
His gaze alone had grown deeper and more profound.
I could tell at a glance that his abilities had advanced significantly.
*And he’s learned some patience.*
Go Jun was the most loyal of all the loyal hounds Lee Jungryong had raised.
In the past, he would have rushed at me without hesitation.
But this time, he had gathered up his killing intent until not a trace remained and chosen silence instead of drawing his weapon.
Lee Jungryong regarded his Disciple with satisfaction before speaking.
“We’ve reached the Arch Lich’s doorstep.
According to the coordinates, only twenty kilometers remain.”
I swept back my blood-sticky hair.
“Probably the longest and fiercest twenty kilometers on Earth.”
“Indeed.
The Arch Lich has kept a considerable force in reserve.”
“How many?”
“An estimated fifty thousand.”
The moment those words left his mouth, a groan escaped from the members of the suicide squad who had been listening intently to our conversation.
The suicide squads led by Lee Jungryong, Wu Heixing, and me numbered only around five hundred in total.
The mere estimate was enough to fill them with despair.
To reach the Arch Lich, we would have to break through an army a hundred times our size.
Perhaps that was why someone shouted in a frightened voice.
“We should retreat while we still can!”
As if a dam had burst, cries rose from the other Hunters.
“Fuck!”
“There are too many monsters!”
“We’ll all be wiped out if we keep this up!”
“I came here to defeat the Arch Lich, not to die a meaningless death!”
Even the roughly two hundred members of the Western Front’s suicide squad, who had made it this far with almost no losses, were no exception.
Yet amid the fear spreading like wildfire, two people remained unshaken.
Xiao Shen, who watched me with unwavering trust, and...
“There’s a possibility.”
Team Leader Choi had gone beyond simply trusting me.
He had independently deduced one possible explanation for the situation.
He continued in a calm voice.
“An estimated fifty thousand is far beyond the High Command’s prediction.”
“Then shouldn’t we obviously retreat?”
Team Leader Choi immediately shook his head at the shout from one of the suicide squad members.
“The number of monsters we faced was also lower than expected.”
“Huh?”
“There were certainly many of them, but the monster forces we encountered on the front lines were not as overwhelming as we anticipated.”
“Then...”
“The Arch Lich may have been guarding against precisely this situation.
Rather than commit all its forces to the front lines, it kept an army of fifty thousand in reserve as a final move it could use under any circumstances.”
The faces of the Hunters watching Team Leader Choi stiffened—not because they fully understood what he meant, but because the ground beneath their feet had begun to shake with increasing force.
*Grk.
Gr-r-r-r-rk.*
The rumbling could be felt from dozens of kilometers away.
Everyone’s body trembled with it.
A ruined road stretched ahead, vast plains spreading out on either side.
Beyond the dense fog filling the landscape, the roars and footsteps of tens of thousands of monsters merged into a faint, distant thunder.
“Grooooooar!”
“This is insane...”
“Run.
We have to run.
We can’t win this.”
People began to edge backward.
The only exception was the Ares Guild members, who stood firm without wavering.
In front of them, Lee Jungryong watched Team Leader Choi with interest.
“So?”
Their gazes met.
I saw Team Leader Choi’s grip tighten around **Hero’s Soul**.
“Although the High Command’s prediction was wrong, the front lines must have had forces to spare because the Arch Lich did not launch an all-out attack.”
“Even so, our forces were still insufficient compared to the enemy’s.”
“That is exactly why certain people were left behind—to make up the difference.”
*Grk.
Gr-r-r-rk.*
The vibrations and roars grew stronger.
Amid the anxious, agitated murmuring, Team Leader Choi’s mana-charged voice pierced everyone’s ears.

S-rank Hunters, each of whom is called a one-person army.”
At that exact moment—
*Fwoooooosh!*
A dazzling mass of light erupted above our heads.

Gag him, at least.”

“Oh my.”
Faye Chen’s eyes widened at my answer, then she broke into a bright smile.
“That’s nice to hear.

Don’t you agree?”

chapters.title: Chapter 415
paragraphs: The battle came quickly.

Before tens of thousands of monsters and the thick fog rolling over the wasteland like waves, a black-skinned Grand Mage stood tall, stepping on empty air, and uttered a single word heralding the beginning of the battle.
“Fire Cannon.”
*Fwoooooosh.*
An immense torrent of mana swirled around him. Five flames sprang to life in midair, swelled to enormous size, and shot forward like cannonballs.
*Fwoooooosh—BOOM!*
The black tide of tens of thousands of monsters split apart. Blistering heat burned flesh and bone and melted the ground.
An area-of-effect spell that reduced at least a thousand soldiers to ash.
But the monsters did not stop.
Neither did Magic Johnson.
“Water Blaster.”
The air, dry as sand after the Fire Cannon, grew heavy with moisture.
Magic Johnson spread his arms, and an enormous wave rose behind him.
The sight defied every law of the world.
It was magic in the truest sense—the supernatural power of the greatest War Mage among countless mages.
“Engulf them.”
The cheerful, ever-laughing man was nowhere to be seen.
Magic Johnson flung both hands out, his gaze grave. A wave dozens of meters high cast a broad, dark shadow over the tens of thousands of monsters.
*Roooooar!*
Brimming with mana, the wave crashed down. The tremendous water pressure crushed the monsters, bursting their bodies and tearing them apart.
The flames left behind by Fire Cannon went out, and the surrounding area was flooded with water.
Magic Johnson knew exactly what to do next.
“Strike. Lightning Rain.”
It happened in an instant.
Black storm clouds gathered over the monsters’ heads, and dozens of bolts of lightning came crashing down.
*BOOM! Crackle!*
—Kraaaaaaar!
—Kyaaak!
The lightning struck without distinction, tearing through targets both in the air and on the ground.
Blackened Gargoyles and Griffins plummeted from the sky, while the ground, soaked by Water Blaster, carried the current.
The living monsters trembled violently and dropped to their knees with a single shriek. The undead collapsed into piles of ash.
At the unbelievable sight unfolding before our eyes, a groan escaped someone’s lips.
“So this is a Grand Mage...”
The results of only three area-of-effect spells were staggering.
At least several thousand monsters had either died or been rendered incapable of fighting, and one flank of the monster army had collapsed.
But even the Grand Mage who had single-handedly unleashed a natural disaster could not escape the crushing fatigue.
“Fuck. If I’d known this would happen, I would’ve saved a few more spells.”
Casting magic was no simple task. Area-of-effect magic in particular—Magic Johnson’s specialty—consumed mental strength and mana on a scale proportionate to its destructive power.
Considering how much magic he had already poured into the front lines before coming here, this was his limit.
“Mrs. Chen. I guess I’m getting old too.”
“Move aside. We old folks have to look out for each other. And...”
Faye Chen tossed aside the whiskey bottle in her hand, drew the bow strapped at her side with lightning speed, and pulled back the string.
An arrow of mana formed against the empty bowstring.
“It’s not Mrs. Chen. It’s Miss Chen. Who decided I was married?”
Faye Chen snorted and released the string.
The mana arrow, scattering a dazzling radiance, shot forward with a sharp whistle. It erased the space in its path and split through the thick fog.
And then—
*BOOM!*
A tremendous explosion erupted.
After confirming that the Death Knight hiding among the countless monsters had vanished without even managing a final cry, Faye Chen pulled back her bowstring again.
*Thrum-thrum-thrum!*
Arrows loosed in the blink of an eye became streaks of light across the wasteland. Thunderous explosions followed, each arrow sweeping away and annihilating dozens of monsters.
If Magic Johnson was one of the world’s three greatest Grand Mages and its finest War Mage, Faye Chen was the finest archer alive.
But...
—Gwooooooar!
—Kyaaaaa!
The monster army, tens of thousands strong, ignored it all and charged.
Cut down dozens, and dozens more filled their places. Cut down hundreds, and hundreds more took their place.
Charging through the thick fog, they were stronger and more ferocious than ordinary monsters.
All that remained was an unavoidable head-on battle.
Facing the oncoming monster army, two men stepped forward at the same time.
“Ares Guild. Formation B. Break through them.”
*Clatter-clatter-clatter!*
At Lee Jungryong’s quiet command, the elite Guild members who had made it this far without a single casualty moved as one.
Jin Taekyung studied them closely, then addressed the suicide squad he had brought from the Western Front.
“Everyone, Formation J.”
“Yes, sir!”
“Formation J! Get into position!”
The suicide squad moved swiftly, repeating the command in thunderous voices.
Behind Jin Taekyung, Wu Heixing had been gathering the handful of Red Guard Gang Hunters who remained. He grabbed one of the Western Front suicide-squad members and asked,
“Hey, rookie. What the hell is Formation J?”
Recognizing Wu Heixing, Xiao Shen frowned before answering.
“Hyung came up with the formation himself.”
“So what does it mean?”
“Nothing special. He said it means, ‘Just fucking fight.’”
Wu Heixing was momentarily speechless, and Lee Jungryong and Jin Taekyung launched themselves forward at the exact same time, as if they had planned it.
Prince Felix and ten thousand Hunters surged fiercely after them.
“Aaaaaaaaah!”
—Kraaaaaaaargh!
Humans and monsters.
Monsters and humans.
Deafening battle cries and killing intent erupted. Racing across the wasteland at blinding speed, the two sides bared their teeth and leveled their spears and blades at one another.
*Fwoooooosh—Kra-d-d-d-d-k!*
The great battle had begun.
I leaned back and put my shoulder into it. The movements flowed seamlessly together as I whipped my arm forward with all my strength.
*Whoosh—thud-thud-thud-thud!*
White Flame shot from my hand, piercing dozens of monsters and opening a path.
A gap appeared in an instant.
Without hesitation, I plunged into it and lashed out with my arms and legs at everything within reach.
*Crack!*
My fist shot forward too fast to see, crushing the head of the charging Lycanthrope like a watermelon.
Before the brain matter spilling from its skull could hit the ground, I leaped into the air.
*Tap—whoosh!*
A four-meter-tall figure loomed before me. My reflection appeared in its pale pupils, long since drained of light.
But before the Undead Troll could swing its club, my palm slammed into its chest.
*Boom!*

Smoke curled from the Undead Troll’s seven apertures along with a surge of tremendous heat. Its insides had suffered catastrophic damage, and it met its final death before its extraordinary regenerative power could even come into play.
“Wicked human! Behind you!”
*I know, idiot. Who asked for your advice?*
I turned my head. A lance wreathed in pitch-black magic grazed my neck and hurtled into the sky.
It had been thrown to catch me while I was suspended in midair. The timing was good, but the enemy had made one mistake.
It had underestimated me.
“Fuck. Why are there so many Death Knights? What is this, a chicken joint?”
I landed lightly after evading the lance, and a Death Knight mounted on a skeletal horse charged straight at me.
“This. Is. As. Far. As. You. Go!”
*Fwoooooosh!*
With that shout, it swung a sword wreathed in ominous magic. The energy it gave off could not compare to an S-rank Hunter’s, but it was on par with that of a top-tier A-rank Hunter.
Or perhaps...
*This Death Knight must have been a Hunter once too.*
Maybe that was why.
The sight of the Death Knight reminded me of Lei Fei, leaving a sudden bitter taste in my mouth.
The Skeleton Warlord screamed when it saw my reaction.
“Dodge, human!”
*Thud!*
The magic clinging to the Death Knight’s sword vanished without a trace.
The Death Knight stared blankly at the transparent spearhead that had pierced through its chest and emerged from its back. Then it muttered weakly,
“This is as far as you go.”
I returned the Death Knight’s own words to it and brought down the edge of my hand.
“I don’t know who you used to be, but you’ve suffered enough.”
*Slash—thud!*
The skeletal horse and Death Knight split in two and vanished.
As before, I used Seizing an Object Through Empty Space to draw White Flame back toward me, cutting down a monster along the way. Then I abruptly asked,
“How come you’re not pestering me for food today?”
“Ahem. What do you take me for? How dare you mistake this commander for—”
*Slash!*
“A freeloader. You call yourself a pacifist, but you only start drooling at times like this. Shameless bastard.”
“What did you say?”
“Why? Was any of that wrong?”
“You, wicked human, agreed that I should not participate in the battle! And were you not the one who said the other humans could not find out about me?”
“Quit making excuses. So, are you going to absorb that mana or not?”
*Crack!*
“Hey. You hear me?”
“Hmm. I don’t particularly want to absorb it.”
“...What?”
*Fwoooooosh!*
I was so startled that I nearly let an attack through.
I swept my spear in a wide arc, wiping out a dozen monsters, then asked in all seriousness,
“What’s wrong? Is it time for you to vanish?”
“Hmm... I do not know either. I simply feel that way.”
“You feel that way?”
“Yes. I am undead too. Sometimes even I feel unsettled. Leave me be.”
“...Since when do the undead feel unsettled?”
Normally, he would have charged in like a Beggars’ Sect disciple who had not eaten in four days. Why was he acting like this?
*Can undead go through puberty too?*
Even for an oddball monster like the Skeleton Warlord, that made no sense.
I gave up trying to figure him out and continued cutting down monsters.
That was when it happened.
*Rooooooar!*
Aura—no, Sword Energy—blanketed a radius of more than ten meters.
One person landed lightly at the center of the front line, now suddenly empty.
“There are too many monsters. We can’t clear a path for the entire suicide squad.”
I knew exactly what Lee Jungryong meant.
“You’re saying we should go with a small elite force?”
“Precisely. Duck.”
I bent backward at Lee Jungryong’s warning. A crescent of Sword Energy flew over me and sliced three or four enormous monsters apart like cheesecake.
*What if that Sword Energy had been aimed at me? If Lee Jungryong and I fought...*
“You, me, and Wu Heixing. The three of us should be enough.”
I licked my dry lips before answering.
“That’s a strange thing to say.”
“What is?”
“You never know until you fight. We won’t know how strong the Arch Lich is until we face it.”
“There are three S-rank Hunters here. No matter how powerful the Arch Lich may be, it cannot stand against us.”
It was a wonderful word. So why did I dislike the way it felt rolling off my tongue?
Maybe it was because of the people included in it.
But I had already made up my mind when I proposed the suicide-squad operation. In that sense, Lee Jungryong’s suggestion was the best option.
“Let’s do that. Where’s Wu Heixing?”
*Kra-d-d-d-d-k!*
Before I had even finished speaking, Wu Heixing tore his way through the monsters and appeared.

Unlike Lee Jungryong, who remained so immaculate that it was hard to believe he was in the middle of a battle, Wu Heixing looked terrible. But the fierce light in his eyes proved he still had plenty of strength left.
“Good. You made it in time.”
Wu Heixing let out a ragged breath. “Mere monsters could never stop me.”
*Didn’t that bastard nearly die to those same mere monsters about an hour ago?*
I was inwardly clicking my tongue at how little Wu Heixing had changed when a shout came from far away.
“Mr. Jin!”
It was Team Leader Choi.
Beyond the hundreds of monsters between us, his face briefly appeared before vanishing again.
Then something gleaming spun through the air and embedded itself in the ground nearby.
*This is...*
I recognized it immediately.
It was **Hero’s Soul**.
From somewhere beyond my sight, Team Leader Choi shouted,
“I’m not going to say I’ll go with you, so take that sword with you instead. And... be careful!”
Those words carried a great deal of meaning.
Without a word, I pulled **Hero’s Soul** from the ground.
Beyond the countless monsters still filling my vision, I could see a city shrouded in darkness.
“Let’s go.”
Lee Jungryong smiled gently.

The monster army, tens of thousands strong, ignored it all and charged.
Cut down dozens, and dozens more filled their places.
Cut down hundreds, and hundreds more took their place.
Charging through the thick fog, they were stronger and more ferocious than ordinary monsters.
All that remained was an unavoidable head-on battle.
Facing the oncoming monster army, two men stepped forward at the same time.
“Ares Guild.
Formation B.
Break through them.”
*Clatter-clatter-clatter!*
At Lee Jungryong’s quiet command, the elite Guild members who had made it this far without a single casualty moved as one.
Jin Taekyung studied them closely, then addressed the suicide squad he had brought from the Western Front.
“Everyone, Formation J.”
“Yes, sir!”
“Formation J!
Get into position!”
The suicide squad moved swiftly, repeating the command in thunderous voices.
Behind Jin Taekyung, Wu Heixing had been gathering the handful of Red Guard Gang Hunters who remained.
He grabbed one of the Western Front suicide-squad members and asked,
“Hey, rookie.
What the hell is Formation J?”
Recognizing Wu Heixing, Xiao Shen frowned before answering.
“Hyung came up with the formation himself.”
“So what does it mean?”
“Nothing special.
He said it means, ‘Just fucking fight.’”
Wu Heixing was momentarily speechless, and Lee Jungryong and Jin Taekyung launched themselves forward at the exact same time, as if they had planned it.
Prince Felix and ten thousand Hunters surged fiercely after them.
“Aaaaaaaaah!”
—Kraaaaaaaargh!
Humans and monsters.
Monsters and humans.
Deafening battle cries and killing intent erupted.
Racing across the wasteland at blinding speed, the two sides bared their teeth and leveled their spears and blades at one another.
*Fwoooooosh—Kra-d-d-d-d-k!*
The great battle had begun.
I leaned back and put my shoulder into it.
The movements flowed seamlessly together as I whipped my arm forward with all my strength.
*Whoosh—thud-thud-thud-thud!*
White Flame shot from my hand, piercing dozens of monsters and opening a path.
A gap appeared in an instant.
Without hesitation, I plunged into it and lashed out with my arms and legs at everything within reach.
*Crack!*
My fist shot forward too fast to see, crushing the head of the charging Lycanthrope like a watermelon.
Before the brain matter spilling from its skull could hit the ground, I leaped into the air.
*Tap—whoosh!*
A four-meter-tall figure loomed before me.
My reflection appeared in its pale pupils, long since drained of light.
But before the Undead Troll could swing its club, my palm slammed into its chest.
*Boom!*
Smoke curled from the Undead Troll’s seven apertures along with a surge of tremendous heat.
Its insides had suffered catastrophic damage, and it met its final death before its extraordinary regenerative power could even come into play.
“Wicked human!
Behind you!”
*I know, idiot.
Who asked for your advice?*
I turned my head.
A lance wreathed in pitch-black magic grazed my neck and hurtled into the sky.
It had been thrown to catch me while I was suspended in midair.
The timing was good, but the enemy had made one mistake.
It had underestimated me.
“Fuck.
Why are there so many Death Knights?
What is this, a chicken joint?”
I landed lightly after evading the lance, and a Death Knight mounted on a skeletal horse charged straight at me.
“This.
Is.
As.
Far.
As.
You.
Go!”
*Fwoooooosh!*
With that shout, it swung a sword wreathed in ominous magic.
The energy it gave off could not compare to an S-rank Hunter’s, but it was on par with that of a top-tier A-rank Hunter.
Or perhaps...
*This Death Knight must have been a Hunter once too.*
Maybe that was why.
The sight of the Death Knight reminded me of Lei Fei, leaving a sudden bitter taste in my mouth.
The Skeleton Warlord screamed when it saw my reaction.
“Dodge, human!”
*Thud!*
The magic clinging to the Death Knight’s sword vanished without a trace.
The Death Knight stared blankly at the transparent spearhead that had pierced through its chest and emerged from its back.
Then it muttered weakly,
“This is as far as you go.”
I returned the Death Knight’s own words to it and brought down the edge of my hand.
“I don’t know who you used to be, but you’ve suffered enough.”
*Slash—thud!*
The skeletal horse and Death Knight split in two and vanished.
As before, I used Seizing an Object Through Empty Space to draw White Flame back toward me, cutting down a monster along the way.
Then I abruptly asked,
“How come you’re not pestering me for food today?”
“Ahem.
What do you take me for?
How dare you mistake this commander for—”
*Slash!*
“A freeloader.
You call yourself a pacifist, but you only start drooling at times like this.
Shameless bastard.”
“What did you say?”
“Why?
Was any of that wrong?”
“You, wicked human, agreed that I should not participate in the battle!
And were you not the one who said the other humans could not find out about me?”
“Quit making excuses.
So, are you going to absorb that mana or not?”
*Crack!*
“Hey.
You hear me?”
“Hmm.
I don’t particularly want to absorb it.”
“...What?”
*Fwoooooosh!*
I was so startled that I nearly let an attack through.
I swept my spear in a wide arc, wiping out a dozen monsters, then asked in all seriousness,
“What’s wrong?
Is it time for you to vanish?”
“Hmm...
I do not know either.
I simply feel that way.”
“You feel that way?”
“Yes.
I am undead too.
Sometimes even I feel unsettled.
Leave me be.”
“...Since when do the undead feel unsettled?”
Normally, he would have charged in like a Beggars’ Sect disciple who had not eaten in four days.
Why was he acting like this?
*Can undead go through puberty too?*
Even for an oddball monster like the Skeleton Warlord, that made no sense.
I gave up trying to figure him out and continued cutting down monsters.
That was when it happened.
*Rooooooar!*
Aura—no, Sword Energy—blanketed a radius of more than ten meters.
One person landed lightly at the center of the front line, now suddenly empty.
“There are too many monsters.
We can’t clear a path for the entire suicide squad.”
I knew exactly what Lee Jungryong meant.
“You’re saying we should go with a small elite force?”
“Precisely.
Duck.”
I bent backward at Lee Jungryong’s warning.
A crescent of Sword Energy flew over me and sliced three or four enormous monsters apart like cheesecake.
*What if that Sword Energy had been aimed at me?
If Lee Jungryong and I fought...*
“You, me, and Wu Heixing.
The three of us should be enough.”
I licked my dry lips before answering.
“That’s a strange thing to say.”
“What is?”
“You never know until you fight.
We won’t know how strong the Arch Lich is until we face it.”
“There are three S-rank Hunters here.
No matter how powerful the Arch Lich may be, it cannot stand against us.”
It was a wonderful word.
So why did I dislike the way it felt rolling off my tongue?
Maybe it was because of the people included in it.
But I had already made up my mind when I proposed the suicide-squad operation.
In that sense, Lee Jungryong’s suggestion was the best option.
“Let’s do that.
Where’s Wu Heixing?”
*Kra-d-d-d-d-k!*
Before I had even finished speaking, Wu Heixing tore his way through the monsters and appeared.
Unlike Lee Jungryong, who remained so immaculate that it was hard to believe he was in the middle of a battle, Wu Heixing looked terrible.
But the fierce light in his eyes proved he still had plenty of strength left.
“Good.
You made it in time.”
Wu Heixing let out a ragged breath.
“Mere monsters could never stop me.”
*Didn’t that bastard nearly die to those same mere monsters about an hour ago?*
I was inwardly clicking my tongue at how little Wu Heixing had changed when a shout came from far away.
“Mr.
Jin!”
It was Team Leader Choi.
Beyond the hundreds of monsters between us, his face briefly appeared before vanishing again.
Then something gleaming spun through the air and embedded itself in the ground nearby.
*This is...*
I recognized it immediately.
It was **Hero’s Soul**.
From somewhere beyond my sight, Team Leader Choi shouted,
“I’m not going to say I’ll go with you, so take that sword with you instead.
And... be careful!”
Those words carried a great deal of meaning.
Without a word, I pulled **Hero’s Soul** from the ground.
Beyond the countless monsters still filling my vision, I could see a city shrouded in darkness.
“Let’s go.”
Lee Jungryong smiled gently.

paragraphs: Breaking through a fierce battlefield where an army numbering in the tens of thousands was locked in combat was nearly impossible.
But...
“Rage, Blizzard!”
“Johnson, aren’t you pushing yourself too hard? If you keep this up, I can’t just stand by either.”
If the war hero of the Great Cataclysm and the world’s greatest War Mage and archer unleashed devastating area-of-effect magic and arrows like bolts of lightning...
“For Her Majesty the Queen!”
“Long live the Queen!”
If an S-rank Hunter who had appeared like a comet—the prince of the United Kingdom—led the kingdom’s elite royal knights into a charge...
“Formation J! Wipe them all out!”
“Just fucking fight!”
“Yeeeeeeah! Let’s gooo!!!”
And if the hundreds of suicide squad members who had come this far prepared to make the ultimate sacrifice advanced as one...
*Roooooar!*
*Crack-crack! Slash!*
A path opened.
A path meant for only three people.
It was the final path to ending this war, and they crossed through tens of thousands of monsters like a streak of light.
*Shraaaaaaash!*
A dazzling storm of light erupted from two swords and a single spear, sweeping through the monsters.
The head of a Lycanthrope baring its sharp fangs shot into the air, while the limbs of a six-meter-tall boss monster, a Twin-Headed Ogre, were torn from its body.
Five Death Knights, each commanding a legion, appeared to block their way, but it made no difference.
—In. The. Name. Of. Our. Lord.
—Let. Death. Descend.
Jin Taekyung tossed out a casual remark.
“Two, two, one. Sound good?”
Lee Jungryong nodded.
“Let’s do that.”
“Wait. What the—!”
Before Wu Heixing could finish objecting, the other two had already dashed forward.
They closed the distance in only two steps, then swung their sword and spear without hesitation.
*Boom!*
The first exchange. The Death Knight staggered after blocking the whip-like arc of Force.
Its eyes widened as its magic-infused sword shattered into pieces.
*Boom! Crunch!*
The second exchange. The third. And then—
*Slash!*
A single lightning-fast strike that signaled the end.
The upper half of the Death Knight’s body, armor and all, slowly slid away. Beneath its low-pulled helmet, the light in its eyes flickered like a candle in the wind, then vanished.
Before the bodies of the Death Knights they had each taken responsibility for even touched the ground, Jin Taekyung and Lee Jungryong were already charging toward another enemy.
“Damn it! I’m here too!”
Wu Heixing joined them a moment later.
The fate of the three remaining Death Knights was as good as sealed.
The monsters that witnessed their commanders’ destruction instinctively recoiled in fear.
*More. More. More.*
*Slash! Shraaaaaash!*
Jin Taekyung cut and smashed his way through everything around him as he advanced. Then, at some point, he realized it.
*They’re gone.*
The monsters that had endlessly blocked their path were nowhere to be seen. Only a ruined road and vast plains stretching out on either side remained.
At the end of the road, a city shrouded in thick fog awaited them.
Lee Jungryong, Wu Heixing, and I raced toward the city where the Arch Lich was.
—Wicked human. This commander has a long-held wish.
*What is it?*
—To return to my homeland and enjoy a peaceful life.
*You don’t even remember where your homeland is.*
—...How could you say something so cruel?
*Ah, sorry. I didn’t mean it like that. So where is your homeland?*
—The first place where I regained consciousness. Korea. I have decided to make it the homeland of my heart.
I faltered as I ran toward the city.
*Is he insane?*

A monster trying to obtain citizenship. An undead illegal immigrant who had slipped into the country through a Gate, yet he had no shortage of things to say. His reasons for going this far were obvious, of course.
—So please, let’s turn back.
*I don’t want to.*
—My head has felt dizzy and my stomach has been churning for a while now.
*That’s strange. The more I talk to you, the more I think I’m developing similar symptoms.*
—It isn’t too late yet! Please stop! If we go in there, there really will be no turning back!
*No.*
*It’s already too late.*
I muttered the words inwardly and took another step.
As we entered the city, the first things to greet us were the ominously thick fog and frigid air.
At the same time, a familiar energy I had felt countless times before—yet somehow different—brushed across my entire body.
“This is...”
Sticky and unpleasant. It did not take me long to realize what the energy was, and Lee Jungryong and Wu Heixing reached the same conclusion.
“Mr. Lee...”
“Yes. I see.”
Lee Jungryong swept his surroundings with a somber gaze, then spoke.
“It’s a Gate. I wondered where so many monsters were pouring out from. Now we know why.”
Lee Jungryong’s guess was wrong.
Or rather, it would be more accurate to say he was half right.
I gave a small shake of my head and corrected him.
“I don’t think the Gate transformation is complete yet.”
Wu Heixing swallowed hard.
“How do you know that?”
“Just a feeling.”
“What?”
“If you don’t believe me, never mind.”
“...What kind of person says something like that?”
As expected, Wu Heixing looked dumbfounded. Lee Jungryong, however, reacted differently.
His gaze held a clear mixture of suspicion and surprise.
“How did you know?”
“You already knew?”
“I only just realized it. I felt this same sensation a very long time ago, in North America during the Great Cataclysm.”
“I see.”
“But this phenomenon hasn’t occurred even once since the Great Cataclysm. How did you know?”
“As I said, it’s just a feeling. I had a hunch.”
“A hunch...”
Lee Jungryong studied me with an unreadable expression after my firm answer.
But that was all I could say. Even if I told him the truth, he would not be able to understand it anyway.
*It’s not as if I can show him the System window.*
I raised my head and glanced at the empty air. A System message had appeared before my eyes the instant we entered the city.
*Ding.*

**System** You have entered a ???-Grade Gate, **City Consumed by Darkness**! You have infiltrated the stronghold of the **Arch Lich**! The city, consumed by mana, is already transforming into one enormous Gate. Defeat the Arch Lich, the source of everything, to stop the city’s transformation and prevent the catastrophe that will follow. Quest **One Who Returned from Death** has been created! You cannot use the **Login** function until the Quest ends!
*Gate transformation.*
It was a phenomenon from the past that I had only ever read about in textbooks.
Lee Jungryong gazed beyond the thick fog and spoke.
“Gate transformations were rare even during the Great Cataclysm. For one to occur, an extremely powerful monster must serve as its core and put down roots with its mana.”
There was no need to wonder which extremely powerful monster that might be.
I blurted out its name.
“The Arch Lich.”
“Yes. It has to be the Arch Lich. It must be contaminating the city with mana and turning it into one enormous Gate. That must also be why it has not appeared on the battlefield until now.”
Nearly two hundred thousand monsters had appeared on the battlefield so far.
That alone was a catastrophe of staggering proportions. But if the Gate transformation were completed...
*We’re finished.*
Humanity would undoubtedly emerge victorious in the end, but countless cities would be destroyed, and hundreds of thousands—no, perhaps millions—of people would die.
We had to stop it before it was too late.
“We don’t have much time. We need to hurry.”
Lee Jungryong nodded.
“We should avoid the monsters whenever possible. We’ll need to conserve every bit of strength we can before facing the Arch Lich. Mr. Wu, that includes you.”
We began moving through the thick fog.
Unlike the small city where I had fought Lei Fei last time, this place—the Arch Lich’s stronghold—covered more than ten times the area and still bore traces of having once been a bustling city.
A forest of collapsed skyscrapers. A downtown district that must once have been the most dazzling part of the city, now reduced to desolation...
We moved as quickly and quietly as possible.
After traveling for some time with our senses stretched to their limits, Lee Jungryong, who had been leading the group, suddenly spoke.
“Did you know?”
“If you put it like that, of course I don’t. And this doesn’t seem like a particularly good time to play Twenty Questions.”
Lee Jungryong let out a low laugh at my immediate reply.
“These days, I find myself thinking about you more than usual.”
“Are you confessing your feelings to me? This is a bad time for that too.”
“In a sense, perhaps I am. How should I put it? I find myself thinking that you will surpass me someday.”
“You don’t need to worry about that. Even in ten years, I won’t come close to catching up with you, Vice Guild Master.”
“Haha. Do you really think so?”
“No. I just said it because I thought you’d like to hear it.”
“You’re as honest as ever. Just like when I first met you.”
“That first blind date did have a pretty terrible atmosphere.”
My memory was not particularly good, but I could still vividly remember my first meeting with him.
Lee Jungryong seemed to remember it just as clearly.
“We got off to an ill-fated start. The more I think about it, the more regrettable it seems.”
“Tell me about it. If we had talked things out from the start instead of cutting off someone’s arm, we might have begun on relatively friendly terms.”
“Park Jihoon made a mistake in the heat of the moment. I apologize.”
“How could that have been the Disciple’s fault alone?”
“Heh. I see. Then it was also my fault for failing to teach him properly.”
I watched Lee Jungryong’s back as he moved ahead of us. He leaped between buildings with swift, elusive movements, and I wondered what expression he was wearing now.
Lee Jungryong let out another quiet laugh and continued.
“You seem to have grown quite close to Minwoo.”
“We’re reasonably friendly.”
“You two seem to get along surprisingly well.”
“He pays me a lot.”
“A business relationship. That’s good to hear. Then do you think I could become close to you as well?”
I answered with a snort of laughter.

“Was it about seven years ago? I had a red-bean bun as a snack at the Hunter Training Center, and it tasted so good I cried. But when I tried one after getting out into the real world, it wasn’t that great. I haven’t really eaten them since.”
“So now you’ve had your fill?”
“I’ve already earned enough for several generations to live without working. My stomach is full, so what’s the point of forcing down more? I’ll just burst and die.”
“You’re wrong. Humans are always hungry creatures. No matter how much they stuff themselves, they never know satisfaction. Do you know why?”
“Hmm. Do you happen to have a binge-eating disorder?”
Lee Jungryong continued in a gentle voice.
“Greed. More money, more honor, or the opposite sex. We constantly desire and crave more.”
“Like you, Vice Guild Master?”
“That’s right. Like me.”
Lee Jungryong laughed aloud. His booming laughter spread through the thick fog, but he did not seem concerned in the slightest.
“They say laughter brings good fortune, but in this case, don’t you think it might bring monsters instead?”
“There aren’t any monsters in this area. You know that too, don’t you?”
“Well, I’m just saying we should be a little more careful.”
*Whoooooosh!*
A foul-smelling wind brushed across my entire body.
From one building to the next, we continued running, leaping across gaps more than twenty meters wide.
We sensed no sign of monsters, and the buildings around us gradually grew fewer.
“Let’s slow down from here.”
“It’s dark. And narrow.”
“Bear with it a little longer. More importantly, may I ask you one more thing?”
“Anything.”
“What did Minwoo say about this operation?”
“He didn’t say much...”
I looked between Lee Jungryong and Wu Heixing before continuing slowly.
“He told me not to go because it was dangerous.”
“More precisely?”
“Don’t go with people you can’t trust. Something like that.”
The smile on Lee Jungryong’s lips deepened.
“Do you suspect me and that fellow too?”
*No.*
“Then?”
“If anything...”
I smiled as I continued.
“If anything, I’m certain.”
“Certain?”
“Yes.”
Still smiling, I went on.
“I’m certain these fucking bastards are more interested in the back of my head than the Arch Lich.”
Lee Jungryong stopped dead.

A downtown district that must once have been the most dazzling part of the city, now reduced to desolation...
We moved as quickly and quietly as possible.
After traveling for some time with our senses stretched to their limits, Lee Jungryong, who had been leading the group, suddenly spoke.
“Did you know?”
“If you put it like that, of course I don’t.
And this doesn’t seem like a particularly good time to play Twenty Questions.”
Lee Jungryong let out a low laugh at my immediate reply.
“These days, I find myself thinking about you more than usual.”
“Are you confessing your feelings to me?
This is a bad time for that too.”
“In a sense, perhaps I am.
How should I put it?
I find myself thinking that you will surpass me someday.”
“You don’t need to worry about that.
Even in ten years, I won’t come close to catching up with you, Vice Guild Master.”
“Haha.
Do you really think so?”
“No.
I just said it because I thought you’d like to hear it.”
“You’re as honest as ever.
Just like when I first met you.”
“That first blind date did have a pretty terrible atmosphere.”
My memory was not particularly good, but I could still vividly remember my first meeting with him.
Lee Jungryong seemed to remember it just as clearly.
“We got off to an ill-fated start.
The more I think about it, the more regrettable it seems.”
“Tell me about it.
If we had talked things out from the start instead of cutting off someone’s arm, we might have begun on relatively friendly terms.”
“Park Jihoon made a mistake in the heat of the moment.
I apologize.”
“How could that have been the Disciple’s fault alone?”
“Heh.
I see.
Then it was also my fault for failing to teach him properly.”
I watched Lee Jungryong’s back as he moved ahead of us.
He leaped between buildings with swift, elusive movements, and I wondered what expression he was wearing now.
Lee Jungryong let out another quiet laugh and continued.
“You seem to have grown quite close to Minwoo.”
“We’re reasonably friendly.”
“You two seem to get along surprisingly well.”
“He pays me a lot.”
“A business relationship.
That’s good to hear.
Then do you think I could become close to you as well?”
I answered with a snort of laughter.
“Was it about seven years ago?
I had a red-bean bun as a snack at the Hunter Training Center, and it tasted so good I cried.
But when I tried one after getting out into the real world, it wasn’t that great.
I haven’t really eaten them since.”
“So now you’ve had your fill?”
“I’ve already earned enough for several generations to live without working.
My stomach is full, so what’s the point of forcing down more?
I’ll just burst and die.”
“You’re wrong.
Humans are always hungry creatures.
No matter how much they stuff themselves, they never know satisfaction.
Do you know why?”
“Hmm.
Do you happen to have a binge-eating disorder?”
Lee Jungryong continued in a gentle voice.
“Greed.
More money, more honor, or the opposite sex.
We constantly desire and crave more.”
“Like you, Vice Guild Master?”
“That’s right.
Like me.”
Lee Jungryong laughed aloud.
His booming laughter spread through the thick fog, but he did not seem concerned in the slightest.
“They say laughter brings good fortune, but in this case, don’t you think it might bring monsters instead?”
“There aren’t any monsters in this area.
You know that too, don’t you?”
“Well, I’m just saying we should be a little more careful.”
*Whoooooosh!*
A foul-smelling wind brushed across my entire body.
From one building to the next, we continued running, leaping across gaps more than twenty meters wide.
We sensed no sign of monsters, and the buildings around us gradually grew fewer.
“Let’s slow down from here.”
“It’s dark.
And narrow.”
“Bear with it a little longer.
More importantly, may I ask you one more thing?”
“Anything.”
“What did Minwoo say about this operation?”
“He didn’t say much...”
I looked between Lee Jungryong and Wu Heixing before continuing slowly.
“He told me not to go because it was dangerous.”
“More precisely?”
“Don’t go with people you can’t trust.
Something like that.”
The smile on Lee Jungryong’s lips deepened.
“Do you suspect me and that fellow too?”
*No.*
“Then?”
“If anything...”
I smiled as I continued.
“If anything, I’m certain.”
“Certain?”
“Yes.”
Still smiling, I went on.
“I’m certain these fucking bastards are more interested in the back of my head than the Arch Lich.”
Lee Jungryong stopped dead.

paragraphs: I knew. I had simply been waiting.
Waiting for the moment they sank their fangs into me.
“More than that... I’m certain.”
“Certain?”
“Yes.”
The corners of my mouth rose before I could stop them. I finally let out the words I had swallowed time and time again.
“I’m certain these fucking bastards are more interested in the back of my head than the Arch Lich. That’s what I’m certain of.”
The brief masquerade came to an end.
*Step.*
Lee Jungryong stopped walking.
*Fwish!*
The sound of displaced air came from behind me. Three streaks of wind tore toward vital points across my body.
I didn’t need to turn around to know where Wu Heixing’s daggers were headed.
Or what I needed to do.
*Fwish-fwish-fwish!*
The three daggers aimed at my nape, spine, and right arm missed their targets and pierced empty air.
*No. That’s not it.*
Maybe it was because I had pushed my senses to their absolute limit.
Everything moved slowly, each detail crystal clear.
I reached out and caught the hilt of the dagger skimming past my right arm. At the same time, I twisted at the waist and whipped my arm forward like lightning.
*Shraaaaaaaaaash!*
“Hup!”
Wu Heixing, who had been charging toward me, hurriedly swung his sword.
*Boom!*
Along with a muffled, thunderous roar, his body was knocked backward. A low voice stopped Wu Heixing as he prepared to charge again, his face twisted in anger.
“Enough.”
“Mr. Lee. Why...?”
“He’s not someone you can handle. Wait a moment.”
After restraining Wu Heixing, Lee Jungryong gazed at me calmly.
“You’re remarkably perceptive.”
I let out a quiet laugh at his sudden change in tone.
“An old man who knows everything is saying something obvious. If I didn’t have even this much sense, I’d have died a long time ago.”
“When did you know?”
I answered without hesitation.
“The moment we first met.”
The day I stormed into Myeongdong Guild alone, Lee Jungryong and I had already become irreconcilable enemies.
It had been decided the moment that bastard Park Jihoon sent a Black Hunter to cut off Uncle Kkeokjeong’s arms.
“If you’re about to tell me that was merely your subordinates being overzealous, roll up that white-coated tongue of yours and shove it back in your mouth.”
“Of course not. I merely find it regrettable.”
“What do you regret? Your future spent smelling funeral incense from behind a folding screen?”
Lee Jungryong shook his head.
“No. I had taken quite a liking to you.”
“Then you shouldn’t have cut off my man’s arms.”
“It was a light warning. I wanted to teach that boy Choi Minwoo a lesson. At the time, a brat named Jin Taekyung wasn’t someone I needed to take seriously.”
“And now?”
Lee Jungryong answered with a gentle smile.
“I came here myself. Is that answer enough?”
“More than enough.”
I leaned my back against a pile of collapsed concrete, holding White Flame at an angle.
Wu Heixing stood to my left and Lee Jungryong to my right. Each was a little over ten meters away, but any of us could erase that distance in the blink of an eye.
“But this is unexpected. I thought you’d at least wait until after we killed the Arch Lich before making your move.”
“Pfft! You stupid bangzi!”
Wu Heixing abruptly cut in with a snicker.
Only a few days ago, he hadn’t even been able to meet my eyes. Now he declared triumphantly,
“Fighting the Arch Lich is your job, Jin Taekyung.”
“What kind of bullshit... Ah.”
A thought flashed through my mind, and a hollow laugh escaped me.
I had wondered if it could really be true, but they had actually gone that far.
Their brains were wired completely differently from mine.
“Hah. These fuckers really thought of everything. This is beyond anything I imagined.”
“Do you understand now? Do you understand what kind of situation you’re in?”
“So... you never intended to fight the Arch Lich in the first place?”
Wu Heixing curled his lips and spoke.
“Why should I—why should I take that kind of risk?”
“Today’s battle will go down as a defeat. And your name will be written at the very top of the list of the war dead. I’ve already decided on your epitaph.”
Wu Heixing spread his arms like a stage actor.
“Bangzi from Korea, killed by the Arch Lich. What do you think? Isn’t that a fine epitaph?”
Even after Wu Heixing finished speaking, I could not find anything to say for a while. I stood there blankly, like a madman, and the goose bumps covering my body refused to fade.
Was it because of his scheme?
No.
One question Wu Heixing had thrown back at me continued to circle through my empty mind.
*Why should I take that kind of risk?*
I felt completely blindsided.
At the same time, countless deaths I had witnessed over the past month flashed before my eyes, along with horribly mutilated bodies.
Young parents who had met their end while holding their precious child tightly, hoping against hope that their little one might survive.
An elderly person too infirm to flee, torn apart and eaten.
A pregnant woman who had died clutching her full-term belly.
And...
*The day I became a Hunter, I swore that I would fight monsters until the moment my life ended. That oath still stands.*
Lei Fei, who had fulfilled his mission until the very last moment.
The five hundred Public Security Armed Forces Department Hunters who defied death and launched their heroic charge.
Team Leader Choi and Xiao Shen, who had prepared to die and bound their hands to their sword hilts with strips of cloth so they could kill one more monster.
*You’re right. Why did all of them take such risks? Like fucking idiots.*
Their faces flashed before my eyes, one after another.
My insides burned as though I had swallowed a fireball, and a hot breath escaped me.
I drew a deep breath, then looked at one man.
“Tell me.”
“What should I tell you?”
“Whether you think the same way as that bastard.”
“I don’t. Not at all. That fellow is afraid of the Arch Lich, but...”
Lee Jungryong continued gently.
“I seized an opportunity. The longer this war lasts, the more I stand to gain.”
After a brief silence, I gave a small nod.
“I see.”
I pushed away from the concrete. Scorching Yang Qi boiled like lava, surging through every limb and bone and hundreds of acupoints. Blue flames danced along White Flame’s spearhead.
“Let me ask you one thing too.”
“Anything.”
“‘The only good chink is a dead chink. Fucking Lee Jungryong.’ Those are the epitaphs I just came up with for you two. Do you like them?”
Wu Heixing’s face crumpled, while Lee Jungryong’s eyes curved like crescent moons.
Then—
*Fwoooooosh!*
Blinding flashes burst from both sides.
Lee Jungryong had already made up his mind.
*I must not let my guard down. I’ll kill him by any means necessary.*
A lion gives its all even when hunting a rabbit.
All the more so when its prey was a wolf named Jin Taekyung. To hunt him, the lion would have to use every ounce of its strength.
No matter how much of a lion Lee Jungryong was, he couldn’t afford to ignore the wolf’s fangs.
*Fwish!*
One step.
In a split second, Lee Jungryong closed the distance of more than ten meters, and his hand blurred.
A longsword flashed from its scabbard and shot forward in a dazzling streak of light.
Straight at one man—Jin Taekyung.
*Fwoooooosh!*
It was a full-power strike, the likes of which Lee Jungryong had not unleashed anywhere else in this war.
Wu Heixing had joined the attack as well.
Compared to Jin Taekyung, he was a fledgling far behind in ability, but he was still an S-rank Hunter capable of wielding an Aura Blade.
“Dieeeee!”
As Wu Heixing screamed, his eyes bloodshot, Lee Jungryong saw it clearly.
Jin Taekyung’s smooth, gliding movement.
The spearhead wreathed in blue flames.
*Boom!*
Two swords and one spear collided.
An immense wave of qi erupted with a thunderous roar, collapsing buildings and pulverizing concrete.
*Rumble! Rumble-rumble-rumble!*
It looked as though the city had been bombarded.
The ground caved in, and a tremendous tremor swept across a radius of several hundred meters.
But this was only the beginning.
*Fwish-fwish-fwish-fwish!*
Dozens, then hundreds of lines slashed through the air.
Lee Jungryong’s sword moved too quickly for the eye to follow, carving Jin Taekyung to pieces.
Or so he had believed.
Until Jin Taekyung slammed a flame-wreathed palm into Wu Heixing’s chest and sent him flying, then brought down his spear.
*Fwoosh—whoooooosh!*
Blistering heat blazed up, burning the air itself.
The spearhead devoured both the thick fog blanketing the city and the humidity in the air as it came down diagonally at Lee Jungryong with ferocious momentum.
It was like the claw of a dragon striking down from the heavens.
*What is this...?*
Lee Jungryong frowned.
Jin Taekyung’s spearhead was rushing toward him, erasing the Aura he had scattered.
The tremendous heat stole his breath and made his body seize up.
The young man before him, not yet thirty, was no longer the Jin Taekyung he had known.
*How did he improve this much in such a short time...?*
But although Jin Taekyung’s strength far exceeded his expectations, Lee Jungryong was also a superhuman who stood above other S-rank Hunters.
In that split second, he laid his blade across the spearhead’s path.
*Kwaaaaaaaaaang!*
Jin Taekyung’s spear was faster and stronger than Lee Jungryong had expected.
But the same was true of Lee Jungryong.
*Swing—fwish-fwish-fwish-fwish!*
Within a moment sliced into ever smaller fractions, spear and sword tangled and collided.
Lightning-like flashes and thunderous roars erupted without pause.
*Clack-clack-clack!*
Jin Taekyung pressed Lee Jungryong’s sword down with his spearhead, then thrust out his hand.
Just before a palm strike carrying the heat of the Flame Divine Palm could slam into Lee Jungryong’s chest, Lee Jungryong’s fist shot forward like lightning and met Jin Taekyung’s palm.
*Boom!*
With the sound of compressed air bursting apart, the two men stepped backward as though they had planned it.
The result left Lee Jungryong stunned.
He had retreated two steps.
Jin Taekyung had retreated only one.
*He pushed me back?*
Lee Jungryong had accumulated an enormous amount of qi over many years.
Yet a brat barely in his late twenties had forced him backward.
It was impossible to believe that such a change had occurred in the short span of just over a month.
*And that isn’t all.*
His incredible power and speed seemed to have no bottom. His movements, too—everything about him was astonishing. Beyond anything that could be put into words.
Just as he was now.
*Whoooooosh! Fwish!*
Lee Jungryong twisted his head aside.
The spearhead missed him by half a handspan, then changed direction in midair.
*Slash!*
A searing sensation, followed by droplets of blood scattering through the air.
For the first time in a very long while, Lee Jungryong felt pain.
He swung his sword.
*Boom!*
Their weapons crashed together.
Through the transparent spearhead, Lee Jungryong saw the young man’s blazing eyes.
The lips that had remained tightly sealed throughout the battle finally parted, and a cold, level voice emerged.
“You’re fucked.”
The moment Lee Jungryong heard those chilling words, he realized he needed to revise his earlier assessment.
*A lion.*
He had been wrong.
Jin Taekyung was not a wolf.
He was a lion—a powerful young male who might drive out the old lion that had ruled the pride for so long and become its new king.
*Craaaaaack! Boom!*
The old lion was hurled away by an irresistible force.
Lee Jungryong flipped in midair and landed on the ground.
The first thing he saw was the young male lion gripping Wu Heixing by the throat after Wu had attempted a surprise attack.
“Guhk! M-my father belongs to the Crown Prince Party...!”
“I don’t care.”
“If you let me live, I’ll repay you! Guh! So please...”
“Me? Let you live after you tried to kill me?”
A reddish gaze turned toward Wu Heixing.
Then a sentence Lee Jungryong had heard somewhere before slipped from Jin Taekyung’s lips.
“Why should I—why should I take that kind of risk?”
*Crunch!*

A reddish gaze turned toward Wu Heixing.
Then a sentence Lee Jungryong had heard somewhere before slipped from Jin Taekyung’s lips.
“Why should I—why should I take that kind of risk?”
*Crunch!*
