paragraphs: Sometimes, when I took someone’s life—when I faced the desperate voices and pleading eyes of enemies begging to be spared—I found myself wondering.
*Why? Why on earth?*
Why didn’t they stop to think about what they themselves had done? Why did they always look to others for the cause of everything that befell them?
*Too late.*
If you tried to kill someone, you had to consider the possibility that you might be killed instead.
The seeds had already been sown. At last, it was time to reap the harvest.
I stared into Wu Heixing’s bloodshot eyes and whispered,
“Why should I take that kind of risk?”
I hadn’t asked because I wanted an answer.
There was nothing more to hear or see. Without hesitation, I grabbed Wu Heixing by the neck and twisted.
*Crunch.*
Flesh was crushed and bones splintered beneath a grip strong enough to tear steel like paper.
The last light faded from his wide, frozen eyes.
The instant his struggling body went limp, a System notification rang out.
**System Defeated **Lv. 135 Wu Heixing**! - Gained a substantial amount of **EXP**! - Gained no **Fame**. If it becomes known that you killed this person, significant repercussions are expected!
That was when Lee Jungryong rose to his feet more than twenty meters away and spoke.
“Not even a moment’s hesitation.”
I tossed Wu Heixing’s lifeless body aside.
“He needed to die.”
“Do you know who that boy’s father is?”
“I’ve heard of him. Apparently, he was one of the men who took a sledgehammer to Confucius’s tomb decades ago.”
“And that young Red Guard grew up to become the most powerful man in Chinese politics and the leader of the Crown Prince Party. Even Chairman Xiao Yang does not dare touch him.”
“Damn. What a fucking amazing continent. In our country, that’d be like the arsonist who burned down Sungnyemun becoming President. Don’t you think?”
“There is no need to understand it. But there is one fact you must know. With your own hands, you killed the only son that the most powerful man among one billion people had after turning fifty.”
“Me? No, I didn’t.”
I smiled shamelessly.
“Wu Heixing died after a fierce battle with the Arch Lich.”
“I told you, I already picked out his epitaph. *Here lies a bad chink who became a good Chinese man.* Of course, your gravestone will be right beside his.”
Lee Jungryong stared at me with an inscrutable expression, then let out a quiet laugh.
“You’re a crafty one.”
“I liked the scenario you two came up with. Let me borrow it.”
“Do as you please. It will not go the way you wish regardless.”
“Maybe...”
I gestured toward Wu Heixing’s sprawled corpse with my chin.
“So far, things seem to have gone more or less my way.”
“Yes. In that respect, you and I are alike.”
“What?”
As I frowned, Lee Jungryong gave me a faint smile.
“Wu Heixing was easily swayed and loose-lipped. A terrible man to conspire with, but even someone like him had his uses.”
“...What the fuck are you talking about?”
“This is what I mean.”
Lee Jungryong pressed something in his hand. A beam pierced the thick fog and struck a chunk of concrete, projecting a hologram above it.
The short video, barely ten seconds long, showed Wu Heixing begging for his life—and me breaking his neck without a moment’s hesitation.
“Huh.”
I let out a hollow laugh.
“Nice image quality. Perfect for giving people the wrong idea.”
“Indeed. Especially an old father who has lost his only son, born late in life.”
“Are you planning to show them the unedited version?”
“Perhaps because of the magical power’s influence, an error will probably cause the beginning of the video to be lost.”
“That’s one hell of a coincidence.”

“Anyone who sees it will be appalled. Not only those who delight in tearing others down, but even those who worshipped you will turn against you. And the people you cherish so dearly will slowly crumble beneath the public’s condemnation.”
The Peace Guild.
And Mom and Hayeon.
Their names and faces flashed before my eyes the moment I heard Lee Jungryong’s words.
I stepped forward, planting my foot on Wu Heixing’s corpse.
*Step.*
“Was this your plan from the beginning?”
“Wu Heixing was merely a tool from the start. He could never have been anything more.”
*Step.*
Lee Jungryong began walking toward me as well.
But the qi pouring from his entire body was on a completely different level from anything he had shown before.
That was why Wu Heixing’s death had failed to disturb his composure.
The cunning beast had achieved its objective. Now, at last, it had bared the claws it had kept hidden.
“Damn it. No wonder it seemed so easy.”
Lee Jungryong gave a dry laugh at my complaint.
“I will praise you for one thing. You far exceeded my expectations.”
“Let me ask you one last time. Why are you going this far?”
“Could a young pup like you possibly understand?”
*Step.*
“Were you really that afraid of Team Leader Choi—no, Choi Minwoo?”
“Will you not shut that mouth of yours?”
*Kuwaaaaaaaang!*
A massive wave of qi surged outward, driving back the fog and seizing control of the space around us.
The razor-sharp killing intent made my skin prickle. Anger unlike anything I had ever seen rose in Lee Jungryong’s once-placid eyes.
“I won my place entirely through my own strength. It is my empire, built over the course of my entire life!”
It was anger he had kept buried, an emotion he had not allowed himself to show in a very long time.
Lee Jungryong glared at me with fire blazing in his eyes and ground out each syllable.
“No one can bring it down. Not you, not that boy Minwoo, and... not even my hyung!”
*Hyung?*
I was given no time to question the unexpected word.
*Step.*
A single step rang out, unusually heavy and deep.
At the same time, Lee Jungryong’s form rippled like water.
The beast vanished, leaving behind an afterimage, and appeared right in front of me.
*Fweeeeeeeeng!*
A mass of light filled my vision. I twisted at the waist and swung White Flame.
The instant light and flame collided, a thunderous roar erupted as though the sky itself had split apart.
*Kwaaang!*
The explosion was enormous.

The high-rise building that had barely been holding together collapsed as if it had burst apart, while glass and concrete broke into countless tiny fragments that pierced through everything in every direction.
The impact of the clash could likely be felt from dozens of kilometers away.
Amid the successive collapses and thunderous booms, I thrust out my foot.
*Fwish!*
Beyond the dust cloud splitting apart before me, a man stood poised in midair as though on solid ground.
His clear eyes, always impossible to read, now blazed with fury.
“Jin Taekyung!”
Neither of us waited for the other.
I shattered the ground as I sprang upward, while he stepped on empty air and plunged toward me.
The sword and spear we swung at each other collided dead-on, and an immense shock wave engulfed us both.
Hurled backward at the same instant as though we had planned it, we kicked off the structures of the already-ruined city and shot toward each other again.
*Shweeeeeek—Kwang!*
With a thunderous boom, Lee Jungryong’s sword deflected my spearhead and thrust straight toward my throat.
*Boom!*
I jerked my head aside. Air shrieked past, and severed strands of hair scattered behind me.
But it wasn’t over.
*Shwish-shwish-shwish!*
Lee Jungryong’s sword shot forward as a streak of pure white light.
A net of Force flowed along the blade.
Faced with that spectacle of light filling my vision, I awakened all the internal energy sleeping within my dantian.

Three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi rose like a wildfire and seeped into my four limbs and hundreds of bones. Blue hellfire surged along the transparent spearhead, rippling smoothly like a dragon’s tail.
*Fire Dragon’s Single Tail.*
*Whoooooosh!*
A single swing.
The fire dragon’s tail fanned outward, erasing part of the onrushing net of Force.
Now it was time to tear the loosened net apart with sharpened claws.
*Heavenly Strike.*
The Fire Dragon Divine Spear consisted of only two forms.
And yet the former Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan who created it earned the epithet of the greatest spearman under heaven, leaving behind a brief final testament about his martial arts.
“A martial art I devoted my entire life to, yet failed to complete. Even so, a spear art worthy of being called the greatest under heaven.”
His words were true.
That was the Fire Dragon Divine Spear. A spear art that could proudly call itself the greatest under heaven with only two forms, and...
*Kuwaaaaaang!*
Heavenly Strike, unleashed with all my power, tore through the net of Force and swept across everything ahead of it.
The flames were upon Lee Jungryong before he had any chance to react. Watching them rush toward him, he brought his sword down with a forceful shout.
“Ha!”
*Fwish!*
The flames split at the tip of his sword.
His form shot forward like an arrow through the paths of fire opening to either side, unleashing countless sword strikes.
*Shu-shu-shu-shu-shuk!*
Chest, throat, shoulder, arms, legs...
Within a span of time short enough to be called an instant—
Faced with arcs of swordlight slashing toward me like rays of light, I was suddenly seized by wonder.
*How? How is this possible?*
I was a Hunter. At the same time, I was a martial artist.
No. Perhaps *Player* was the name that suited me best.

On a sweltering summer day, I had picked up a discarded VR capsule at a recycling station and gained a new power called the System. I had become the only person to stand astride both the modern world and Murim.
But still...
*Boom!*
Movements without a single wasted inch, nearly perfect control of power, and even control over qi.
After parrying Lee Jungryong’s attack, I found myself admiring him. It had nothing to do with what kind of person he was. I was simply stunned by his skill.
*So he was this strong.*
After reaching the Supreme Peak realm, I had thought there would not be many people in the modern world capable of matching me.
After coming to Sichuan and meeting several S-rank Hunters, that belief had only grown stronger.
No matter how much energy each of them possessed, martial arts did not exist here.
The so-called Hunters could fight efficiently, but when it came to efficient qi manipulation, they were practically illiterate.
Lee Jungryong? I knew he had learned a cultivation technique called the Mana Cultivation Method in the modern world, but I had assumed it wouldn’t be much different.
Now I realized the truth.
My arrogance had led me to the wrong conclusion.
*Slash!*
My thigh suddenly felt cool. A heartbeat later, pain as hot as fire followed.
But why did my mind clear and my vision sharpen, as though I had just awakened from a long sleep?
*Slash, slash, slash!*
My arm. My calf. The back of my neck.
Blood sprayed out, and the qi carried through his Force disrupted the flow of my internal energy.
As I staggered, I looked at Lee Jungryong’s face while he continued raining sword strikes down upon me.
His forehead glistened with sweat. At the same time, his eyes seemed certain of victory, and a smile hung at the corners of his mouth.
*Ah. I don’t like this.*
I didn’t like that smile. I didn’t like the fact that a man like him possessed this much power.
Something surged inside me, and I swung White Flame.
*Kwaang!*
The first exchange.
Blood flowed from the cuts inflicted earlier, and pain spread through me. Without a word, I thrust my spear forward again.
Lee Jungryong, who had stepped back, charged into me with a calm smile.
*Boom!*
The second exchange.
Lee Jungryong retreated two steps and stared at me in surprise.
*He still had that much strength left?*
The thought was written plainly across his face.
*Of course I do.*
I muttered inwardly, adjusted my grip on the spear, ignored the faint pain spreading through me, and stepped forward.
*Boom! Boom! Kwaang!*
Three times. Four times. Five times.
Each time spear and sword collided and thunderous roars erupted, Lee Jungryong’s expression hardened further.
The smile at the corners of his mouth had vanished long ago.
“You bastard...!”
Hearing that growling shout instead of his usual voice, soft as a cat’s paw, made me laugh for some reason.
Intoxicated by my own strength, I had underestimated his skill and made a foolish mistake.
But Lee Jungryong had done the same.
The claws he had bared were certainly strong and sharp, but they were not enough to kill me.
“Jungryong.”
I drew a deep breath, and stale air and a foul stench flooded my lungs.
Even so, I felt refreshed, as though something inside me had finally opened wide.
Yes. Now I understood.
“Let’s clip those claws.”
Lee Jungryong would die here today.

chapters.title: Chapter 419
paragraphs: Lee Jungryong suddenly wondered.
*Where had things gone wrong? And what had gone wrong?*
Driving out his hyung’s bloodline and seizing control of Ares Guild?
Committing all manner of crimes to keep the Guild growing, then feeding his greed without ever learning to be satisfied?
Or perhaps...
*Making an enemy of him?*
Lee Jungryong’s gaze settled on one person—a young man whose body was stained with blood from the bleeding wounds covering him.
The young man looked up at the sky, drew a deep breath, and parted his lips.
“Jungryong.”
Why was it? The moment Lee Jungryong heard that quiet voice, a chill ran down his spine. Though he had not suffered a single wound, he felt as if a blade had cut him.
Looking at him, Jin Taekyung formed a savage grin.
“Let’s clip those claws.”
*Fwish!*
The wind stirred, and in the instant the space between them vanished, Lee Jungryong swung his sword with a sharp whistle.
*Shwick!*
A dazzling concentration of qi sliced through Jin Taekyung’s body. But instead of blood, only wind scattered through the air.
An afterimage. Not the real thing.
A red alarm bell rang in Lee Jungryong’s mind.
*Behind me!*
It was too late to swing his sword. Lee Jungryong spun around like lightning and drove out his fist.
A fist wrapped in pure-white Force collided with a palm carrying blue flame.
*Kwaang!*
The world shook.
No—the thing shaking was Lee Jungryong’s vision.
Flung backward by an irresistible force, he twisted in midair and righted himself.
His fist throbbed, and something surged up from deep inside him. But he was not even given time to spit out the blood.
*Shweeeeeek!*
A spearhead had already rushed up to his face.
The spear Jin Taekyung had hurled was aimed straight at Lee Jungryong’s chest. Gritting his teeth, he poured all his strength into knocking it upward with his sword.
*Kagagagagak! Kwaang!*
The spear narrowly missed and smashed through the concrete, leaving a massive crater.
Lee Jungryong succeeded in deflecting it, but the spear’s terrifying power and spin tore his hand open, sending blood spraying into the air.
He paid it no mind and thrust his foot through the thick cloud of dust.
*Boom!*
The dust and fog scattered in every direction, unable to withstand his blinding speed.
At the end of Lee Jungryong’s step stood a single person.
“Reckless, aren’t you? My kind of guy.”
Jin Taekyung was already holding a new spear. He brought the spearhead down in slashes from every direction. Space split apart, and flames surged upward.
The tip of Lee Jungryong’s sword pierced straight through the center.
*Whoom! Boom!*
Compressed air burst outward. The flames parted, opening a new path.
Lee Jungryong shot through it like an arrow, charging toward Jin Taekyung.
*Die.*
His sword held a single thought. It shone brilliantly and moved as fast as light.
Yet within the slowed-down world, Jin Taekyung’s eyes were clearly smiling.
*This is...*
Something was wrong.
Before Lee Jungryong could finish the thought, Jin Taekyung’s hand gripping the spear blurred.
At the same time, tremendous force slammed into the blade that had seemed poised to pierce Jin Taekyung’s throat.
*Shick! Kwaang!*
A thunderous boom rang out, loud enough to leave his ears ringing.
Lee Jungryong slid more than ten meters against his will and swallowed the blood rising in his throat.
*It isn’t over yet.*
He could not fall. He could not show weakness.
He was Lee Jungryong—the man who had fought his way through the vortex of the Great Cataclysm, the most violent upheaval in human history. An ambitious warlord born of his age.
Lee Jungryong tightened his grip on his sword, now webbed with fine cracks.
*I won’t die. I can’t die.*
There had been countless twists and turns on the road that had brought him here. He had known bottomless despair and days of unbearable rage.
He had spent half his life in someone else’s shadow, branded as number two.
No. Perhaps even now...
But...
“Not anymore.”
*Crack. Crack-crack-crack.*
Veins bulged across his body, and his muscles swelled.
Powerful qi erupted from Lee Jungryong’s entire body, pressing down on everything around him.
He drew out every last scrap of strength he had saved for the very end and glared at Jin Taekyung with bloodshot eyes.
“He’s as good as gone now. The greatest in the world is... me.”
*Vrrrrrrm.*
Everything around Lee Jungryong trembled.
Jin Taekyung watched him with calm eyes that held not the slightest hint of doubt.
“I don’t think so.”
*Kuwaaaaaang!*
The waves of energy pouring from both men clawed at everything around them.
In a fleeting instant split into countless fragments, they charged toward each other at the same time.
*Kwaang!*
Their collision came like a flash of light, and the aftermath was immense.
Amid thunderous booms that shook the world, they became two streams of wind twisting together.
A spearhead wrapped in blue flame and a sword enveloped in dazzling light flew at each other.
*Shwish-shwish-shwish-shwish!*
Masses of light tore through space as they charged.
Jin Taekyung kicked off the ground and soared into the air, driving his spear down with tremendous force.
One strike. Two. Three.
Every time spear and sword collided, a thunderous boom erupted along with a massive shock wave.
Before long, blood from the corner of Lee Jungryong’s mouth was scattering in droplets.
“Cough.”
He staggered for an instant.
At the brief glimpse of weakness shown by the old lion, the young male lion bared his teeth.
The spearhead swept horizontally, slashing fiercely toward Lee Jungryong’s side.
*Kwaang!*
The ground shook as though an earthquake had struck.
They were close enough to feel each other’s breath. Lee Jungryong barely managed to block the spear, and over their locked weapons, his gaze met Jin Taekyung’s blazing eyes.
*He’s young. Just as I once was.*
Why?
Why had that thought come to him now, of all times?
Why had remembering his own pathetic, wretched past kept him from blocking Jin Taekyung’s flame-wreathed palm?
*Boom!*
Heat.
The qi protecting every inch of his body shattered, and terrible heat seeped deep into his lungs.
Amid the blue flames filling his vision and the searing pain, memories from long ago flashed through Lee Jungryong’s mind like arrows.
“Your name?”
“Pardon?”
“Ah, yes. I meant you.”
“What’s this sudden exchange of names?”
It was the early days of the Great Cataclysm. They had met while surrounded by countless monsters, trapped in a desperate life-or-death crisis.
“Just because. You looked about my age, and it was nice to see someone my age.”
“Young fellow, you’ve suddenly gotten awfully casual. You look much younger than me.”
“Then should we be friends? I don’t mind.”
“...Do you really have time to say things like that in a situation like this?”
“Maybe not.”
Lee Jungryong had thought the man was half-mad with fear of death.
At least, he had thought so until that madman suddenly stepped forward and swept away more than several thousand monsters.
*Crack-crack-crack!*
“What the hell...”
“Now! Charge!”
After the battle, the man returned and asked him the same question.
“Your name?”
“Lee Jungryong... sir.”
“Cool name. How old are you? Oh, I’m five years older. That’s hardly a difference. Should we just be friends?”
“No. Hyung.”
He looked absurdly young and was unbelievably strong.
At their first meeting, A-rank Hunter Lee Jungryong had found his hero—and, at the same time, an immense mountain range he could never cross.
“By the way, hyung.”
“Yeah?”
“What’s your name...?”
“Oh, I haven’t told you yet.”
The man had grinned and said,
“Cheon Taemin.”
Cheon Taemin. Cheon Taemin. Cheon Taemin...
No matter how many times he repeated the name, it resonated deeply within him.
Even when he tried to forget, the face remained etched in his mind.
A giant who cast an immense shadow over Lee Jungryong’s life.
“Get lost! I said get out of my sight right now—!”
Lee Jungryong roared, his voice boiling with rage.
The vision that had been bleached white with pain shattered like glass, and the wind rushing past his ears was fierce.
When he came to his senses, he was crashing through a high-rise building and slamming into cold concrete with tremendous force.
*Kwa-gwa-gwang!*
“Cough.”
Dark-red blood spurted between his lips.
His vision blurred, and pain assailed him from every part of his body.
Perhaps his shattered ribs had pressed against his organs, because breathing was difficult. His broken left arm and leg dangled uselessly.
*A potion. The potion...*
This was his last chance.
The attack had stopped, if only for a moment. He had to heal himself now.
Lee Jungryong groped at his side with his relatively uninjured right arm, but the spot where his dimensional pouch should have been was empty.
Instead, he found someone approaching from far away.
“Ah, looking for this?”
*Rrrrrroll. Clink.*
A magic-enhanced glass bottle rolled over and came to rest at Lee Jungryong’s feet.
It was a Top-Grade Potion, a miraculous medicine said to save anyone as long as they still drew breath.
There was, however, a considerable difference between it and the state Lee Jungryong remembered.
“I was so thirsty that I drank it. Man, it was refreshing. Did you just come back from a mineral spring?”
As Jin Taekyung approached, speaking as casually as ever, Lee Jungryong let out a hollow laugh.
*Jin Taekyung.*
His name, face, and personality were all different.
But at that moment, Lee Jungryong finally understood.
When he had first encountered Jin Taekyung, he had felt something familiar deep in his chest. He had tried to ignore it, disguising it beneath the words *anxiety* and *interest*.
“Jungryong.”
The quiet voice pierced his ears.
Jin Taekyung was already standing before him, the image of another person superimposed over his face.
Lee Jungryong groaned out the words.
“Who are you? Who the hell are you?”
He wanted to ask. He was desperate to know.
How could Jin Taekyung resemble him so closely?
Why had some lowly F-rank Hunter grown stronger instead of Lee Jungryong—the man who had followed Cheon Taemin, accomplished countless feats, and been hailed as a hero?
“Me?”
The next moment, Jin Taekyung smiled and continued,
“Jungryong’s personal bully.”
Then, like an echo returning from far away, the face and voice of someone buried deep in Lee Jungryong’s old memories overlapped with his.
“Brothers. Sworn brothers.”
The two men had spoken different words with different meanings, yet both were smiling.
Lee Jungryong stared blankly at those goddamn similar smiles, then slowly—very slowly—opened his mouth.
Decades of his life and countless emotions rose and faded.
The wait lasted no more than an instant, yet felt like eternity. At last, a hollow voice slipped between his lips.
“I don’t regret it. Never.”
If someone asked whether he had not even a handful of regrets, the answer was no.
But Lee Jungryong could not regret it. He did not want to.
He simply believed this was the ending that suited him best.
“Kill me.”
A cold reply fell upon Lee Jungryong’s bright smile.
“Your last words. I heard them.”
*Fwoom.*
The spearhead that followed, wreathed in blue flame unlike that cold voice.
The flames roared to life in an instant, searing with tremendous heat. Once they had burned everything away, they died down.
All that remained amid the melted concrete and blackened ruins was the trace of someone who had once been there.
And the chime of a bell that only one person in the world could hear.
*Ding.*
**System Defeated **Lv. 153 Lee Jungryong**! - Gained a massive amount of **EXP**! - Level up! - Level up!
Listening to the cheerful System notification, I slowly withdrew my spear.
*Damn old man.*
That final smile kept coming back to me.
What kind of life had Lee Jungryong lived? What had he been thinking at the end? And then there were those movements and his strange behavior...
*No. I’ll think about it later.*
The fight with Lee Jungryong had not been easy for me, either.
Mental exhaustion suddenly washed over me, but ironically, my body felt lighter than ever thanks to the Top-Grade Potion and the effects of leveling up.
More than anything, I had a reason to keep moving forward.
*The Arch Lich.*
The source of all this.
Before that bastard transformed the enormous city into a Gate, I had to kill—
“H-human.”
The Skeleton Warlord’s trembling voice reached me.
Every hair on my body stood on end as I raised my head.
There he was.

chapters.title: Chapter 420
paragraphs: What did people feel when they first encountered a monster?
Surprise, terror, fear, confusion?
I had no idea. It happened before I was born—or, technically speaking, back when I was still on my father’s side rather than inside my mother’s womb.
But those who witnessed that historic moment must have thought of the countless legends and myths handed down since ancient times.
Just as I did now.
*Demon.*

That was the word that flashed through my mind the instant I saw it. A massive body reaching three meters tall. Bones covered in a black sheen. A shape resembling a human’s, yet fundamentally something else.
*Fwoooosh.*
Like the wings of a demon from myth, the robe draped over its body billowed as though it were alive.
The demon’s mere presence darkened the world—or rather, the Arch Lich’s red eyes cast an eerie glow.
“Human.”
Just one word.
The air around me trembled. From inside my Inventory, the Skeleton Warlord muttered with a groan.
“The lord of the undead...”
His voice was steeped in fear. The law of power applied to monsters, too.
Yes. Just as the Skeleton Warlord had said, the Arch Lich was likely the lord of every undead monster in this land.
“Human. It is not too late. Even now...”
Instead of answering, I gave a small nod.
The Skeleton Warlord was right. It was not too late, and I still had more than enough opportunity left.
*A chance to stop that bastard.*
If this sprawling metropolis transformed into a single Gate, there would truly be no turning back.
Countless undead monsters would spread like a plague, and the Arch Lich’s power would grow even stronger.
*It has to be now.*
I drew a deep breath and extended my hand. White Flame flew toward me through Seizing an Object Through Empty Space, its shaft landing in my grasp.
I stepped over the piles of collapsed concrete and trudged outside. Nothing awaited me but ruins blanketed in thick fog.
Above and below. Left and right.
No matter where I looked, there wasn’t a monster in sight.
Ah, scratch that. There was one.
“Nice to meet you, you fucking bastard.”
Some twenty meters overhead, the Arch Lich stood upon empty air and gazed down at me. Its red eyes gleamed.
“So it is true. You know the language of the Demon Realm. I did not mishear you.”
“I studied hard. But you know me, don’t you?”
“I am a being with hundreds of eyes and ears. I have been watching you all along, human.”
I frowned.
“All along?”
“Yes. Your performance on the battlefield was remarkable.”
*A Familiar spell.*
I kept the thought to myself and clicked my tongue.
“So you’re a hidden-camera creep. You didn’t install one in my bathroom, did you?”
“A hidden-camera creep? You speak nonsense, human.”
“True. If you’d seen me through a hidden camera in my bathroom, you would’ve vanished from shock already. No one has ever survived looking my enormous Black Anaconda in the eye.”
“Do you mean a Basilisk?”
A Basilisk was a monster from mythology whose gaze inflicted a curse of petrification.
It was also a Named Monster that had appeared exactly once during the Great Cataclysm.
“Something like that.”
At least the part about being so startled that you froze was the same, right?
But the Arch Lich’s response was not what I expected.
“So that is why. Why you feel strangely familiar to me.”
“What?”
“Human. I sense the energy of death upon you. Dense and dark—an energy like my own.”
A jolt of surprise ran through me. I thought I knew what the Arch Lich meant by the energy of death.
There was someone who had been unable to hide his agitation at every word the creature spoke.
*The Skeleton Warlord.*
Even as a Named Monster, the Skeleton Warlord was still undead.
Had the Arch Lich caught a scent that had seeped into me after all the time I had spent with him? Or had it seen through even that other unknown space called the Inventory?
If it was the latter...
*Just how far do that bastard’s abilities reach?*
I activated Qi Sense. A blue line shot into the sky along with a System notification.
At the same time, the Arch Lich’s red eyes, flickering between its bones, curved like crescent moons.
“How interesting.”
The next instant, black mana erupted from the Arch Lich’s entire body and lashed against the blue line.
*Beep!*
**System ???** protects itself with a powerful, incomprehensible force! Qi Sense** failed! Unable to determine the designated target!
I’d suspected as much, and sure enough.
The Arch Lich looked down at my stiffened face and let out a low laugh.
“What an interesting human. Truly. Perhaps... my guess was correct after all.”
“What guess? That you’re about to die?”
“That will not happen. I am the lord of all undead. I am nothing like those weak and foolish humans.”
The Arch Lich raised a hand made of black, glossy bone and pointed toward Wu Heixing, whose breath had stopped, and Lee Jungryong, who had been reduced to black ash.

“It was a most entertaining sight. Watching you humans kill one another brought me immense joy for the first time in a very long while. I thank you for helping me understand just how insignificant your kind truly is.”
“Get lost.”
“Anger makes humans stronger. Is that true of you as well?”
*Fwoooosh.*
The fog filling the area began to move like a living creature. As though an unseen hand were painting upon empty air, it formed a scene before me.
A city in ruins.
At the center of a horrific battlefield, where blood flowed in rivers and corpses lay piled like mountains, a man used his sword as a cane to pull himself upright.
I had seen that face only once, but I could never forget it.
The Arch Lich’s low voice echoed through the air.
“Lei Fei. That was certainly his name.”
“He possessed a great and radiant soul. So dazzling that I coveted him merely from watching afar.”
With another small gesture, the fog shifted and painted a new scene.
Lei Fei staggering toward the Arch Lich.
Lei Fei dropping to his knees before he could reach it.
Lei Fei glaring at the sky with a face filled with rage and resentment as he breathed his last.
And then...
Lei Fei reborn as a corrupted being through the Arch Lich’s power, kneeling before his new master.
No.
The Death Knight Lord.
*Fwoooosh.*
A wind blew from somewhere, scattering the fog. The Arch Lich continued slowly.
“Did you know? Humans with noble souls wield even greater power once they fall. He truly was the finest material... The outcome was regrettable, but he did not turn out too badly.”
I slowly nodded.
“Keep talking.”
“I have found new material. You, human—with an even stronger and more massive soul!”
Its chilling voice thundered through the air.
Mana poured from the Arch Lich’s entire body, covering the sky like dark storm clouds and casting the city into darkness.
At the center of it all, its red eyes burned like an ominous sun.
I stood silently and watched the scene. Then I suddenly opened my mouth.
“Right, so... are you finally done running your mouth?”
My stomach was burning.
The rage I had stored up and suppressed until I met the Arch Lich reared its head.
It surged like lava from a volcanic field.
“If you’ve said everything you wanted to say...”
Something snapped inside my head.
For that moment, I forgot even the mental exhaustion from hours of fighting at the head of the suicide squad and my battles against Lee Jungryong and Wu Heixing.
“Then get down here, you fucking bastard.”
If the Arch Lich’s voice was thunder, my shout was lava.
The fire dragon raced through hundreds of acupoints boiling like an active volcano. Blue flames engulfed White Flame’s transparent spearhead, radiating tremendous heat.
And then—
*Shweeeeeek! Boom!*
The spear of flame I launched with all my strength blew apart the dark clouds of mana and tore through the darkness.
*Rumble-rumble-rumble! Fwoom!*
The earth shook as dazzling blue flames painted the sky.
Several kilometers away, the humans and monsters locked in fierce battle forgot their own circumstances for a moment and stared blankly at the spectacle.
“Grrrrr...”
“What is that...?”
The light bursting from the enormous city shrouded in thick fog was warmer and more dazzling than anything else.
At least, that was how it seemed to one man standing tall and gazing at the city.
Choi Minwoo.
*Mr. Jin Taekyung.*
It was him. It had to be.
No one but Jin Taekyung came to mind. He was alive, and he was fighting the Arch Lich.
No. Perhaps he was fighting someone else, too.
*Lee Jungryong. Wu Heixing.*
Others might dismiss his concern as premature and his suspicions as baseless accusations, but Choi Minwoo knew how evil a person could become.
At least, that was what the Lee Jungryong he had known had been like.
And at the same time...
He knew Jin Taekyung well, too.
*You’re strong. Stronger than anyone I know.*
Choi Minwoo had said those words to Jin Taekyung once.
Some people might have laughed at him, but Choi Minwoo had meant them.
He believed no S-rank Hunter—not even Cheon Taemin, his maternal grandfather and the man who had defeated the Demon King Asmodeus—could be stronger than Jin Taekyung.
It wasn’t a matter of skill, much less a question of whose aura was greater or stronger.
It was something only those who had come to know Jin Taekyung possessed.
*Faith.*
Jin Taekyung had given Choi Minwoo faith.
Cheon Taemin, the hero who had saved humanity, had pushed his young grandson out of his thoughts after the boy lost his parents.
Jin Taekyung had not.
He had rejected every temptation around him that whispered of wealth and honor, remained with the Peace Guild, and protected his people through every danger.
No matter who stood against him.
“Our opponent is the Ares Guild. It’ll be a dangerous road.”
“Thorny roads are kind of my specialty.”
“More dangerous than anything we’ve faced so far.”
“Team Leader.”
“Yes?”
“Sometimes it’s okay to be honest.”
It was the first time anyone had ever said that to him.
Butler Kim, who had been by his side since childhood, was thoughtful and warm, but he had never given Choi Minwoo that same certainty.
Jin Taekyung had, and that gave Choi Minwoo the courage to speak.
“Will you... continue staying with the Peace Guild?”
“Yeah. That’s more like it.”
Choi Minwoo could never forget Jin Taekyung’s crooked grin.

Isolated and lonely.
For as long as he could remember, he had been cut off from everything around him.
The children he met in his youth were wary of him, and the adults whispered among themselves.
It hurt, but he never let it show. Only the aging Butler Kim had ever been someone he could truly confide in.
But not anymore.
A smile appeared on Choi Minwoo’s lips.
Far in the distance, he watched the flames rising through the thick fog and darkness, then gripped his sword once more.
*Shhk!*
A monster’s body split apart beneath a flash of dazzling aura.
As the brief silence and stillness that had settled over the battlefield shattered, a tremendous cry burst from Choi Minwoo’s lips.
“Attack—!”
He raised his sword and charged toward the monsters, looking much like someone Lee Jungryong had seen several decades ago.

sentences.text: What did people feel when they first encountered a monster?
Surprise, terror, fear, confusion?
I had no idea.
It happened before I was born—or, technically speaking, back when I was still on my father’s side rather than inside my mother’s womb.
But those who witnessed that historic moment must have thought of the countless legends and myths handed down since ancient times.
Just as I did now.
*Demon.*
That was the word that flashed through my mind the instant I saw it.
A massive body reaching three meters tall.
Bones covered in a black sheen.
A shape resembling a human’s, yet fundamentally something else.
*Fwoooosh.*
Like the wings of a demon from myth, the robe draped over its body billowed as though it were alive.
The demon’s mere presence darkened the world—or rather, the Arch Lich’s red eyes cast an eerie glow.
“Human.”
Just one word.
The air around me trembled.
From inside my Inventory, the Skeleton Warlord muttered with a groan.
“The lord of the undead...”
His voice was steeped in fear.
The law of power applied to monsters, too.
Yes.
Just as the Skeleton Warlord had said, the Arch Lich was likely the lord of every undead monster in this land.
“Human.
It is not too late.
Even now...”
Instead of answering, I gave a small nod.
The Skeleton Warlord was right.
It was not too late, and I still had more than enough opportunity left.
*A chance to stop that bastard.*
If this sprawling metropolis transformed into a single Gate, there would truly be no turning back.
Countless undead monsters would spread like a plague, and the Arch Lich’s power would grow even stronger.
*It has to be now.*
I drew a deep breath and extended my hand.
White Flame flew toward me through Seizing an Object Through Empty Space, its shaft landing in my grasp.
I stepped over the piles of collapsed concrete and trudged outside.
Nothing awaited me but ruins blanketed in thick fog.
Above and below.
Left and right.
No matter where I looked, there wasn’t a monster in sight.
Ah, scratch that.
There was one.
“Nice to meet you, you fucking bastard.”
Some twenty meters overhead, the Arch Lich stood upon empty air and gazed down at me.
Its red eyes gleamed.
“So it is true.
You know the language of the Demon Realm.
I did not mishear you.”
“I studied hard.
But you know me, don’t you?”
“I am a being with hundreds of eyes and ears.
I have been watching you all along, human.”
I frowned.
“All along?”
“Yes.
Your performance on the battlefield was remarkable.”
*A Familiar spell.*
I kept the thought to myself and clicked my tongue.
“So you’re a hidden-camera creep.
You didn’t install one in my bathroom, did you?”
“A hidden-camera creep?
You speak nonsense, human.”
“True.
If you’d seen me through a hidden camera in my bathroom, you would’ve vanished from shock already.
No one has ever survived looking my enormous Black Anaconda in the eye.”
“Do you mean a Basilisk?”
A Basilisk was a monster from mythology whose gaze inflicted a curse of petrification.
It was also a Named Monster that had appeared exactly once during the Great Cataclysm.
“Something like that.”
At least the part about being so startled that you froze was the same, right?
But the Arch Lich’s response was not what I expected.
“So that is why.
Why you feel strangely familiar to me.”
“What?”
“Human.
I sense the energy of death upon you.
Dense and dark—an energy like my own.”
A jolt of surprise ran through me.
I thought I knew what the Arch Lich meant by the energy of death.
There was someone who had been unable to hide his agitation at every word the creature spoke.
*The Skeleton Warlord.*
Even as a Named Monster, the Skeleton Warlord was still undead.
Had the Arch Lich caught a scent that had seeped into me after all the time I had spent with him?
Or had it seen through even that other unknown space called the Inventory?
If it was the latter...
*Just how far do that bastard’s abilities reach?*
I activated Qi Sense.
A blue line shot into the sky along with a System notification.
At the same time, the Arch Lich’s red eyes, flickering between its bones, curved like crescent moons.
“How interesting.”
The next instant, black mana erupted from the Arch Lich’s entire body and lashed against the blue line.
*Beep!*
**System ???** protects itself with a powerful, incomprehensible force!
Qi Sense** failed!
Unable to determine the designated target!
I’d suspected as much, and sure enough.
The Arch Lich looked down at my stiffened face and let out a low laugh.
“What an interesting human.
Truly.
Perhaps... my guess was correct after all.”
“What guess?
That you’re about to die?”
“That will not happen.
I am the lord of all undead.
I am nothing like those weak and foolish humans.”
The Arch Lich raised a hand made of black, glossy bone and pointed toward Wu Heixing, whose breath had stopped, and Lee Jungryong, who had been reduced to black ash.
“It was a most entertaining sight.
Watching you humans kill one another brought me immense joy for the first time in a very long while.
I thank you for helping me understand just how insignificant your kind truly is.”
“Get lost.”
“Anger makes humans stronger.
Is that true of you as well?”
*Fwoooosh.*
The fog filling the area began to move like a living creature.
As though an unseen hand were painting upon empty air, it formed a scene before me.
A city in ruins.
At the center of a horrific battlefield, where blood flowed in rivers and corpses lay piled like mountains, a man used his sword as a cane to pull himself upright.
I had seen that face only once, but I could never forget it.
The Arch Lich’s low voice echoed through the air.
“Lei Fei.
That was certainly his name.”
“He possessed a great and radiant soul.
So dazzling that I coveted him merely from watching afar.”
With another small gesture, the fog shifted and painted a new scene.
Lei Fei staggering toward the Arch Lich.
Lei Fei dropping to his knees before he could reach it.
Lei Fei glaring at the sky with a face filled with rage and resentment as he breathed his last.
And then...
Lei Fei reborn as a corrupted being through the Arch Lich’s power, kneeling before his new master.
No.
The Death Knight Lord.
*Fwoooosh.*
A wind blew from somewhere, scattering the fog.
The Arch Lich continued slowly.
“Did you know?
Humans with noble souls wield even greater power once they fall.
He truly was the finest material...
The outcome was regrettable, but he did not turn out too badly.”
I slowly nodded.
“Keep talking.”
“I have found new material.
You, human—with an even stronger and more massive soul!”
Its chilling voice thundered through the air.
Mana poured from the Arch Lich’s entire body, covering the sky like dark storm clouds and casting the city into darkness.
At the center of it all, its red eyes burned like an ominous sun.
I stood silently and watched the scene.
Then I suddenly opened my mouth.
“Right, so... are you finally done running your mouth?”
My stomach was burning.
The rage I had stored up and suppressed until I met the Arch Lich reared its head.
It surged like lava from a volcanic field.
“If you’ve said everything you wanted to say...”
Something snapped inside my head.
For that moment, I forgot even the mental exhaustion from hours of fighting at the head of the suicide squad and my battles against Lee Jungryong and Wu Heixing.

Choi Minwoo.

chapters.title: Chapter 421
paragraphs: There was an old saying passed down among Hunters.
Mages came in two kinds: Grand Mages, and everyone else.
Magic Johnson had proven that saying true firsthand.
Among the seven billion people on Earth, there were only three Grand Mages.
And of those three, he was the strongest War Mage. During the Great Cataclysm, he had slain countless monsters and led innumerable battles to victory.
Yet even Magic Johnson, for all his incredible achievements, had encountered a being before whom he was forced to swallow his pride.
*I hate to say this, but the Arch Lich’s magic is a cut above mine. Be careful, Jin.*
That was how powerful the Arch Lich was. There could be no hesitation or carelessness—not even for an instant—when facing him.
—Human, hurry!
*I know, damn it.*
I let the Skeleton Warlord’s shriek go in one ear and out the other as I poured internal energy into both legs.
*Crack-crack-crack!*
The solid concrete floor sank beneath me, unable to withstand the pressure transmitted into it. I bent my knees slightly, then kicked off with all my strength.
*Boom!*
With a thunderous roar like an exploding bomb, I shot into the air like a streak of light.
A fierce wind tore across my body, and the Arch Lich rapidly drew closer, his black robe spread like wings.
—You...
I could see them.
His trembling red eyes.
White Flame, launched with all my strength, had shattered the invisible barrier surrounding the Arch Lich and was now falling with everything it had.
*Come.*
I stretched out my hand. Seizing an Object Through Empty Space caught White Flame’s shaft from several meters away and pulled it into my grasp.
*Now!*

I thrust the spear with all my strength. Three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi surged up from my dantian and raced forward without restraint. Force like blue hellfire erupted over the transparent spearhead.
*Fwoooooom!*
And just as I became certain I had succeeded—
—Gravity.
*Fwoosh!*
“Hngh!”
With that sinister voice, something invisible pressed down on my entire body.
No.
It struck me.
I swallowed a breath and reached out as far as I could, but before the spearhead brimming with Force could touch the Arch Lich’s foot, my body was already falling toward the ground.
The Arch Lich, who had seemed close enough to touch, receded in an instant.
“You fucking—”
*Booooom!*
I crashed down like a meteor. Above my head, laughter like scraping metal rang out.
—Not bad. Amusing in its own way.
*Damn skeleton bastard.*
I spat out a wad of phlegm and looked up at the Arch Lich looming over me like a god.
“Good to hear. It’s only going to get more entertaining from here.”
—Humans are always dreaming futile dreams. I have seen it countless times. Driven by anger and longing, you challenge what cannot be surpassed, only to confront reality at last and fall into despair.

“That sounds a lot like the bullshit spewed by all the guys who’ve died by my hand... Do you people share a *Hundred Questions and Answers for Dealing with Jin Taekyung* or something? Hold study sessions every now and then?”
—Even so, those who died by your hand were still insignificant humans. But I am different.
“Of course you’re different, you son of a bitch. You’re already dead.”
The Arch Lich fell silent for a moment, so I continued.
“Looking at you now, someone must’ve killed you, too. Was it a human? Is that why you’ve been flaunting your inferiority complex this whole time?”
—You...
“Yep. This bastard was killed by a human.”
—Will you shut your mouth!
At his thunderous shout, the magic surrounding the Arch Lich surged violently. His red eyes, far brighter than before, glared down at me.
—I am a servant of a great king. I am not a being who can be compared to insignificant creatures like you!
I was about to fire back when the unexpected word stopped me.
*Wait. A king?*
*Did I hear that wrong?*
As the question flashed through my mind, the Skeleton Warlord answered in a trembling voice.
—This commander heard it clearly, too, wretched human. Th-then, could it be...
*No way. It can’t be.*
I swallowed dryly and asked,
“Is the great king you just mentioned the Demon King Asmodeus?”
—Do not speak the name of His Highness.
So much for *no way*.
It really was the Demon King Asmodeus.
The Skeleton Warlord sucked in a breath despite not needing to breathe, while I muttered in disbelief,
“Huh. Asmodeus? Seriously?”
—The name of His Highness...
“But I was sure Asmodeus had been destroyed.”
—The name of His Highness...
“Is Asmodeus still alive? As an Arch Demon King or something?”
—His Highness...

“Yeah, yeah, I get it—he’s fucking adorable. Now answer me. Asmodeus died back then, didn’t he? Or did he come back to life? If he was resurrected as an undead like you, where is he, and what’s he doing now?”
At that moment, the Skeleton Warlord murmured fearfully,
—At this hour, he might be asleep...
*What the fuck are you talking about? You don’t sleep, either.*
—I do not, but His Highness might be different.
*What is the Demon King, some good little schoolboy? Do you think he turns off the television, brushes his teeth, and goes to bed when the sun goes down? And why are you using such an honorific?*
—Ah! I did not even realize... But from this commander’s perspective, is that not only natural?
*That’s true.*
—Indeed. Because I am a monster.
*Then don’t use it.*
—Why not...?
*The Demon King is far away, and my fist is close.*
—Ah.
The Skeleton Warlord let out an exclamation of enlightenment, then added,
—But, human. It seems the Arch Lich’s magic will be getting closer in a moment.
*Damn it. He’s right.*
I hurriedly threw myself aside. A green mist grazed me by a hair and engulfed the spot where I had been standing moments earlier.
*Ssssssssss!*
Stone, steel, even concrete—everything within a radius of dozens of meters melted away, leaving a gaping hole.
The Arch Lich had fired a poison cloud of terrifying power. His eyes were not merely clear—they burned like torches.
—I intended to take you under my command.
“Uh, what brought that on all of a sudden?”
—I would have subdued your body and soul and used you as the vanguard of my glorious undead army.
“How much does it pay?”
—But I have changed my mind.
“No, I asked how much it pays. Don’t tell me you people pay in passion, too?”
—Your flesh will be torn to pieces, and your soul will wander the River of Death for all eternity.

“Are you acquainted with the deacon at the church I went to as a kid? He said something similar to me. Said a devil like me would go to hell. If my mom hadn’t stopped me, he would’ve become the first martyr in that church’s history.”
—You insignificant human. Pay the price for insulting His Highness and defiling his name.
“For once, we agree on something. Paying the price. I like that.”
I nodded and lowered White Flame at an angle.
“So I’m planning to make you pay the price, too... What do you think?”
The Arch Lich opened his mouth.
The four-syllable incantation, uttered in a voice deeper and more sinister than ever, was not an answer to my question.
It was a curse that called forth death.
—Dark Hand.
*Whoooom!*
A pair of black hands burst through the thick fog. They hurtled in from both sides as if coming together in prayer.
I leaped to avoid the Dark Hands—and another spell was waiting for me.
—Curse.
I twisted to evade the black fog descending like a net, but this time, I was too late.
No.
Perhaps the Arch Lich had anticipated my movement.
The fog had already been closing in before I even finished dodging the Dark Hands.
*Shhk.*
Only a paper-thin margin.
At the instant the sticky fog grazed the tip of my little finger—
*Beep!*

**System You have been afflicted with the status effect **Curse**! - Due to **Curse**, all physical attributes have been temporarily reduced! Strength** has temporarily decreased by 20! Stamina** has temporarily decreased by 20! Agility**...
The System notification had barely sounded when my body grew heavier. I clicked my tongue inwardly.
*Damn it.*
I was already short on points, and now a curse had slapped me with a debuff.
This wasn’t a loss of one or two points, either. With twenty points stripped from each attribute at once, I could clearly feel the difference.
But even with a debuff, I was not so helpless that I could do nothing but take his attacks.
Just like now.
—Dark Vine.
*Crack! Whoooosh!*
Hundreds of thorny vines burst through the ground, filling the air in every direction as they shot toward me.
I exhaled sharply and swung my spear.
*Shhk!*
A line of blue flame cut through the air, severing every vine formed from magic.
—Dark Vine. Dark Vine. Dark Vine.
*Shwoooooosh!*
From the severed ends of the thorny vines, which had been collapsing after losing their strength, new vines began to grow.
They budded, grew thorns, and swelled even larger in barely a second.
But to me, one second was as good as a minute.
*Fwoom! Shhk!*
A thorny vine several meters around was severed in a single blow.
Cut off from its magical connection, the dark plant toppled onto a half-collapsed high-rise building.
Amid the cloud of dust rising from the thunderous impact, I sensed an ominous fluctuation of energy.
*Magic.*
My prediction was right.
*Shhh-shhh-shhh-shhh!*
A spear stained a dull black.
A Bone Spear made entirely of bone became a streak of light and shot toward me.
No.
That wasn’t it.
*There isn’t just one.*
—Be careful, human!
Along with the Skeleton Warlord’s desperate shout—
*Boom!*
The dust cloud exploded outward with a blast of compressed air.
More Bone Spears than I could possibly count surged toward me.
Some flew in straight lines. Some fell like meteors. Others curved through the air.
—Ah.
The Skeleton Warlord and I groaned at the same time.
*How many are there? Hundreds? No, thousands?*
The overwhelming sight left me speechless for a moment.
A chill ran down my spine, and my mouth fell open on its own. A bead of cold sweat that had formed on my forehead slid down the bridge of my nose.
And then...
Everything stopped.
*This is...*
It was that same phenomenon that had sometimes come to me in moments of crisis.
My five senses sharpened to a razor’s edge, and the world slowed down. Into the space between those moments crept something unfamiliar.
A new sense.
A sixth sense that science could not explain.
I knew its name.
*The sixth sense.*
At the same time, something inside me shed its shell.
My gaze traveled more and more slowly across the enormous net formed by hundreds—thousands—of Bone Spears.
*Because I had already given up everything?*
No.
What mattered was the essence.
Appearances could be layered over it, but the essence itself did not change.
And at that very moment, I could see it.
My parched lips parted, and an exclamation slipped out.
“Ah.”
*So that was it. That’s what it was.*
It was something I had yet to understand, even after reaching the Supreme Peak.
A flash of enlightenment streaked through my mind like lightning, and the slowed world resumed its proper speed.
Before the rain of spears pouring in from every direction, I raised my spear almost in a daze.
Then I brought White Flame down along the path I could see.
*Heavenly Strike.*
*Fwoooooom!*
The erupting flames swallowed everything.
The Bone Spears, too numerous to count, vanished.
No.
The things that vanished the instant the flames touched them were illusions made of magic.
Only the essence collided with my strike, and unable to withstand its power, it burned away.
*Shhhhhhh.*
Ash scattered in the wind that blew from somewhere.
Carried on that breeze, I heard a bright, cheerful ringing.
*Ding. Ding. Ding...*
It was such a pleasant sound that I found myself smiling without realizing it.

—I am a servant of a great king.
I am not a being who can be compared to insignificant creatures like you!
I was about to fire back when the unexpected word stopped me.
*Wait.
A king?*
*Did I hear that wrong?*
As the question flashed through my mind, the Skeleton Warlord answered in a trembling voice.
—This commander heard it clearly, too, wretched human.
Th-then, could it be...
*No way.
It can’t be.*
I swallowed dryly and asked,
“Is the great king you just mentioned the Demon King Asmodeus?”
—Do not speak the name of His Highness.
So much for *no way*.
It really was the Demon King Asmodeus.
The Skeleton Warlord sucked in a breath despite not needing to breathe, while I muttered in disbelief,
“Huh.
Asmodeus?
Seriously?”
—The name of His Highness...
“But I was sure Asmodeus had been destroyed.”
—The name of His Highness...
“Is Asmodeus still alive?
As an Arch Demon King or something?”
—His Highness...
“Yeah, yeah, I get it—he’s fucking adorable.
Now answer me.
Asmodeus died back then, didn’t he?
Or did he come back to life?
If he was resurrected as an undead like you, where is he, and what’s he doing now?”
At that moment, the Skeleton Warlord murmured fearfully,
—At this hour, he might be asleep...
*What the fuck are you talking about?
You don’t sleep, either.*
—I do not, but His Highness might be different.
*What is the Demon King, some good little schoolboy?
Do you think he turns off the television, brushes his teeth, and goes to bed when the sun goes down?
And why are you using such an honorific?*
—Ah!
I did not even realize...
But from this commander’s perspective, is that not only natural?
*That’s true.*
—Indeed.
Because I am a monster.
*Then don’t use it.*
—Why not...?
*The Demon King is far away, and my fist is close.*
—Ah.
The Skeleton Warlord let out an exclamation of enlightenment, then added,
—But, human.
It seems the Arch Lich’s magic will be getting closer in a moment.
*Damn it.
He’s right.*
I hurriedly threw myself aside.
A green mist grazed me by a hair and engulfed the spot where I had been standing moments earlier.
*Ssssssssss!*
Stone, steel, even concrete—everything within a radius of dozens of meters melted away, leaving a gaping hole.
The Arch Lich had fired a poison cloud of terrifying power.
His eyes were not merely clear—they burned like torches.
—I intended to take you under my command.
“Uh, what brought that on all of a sudden?”
—I would have subdued your body and soul and used you as the vanguard of my glorious undead army.
“How much does it pay?”
—But I have changed my mind.
“No, I asked how much it pays.
Don’t tell me you people pay in passion, too?”
—Your flesh will be torn to pieces, and your soul will wander the River of Death for all eternity.
“Are you acquainted with the deacon at the church I went to as a kid?
He said something similar to me.
Said a devil like me would go to hell.
If my mom hadn’t stopped me, he would’ve become the first martyr in that church’s history.”
—You insignificant human.
Pay the price for insulting His Highness and defiling his name.
“For once, we agree on something.
Paying the price.
I like that.”
I nodded and lowered White Flame at an angle.
“So I’m planning to make you pay the price, too...
What do you think?”
The Arch Lich opened his mouth.
The four-syllable incantation, uttered in a voice deeper and more sinister than ever, was not an answer to my question.
It was a curse that called forth death.
—Dark Hand.
*Whoooom!*
A pair of black hands burst through the thick fog.
They hurtled in from both sides as if coming together in prayer.
I leaped to avoid the Dark Hands—and another spell was waiting for me.
—Curse.
I twisted to evade the black fog descending like a net, but this time, I was too late.
No.
Perhaps the Arch Lich had anticipated my movement.
The fog had already been closing in before I even finished dodging the Dark Hands.
*Shhk.*
Only a paper-thin margin.
At the instant the sticky fog grazed the tip of my little finger—
*Beep!*
**System You have been afflicted with the status effect **Curse**! - Due to **Curse**, all physical attributes have been temporarily reduced!
Strength** has temporarily decreased by 20!
Stamina** has temporarily decreased by 20!
Agility**...
The System notification had barely sounded when my body grew heavier.
I clicked my tongue inwardly.
*Damn it.*
I was already short on points, and now a curse had slapped me with a debuff.
This wasn’t a loss of one or two points, either.
With twenty points stripped from each attribute at once, I could clearly feel the difference.
But even with a debuff, I was not so helpless that I could do nothing but take his attacks.
Just like now.
—Dark Vine.
*Crack!
Whoooosh!*
Hundreds of thorny vines burst through the ground, filling the air in every direction as they shot toward me.
I exhaled sharply and swung my spear.
*Shhk!*
A line of blue flame cut through the air, severing every vine formed from magic.
—Dark Vine.
Dark Vine.
Dark Vine.
*Shwoooooosh!*
From the severed ends of the thorny vines, which had been collapsing after losing their strength, new vines began to grow.
They budded, grew thorns, and swelled even larger in barely a second.
But to me, one second was as good as a minute.
*Fwoom!
Shhk!*
A thorny vine several meters around was severed in a single blow.
Cut off from its magical connection, the dark plant toppled onto a half-collapsed high-rise building.
Amid the cloud of dust rising from the thunderous impact, I sensed an ominous fluctuation of energy.
*Magic.*
My prediction was right.
*Shhh-shhh-shhh-shhh!*
A spear stained a dull black.
A Bone Spear made entirely of bone became a streak of light and shot toward me.
No.
That wasn’t it.
*There isn’t just one.*
—Be careful, human!
Along with the Skeleton Warlord’s desperate shout—
*Boom!*
The dust cloud exploded outward with a blast of compressed air.
More Bone Spears than I could possibly count surged toward me.
Some flew in straight lines.
Some fell like meteors.
Others curved through the air.
—Ah.
The Skeleton Warlord and I groaned at the same time.
*How many are there?
Hundreds?
No, thousands?*
The overwhelming sight left me speechless for a moment.
A chill ran down my spine, and my mouth fell open on its own.
A bead of cold sweat that had formed on my forehead slid down the bridge of my nose.
And then...
Everything stopped.
*This is...*
It was that same phenomenon that had sometimes come to me in moments of crisis.
My five senses sharpened to a razor’s edge, and the world slowed down.
Into the space between those moments crept something unfamiliar.
A new sense.
A sixth sense that science could not explain.
I knew its name.
*The sixth sense.*
At the same time, something inside me shed its shell.
My gaze traveled more and more slowly across the enormous net formed by hundreds—thousands—of Bone Spears.
*Because I had already given up everything?*
No.
What mattered was the essence.
Appearances could be layered over it, but the essence itself did not change.
And at that very moment, I could see it.
My parched lips parted, and an exclamation slipped out.
“Ah.”
*So that was it.
That’s what it was.*
It was something I had yet to understand, even after reaching the Supreme Peak.
A flash of enlightenment streaked through my mind like lightning, and the slowed world resumed its proper speed.
Before the rain of spears pouring in from every direction, I raised my spear almost in a daze.
Then I brought White Flame down along the path I could see.
*Heavenly Strike.*
*Fwoooooom!*
The erupting flames swallowed everything.
The Bone Spears, too numerous to count, vanished.
No.
The things that vanished the instant the flames touched them were illusions made of magic.
Only the essence collided with my strike, and unable to withstand its power, it burned away.
*Shhhhhhh.*
Ash scattered in the wind that blew from somewhere.
Carried on that breeze, I heard a bright, cheerful ringing.
*Ding.
Ding.
Ding...*
It was such a pleasant sound that I found myself smiling without realizing it.

chapters.title: Chapter 422
paragraphs: *Ding. Ding. Ding.*

**System In crisis lies opportunity. You have gained new insight during a battle in which life and death hung in the balance! - Your **Middle Dantian** has opened! - The opening of your **Middle Dantian** has increased all attributes by 20! - Circulating your qi has become vastly more effective! - Your ability to perceive and control the flow of qi has greatly improved! Muscles and Bones** and **Sinews and Meridians** have increased!
The System notifications kept ringing in my ears without pause.
A breeze stirred my sweat-soaked hair, and I felt the new power and changes permeating my entire body.
Even the final, crystal-clear chime.
*Ding.*

**System As a reward for your enlightenment, you have gained a large amount of EXP! - As a reward for your enlightenment, you have gained 50 points! - Level Up! - As an effect of leveling up, all status ailments and fatigue have been cleared, and some injuries have healed! - The status effect **Curse** has been removed! - Your temporarily reduced attributes have returned to normal!
And I wasn’t the only one who sensed the changes.
A master could hardly fail to notice what his own hand had done. Realizing that his curse magic had been broken, the Arch Lich asked in disbelief,
“How in the world?”
I shrugged at the single word that contained every question he had.
“Well.”
“‘Well’?”
“Yeah. Well.”
“Do you think that explains anything?”
“Of course not. But why should I explain it to you?”
The faint tremor in the Arch Lich’s glowing eyes conveyed his sheer incredulity.
“You are clearly not a mage.”
“I wanted to be one. Mages get paid more. But I didn’t have the talent. I wasn’t smart enough, either.”
“Even the humans you call Grand Mages could not break my magic so easily.”
“They can’t. But it’s done.”
“What utter nonsense!”
I had to admit it.
The Arch Lich’s magic—no, his skill—was unquestionably superior to mine.
Even I, who had already far surpassed the limits of an ordinary Hunter, had been unable to avoid his curse magic. And his massive illusion spell using Bone Spears had been genuinely dangerous.
If I hadn’t gained that insight, I might not even be standing here now.
But...
“So what are you going to do about it?”
I had the System, and I had merely done my best with the power and effort I had been given to overcome the crisis.
If he thought that was unfair, he could use the System, too.
“That’s just how the world works. Even if it feels like shit and pisses you off, you have to suck it up and move on. What else can you do? It’s already happened. Right?”
The Skeleton Warlord, who had been screaming only moments ago, muttered,
“Wow. You really have a way with words.”
I could be like that sometimes.
“But, devious human, that one does not appear willing to suck it up and move on.”
The Skeleton Warlord was right.
The next moment, an enormous vortex of magical power formed, and an eerie voice rang out.
“Explode. Sonic Buster.”
And at the same time—
*Fwoooooosh! Boom!*
Highly compressed wind exploded outward all at once.
The sphere of wind shot forward at the speed of sound, pulverizing concrete and snapping steel rebar with the slightest touch.
Every window in the high-rise buildings shattered under the aftershock, and countless shards of glass were swept into the gale.
In a single instant—before I could even blink—the enormous mass of wind had reached the tip of my nose.
“Human!”
The Skeleton Warlord’s scream from inside my Inventory echoed like a cry from far away.
Was that bastard worried about his own safety, or mine?
Whatever the real reason, it didn’t matter.
There was a world of difference between who I’d been a few minutes ago and who I was now.
*Ah.*
The area around my chest grew hot.
The place martial artists called the Tanzhong acupoint, or the Middle Dantian, had opened wide.
It allowed me to take in everything around me—to feel it against my skin and see it with my own eyes.
*So that’s what it was.*
The world slowed, and everything became clear enough to see and understand.
The enormous sphere of wind, its currents whipping like blades.
And the flow of magical power that made it possible.
*Shh-shh-shh-shh-shhk!*
Everything had a center. Magic was no exception.
And now, I could see it.
*Now.*
I swung my spear through the slowed world.
The sphere of wind that looked ready to sweep away everything in its path split in two along White Flame’s spearhead.
The single enormous mass broke into hundreds—thousands—of wind blades. Freed from the magical power controlling them, they veered left and right, tearing through everything around them.
*Shhk! Kwa-gwa-gwa-gwa!*
The raging wind whipped my clothes and hair around. With a faint smile on my lips, I looked up at the Arch Lich.
“Come down. My neck hurts.”
“Or I can come to you.”
*Crack-crackle! Boom!*
One stomp.
The solid ground caved in, and I shot toward the ash-gray sky.
*Boom!*
The instant Jin Taekyung launched himself from the ground, the Arch Lich realized what he had to do.
*I must not let that human come any closer.*
Every mage knew to avoid close combat, but for the Arch Lich, those words carried a different weight.
*This body feels threatened by a mere human.*
He prided himself on having reached the pinnacle of dark magic.
Although he had lost considerable power during his resurrection as an Arch Lich, even now he possessed enough magical power to regard Grand Mages as beneath him.
But the human hurtling toward him now...
*He is dangerous.*
*Yes. Just like that bastard back then.*
It was a memory the Arch Lich never wanted to recall again. Clenching his still-intact teeth, he cast a spell.
“Gravity!”
Unlike before, the shout carried palpable power. Invisible gravity bore down over a radius of several dozen meters.
Just as the pressure—too great for even an S-rank Hunter to resist—was about to engulf Jin Taekyung’s entire body—
*Pop!*
Compressed air burst from the tip of Jin Taekyung’s foot.
His body escaped the range of the gravity magic with *Stepping on Empty Air*, then stepped on the empty air again.
His graceful movements resembled a hawk’s, but no mere bird could compare to his speed.
*What is this?*
The red glow in the Arch Lich’s eyes darkened as he watched Jin Taekyung race through the air toward him.
Jin Taekyung had not only identified the precise range of his gravity magic but had also evaded it with some strange technique.
*As I thought. He did not dispel the illusion magic through mere luck. Then...*
*Whoooooooom!*
Magical power poured from the Arch Lich’s entire body, shaking the surrounding space.
“Gravity. Gravity. Gravity.”
High-level spells that even a skilled high-ranking mage would have needed to chant at length came pouring out without pause.
This time, the Arch Lich was certain he could knock Jin Taekyung from the sky.
*Fall, human.*
This time, he reduced the strength of his gravity magic in exchange for expanding its range.
How could Jin Taekyung possibly escape gravity pressing down over a radius of several hundred meters—
*Shhk!*
The Arch Lich’s glowing eyes trembled.
The gravity magic bearing down on Jin Taekyung dispersed, and the Arch Lich felt the magical power connecting him to the spell snap like a thread.
He froze for an instant, stunned that his magic had been broken.
Then Jin Taekyung stepped on empty air once more and shot toward him like a cannonball.
*Bang! Shweeeeeek!*
With a sharp crack through the air, Jin Taekyung hurtled in front of the Arch Lich—no, a step above him—and brought White Flame down.
*Fwoom!*
A line of blue flame streaked toward the Arch Lich.
*Crash!*
In the slowed world, the invisible barrier surrounding the Arch Lich shattered.
The flames of Force, fueled by three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi, smashed through dozens of layered defensive spells and surged toward the Arch Lich’s body.
At that very moment—
“Great Bone Wall!”
With an eerie cry, a wall of black bones rose into the air.
The highest-level defensive spell, manifested barely a meter away, collided with the flame-wreathed spearhead.
High in the ash-gray sky, an enormous shock wave and a thunderous roar erupted around the two figures facing each other across the bone wall.
*Kwaaang!*
Compressed wind exploded outward.
The clouds circling far above scattered. Buildings that had barely maintained their shape collapsed, and half-rotted corpses were swept away by the wind.
Yet the two beings responsible for it all remained perfectly still, staring at each other through the barrier.
“That was close, wasn’t it?”
“Yes, quite impressive. No...”
The Arch Lich stared at the transparent spearhead piercing the center of the wall and continued,
“I shall call it dangerous.”

The length of the spearhead that had passed through the bone barrier was no more than the width of a finger joint, but the Force that erupted in that instant had reached the tip of the Arch Lich’s nose.
It had been a fortunate escape for the Arch Lich.
For Jin Taekyung, it had been unfortunate.
“You got lucky.”
“You are arrogant, human. But I will admit this much.”
“What?”
The Arch Lich slowly continued as Jin Taekyung stared at him in confusion.
“You have earned the right to be. If you truly are the Adversary.”
“...The Adversary?”

“That is right. The king’s Adversary. His eternal nemesis, bound to him by a god’s machinations. I cannot yet be certain, but... that must also be why I was able to rise again after stepping into the River of Death.”
Jin Taekyung frowned.
What was the king’s Adversary? And what kind of nonsense was this about a god’s machinations?
“Do you have middle-school syndrome or something? Get rid of those bones and show me your right hand. Let’s see if there’s a Black Flame Dragon in there.”
The Arch Lich shook his head.
“This is something neither you nor I can understand. But one thing is certain.”
The deeply sunken red eye-lights flared fiercely.
At first, he had thought Jin Taekyung was merely a strong and unusual human.
Not anymore.
He remembered sweeping across this planet decades ago while serving the king.
He also recalled the figure of the human he had encountered on the day he lost everything and fell into the River of Death—the first and last time he had ever met that human.
*The Adversary.*
The human who had killed him and even assassinated the king.
The one he had tried to stop but could not, the one he had tried to approach but could never reach—the only human he had ever feared.
And today, during his battle with Jin Taekyung, the Arch Lich had remembered that day.
“You... will definitely die here.”
His voice was eerie but more resolute than ever.
Jin Taekyung’s answer was simple.
“What the hell are you talking about, dumbass?”
And the next moment—
“Eat this, fucker.”
*Fwoom! Kwaaaaaa!*
With those quiet words, a fist wreathed in blue hellfire shot forward, erasing everything in its path.
It struck the curtain of black bones.
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
*Crack-crack-crack!*
The bone barrier that had seemed capable of blocking any attack collapsed.
Beyond the countless fragments of bone scattering in every direction, the Arch Lich’s face came into view.
Jin Taekyung spoke with an expressionless face.
“See how much better this is? My neck doesn’t hurt, either.”
“Down you go.”
*Wham!*
A single punch, fired like a ray of light, slammed into the Arch Lich’s jaw.
