“Do you have middle-school syndrome or something?
Get rid of those bones and show me your right hand.
Let’s see if there’s a Black Flame Dragon in there.”
The Arch Lich shook his head.
“This is something neither you nor I can understand.
But one thing is certain.”
The deeply sunken red eye-lights flared fiercely.
At first, he had thought Jin Taekyung was merely a strong and unusual human.
Not anymore.
He remembered sweeping across this planet decades ago while serving the king.
He also recalled the figure of the human he had encountered on the day he lost everything and fell into the River of Death—the first and last time he had ever met that human.
*The Adversary.*
The human who had killed him and even assassinated the king.
The one he had tried to stop but could not, the one he had tried to approach but could never reach—the only human he had ever feared.
And today, during his battle with Jin Taekyung, the Arch Lich had remembered that day.
“You... will definitely die here.”
His voice was eerie but more resolute than ever.
Jin Taekyung’s answer was simple.
“What the hell are you talking about, dumbass?”
And the next moment—
“Eat this, fucker.”
*Fwoom!
Kwaaaaaa!*
With those quiet words, a fist wreathed in blue hellfire shot forward, erasing everything in its path.
It struck the curtain of black bones.
Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
*Crack-crack-crack!*
The bone barrier that had seemed capable of blocking any attack collapsed.
Beyond the countless fragments of bone scattering in every direction, the Arch Lich’s face came into view.
Jin Taekyung spoke with an expressionless face.
“See how much better this is?
My neck doesn’t hurt, either.”
“Down you go.”
*Wham!*
A single punch, fired like a ray of light, slammed into the Arch Lich’s jaw.

chapters.title: Chapter 423
paragraphs: *Wham!*
The instant the heavy blow sent the Arch Lich hurtling toward the ground, I drew up my internal energy and kicked off the air.
*Bang!*
Compressed air exploded beneath my feet, launching me at terrifying speed toward his plummeting figure.
The Skeleton Warlord let out a cry that might have been a scream or a cheer.
“You did it, human! Hurry and finish it!”
*Finish what?*
Unfortunately, he was wrong. Having driven my fist directly into the Arch Lich’s jaw, I knew that better than anyone.
*He cast a defensive spell in that split second...!*
Before my all-out Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist could connect, he had covered his face with a Bone Shield.
Considering the force behind the blow, he could not have escaped completely unharmed, but this was not enough to bring him down.
And sure enough, the Arch Lich abruptly stopped in midair after plummeting like a meteor. Immense mana rippled through the atmosphere.
“Darkness Hold.”
*Fwoooooosh!*
A pair of enormous hands burst out of thin air. At a glance, they looked similar to Dark Hand, but as its name implied, Darkness Hold was a spell designed solely to bind its target.
I brought my spear down toward the two hands hurtling at me.
*I can see it.*
Everything had a grain. Living creatures had one. So did the wind, and even invisible energy.
Opening my Middle Dantian had allowed me to sense and see the core and grain of things.
Just like now.
*Shhk!*
Flames blossomed, and the darkness split apart. The black hands writhed as if in pain before dissolving into mist, and the Arch Lich’s eye-lights flashed.
The next instant, his hand of dark, weathered bone clawed through the air.
“Dark Claw!”
*Fsssssh! Shhk!*
The dispersing black mist transformed into a beast’s claws and rained down.
Countless attacks hurtled in from every direction, each tracing a different path. I could have blocked them easily enough if I committed to it.
But then I would lose the Arch Lich after finally closing the distance.
*I have to choose.*
I could not catch two rabbits at once—especially when the other side was not a rabbit, but a tiger.
I made my decision in that brief instant and hurled White Flame with all my strength.
Not at the magic surrounding me, but at the Arch Lich.
*Fwoooooom!*
Wreathed in blue hellfire, White Flame cleaved through everything in its path like a streak of light.
The Arch Lich cried out with more urgency than ever before.
“Bone Shi—”
*Too late, you son of a bitch.*
*Fwoooooosh!*
Blue hellfire swallowed the Arch Lich whole.
His half-formed bone shield turned to ash and crumbled before the blistering heat.
*Crunch!*
White Flame’s spearhead punched through the Arch Lich’s chest. Impaled like meat on a skewer, he plunged toward the ground with a shriek unlike any sound I had ever heard from him.
At that moment, I felt a chilling wind slicing in from every direction.
“Human, danger...!”
I already knew. I did not need the Skeleton Warlord’s warning.
I had known and done it anyway. To take the bones, I had to give up my flesh. Even knowing I would not emerge unscathed, I had believed this was the right decision.
As I watched the claws of mana rain down from every direction, a thought crossed my mind.
*...Maybe I should’ve just blocked them.*
But there were no take-backs now.
*Shh-shh-shh-shh-shhk!*
A violent gust swept over my entire body.
It was not an illusion like Bone Spear, nor was it slow enough to block. I twisted my body as much as possible and gathered my internal energy, but there was a definite limit.
*Shhk! Shhk! Shhk! Shraaaak!*
Shoulder, side, thigh, arm...
Countless claws of mana slashed and raked across my entire body. Blood burst from the deep gashes in my skin, and overwhelming pain crashed over me.
*Damn it.*
It hurt. Enough to kill me.
Enough to make me want to die.
No matter how many times I experienced it, pain was something that was difficult to grow accustomed to.
My vision blurred, and the strength drained from my body before I realized it.
The agony lasted only a moment, yet seemed to stretch on forever.
When I finally opened my eyes, the first thing I saw was an enormous pile of concrete looming right in front of me.
“Get a hold of yourself, human!”
The Skeleton Warlord’s frantic shout snapped me back to my senses.
I forced internal energy into my stiffened body. Along with the tearing pain in my acupoints, the senses that had fallen asleep awakened.
*Now!*
Without a moment’s hesitation, I flipped over in midair.
*Crash!*
A thunderous roar rose with a cloud of dust. Violent vibrations and pain slowly crawled up the leg with which I landed roughly on the concrete pile.
“Urgh.”
As I clenched my teeth against the pain, the Skeleton Warlord spoke.
“Human, you do not... appear to be all right.”
I answered between ragged breaths.
“Huff. If you know that, huff, then shut up. My head’s ringing.”
I was not exaggerating. It really was.
The System notifications drilling into my ears were enough to make me want to throw up.
*Beep.*

**System The status effect **Severe Injury** has been applied! - The status effect **Excessive Bleeding** has been applied! - Due to severe injuries, your physical attributes have been drastically reduced! Strength**, **Agility**, and **Stamina** have each decreased by 200 points! - You have suffered severe injuries! Immediate treatment is required!
*Yeah. I thought so, too.*
Whether from losing too much blood or the relentless agony coursing through me, my vision was hazy and my thoughts barely worked.
But even in that state, there was one presence I could not forget.
“The Arch Lich. Where’s the Arch Lich?”
At the sound of my cracked voice, the Skeleton Warlord roared.
“Have you gone completely insane, human?! Treat yourself first!”
“I haven’t gotten a kill notification yet. That means he’s still ali—”
“Who cares about your kill notification?! Treat yourself first!”
“Hngh.”
*I told you not to shout.*
Dizzy, I leaned against the pile of concrete. Blood dripped from my body, leaving me soaked from head to toe, while my arms and legs trembled like aspen leaves beyond my control.
*Damn it.*
I had really taken a beating.
My one consolation was that the Arch Lich had to be in even worse shape than I was—or at least no better.
“You stupid human!”
*I know. I know.*
With his shout reverberating through my head, I slowly opened my palm and muttered inwardly.
*Inventory open. Summon.*
*Pop!*
The thought became reality at once.
I drew out an item from the subspace pocket that had once belonged to Lee Jungryong and now belonged to me.
*A Top-Grade Potion.*
Had Lee Jungryong ever imagined that both Top-Grade Potions he had brought along just in case would end up being used on me?
My hand trembling, I uncorked the potion and raised it to my lips, ready to gulp it down like the elixir of life.
Or rather, I was just about to.
*Tap! Fwoooooosh!*
It happened in an instant.
A black thorny vine sprang from between the slabs of concrete and struck my wrist. In the slowed world, the Top-Grade Potion flew from my hand and vanished beyond the pale haze.
I stared blankly at the few drops of potion scattered through the air as they soaked into the ground. Then I suddenly spoke.
“Dark Vine.”
Someone’s all-too-familiar magic.
The Skeleton Warlord muttered like he was groaning.
“It is him.”
I slowly raised my head. Beyond the dense fog, a pair of red eye-lights blazed like torches as they drew closer.
A three-meter body with a black sheen emerged through the mist with heavy steps. He resembled a human, but no one could have called him one.
“You, human.”
His low voice seethed with unmistakable fury.
Deep within my Inventory, the Skeleton Warlord trembled. I smiled faintly.
“You son of a bitch. You stole the food right out of my mouth.”
“Your futile struggle ends here.”
*Shhk! Snap!*
I did not even have time to reach out. The Arch Lich snapped his fingers, and Dark Vine swept up Lee Jungryong’s subspace pocket—an ordinary-looking leather pouch—and flung it far out of sight.
“No more cheap tricks will work.”
The mana surrounding the Arch Lich reacted to every word he spoke.
But just as I had suffered a severe injury, the power he emitted was also weaker than before.
The White Flame piercing the center of his chest had to be the decisive cause.
*I can do this.*
I forced myself upright. As I reached out, a spear summoned from my Inventory landed in my hand.
“That spear in your chest looks good on you. Want me to plant another one?”
“Will you have the chance?”
“Of course. Looking at the state you’re in, I’d say my chances are pretty good.”
“Humans never know the difference between courage and recklessness. How foolish. Truly, how foolish.”
The Arch Lich laughed aloud and spread his arms.
His robe had been reduced to ash by my earlier attack. In its place, pitch-black mana poured from his entire body and took shape.
*That’s...*
A vortex of mana that felt ominous just to look at.
I instinctively realized what the Arch Lich was trying to do.
*A Gate.*
It was unstable, as if it might explode at any moment, but it had unmistakably taken the shape of a Gate.
The Arch Lich’s next words confirmed my suspicions.
“It is not yet complete, but... if I can merely bring you down, I should be able to complete everything.”
At the same time, a low voice that seemed to come from the heavens reverberated through the space.
“Descend upon this place. Gate Open.”
I had to stop it somehow. But pain slowed my body, and the change had already begun.
I stared wide-eyed at the sight that unfolded the next moment.
*Kwaaaaaaaaaaang!*
The few faint rays of sunlight piercing the ash-gray sky vanished completely.
The sky split with a thunderous roar, and a storm swept in every direction. In the void left behind, a mass of darkness rose like an ancient giant climbing to its feet.
*Fwoooooosh!*
The churning darkness surged from the heart of the ruined city.
As tall as a high-rise and wider than a soccer field, it dwarfed every Gate I had ever seen. The mere sight of it filled me with fear that seeped into my bones.
“Ah... ahh.”
Even the Skeleton Warlord, an undead monster, trembled before it.
I stood there with my mouth hanging open, staring blankly at the Gate. Then I suddenly realized something I had forgotten.
*I have to stop it. No matter what.*
The Gate might still be incomplete, but if this continued, an uncontrollable disaster would begin.
Millions—perhaps tens of millions—could die.
And among them...
Some might be my people.
Team Leader Choi, out on the battlefield. Xiao Shen, whom I had grown attached to despite our short time together.
If the Arch Lich moved beyond China and reached the Korean Peninsula... the members of the Peace Guild and even my beloved family would be in danger.
*I have to go.*
Will drove my body, paralyzed by pain and shock, back into motion.
I dredged up every last ounce of internal energy. My acupoints, already ravaged by internal injuries, screamed in pain, and blood burst anew from wounds all over my body.
But I did not stop.
I needed only one chance.
Just one.
*Flamefire Path.*
My battered leg pushed against the ground. A path of flame opened amid shattering pain.
At its end stood a single being.
The one who had started all of this.
The one who could end it all.
*Die.*
*One Annihilation.*
In the slowed world, I drew my spear back as far as I could and thrust.
The vortex unleashed with all my strength reached the Arch Lich.
*Kwaaaaaaaaaaang!*
And amid the blue flames filling the world, one laughter-laced word pierced my ears.
“Blink.”

chapters.title: Chapter 424
paragraphs: *Kwaaaaaaaaaa!*
The vortex wreathed in blue flame devoured everything in its path.
Ruined buildings with shattered concrete and bare steel frames. Human and monster corpses strewn together throughout the wreckage.
The ultrahigh heat burned and melted countless things.
All but one.
“Blink.”
All but him.
*Beep.*

**System Skill **One Annihilation** has been used! - All **internal energy** has been consumed! - Everything comes at a price. Despite your severe injuries, you have expended an excessive amount of power. - The status effect **Exhaustion** has been applied! Strength**, **Stamina**, and **Agility** have temporarily decreased drastically!
I felt the strength drain from my entire body. I could barely hear the System notification drilling into my ears—or the Skeleton Warlord’s shouts from inside my Inventory.
My body felt as heavy as waterlogged cotton, and only one thought kept circling through my cold, numb mind.
*That was my last chance.*
Why? Why hadn’t I known? Why hadn’t I guessed?
The Arch Lich had clearly said he had watched me through Familiars planted throughout the battlefield.
Then I should have accounted for the fact that I had used One Annihilation against the Liches and Death Knights on my way here.
Even if I could not be certain, I should at least have suspected it.
*Idiot.*
A self-deprecating laugh escaped me. I had sworn not to let my guard down... yet at the most important moment, I had made my greatest mistake.
Having no other choice was no excuse. A fight was not about the process, but the result.
And this was what letting my guard down had earned me.
*Clang!*
The iron spear slipped between my fingers and rolled across the ground. My legs, drained of strength, slowly gave way.
As I sank to my knees and lowered my head, a deep darkness fell over me.
“You, human. How does it feel to pay the price for your reckless bravado?”
I barely managed to raise my head and met a pair of burning red eye-lights. A voice squeezed through my cracked lips.
“Of course it feels like shit, you fucking bastard.”
“It was a fearsome strike. I shall commend you for that much.”
The Arch Lich’s voice was steeped in triumph.
Even his teleportation magic had not allowed him to evade One Annihilation completely. His left arm was gone.
But in the end, he was the one standing here as the victor.
The red eye-lights looking down at me, kneeling like a criminal, glimmered with joy.
“I waited until the very end. I restrained myself and endured the humiliation of suffering at a human’s hands. And at last... victory belongs to me.”
Smart. Cunning.
Just as I had thought, he had been waiting for me to use One Annihilation from the very beginning.

Earlier, I had swept away the Liches and Death Knights with One Annihilation, then recovered my stamina by leveling up. But the Arch Lich had not missed the fact that the attack had exhausted all my strength in an instant.
“Do you understand now? This is your limit. The limit of humanity.”
Limit.
That one word pierced deep into my chest.
The limit called F-rank, which I had been unable to escape no matter how hard I worked. The very limit I had continued to break through day after day after obtaining the System.
*Is this really as far as I go?*
I had worked myself nearly to death. For my own sake, and for the people I loved. No matter what danger came at me, I gritted my teeth and fought my way through it.
That was how I had lived.
Every step had been part of breaking through my limits.
“It’s not... over yet.”
The voice that slipped between my lips sounded like it belonged to someone else, utterly devoid of life.
I looked up at the Arch Lich through hazy eyes.
“What?”
“I said it’s not over yet.”
A life-and-death duel ended only when one of the two combatants fell.
So this fight was not over.
Only when one of us finally died would whoever remained standing be the victor.
I mumbled in my dazed state.
*Inventory open. Summon.*
One of the spears stored in my Inventory appeared in my hand.
No—I thought I had caught it, but it slipped from my grasp at once.
*Clang!*
The truth struck me again.
I no longer had the strength to hold a spear, much less the energy to swing one.
“Kehat! Kahahahah!”
The Arch Lich burst into wild laughter at the sight of me.
But I did not give up.
I couldn’t.
*Inventory open. Summon.*
I kept summoning weapons.
*Clang!*
And kept dropping them.
*Inventory open. Summon.*
*Clang!*
“Human. You foolish, stupid human!”
Even as the Arch Lich mocked me, I never stopped.
The courage to humbly accept death? If that was what people called courage, I would rather be a coward.
I would... survive. No matter what.
I believed that was the final courtesy I owed the life I had fought so hard to live—and the right answer.
*Inventory open. Summon.*
At that very moment—
*Ding.*

**System Endurance** has increased drastically. - The attribute **Endurance** has changed into **Will**! - Those with strong wills are not easily broken, nor do they fall. They will keep their will burning until the very end and fight with every ounce of their strength. - A strong will can sometimes produce the power to transcend one’s limits! - The special effect **Indomitable** has manifested. All attributes temporarily increase slightly, and fatigue is reduced!
I felt warmth spreading from deep within me.
Compared to the power I had once possessed, it was infinitesimal. Yet somehow, it was warmer than anything else.
It was the System’s answer to my desperate plea.
My final chance.
With my hand still trembling, I tightened my grip around the cold spear shaft.
I was not the only one who noticed the change.
The Arch Lich had been watching me as though I were a monkey in a zoo, but now his eye-lights widened. At that moment, I gathered every scrap of strength I had and hurled myself forward.
In a world slowed to a crawl, I thrust the spear toward the Arch Lich standing tall before me.
*Fwoooooosh!*
As the spearhead tore through the air with a piercing shriek, I saw it clearly.
The Arch Lich’s eye-lights curved like crescent moons.
He was mocking me.
“Blood Explosion.”
*Boom!*
An explosion.
Then a shock tore through my entire body.
My body, hurtling forward with every ounce of strength I possessed, abruptly locked up. The spear slipped from my hand and buried itself diagonally in the ground.
I blinked with both eyes, their tiny blood vessels burst. In a world dyed entirely red, something sticky and wet fell from the air and touched my face.
*Drip. Drip-drip-drip.*
Blood.
Blood had erupted from my entire body like a fountain and was now raining down around me.
I raised an arm that trembled like an aspen leaf and saw ragged flesh and stark-white bone.
Blood Explosion.
An explosion of blood.
Beyond my fading consciousness, I heard the Skeleton Warlord cry out.
“...Human!”
How long had he been shouting?
I wanted to answer, but all that spilled between my lips was blood mixed with bits of my organs.
“Cough.”
My vision spun.
I reached toward the Arch Lich, barely visible through the blood covering my face, but I could neither touch him nor reach him.
Perhaps I never would.
“Get a hold of yourself! You have to live!”
Like that needed saying.
Of course I did.
I had to survive, defeat the Arch Lich, and return to the place where I belonged.
But...
*Could I really do that?*
At that moment, the world slowly began to tilt.
No. The world was still.
I was the one tilting.
Unable to withstand the unending blood loss and injuries, my body was finally giving out.
*No. If I fall, it’s all over.*
I forced my already broken ankle to hold me upright.
The faint pain, no sharper than a thorn prick, was proof that I was dying. The Skeleton Warlord’s shouts, breaking through the static like a bad radio signal, were proof that I was still alive.
“...do it, human! Hurry!”
Do what? What?
“Summon me right n—!”
My ruptured eardrums and fading consciousness could not make out the Skeleton Warlord’s words.
Even if I had heard him clearly, I could not have stopped what the Arch Lich did next.
“You possess an interesting item.”
At some point, a familiar object had appeared in the Arch Lich’s hand.
White Flame, my beloved spear that had accompanied me through countless battles, flared in a stranger’s grasp.
But even as his finger bones burned, the Arch Lich merely laughed.
“I have received an extravagant gift. I should return it to its owner now.”
The Arch Lich drew back his arm. Powerful mana suppressed White Flame’s flames and surged toward the spearhead.
“Farewell, new Adversary—or perhaps merely a foolish human who might have been the Adversary.”
*Fwoosh!*
The sound of the spear cutting through the air was brief.
The moment felt eternal.
I silently watched White Flame streak toward me like a flash of light. Countless possibilities raced through my mind before I finally reached a conclusion.
*I can’t dodge it.*
Then only one ending remained.
Death.
I had fought countless battles over the past seven years, but never had the word *death* felt so close.
All I could do was watch it approach.
*Yeah. It’s over.*
The instant I calmly repeated those words to myself—
*Crack!*
White Flame’s spearhead shattered bone and punched through the center of a chest.
My eyes flew wide, and I froze.
Not from pain.
From shock.
“What?”
Unable to find the words, I stared at the blue eye-lights flickering inches from my face.
The Skeleton Warlord, previously no more than a skull the size of a soccer ball, now stood two meters tall. He spoke in his usual gruff voice.
“Do not ask how I managed to come out on my own. This commander has no idea, either.”
“Then why? Why did you...”
I looked at him as I asked.
The spearhead had pierced the Skeleton Warlord’s back and chest, stopping exactly one handspan away from me.
If no one had blocked it, it would have killed me and then some.
The Skeleton Warlord had thrown himself in front of me and saved my life.
“...I do not know that either. Damn it. I do not know anything anymore. Perhaps this sword bewitched me.”
Only then did I recognize the sword in the Skeleton Warlord’s hand.
“Hero’s Soul.”
Lei Fei’s only remaining keepsake.
A sword that could not even be held by someone unworthy of becoming a hero.
That very Hero’s Soul was now in the Skeleton Warlord’s hand.
In the hand of a Named Monster that was not even human.
“Hero’s Soul. That is a decent name for something named by humans. No, to be honest, it is cool. It is a shame I was too late to swing it properly...”
The Skeleton Warlord’s voice faded.
The light was slowly disappearing from his blue eye-lights, which had always shone so clearly.
I knew what this meant.
*Erasure.*
There was no doubt.
Even now, the Arch Lich’s mana carried within White Flame’s spearhead was rapidly eating away at the Skeleton Warlord.
“Say no more. I already regret this enough as it is.”
I did not believe him.
His words were gruff, but I heard the quiet laugh behind them.
“Human. There is something I wish to ask.”
The Arch Lich was approaching beyond the Skeleton Warlord’s slowly crumbling shoulder, but I silently nodded.
“Anything.”
After hesitating for a moment, the Skeleton Warlord asked in a small voice,
“What you said last time. Did you mean it?”
“Last time? What did I...? Ah.”
I suddenly remembered.
It had been right after Lei Fei’s death, when the Skeleton Warlord was thinking about the past he could no longer remember.
And the words I had casually tossed his way.
“Well, I think he was probably a pretty decent guy.”
“...Huh? Were you saying that to this commander?”
“No. Just talking to myself.”
“Ahem. Right?”
So that was why.
That was what it had been about.
For the Skeleton Warlord, who had awakened after drawing strength from a spirit that had lost all its memories, I might have been his only friend—the one who had always been by his side.
One small remark I had tossed out like a pebble had sent ripples through the pond of his heart.
*What an idiot.*
Why did that matter? Why was one little thing worth going this far?
For a moment, I could not speak. Something hot rose inside me, but I forced it down and barely managed to answer.
“Of course I meant it.”
“Yes. I see.”
The Skeleton Warlord’s flickering blue eye-lights curved into a smile.
At that very moment, a chilling voice rang out and brought everything to an end.
“Have you finished saying your farewells?”
“Bone Explosion.”
*Boom!*
I instinctively crossed both arms over my face. The impact swept through my entire body and sent me flying.
When I barely managed to push myself upright, I saw a skull soaring high into the air and bones shattering into countless pieces.
And...
That was all.
The Skeleton Warlord was nowhere to be seen.
*Thud!*
Hero’s Soul fell from the air and plunged deep into the ground.
Along with the hand of someone who had never released its hilt, even at the very end.

chapters.title: Chapter 425
paragraphs: *Clang-clatter!*
White Flame, having lost its target, rolled across the ground.
*Ah.*
The Arch Lich snapped his fingers at me as I stood frozen like a statue. A pair of black hands materialized in midair and constricted around my entire body.
He no longer needed an incantation to cast his magic.
*Step. Step.*
With every step the Arch Lich took, something seeped into various parts of his body, which was as hazy as mist.
The left arm that had vanished in One Annihilation slowly regenerated, while his shattered, fractured bones knit back together, sturdier than before and gleaming with an even darker hue.
The closer the Gate came to completion, the stronger the Arch Lich became.
—So there was a reason I smelled death upon you. Friendship between a human and a monster... How touching.
*Crack.*
I heard bones shifting out of place throughout my body, but I stared blankly over the Arch Lich’s shoulder.
More precisely, at the sword buried in the ground—and the hand of someone who had held on to its hilt until the very end.
*The Skeleton Warlord.*
Humans and monsters were sworn enemies, as ordained by God.
The same had been true of me and the Skeleton Warlord. At least, it had been at first.
But... now I finally understood. At some point, the Skeleton Warlord had stopped being a monster to me.
*If I’d still thought of him as a monster, I would’ve erased him with my own hands.*
If I had killed the Skeleton Warlord myself, the resulting level-up might have given me one last hope.
But I had hesitated, and ultimately given up.
Not because he had saved my life. Because in my heart, I had already accepted him as a friend.
A hollow laugh escaped me.
*Damn it. I never should’ve gotten attached.*
The Arch Lich’s eye-lights narrowed at the sight of me.
—Are you laughing? In a situation like this?
“My mother used to say that fortune comes to those who smile.”
—You have lost your mind.
“Why the fuck do you care if I laugh? What are you, my immediate senior in the army?”
I spat toward the Arch Lich’s face. A thick liquid, impossible to distinguish as blood or phlegm, trickled down between his brows.
At the same time, the red eye-lights in the places where his eyes should have been flared violently.
—I heard your answer clearly.
“Go eat a dick.”
It would have been a lie to say I had no regrets about the life I had lived, but none of that mattered now. Regret always came too late, and I had fought until the bitter end.
I had done enough.
Once I let go of everything, it all felt like one long dream. My face, smiling peacefully at the Arch Lich’s eye-lights, was reflected in them.
—I told you, did I not? Your flesh would be torn to pieces, and your soul would wander the River of Death forever.
I readily nodded in agreement.
“I guess so. Just like that Demon King bastard you serve.”
“If I run into him, I’ll give him your regards. What’s his address?”
—...We shall see how long you can continue spouting such nonsense.
At the Arch Lich’s gesture, the enormous hands of mana squeezing me seized all four of my limbs. Then they began pulling my body apart with tremendous force.
Slowly.
Little by little.
*Crack. Craaack.*
Small ruptures sounded inside me, and the sensation of pain I had momentarily forgotten awakened.
I thought I no longer had the strength even to scream, but a cry tore itself from between my lips.
“Gnh... graaaaagh!”
—That sounds much better.
Pain bleached my vision white. I let out all the screams I had been holding back and waited for death to come.
But when even the pain began to fade, what came for me was not death.
It was a System notification.
*Beep.*

**System High-grade Potion** has been used! - The amount of potion used is too small. Your injuries have been healed slightly! - Your injuries are extremely severe. You require a greater amount of higher-quality healing than this!
...What?
A cool sensation spread through me, and the pain surged back to life. My eyes flew open.
The Arch Lich was staring at me with mockery gleaming in his eye-lights.
And in his hand was a glass bottle.
*That’s...*
It was one of the potions that had been in Lee Jungryong’s subspace pocket—the one the Arch Lich had stolen long ago.
And now he was using a potion made for healing as an instrument of torture.
Just enough healing to keep me poised at the threshold of death.
Just enough to make me feel the greatest possible pain.
—Foolish human. Did you truly think this body would grant you such an easy, peaceful death?
—Continue to howl. Weep like a coward and writhe in agony. Only once you have realized your folly shall you be permitted to cross into the River of Death.
The Arch Lich shook the glass bottle, his voice thick with mockery.
Not even a tenth of the potion was gone. The amount that remained represented all the pain I had yet to endure.
Time would crawl by without end, each moment stretching into an eternity.
Weak healing spread through my body, but so did pain that came crashing down over every inch of me. My breathing grew ragged. I forced a smile and asked the Arch Lich,
“If I give three cheers for the Demon King, will you finish me off sooner?”
—Perhaps. If you do so with sufficient passion and sincerity, I may consider it.
“I’m not doing that, you son of a bitch.”
—Very well. We have plenty of time, after all. There is no harm in considering it at your leisure—
*Crunch!*
The Arch Lich’s eye-lights trembled.
So did I.
Neither of us had expected what happened next.
No one had.
—...What is this?
With a doubtful voice, the Arch Lich looked down at his chest.
Light.
It was light. A dazzling radiance bright enough to illuminate the entire world had burst through his chest.
*No. That isn’t light.*
I stared at it with vacant eyes.
It was a sword, shining more brilliantly than ever before.
I knew the name of that all-too-familiar sword.
*Hero’s Soul.*
And I knew the owner of the hand wrapped tightly around its hilt beyond the Arch Lich’s skeletal chest.
It was as if the entire world had stopped moving.
In that impossibly slowed world, I watched hundreds—thousands—of bone fragments gather.
They had been nothing more than the last traces someone had left behind, but now they pulled toward one another and began taking shape.
*Click. Clack!*
Bones fused together.
Two arms and two legs formed first, followed by a chest and abdomen.
The black sheen washed from the bones beneath the radiance spilling from Hero’s Soul. Before long, they had taken on a soft golden hue, growing longer and sturdier.
*Ah.*
It was an astonishing sight.

Countless fragments of bone gathered to form a body, as though time itself were flowing backward. The light streaming from the sword drove the darkness from every joint, heralding the birth of a new being.
And finally, when a skull settled onto the completed body—
*Flash!*
Golden eye-lights burst from its empty sockets.
The feeling was both utterly familiar and completely strange.
The next moment, a voice rang out, and the time that had stopped began to flow again.
—You asked me why, did you not?
My body trembled as if lightning had pierced through me. A memory from less than an hour ago flashed through my mind.
*Then why, exactly?*
Yes. That was what I had asked back then.
Why had he saved me? Why had he chosen to become my shield even though he had been prepared to face Erasure?
He had said he did not know. He did not know why he had done such a thing. Perhaps the sword had bewitched him.
And now, the answer I had not heard then pierced my ears.
—Because though you are devious, you are a pretty decent human. That was all.
*A pretty decent guy.*
Words I had once said to someone.
I stared at him in disbelief.
His faintly golden body was larger and sturdier than before. An unknown silver pattern was engraved across the forehead of his skull, resembling a crown.
No.
It was unmistakably a crown.
**System Lv. 160 Skeleton King**
The moment I saw the System window hovering above his head, a hollow laugh escaped me.
“Look how much you’ve grown, Bones.”
—No wonder I have felt itchy all over for so long.
The small black caterpillar had finally shed its skin and spread its wings.
The Skeleton Warlord—or rather, the Skeleton King’s eye-lights curved like crescent moons.
He was smiling.
So was I.
And there was one being who could not smile.
—Graaaagh! Graaaaaaaaaagh!
The Arch Lich.
The unprecedented Named Monster, who commanded hundreds of thousands of undead and possessed inexhaustible, tremendous mana, writhed in agony.
A single sword had pierced straight through the center of his chest.
The golden radiance flowing from Hero’s Soul devoured his mana and melted his body.
Perhaps even his soul.
—Human.
At the Skeleton King’s quiet call, I realized what I had to do.
*Now... let’s finish this.*
*Beep.*
**System Hero’s Soul** grants you the light of healing! - All status effects have been removed! - All injuries have been healed, and all attributes restored! - Someone who is not here smiles at you.
*Fwoooooosh!*
A pillar of light burst from Hero’s Soul and enveloped me.

Gentle warmth flooded my body. Shattered bones knit together, torn flesh healed, and my damaged organs and meridians recovered. At the same time, heat seethed through me like lava, ready to erupt at any moment.
*I can do this.*
The certainty was so absolute that it surprised even me.
And it was true.
With this strength, there was nothing I could not do.
*Come.*
*Fwoooooosh! Clack!*
At the same time that I pulled White Flame, rolling across the ground, into my hand—
*Fwoosh!*
I thrust out my foot, feeling myself rise into the air.
At the end of that step stood the Arch Lich, writhing in agony as streams of tremendous mana poured from his body.
—What in the world! What magic have you used?!
The Arch Lich spotted me and shrieked in a frenzy.
His red eye-lights shook wildly, swelling larger and larger.
That alone told me how much pain he was in.
—Damn you! Damn you, human! Graaaaagh!
Instead of answering, I slowly raised White Flame.
I aimed its transparent spearhead at the Arch Lich, whose limbs were trembling violently from the pain, and at the enormous Gate looming behind him.
*Whoosh.*

The fire dragon spread its wings and soared from my dantian, transforming into a ball of flame as it surged through every limb and bone in my body. It flowed along my fingertips, kindling blue flames atop White Flame’s spearhead and layering them over and over.
—You cur! How dare you—
The Arch Lich flailed his arms and legs in a frenzy, but the magic he fired collided with the heat surrounding me like a barrier and vanished before it could even reach me.
Unlike the weakened Arch Lich, however, the darkness around the Gate churned with ever greater violence.
And at last, I realized.
*Now!*
White Flame trembled as rotational force traveled up through my leg, waist, shoulder, and wrist.
The unprecedented surge of qi drawn from my entire body kindled flames larger than ever before.
Yes.
This was the moment.
*Fwoosh.*
One step.
All the space separating the Arch Lich and me vanished, and time slowed.
Before the Arch Lich’s slowly moving lips could finish the incantation, I launched a single strike filled with every ounce of my will and strength.
—Blink...!
*One Annihilation.*
There would be no second mistake.
The blue fire dragon bursting from White Flame’s spearhead swallowed both the Arch Lich and the Gate.
*Kwooooooooooong!*

sentences.text: *Clang-clatter!*
White Flame, having lost its target, rolled across the ground.
*Ah.*
The Arch Lich snapped his fingers at me as I stood frozen like a statue.
A pair of black hands materialized in midair and constricted around my entire body.
He no longer needed an incantation to cast his magic.
*Step.
Step.*
With every step the Arch Lich took, something seeped into various parts of his body, which was as hazy as mist.
The left arm that had vanished in One Annihilation slowly regenerated, while his shattered, fractured bones knit back together, sturdier than before and gleaming with an even darker hue.
The closer the Gate came to completion, the stronger the Arch Lich became.
—So there was a reason I smelled death upon you.
Friendship between a human and a monster...
How touching.
*Crack.*
I heard bones shifting out of place throughout my body, but I stared blankly over the Arch Lich’s shoulder.
More precisely, at the sword buried in the ground—and the hand of someone who had held on to its hilt until the very end.
*The Skeleton Warlord.*
Humans and monsters were sworn enemies, as ordained by God.
The same had been true of me and the Skeleton Warlord.
At least, it had been at first.
But... now I finally understood.
At some point, the Skeleton Warlord had stopped being a monster to me.
*If I’d still thought of him as a monster, I would’ve erased him with my own hands.*
If I had killed the Skeleton Warlord myself, the resulting level-up might have given me one last hope.
But I had hesitated, and ultimately given up.
Not because he had saved my life.
Because in my heart, I had already accepted him as a friend.
A hollow laugh escaped me.
*Damn it.
I never should’ve gotten attached.*
The Arch Lich’s eye-lights narrowed at the sight of me.
—Are you laughing?
In a situation like this?
“My mother used to say that fortune comes to those who smile.”
—You have lost your mind.
“Why the fuck do you care if I laugh?
What are you, my immediate senior in the army?”
I spat toward the Arch Lich’s face.
A thick liquid, impossible to distinguish as blood or phlegm, trickled down between his brows.
At the same time, the red eye-lights in the places where his eyes should have been flared violently.
—I heard your answer clearly.
“Go eat a dick.”
It would have been a lie to say I had no regrets about the life I had lived, but none of that mattered now.
Regret always came too late, and I had fought until the bitter end.
I had done enough.
Once I let go of everything, it all felt like one long dream.
My face, smiling peacefully at the Arch Lich’s eye-lights, was reflected in them.
—I told you, did I not?
Your flesh would be torn to pieces, and your soul would wander the River of Death forever.
I readily nodded in agreement.
“I guess so.
Just like that Demon King bastard you serve.”
“If I run into him, I’ll give him your regards.
What’s his address?”
—...We shall see how long you can continue spouting such nonsense.
At the Arch Lich’s gesture, the enormous hands of mana squeezing me seized all four of my limbs.
Then they began pulling my body apart with tremendous force.
Slowly.
Little by little.
*Crack.
Craaack.*
Small ruptures sounded inside me, and the sensation of pain I had momentarily forgotten awakened.
I thought I no longer had the strength even to scream, but a cry tore itself from between my lips.
“Gnh... graaaaagh!”
—That sounds much better.
Pain bleached my vision white.
I let out all the screams I had been holding back and waited for death to come.
But when even the pain began to fade, what came for me was not death.
It was a System notification.
*Beep.*
**System High-grade Potion** has been used! - The amount of potion used is too small.
Your injuries have been healed slightly! - Your injuries are extremely severe.
You require a greater amount of higher-quality healing than this!
...What?
A cool sensation spread through me, and the pain surged back to life.
My eyes flew open.
The Arch Lich was staring at me with mockery gleaming in his eye-lights.
And in his hand was a glass bottle.
*That’s...*
It was one of the potions that had been in Lee Jungryong’s subspace pocket—the one the Arch Lich had stolen long ago.
And now he was using a potion made for healing as an instrument of torture.
Just enough healing to keep me poised at the threshold of death.
Just enough to make me feel the greatest possible pain.
—Foolish human.
Did you truly think this body would grant you such an easy, peaceful death?
—Continue to howl.
Weep like a coward and writhe in agony.
Only once you have realized your folly shall you be permitted to cross into the River of Death.
The Arch Lich shook the glass bottle, his voice thick with mockery.
Not even a tenth of the potion was gone.
The amount that remained represented all the pain I had yet to endure.
Time would crawl by without end, each moment stretching into an eternity.
Weak healing spread through my body, but so did pain that came crashing down over every inch of me.
My breathing grew ragged.
I forced a smile and asked the Arch Lich,
“If I give three cheers for the Demon King, will you finish me off sooner?”
—Perhaps.
If you do so with sufficient passion and sincerity, I may consider it.
“I’m not doing that, you son of a bitch.”
—Very well.
We have plenty of time, after all.
There is no harm in considering it at your leisure—
*Crunch!*
The Arch Lich’s eye-lights trembled.
So did I.
Neither of us had expected what happened next.
No one had.
—...What is this?
With a doubtful voice, the Arch Lich looked down at his chest.
Light.
It was light.
A dazzling radiance bright enough to illuminate the entire world had burst through his chest.
*No.
That isn’t light.*
I stared at it with vacant eyes.
It was a sword, shining more brilliantly than ever before.
I knew the name of that all-too-familiar sword.
*Hero’s Soul.*
And I knew the owner of the hand wrapped tightly around its hilt beyond the Arch Lich’s skeletal chest.
It was as if the entire world had stopped moving.
In that impossibly slowed world, I watched hundreds—thousands—of bone fragments gather.
They had been nothing more than the last traces someone had left behind, but now they pulled toward one another and began taking shape.
*Click.

Bones fused together.

The black sheen washed from the bones beneath the radiance spilling from Hero’s Soul.

*Ah.*
It was an astonishing sight.
Countless fragments of bone gathered to form a body, as though time itself were flowing backward.

Golden eye-lights burst from its empty sockets.

chapters.title: Chapter 426
paragraphs: *Fwoooooosh!*
The instant the Arch Lich faced the enormous fire dragon that burst from the spearhead, it realized the truth.
*Too late.*
There was no avoiding this attack.
The Spell it had not yet managed to unleash and the magical power that had been on the verge of completion scattered beneath the flames rushing straight toward it.
The fire dragon, blazing with hellfire, opened its jaws at the Arch Lich, which had frozen in place, oblivious even to the pain.
*Kwooooooong!*
Blue flames swept in every direction with a thunderous roar like that of a dragon. The terrible heat distorted space and vaporized everything in its path.
The Arch Lich felt the magical power and barriers surrounding it melt away. It even felt a sensation it had long since forgotten.
*It’s hot.*
*Fwoosh!*
Blue hellfire filled the Arch Lich’s vision. The fire dragon swept over its entire body and continued onward without stopping.
Straight toward the enormous black door towering over the center of the ruined city.
The Gate.
*No!*
The Arch Lich’s red eye-lights flared wide as it stretched out a hand, but no voice emerged. The fire dragon swallowed the Gate, which was as large as itself, whole.
The moment the unprecedented mass of magical power gathered from the life force of hundreds of thousands of humans collided with the flames, a blinding flash erupted.
*Fwoosh!*
A pillar of light rose into the sky, bright enough to be seen from hundreds, perhaps thousands, of kilometers away.

Darkness and blue flames collided with one another, then soon blended together. The forest of buildings that had been struggling to remain standing bent at the waist, and a ring of wind burst outward.
*Krrrrooooom—*
A roar and tremor beyond description shook the world.
The gray sky split apart, and the dense fog blanketing the entire city scattered like heat haze.
Then, as though everything that had just happened were a distant dream, silence descended.
*Ah.*
The Arch Lich gazed hollowly upon the world.
The scene looked no different from before, but it knew. Everything had changed, itself included.
Everything had collapsed like a sandcastle.
The Arch Lich slowly turned its head. Its trembling red eye-lights settled on the lone figure standing tall as an iron tower.
—“I should have killed you.”
The single sentence broke the silence.

Jin Taekyung opened his mouth, his complexion utterly bloodless. The accumulated damage and mental exhaustion from his endless battles made him look as though he might collapse at any moment, but his voice alone had not lost its strength.
“Yeah. You should’ve killed me sooner.”
The Arch Lich fell silent.
It had no one but itself to blame for missing its chance to end Jin Taekyung’s life.
One brief lapse in vigilance had reduced everything to nothing.
*My king. Please forgive this disloyal servant.*
The Arch Lich begged forgiveness from its king, wherever he might be.
If it had killed Jin Taekyung without delay... If the monster that had sided with the human had not been reborn as a new being and driven that damned sword into its chest...
Everything would have gone according to plan.
It would have survived and completed the Gate. At the head of an unimaginably vast monster army, it would have hunted down those verminous humans, slaughtered them, and burned the city to the ground.
All while awaiting the great king’s eventual return.
But the plan it had believed perfect had fallen apart spectacularly.
All because of a single human.
Jin Taekyung.
The Arch Lich’s fading red eye-lights flared with the last of their strength.
A vow to itself and an oath of vengeance spilled toward Jin Taekyung.
—“Remember me. Remember this body, which will one day trample your souls beneath its bare feet.”
Jin Taekyung spat out a wad of phlegm.
“Big talk from a bastard who’s about to croak. Go on. Say, ‘Asmodeus is a fucking son of a bitch.’”
The Skeleton King hesitantly opened its mouth.
—“Asmodeus is a fucking son of a bitch...”
“...Not you.”
—“Ah, I know. I just wanted to try it once. But I cannot say that I feel good after uttering something so blasphemous.”
“What’s the problem? You’re a king now, too.”
—“Oh. That is true.”
*I swear upon the River of Death that I will tear those two apart.*
The Arch Lich stretched both hands toward Jin Taekyung and the Skeleton King.
Its skeletal hands clenched as if they would crush the two figures standing far away, but nothing happened.
Instead, a wind that had blown in from somewhere brushed against its entire body.
*Whoooooosh.*
It was collapse.
Beginning with its hands, which turned to ash and scattered, everything that made up the Arch Lich began to crumble.
Its arms. Its legs. Its chest.
And finally, even the skull housing its red eye-lights.
—“Please survive. Until the day we meet again...”
Its final voice, filled with resentment, vanished into the wind.
The wind grew stronger and swept onward, carrying the ashes of what had once been the Arch Lich.
Everything caught within the range of One Annihilation sank and crumbled wherever the wind passed. High-rise buildings, heaps of concrete, overturned cars, and corpses long since emptied of life...
Even the enormous, unfinished Gate that would have marked the beginning of an even greater war.
*Fssshhh.*
As Jin Taekyung silently watched it all, clear chimes rang in his ears—sounds that only he could hear.
*Ding. Ding. Ding.*
Countless System messages filled his vision. They were a victory salute announcing that everything was finally over.
But Jin Taekyung had already exhausted every last bit of his strength, and his body was tipping toward the ground.
*I did it.*
With that final thought, a deep and peaceful sleep overtook him.
The Skeleton King carefully caught Jin Taekyung as he fell and saw the faint smile on his lips.
—“...You worked hard.”
*Devious though he may be, he really is a pretty decent human.*
Murmuring inwardly, the Skeleton King was about to carry Jin Taekyung somewhere safe and comfortable when it remembered something.
—“Ah, right. The sword.”
*Was it called Hero’s Soul?*
It did not know who had named it, but there was no doubt that the sword held a mysterious power.

That sword had awakened it from the brink of Erasure when it had still been the Skeleton Warlord. It was also thanks to the sword that it had managed to deal such a devastating blow to the terrifying Arch Lich.
—“I almost forgot. I need to make sure to keep it safe.”
It did not take long to find. The sword that had remained embedded in its target’s chest until the very end lay quietly where the Arch Lich had stood only moments ago.
But after picking up **Hero’s Soul**, the Skeleton King tilted its head.
—“Huh? Something feels strange.”
It was a peculiar sensation, difficult to explain.
It could not quite put its finger on it, but... how should it describe the feeling? The sword was undeniably a fine blade, yet it no longer possessed the same mysterious quality as before.
—“Did I pick up the wrong sword?”
But no matter how thoroughly the Skeleton King searched the area or examined the blade, nothing changed.
It scratched its golden skull and pondered the matter for a while before finally reaching a conclusion.
—“Hmm. I guess this is it.”
It was probably just a fleeting impression. The sword looked exactly as it remembered, and it had seen the weapon fall from the Arch Lich’s chest with its own eyes.
*Then why does this feel so unsettling?*
It made no sense at all.
The Skeleton King shook its head and slid the sword between its pelvic bones for safekeeping.
As it headed toward the unconscious Jin Taekyung, it remained unaware of what had happened the moment Jin Taekyung exhausted all his strength and lost consciousness.
Mist-like black energy had mingled with the wind scattering into the distance.
And the golden light dwelling within **Hero’s Soul** had left the sword to pursue it.
But one being was different.
The black energy drifted away on the wind.
Reduced by Jin Taekyung to a tiny, powerless fragment of a soul, the Arch Lich stared wide-eyed at the dazzling golden light blocking its path.
*This is impossible.*
The words it had spoken to Jin Taekyung and the Skeleton King before losing its form had contained no trace of falsehood.
It would return in the near future. With even greater power and an even larger army of monsters, it would stain this land with blood.
Life Force Vessel.
The highest order of black magic available only to the undead—a vessel capable of preserving a fragment of the soul.
So long as it had that, the Arch Lich could escape eternal Erasure.
Or so it had believed, until that brilliant golden light barred its way.
—“You... What are you?”
The Arch Lich was now only a pitiful fragment of a soul, utterly insignificant compared to the power emanating from the light.
The black energy writhed violently with rage, confusion, and fear.
Yet even though the Arch Lich’s thoughts reached it, the golden light did not respond. It merely shone brighter and swelled larger.
Then, in the next moment, the Arch Lich realized what the light truly was.
*That is not magic. It is a soul.*
The soul of someone it had once shattered and trampled beneath its feet. A fragment of a soul that had lost even its form, yet remained within the sword through sheer will alone.
Suddenly, the Arch Lich recalled a memory it had buried deep within its mind.
“How noble, human. What is your name?”
That day, when blood had formed rivers and corpses had formed mountains.
One human had remained standing until the very end in a city filled with nothing but destruction and death.
—“Lei Fei.”
The Arch Lich—or rather, the black energy—stopped dead.
A dazzling golden light burst through the air and swept over it like a wave.
*Fwoooooosh!*
*...Damn it.*
That was the Arch Lich’s final thought.
The battle raged fiercely around the main force.
While the S-rank Hunters had moved toward the rear with part of the army to clear a path for the suicide squad, the tens of thousands of monsters had seized the opportunity and charged.
“Fire Rain!”
*Kwaaang!*
The mage units in the rear unleashed an area-wide spell, and a rain of fire poured from the sky.
Hundreds of monsters burned to death, reduced to charred lumps. The mages clenched their fists at the sight.
Then—
*Whoooooosh! Thwack!*
One of the mages wiped the blood from their face with a bewildered expression.
The face of the comrade who had been smiling at them only moments ago was gone.
No—it had burst apart.
A black spear had crossed the distance like a beam of light and struck them.
*Whoooooosh! Boom!*
Another spear flew in and skewered six or seven mages like meat on a spit.
Only then did the belated screams erupt.
“Aaaaargh!”
“Death Knights! They’re Death Knights!”
“Fuck, what the hell are you talking about? Didn’t we take care of all of them?”
“I-I don’t think so! It looks like they hid their elites separately among the others!”
Those words soon proved true.
Having clearly recognized the absence of the S-rank Hunters, the elite monsters revealed themselves, and an unstoppable slaughter began.
*Slash!*
*Kwaaang!*
Death Knights, Liches, and dozens of Wyverns that had remained out of sight appeared and launched a ferocious assault.
People died without end, and monsters surged forward without pause.
With even the S-rank Hunters away from their positions, deep despair settled over the faces of those risking their lives to hold the line.
*It’s all over.*
Then, just as everyone thought of death—
*Shiiiiing!*
A Death Knight’s sword stopped in the middle of cutting through someone.
No.
It crumbled into ash.
“W-What the hell...?”
The Hunter who had narrowly escaped death looked around and gaped.
The sight before him was unbelievable.
First, hundreds fell.
Then thousands crumbled.
Before long, monsters numbering in the tens of thousands were turning to ash and scattering.
*Whoooooosh.*
At long last, the war was over.

Remember this body, which will one day trample your souls beneath its bare feet.”
Jin Taekyung spat out a wad of phlegm.
“Big talk from a bastard who’s about to croak.
Go on.
Say, ‘Asmodeus is a fucking son of a bitch.’”
The Skeleton King hesitantly opened its mouth.
—“Asmodeus is a fucking son of a bitch...”
“...Not you.”
—“Ah, I know.
I just wanted to try it once.
But I cannot say that I feel good after uttering something so blasphemous.”
“What’s the problem?
You’re a king now, too.”
—“Oh.
That is true.”
*I swear upon the River of Death that I will tear those two apart.*
The Arch Lich stretched both hands toward Jin Taekyung and the Skeleton King.
Its skeletal hands clenched as if they would crush the two figures standing far away, but nothing happened.
Instead, a wind that had blown in from somewhere brushed against its entire body.
*Whoooooosh.*
It was collapse.
Beginning with its hands, which turned to ash and scattered, everything that made up the Arch Lich began to crumble.
Its arms.
Its legs.
Its chest.
And finally, even the skull housing its red eye-lights.
—“Please survive.
Until the day we meet again...”
Its final voice, filled with resentment, vanished into the wind.
The wind grew stronger and swept onward, carrying the ashes of what had once been the Arch Lich.
Everything caught within the range of One Annihilation sank and crumbled wherever the wind passed.
High-rise buildings, heaps of concrete, overturned cars, and corpses long since emptied of life...
Even the enormous, unfinished Gate that would have marked the beginning of an even greater war.
*Fssshhh.*
As Jin Taekyung silently watched it all, clear chimes rang in his ears—sounds that only he could hear.
*Ding.
Ding.
Ding.*
Countless System messages filled his vision.
They were a victory salute announcing that everything was finally over.
But Jin Taekyung had already exhausted every last bit of his strength, and his body was tipping toward the ground.
*I did it.*
With that final thought, a deep and peaceful sleep overtook him.
The Skeleton King carefully caught Jin Taekyung as he fell and saw the faint smile on his lips.
—“...You worked hard.”
*Devious though he may be, he really is a pretty decent human.*
Murmuring inwardly, the Skeleton King was about to carry Jin Taekyung somewhere safe and comfortable when it remembered something.
—“Ah, right.
The sword.”
*Was it called Hero’s Soul?*
It did not know who had named it, but there was no doubt that the sword held a mysterious power.
That sword had awakened it from the brink of Erasure when it had still been the Skeleton Warlord.
It was also thanks to the sword that it had managed to deal such a devastating blow to the terrifying Arch Lich.
—“I almost forgot.
I need to make sure to keep it safe.”
It did not take long to find.
The sword that had remained embedded in its target’s chest until the very end lay quietly where the Arch Lich had stood only moments ago.
But after picking up **Hero’s Soul**, the Skeleton King tilted its head.
—“Huh?
Something feels strange.”
It was a peculiar sensation, difficult to explain.
It could not quite put its finger on it, but... how should it describe the feeling?
The sword was undeniably a fine blade, yet it no longer possessed the same mysterious quality as before.
—“Did I pick up the wrong sword?”
But no matter how thoroughly the Skeleton King searched the area or examined the blade, nothing changed.
It scratched its golden skull and pondered the matter for a while before finally reaching a conclusion.
—“Hmm.
I guess this is it.”
It was probably just a fleeting impression.
The sword looked exactly as it remembered, and it had seen the weapon fall from the Arch Lich’s chest with its own eyes.
*Then why does this feel so unsettling?*
It made no sense at all.
The Skeleton King shook its head and slid the sword between its pelvic bones for safekeeping.
As it headed toward the unconscious Jin Taekyung, it remained unaware of what had happened the moment Jin Taekyung exhausted all his strength and lost consciousness.
Mist-like black energy had mingled with the wind scattering into the distance.
And the golden light dwelling within **Hero’s Soul** had left the sword to pursue it.
But one being was different.
The black energy drifted away on the wind.
Reduced by Jin Taekyung to a tiny, powerless fragment of a soul, the Arch Lich stared wide-eyed at the dazzling golden light blocking its path.
*This is impossible.*
The words it had spoken to Jin Taekyung and the Skeleton King before losing its form had contained no trace of falsehood.
It would return in the near future.
With even greater power and an even larger army of monsters, it would stain this land with blood.
Life Force Vessel.
The highest order of black magic available only to the undead—a vessel capable of preserving a fragment of the soul.
So long as it had that, the Arch Lich could escape eternal Erasure.
Or so it had believed, until that brilliant golden light barred its way.
What are you?”
The Arch Lich was now only a pitiful fragment of a soul, utterly insignificant compared to the power emanating from the light.
The black energy writhed violently with rage, confusion, and fear.
Yet even though the Arch Lich’s thoughts reached it, the golden light did not respond.
It merely shone brighter and swelled larger.
Then, in the next moment, the Arch Lich realized what the light truly was.
*That is not magic.
It is a soul.*
The soul of someone it had once shattered and trampled beneath its feet.
A fragment of a soul that had lost even its form, yet remained within the sword through sheer will alone.
Suddenly, the Arch Lich recalled a memory it had buried deep within its mind.
“How noble, human.
What is your name?”
That day, when blood had formed rivers and corpses had formed mountains.
One human had remained standing until the very end in a city filled with nothing but destruction and death.
—“Lei Fei.”
The Arch Lich—or rather, the black energy—stopped dead.
A dazzling golden light burst through the air and swept over it like a wave.
*Fwoooooosh!*
*...Damn it.*
That was the Arch Lich’s final thought.
The battle raged fiercely around the main force.
While the S-rank Hunters had moved toward the rear with part of the army to clear a path for the suicide squad, the tens of thousands of monsters had seized the opportunity and charged.
“Fire Rain!”
*Kwaaang!*
The mage units in the rear unleashed an area-wide spell, and a rain of fire poured from the sky.
Hundreds of monsters burned to death, reduced to charred lumps.
The mages clenched their fists at the sight.
Then—
*Whoooooosh!
Thwack!*
One of the mages wiped the blood from their face with a bewildered expression.
The face of the comrade who had been smiling at them only moments ago was gone.
No—it had burst apart.
A black spear had crossed the distance like a beam of light and struck them.
*Whoooooosh!
Boom!*
Another spear flew in and skewered six or seven mages like meat on a spit.
Only then did the belated screams erupt.
“Aaaaargh!”
“Death Knights!
They’re Death Knights!”
“Fuck, what the hell are you talking about?
Didn’t we take care of all of them?”
“I-I don’t think so!
It looks like they hid their elites separately among the others!”
Those words soon proved true.
Having clearly recognized the absence of the S-rank Hunters, the elite monsters revealed themselves, and an unstoppable slaughter began.
*Slash!*
*Kwaaang!*
Death Knights, Liches, and dozens of Wyverns that had remained out of sight appeared and launched a ferocious assault.
People died without end, and monsters surged forward without pause.
With even the S-rank Hunters away from their positions, deep despair settled over the faces of those risking their lives to hold the line.
*It’s all over.*
Then, just as everyone thought of death—
*Shiiiiing!*
A Death Knight’s sword stopped in the middle of cutting through someone.
No.
It crumbled into ash.
“W-What the hell...?”
The Hunter who had narrowly escaped death looked around and gaped.
The sight before him was unbelievable.
First, hundreds fell.
Then thousands crumbled.
Before long, monsters numbering in the tens of thousands were turning to ash and scattering.
*Whoooooosh.*
At long last, the war was over.

chapters.title: Chapter 427
paragraphs: It was a winter night in December, and snow was pouring down in thick flurries.
People hurried through the streets, trusting the forecast that had confidently predicted unusually clear weather. They were bewildered, and the Meteorological Agency was thrown into confusion.
“What the hell? What’s going on?”
“We’re analyzing it now. This definitely shouldn’t be happening.”
“Snow the size of hailstones is pouring down, and you’re telling me it shouldn’t be happening? Stop spouting nonsense and bring me the data. We have real-time observations, don’t we?”
“We’re checking them now, but... Ah, it looks like an abnormal phenomenon caused by a sudden surge in mana in China’s Sichuan region. The expected snowfall is no joke.”
“Sichuan? Damn it. Is that Arch Lich bastard controlling the weather now, too?”
After the Great Cataclysm, the Meteorological Agency had incorporated various forms of magic and begun issuing forecasts that bordered on prophecy.
An hour after hastily conducting another round of observations, the agency issued a heavy-snow advisory across the country. They predicted record-breaking snowfall, the worst in roughly thirty years.
But before long, the people hurrying home had no choice but to stop in their tracks.
A single sentence rang out from the massive screen at the heart of an ordinary commercial district.
“On a day like today, it is both my pleasure and my honor to bring you this news.”
An elderly East Asian man appeared on the screen.

Behind him sat the leaders of the nations on the United Nations Security Council. The Chairman of the People’s Republic of China addressed the countless microphones, his eyes red and his voice thick with emotion.
“The Arch Lich has been erased. We... have won.”
Victory.
That one word was enough.
For roughly a month—thirty-four days, to be exact—an unprecedented monster wave had raged without pause.
The news that the great war, which had spread unease throughout the world beyond Sichuan Province, had finally come to an end left people standing there with their mouths hanging open.
Then they erupted into thunderous cheers.
“Waaaaaaah!”
“Wait! Hold on! I couldn’t hear that. What did he just say?”
“...It’s over!”
“What?”
“The subtitles! Look at the subtitles!”
“‘The Arch Lich has been erased’... Oh, shit, it’s true! Waaaaaaah! I thought I was going to get called up for reserve duty!”
They heard neither Chairman Xiao Yang’s thirty-minute announcement nor the additional explanation given afterward by the spokesperson for the United Nations Security Council.
With the Arch Lich erased, its countless undead legions had lost their power and been annihilated as well. At last, the peace everyone had longed for had arrived.
“Mom, it’s me. Yeah. Did you see the news? You didn’t? Turn it on right now. Yeah, yeah!”
“We have to celebrate. Assistant Manager Kim, let’s go for a third round!”
“A third round? The server update is tomorrow. Manager Noh is going to lose his shit.”
“Manager Noh is coming too. He’s bringing the corporate card.”
“Ugh, I don’t want to see that bastard’s face. Fine. Let’s go.”
“Unity! Yes, Battalion Commander. This is Captain Lee Junbeom. Could I extend my leave by just one more day—? No, sir. I’m sorry, sir.”

People who had been going back and forth outside while desperately ignoring their unease ran to the bars amid the cheers. Even those who had stayed home, anticipating a second Great Cataclysm, poured into the streets and joined the festive atmosphere.
The cheering did not die down even after midnight.
Nor the next day, or the day after that...
The entire world boiled like a cauldron over a charcoal brazier at the news of this monumental victory, and fresh articles appeared day after day in every language.
People even joked that the victory had generated more coverage than the heavy snow that fell across Korea for three straight days.
And... there was one name that appeared without fail in every one of those articles.
[The New York Times, United States: “A Great Victory, a New Hero.”]
[The Times, United Kingdom: “A New Star Rising in the East. Is He Close to Prince Felix?”]
[Asahi Shimbun, Japan: “Jin Taekyung Is Asia’s Pride. But Japan’s First-String Hunters Could Surpass Him!”]
[People’s Daily, China: “The Young Korean Knight-Errant Who Saved Countless People. And the Tragic Death of Zhonghua’s Genius, Wu Heixing.”]
[China Youth News: “Jin Taekyung Is a Descendant of Chen Lin, a Ming Dynasty General. The Blood of Zhonghua Unmistakably Flows Through Him, and He Will Surely Become a Chinese Citizen Before Long.”]
[Goryeo Daily, Korea: “Ares Guild Vice Guild Master, Hunter Lee Jungryong, Age 68. Presumed Dead...”]

[Daspatch Korea official: “We have devoted every effort to investigating Jin Taekyung for several months, but we could not uncover a single thing. His romantic history is astonishingly clean.” When a reporter asked whether that meant he had dated many women but parted with each of them amicably, the official cut him off: “No. I mean he’s never dated anyone in his life.”]
To the various media outlets, Jin Taekyung was nothing short of a Christmas present.
Every spotlight turned toward him, and all kinds of stories about him came pouring out.

The material was endless. Needless to say, there was plenty to cover about the monster wave now known as the “Winter War,” but his past actions on the way to his current position and even the most trivial details of his private life were considered newsworthy.
Even the trashy articles that would normally have been cursed out as gutter journalism attracted interest.
That was how much of the world’s attention had turned toward the new hero who had led them to this great victory.
But not all that attention was positive.
Information had begun leaking out bit by bit from behind the ironclad internal security, and people began raising questions.
[Four Days After the War. What Was Hidden Behind That Great Victory? The Questions Surrounding Jin Taekyung.]
[Lee Jungryong Presumed Dead. Wu Heixing’s Suspicious Death. The Deaths of Two S-Rank Hunters and the Rise of a New Hero.]

[Secret Testimony from Coalition Commanders Who Were at the Scene: “Considering the ferocity of the battle, Jin Taekyung’s body showed no significant injuries when he was discovered. We are investigating whether he used potions. Once he regains consciousness, the full circumstances will become clear.”]
Although they remained a tiny minority, conspiracy theories began surfacing, and fierce arguments erupted across the internet.

The trashy articles soon vanished beneath a barrage of malicious comments and reports, but they planted doubts in the minds of some members of the public. Eventually, everyone’s attention settled on one thing.
Jin Taekyung.
When, exactly, would he show himself?
Beep. Beep.
State-of-the-art medical equipment emitted mechanical sounds.
The people gathered in one part of the hospital room, which only a select few were permitted to enter, gazed worriedly at Jin Taekyung as he lay there wearing an oxygen mask.
“How is Mr. Jin’s condition?”
Choi Minwoo answered Chairman Xiao Yang’s question.
“It’s always the same. Everything is perfectly normal, but for some reason, he still hasn’t regained consciousness.”
“Did both of them say that?”
“Yes. They said they don’t know the cause.”
“Hmm. If both of them said so, there can be no doubt... Then why on earth hasn’t he regained consciousness?”
Chairman Xiao Yang sighed.
The two people he had mentioned were at the very top of their respective fields of medicine.
One was a civilian physician known as the reincarnation of Hua Tuo, while the other was one of the world’s foremost healers.
If the two of them, invited to serve as Jin Taekyung’s temporary attending physicians, had reached the same conclusion, there could be no doubt.
“I heard his family is here.”
“The Peace Guild is taking good care of them. Fortunately, they’ve regained their composure.”
“I see. Would it be possible for me to meet them, even briefly?”
“I can ask, but their wishes are what matter most, so...”
“I understand. Who could feel otherwise when a blood relative has yet to regain consciousness? I would appreciate it if you simply considered this the foolishness of an old man.”
“No, Chairman. We’re grateful that you even thought of it.”
“Don’t thank me. If not for Mr. Jin, an even greater catastrophe would have occurred. I may be an old man without many years left, but I will carry this gratitude with me to the grave.”
Chairman Xiao Yang was sincere.

Four days had passed since that day. During that time, an investigation team made up of countless experts from around the world had combed through the city that had served as the Arch Lich’s base and discovered traces of the Gate.
Based on the enormous amount of residual mana, the projected scale of that Gate was nothing short of catastrophic.
“If Mr. Jin had failed to stop the Arch Lich that day, not only our country but all of Asia would have become a battlefield. No... Perhaps the entire world could have become one.”
“It was certainly possible.”
It might have been a slight exaggeration, but most of it was true.
So Choi Minwoo did not bother denying it. He simply nodded.

The praise was not directed at him, so he had no reason to feel embarrassed. Nor did he see any reason to diminish the gratitude felt by the leader of a nation with a population of more than a billion.
A debt of gratitude had a way of returning as an even greater gift.
“But Chairman, I’ve been hearing some unfavorable rumors about Jin Taekyung lately... Were you aware of them?”
“Do you mean inside the country or outside it?”
“Inside. The leadership of the Communist Party—or, more precisely, the Crown Prince Party.”
Chairman Xiao Yang nodded.
“I am fully aware of the matter.”
It concerned Wu Heixing’s death.
The investigation team had found his body severely mutilated, and conspiracy theories about it were gradually spreading both inside and outside the country.

“There are people who suspect Mr. Jin. They point to the fact that he had a minor argument with Wu Heixing during their first meeting, as well as the fact that Mr. Jin had no notable injuries when he was first discovered.”
There were two negative theories about what had happened.
The first claimed that Jin Taekyung, who had long harbored ill feelings toward Wu Heixing, had killed him and disguised it as the Arch Lich’s work.
The second claimed that Jin Taekyung and Lee Jungryong, who was now presumed missing or dead, had used Wu Heixing as a shield and seized the opportunity to kill the Arch Lich.
Chairman Xiao Yang knew about these theories and had already reached his own conclusion.
The old statesman spoke to Choi Minwoo in a firm tone.
“They are nothing more than absurd slander and conspiracy theories.”
“Thank you for believing him, but...”
It was a good response, but it was not enough.
Choi Minwoo continued slowly.
“The leader of the Crown Prince Party doesn’t seem to share your view, Chairman.”
It was a conspiracy theory condemned even within China as an embarrassment to the nation. But to a father who had lost his son, it sounded entirely plausible.
Wu Heixing’s father was the head of the Crown Prince Party, which constituted half of the Chinese Communist Party.
A political giant comparable to the Chairman himself, he had begun spreading the rumors in earnest. He had even formed an independent investigation team to dig into the matter.
“If Mr. Jin regains consciousness, the truth will come to light anyway. But for a high-ranking politician to take the lead in spreading such an absurd conspiracy theory...”
Choi Minwoo let his voice trail off, and Chairman Xiao Yang smiled faintly.
*He has no qualms at all.*
No matter how great a feat he had accomplished, the young man before him had lived a very different life and stood in a very different position from his own.
Yet the young man before him was pressing his point without hesitation, carefully controlling his pace and tone as he did so.
*Was that information true?*
As Chairman Xiao Yang suddenly recalled Choi Minwoo’s personal information, he tapped the armrest of his chair.
“Very well. It seems my explanation was insufficient, so let me say it again.”
“I’m listening.”
“My comrades and I already know everything about the matter, and we have completed all the necessary preparations.”
“All the necessary preparations...?”
“Before he can appeal to anyone about his son’s death, he will be standing trial.”
The Arch Lich was not the only one brought down by this war.
Corruption and embezzlement involving astronomical sums had been exposed, and dealing with the fallout would force the Crown Prince Party to tear out its own foundations.
Only then did a faint smile appear on Choi Minwoo’s lips.
“Does that answer your question?”
“More than enough.”
That was all he needed from today’s conversation.
A short while later, after exchanging a few more words, Chairman Xiao Yang left the room. Now alone, Choi Minwoo suddenly spoke.
“That’s what he says.”
And then one person’s eyes snapped open.
“Oh, fuck. I thought I was going to die from how stifling this was.”
