“I am fully aware of the matter.”
It concerned Wu Heixing’s death.
The investigation team had found his body severely mutilated, and conspiracy theories about it were gradually spreading both inside and outside the country.
“There are people who suspect Mr.
Jin.
They point to the fact that he had a minor argument with Wu Heixing during their first meeting, as well as the fact that Mr.
Jin had no notable injuries when he was first discovered.”
There were two negative theories about what had happened.
The first claimed that Jin Taekyung, who had long harbored ill feelings toward Wu Heixing, had killed him and disguised it as the Arch Lich’s work.
The second claimed that Jin Taekyung and Lee Jungryong, who was now presumed missing or dead, had used Wu Heixing as a shield and seized the opportunity to kill the Arch Lich.
Chairman Xiao Yang knew about these theories and had already reached his own conclusion.
The old statesman spoke to Choi Minwoo in a firm tone.
“They are nothing more than absurd slander and conspiracy theories.”
“Thank you for believing him, but...”
It was a good response, but it was not enough.
Choi Minwoo continued slowly.
“The leader of the Crown Prince Party doesn’t seem to share your view, Chairman.”
It was a conspiracy theory condemned even within China as an embarrassment to the nation.
But to a father who had lost his son, it sounded entirely plausible.
Wu Heixing’s father was the head of the Crown Prince Party, which constituted half of the Chinese Communist Party.
A political giant comparable to the Chairman himself, he had begun spreading the rumors in earnest.
He had even formed an independent investigation team to dig into the matter.
“If Mr.
Jin regains consciousness, the truth will come to light anyway.
But for a high-ranking politician to take the lead in spreading such an absurd conspiracy theory...”
Choi Minwoo let his voice trail off, and Chairman Xiao Yang smiled faintly.
*He has no qualms at all.*
No matter how great a feat he had accomplished, the young man before him had lived a very different life and stood in a very different position from his own.
Yet the young man before him was pressing his point without hesitation, carefully controlling his pace and tone as he did so.
*Was that information true?*
As Chairman Xiao Yang suddenly recalled Choi Minwoo’s personal information, he tapped the armrest of his chair.
“Very well.
It seems my explanation was insufficient, so let me say it again.”
“I’m listening.”
“My comrades and I already know everything about the matter, and we have completed all the necessary preparations.”
“All the necessary preparations...?”
“Before he can appeal to anyone about his son’s death, he will be standing trial.”
The Arch Lich was not the only one brought down by this war.
Corruption and embezzlement involving astronomical sums had been exposed, and dealing with the fallout would force the Crown Prince Party to tear out its own foundations.
Only then did a faint smile appear on Choi Minwoo’s lips.
“Does that answer your question?”
“More than enough.”
That was all he needed from today’s conversation.
A short while later, after exchanging a few more words, Chairman Xiao Yang left the room.
Now alone, Choi Minwoo suddenly spoke.
“That’s what he says.”
And then one person’s eyes snapped open.
“Oh, fuck.
I thought I was going to die from how stifling this was.”

chapters.title: Chapter 428
paragraphs: I sat up and released the breath I’d been holding.
“God, I’m dying.”
Pretending to be unconscious for four days took a considerable amount of patience.
Especially while hooked up to a whole array of state-of-the-art medical equipment.
*Besides, it wasn’t exactly a good time to return to Murim.*
Even if I went back, I’d just be stuck aboard the swift ship, staring stupidly at the Yangtze.
I was better off wrapping things up properly in the modern world. As long as I had the System, time was on my side.
Crack. Crack.
As I rolled my stiff neck from side to side, Team Leader Choi let out a quiet laugh.
“If anyone had seen this on CCTV, there would’ve been quite an uproar.”
“That’s a terrible thing to say. If that had happened, I would’ve bitten my tongue and killed myself.”
Fortunately, there were no CCTV cameras, so my tongue was safe.
Then again, I was wearing a brain-wave detector that alerted the medical staff the instant a patient regained consciousness. CCTV would’ve been redundant.
“I have to ask—how on earth did you fool that machine?”
I shrugged.
“Oh, the brain-wave detector? This isn’t a machine.”
“Excuse me?”
“Well, it is, but the thing actually powering it is a Magic Gem.”
“Then did you use mana...? No, internal energy?”
“Yeah. I made it malfunction. A little adjustment like that wasn’t difficult.”
After opening my Middle Dantian this time, my control over my internal energy had improved tremendously.
If I couldn’t even fool a few medical devices, I would’ve been so frustrated that I’d have gone to check the temperature of the Han River.
“Anyway, what do you think will happen with the Wu Heixing situation? From what Grandpa Jongseok said, it sounds like he’s made preparations.”
“This must be the fiftieth time I’ve told you: he isn’t Grandpa Jongseok. He’s Chairman Xiao.”
“What’s wrong with Grandpa Jongseok? It sounds nice and friendly.”
“...Sigh.”
Shaking his head, Team Leader Choi picked up an apple from the fruit basket beside him.
He drew a dagger that looked expensive at a glance, peeled the apple with practiced ease, and held it out to me.
“I don’t think you need to worry about Wu Heixing. Public opinion is on our side, and Chairman Xiao seems to have been sharpening his blade.”
“Chairman Xiao? Honestly, he seemed a little soft to me.”
Crunch.
I bit into the firm apple, and sweet juice filled my mouth.
If Chairman Xiao Yang had been as hard as this apple, the Crown Prince Party wouldn’t have remained at the center of power for so long.
As if he had read my mind, Team Leader Choi said, “Did you know Chairman Xiao was once branded a reactionary and sentenced to five years of hard labor in a pig slaughterhouse?”
“That happened?”
“I heard the Crown Prince Party targeted him when he tried to push through political reforms after the Great Cataclysm. But look where he is now.”
That told me everything I needed to know.
Chairman Xiao had a personal grudge against the Crown Prince Party, and after enduring years of hardship, he had risen to the highest position in the country. In other words, he had an iron will.
“When the time comes, a blade sharpened for years has to be swung. To the Crown Prince Party, Chairman Xiao will be the most dangerous swordsman of all.”
“Then Wu Heixing’s father...”

“Considering his political standing and the public sympathy surrounding Wu Heixing, execution is unlikely. He’ll probably be sent to a political prison camp or a pig slaughterhouse. But given his age, he’ll spend the rest of his life there.”
First Wu Heixing, and now his father.
So this was how father and son met their end.
It wasn’t my imagination. The apple really did taste sweeter today.
I grinned and wiped the juice from the corner of my mouth.
“Lying here for four days was worth it.”
Team Leader Choi peeled a second apple and handed it to me.
“Your judgment was correct. If the press had learned that you woke up after only half a day, there would’ve been no avoiding suspicion.”

According to the news Team Leader Choi had given me, Lee Jungryong had not even left behind a body, and his death was considered certain by the public. Wu Heixing, who had died with his neck broken, had been caught in the aftermath of the battle and discovered as a gruesome corpse.
If I’d woken up perfectly fine after half a day under those circumstances, the press would’ve had a field day tearing me apart.
“When you first woke up, even I had trouble regaining my composure... Had you already anticipated all this before you dealt with those two?”
I answered while biting into the apple.
“I didn’t think that far.”
“What?”
“No, my body was tired and my head hurt, so I just told them not to announce it yet. If people found out I was awake, there’d be hell to pay inside and out.”
“What?”
Team Leader Choi stared at me as though I’d betrayed him, then quietly looked away.
“...It’s nothing.”
“Come on, lose the wounded expression. The result is what matters.”
Just as I said, the result couldn’t have turned out better for us.
Never mind Wu Heixing and the Crown Prince Party. We had legally eliminated our greatest obstacle, Lee Jungryong, and prevented an even greater catastrophe by defeating the Arch Lich.
The praise and adoration of people around the world were just a bonus.
I’d heard the notification about my Fame rising so many times that it was starting to drive me insane.
Like right now.

**System** The attention of the entire world is focused on you! Your **Fame** has risen dramatically! There is too much information to process. From now on, Fame-related notifications will be combined and delivered once a month.
“...You should’ve done that from the start, you bastard.”
The sigh slipped out before I could stop it, and Team Leader Choi tilted his head.
“Pardon?”
“Oh, it’s nothing. More importantly, how’s my family?”

My mother and Hayeon had arrived in China only a few hours earlier aboard a chartered plane sent under Chairman Xiao Yang’s special orders. They had even been escorted by dozens of fighter jets, receiving treatment beyond that afforded to a state guest.
“You don’t need to worry. Your mother is resting, and your younger sister...”
“You don’t have to tell me about her. She’ll be fine on her own.”
“...Ah. Yes.”
I couldn’t bring myself to keep my condition secret from my family, so I’d had Team Leader Choi quietly tell them that I was completely unharmed and already awake.
Even so, I was worried about their first visit, which was coming up soon.
*One or two smacks on the back won’t settle this.*
I’d rather fight several thousand monsters.
I’d left nothing but a single message in the family group chat saying I was going to China. Just imagining the fallout sent a chill down my spine.
“Team Leader Choi.”
“Yes?”
“When my family comes to visit, you absolutely cannot go anywhere. Understood?”
“Promise me you’ll stay right beside me and protect me.”
“Ah. All right.”
And two hours later—
“You little brat! You little braaaat!”
“Mom!”
“M-Ma’am!”
Team Leader Choi stepped in front of my mother as she charged at me with a tearful roar unlike anything I had ever heard.
He became the first victim of her back-smacking assault.
“M-Ma’am, please calm down...”
“Move! Are you going to move or not?!”
Smack! Smack!
“Urgh! Gah!”
“Jin Taekyuuung!”
Then a kick from a fearless soon-to-be college freshman, freshly liberated from the college entrance exam, struck him squarely between the legs.
It was an unfortunate accident.
Wham!
Team Leader Choi, his eyes wide, muttered in a hollow voice.
“M-My special underwear... It doesn’t burn, it doesn’t get wet, and it even has a semipermanent cleaning spell...”
Goodbye, Team Leader Choi.
You should’ve enchanted it with reinforcement instead.
Thump. Thud.
I paid my respects to the modern-day knight-errant brought to his knees by pain, then resolutely prepared for the storm coming my way.
*Open Inventory. Equip Fire Dragon Armor.*
I felt the armor of the divine weapon gently envelop my chest, stomach, and back beneath my hospital gown, and closed my eyes.
At that exact moment, someone’s palm slammed into my cheek.
Smack!
Wait. A slap in the face wasn’t part of my calculations...
I regained consciousness after a week.
No, it was announced that I had regained consciousness.
After another week of complicated medical examinations and various loose ends, I held a brief press conference before a sea of microphones and cheering people.
“Mr. Jin, we have screened out the reporters most likely to cause trouble. Simply call on the reporters selected in advance and answer their questions.”
But contrary to Chairman Xiao’s assurances before the press conference, a few reporters hungry for a sweet scoop swarmed in like bees.
“Mr. Jin! We’ve heard that you and Wu Heixing, one of the casualties of this battle, were on bad terms. Is that true?”
The security guards moved to drag the foreign reporter away, but I stopped them with a gesture.
“I already told the investigators everything, but I’ll say it again. It’s all true.”
Flash! Flash!
Flashes several times brighter erupted, along with a burst of murmuring. A Chinese reporter’s lips twitched with a malicious smile as he asked another question.
“Why? What was the reason?”
“The little bastard was rude from the moment we met.”
“What exactly did he...?”
“He called me a peninsula bangzi and cursed me out. So I called him a chink bastard, and he tried to attack me after the meeting ended.”
The smile vanished from the Chinese reporter’s face.
“A chink? That’s a slur against Chinese people!”
“Oh. Is it?”
I gave a vague nod, then gestured to the security guards.
“Get that chink bastard out of here.”
“Let go of me! This is suppression of the press!”
“Suppress that bastard’s mouth while you’re at it. I’ll talk to Chinese people, but I don’t talk to chinks. He’s exactly like that Wu Heixing bastard.”
Right then, someone among the mass of reporters raised a hand and asked a question. This one was Chinese as well.
“Then did you continue to clash with Wu Heixing afterward?”
“I wouldn’t call it a clash. I beat him to a jajinmori rhythm with the spirit of Korea behind every blow, and he quieted down. We got along well enough after that.”
“Then...”
“Yes.”
I continued solemnly.
“Wu Heixing was killed by the Arch Lich. There was nothing I could do, and I survived thanks to the top-grade potion he left behind. Once again, I offer my condolences for his death.”
There. Condolences.

I had to say what needed saying and patch up what needed patching. No matter what crimes Wu Heixing had committed while he was alive or how rotten his character had been, admitting that I’d killed him would only hurt me down the road.
*Besides, hardly anyone would believe that Lee Jungryong had lured Wu Heixing into conspiring with him.*
People tended to turn away from inconvenient truths.
I imagined the disappearance of a hundred-terabyte USB containing all the treasures of humanity, and tears welled in my eyes.
“And... above all, I feel profound sorrow over the death of Hunter Lee Jungryong, a hero of the Great Cataclysm and the great Senior I respected more than anyone. He was truly a good man.”
The press-conference hall instantly grew solemn. I wiped away the tears rolling down my cheeks and delivered the line I had prepared.
“Although our time together was brief, I will never forget him for as long as I live. I offer my condolences to everyone who died in this war. I’m sorry I couldn’t save even one more person.”
One sentence that brought the wave of criticism to an end.

Considering the gravity of the matter, the press conference was absurdly brief, lasting only around thirty minutes. It was broadcast worldwide by terrestrial and cable networks in numerous countries, as well as through an iTube livestream, drawing a combined live audience of three billion viewers.
Before I could even begin to feel the impact, I went to find someone.

chapters.title: Chapter 429
paragraphs: “Should we head there right away?”
As soon as the press conference ended, the acting Head of Security—no, Xiao Shen—came over and asked. I nodded.
“Let’s do that. You know where he is, right?”
“Yes, I do. Then let’s go.”
Dozens of security officers led by Xiao Shen formed a circle around me and slowly began moving.
Chaos erupted around us at once. Reporters from various networks came swarming over with cameras and microphones in hand.
“Mr. Jin! Is it true that you’re close to His Highness Prince Felix?”
“Jin-san! Jin-san!”
*You’re the real jinsang here, asshole.*
The reporters from various countries hadn’t been satisfied with the press conference and latched onto me, but they couldn’t break through the Hunter security detail.
Though, of course, one man did manage to push close enough to keep shoving a microphone in my face.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung! We’re both Korean, so please, just one interview...”
There was always someone like this wherever you went.
“Oh, sure. Since we’re both Korean, please move aside.”
I gave him a halfhearted answer and was about to walk past when his familiar face made me stop. I held Xiao Shen back as he moved to block the reporter.
“Wait. Are you with Daspatch?”
“I thought so. You published an article about me, didn’t you?”
“N-No, I didn’t.”
*That confirms it. You son of a bitch.*
I’d been wondering where I’d seen him before. He was the reporter who had posted an article about me having been single my entire life and called it an exclusive.
Ever since then, whenever I searched my name on a web portal, “Jin Taekyung single since birth” appeared as a related search.
“Shen.”
Xiao Shen, who had been standing there bewildered because he couldn’t understand our conversation in Korean, bowed his head.
“Yes, hyung.”
“Crack down on him.”
“Yes, sir.”
Xiao Shen answered energetically and grabbed the Daspatch reporter by the wrist.
“Sir, I will enforce balance.”
“W-Wait!”

It was already too late. The reporter went airborne under Xiao Shen’s tremendous strength and dropped into the crowd. Several cameras shattered, and curses in languages from around the world poured down like hail.
I exclaimed in admiration at the feast of profanity spanning five oceans and six continents.
“So this is the global village.”
“Huh?”
“Nothing. Let’s keep going.”
The public-security officers who had been waiting nearby rushed over to join us, clearing a path.
Under the crowd’s watchful eyes and the protection of an impenetrable escort, I headed for my destination.
A short while later, I met him in a suite at the five-star hotel where the VVIPs were staying.
“Johnson.”
“Oh, Jin. You’re earlier than I expected.”
Magic Johnson had been studying something with a grave expression, but he rose from his seat with a bright smile.
He clapped a thick hand on my shoulder, guided me to a seat, and asked, “So, did the press conference go well?”
Judging by the question, he probably hadn’t watched the press conference himself.
I accepted the canned beer Johnson handed me and answered,
“It was all right. I gave them some reasonable answers and wrapped it up in thirty minutes.”
“Ha-ha. I doubt the reporters were very happy.”
“They probably like me a lot more than they like you. At least I held a press conference.”
As soon as the war ended, Magic Johnson had shut himself away in his accommodations and refused to show himself.
Unlike Faye Chen or Prince Felix, the other S-rank Hunters, he hadn’t appeared anywhere. Some people had even begun spreading rumors that he was dead.
Only after things reached that point did he post a brief comment on his official social-media account. That was the full extent of his public activity.
I am researching something new. It is as mysterious and magnificent as the victory we achieved this time.
Most people had probably nodded and moved on without understanding what he meant, but I was one of the few who knew what that “something new” was.
“So? How did it turn out?”
The corners of Magic Johnson’s mouth twitched.
“Who knows?”
“Oh, so it was a success.”
“I didn’t say anything.”
“You’re doing a terrible job of hiding that you’re holding back a laugh.”
“I’m not. Not at all.”
*Yeah, right.*
His eyes were shining with anticipation. I let out a quiet laugh.
“I heard you weren’t happy about it at first.”
“You didn’t come to see me then. Did Choi tell you that?”
“Who else could have told me? At the moment, this secret is known by only three people: me, Johnson, and Team Leader Choi.”
“Ah. But Choi got one thing wrong.”
“What?”
“I didn’t refuse at first.”
Magic Johnson drained his five-hundred-milliliter can of beer in one gulp, then continued gravely.
“I was about to fire off a spell.”
“Ah.”
“I’m not joking. Put yourself in my position. You probably would’ve blown the whole suite apart.”
“If it had been me, I would’ve demolished the hotel.”
The only reason the suite—and the hotel—remained intact was that Magic Johnson was a Grand Mage.
Humans were said to be creatures of curiosity, but mages were curiosity incarnate. That went without saying for a Grand Mage who stood at the pinnacle of magic.
And when presented with an offer involving a “new thing” he had never seen before, he readily accepted it.
“Even after Choi explained everything and I saw it with my own eyes, I couldn’t believe it. This is truly...”
Magic Johnson murmured with a dreamy look in his eyes, then suddenly shook his head.
“No. This won’t do. Come and see for yourself.”
“Good. I nearly died of old age waiting.”
I set down my half-empty beer and rose. Without hesitation, I crossed the spacious suite and stopped in front of one particular spot.
“It’s here, right?”
Magic Johnson nodded. It wasn’t particularly surprising that an S-rank Hunter sensitive to the flow of energy could sense that something was off.
“That’s right. You really know your stuff.”
“Even someone fairly observant would have a hard time noticing this.”
To the naked eye, it looked like an ordinary section of the room.
But I had known from the moment I stepped into the suite.
It was magic that blocked every sound and sight.
“Wait a moment. I’ll dispel the magic right aw—”
Whoosh! Slash!
Magic Johnson’s eyes widened before he could finish speaking.
The edge of my hand, wrapped in Force, swept down through empty air, and the various spells he had laid out split apart cleanly.
“Jin. What on earth...?”
During my battle with the Arch Lich, I had opened my Middle Dantian and gained the ability to see the texture of qi.
That had made things like this possible, but I offered no explanation. I simply stared straight ahead.
As the magic was dispelled, a single layer peeled away from the space before me.
Beyond it stood a man.
“Ah, eh, ee, oh, oo. Hellow. Nishe to meet you. I like rice-soup freaks. I wuv kimchi.”
The blond foreigner had been standing in front of a full-length mirror, holding something as he practiced Korean with awkward pronunciation. He spotted my reflection and turned around.
A hint of laughter crossed his pretty-boy face.
“At last, you have arrived, vile human.”
*Look at this bastard pronouncing only that perfectly.*
For a moment, I considered hitting him. Instead, I let out a quiet laugh.
“You’ve gotten better-looking since I last saw you.”
The blond foreigner—the Skeleton King—replied smugly.
“You have become even uglier since I last saw you.”
“Ugly as hell.”
“...No, you son of a bitch.”
Where the hell had this bastard learned Korean?
“Hmm. Beautiful, as expected. Nothing about him looks out of place.”
Magic Johnson kept smiling in satisfaction like a plastic surgeon in Gangnam.

“Even after seeing him again, I have to say he’s an unprecedented masterpiece. I may be the first mage in human history to carve a Magic Formation into a Skeleton’s bones—and not merely a Skeleton, but an entirely new Named Monster.”
This wasn’t just a surgeon praising his own handiwork. It was true.
Glossy blond hair. Mysteriously gleaming golden eyes. A well-balanced build nearly 190 centimeters tall, with long limbs bearing just the right amount of body hair.
And that wasn’t all.
His muscles and veins stood out clearly, and his body responded naturally whenever he breathed or swallowed.
Even I had to study him closely to notice anything unusual. The Skeleton King looked completely human.
“...Wow. It actually worked.”
I’d made the request thinking I had nothing to lose, but I hadn’t expected the result to be this perfect.
I swallowed hard in amazement and reached out to touch his blond hair.
That was when—
Swish.
The Skeleton King took one step back and looked at me arrogantly.
“Take your filthy hand away. You will damage my hair.”
“Will you take responsibility if I go bald?”
*This bastard really is human now...*
I was too dumbfounded to speak.
Ignoring me, the Skeleton King admired his reflection in the full-length mirror and smiled in satisfaction.
“Hmm. Insanely handsome.”
“I’ve been wondering this for a while. Where did you learn expressions like that?”
“On the Internet.”
“The Internet?”
“Indeed. I spent a whole week browsing the shit out of it.”
“Wait. Do you have a phone, too?”
“That kind human over there bought me one. Thank you, Johnson.”
Magic Johnson, who was using a translation spell, nodded with a pleased smile.
“I wish you every success in your new beginning, Mr. King.”
“Thank you, Johnson.”
*Thank you, Johnson, my ass. When did he learn basic English, too?*
I immediately rounded on Magic Johnson.
“Wait. You even bought him a phone?”
“Hey, Jin. What’s the problem? My youngest daughter is five, and even she uses a smartphone.”
“That’s your youngest daughter. He’s the Skeleton King.”
“Hold on, vile human. I apologize for interrupting your conversation, but this must be said.”
The Skeleton King cut in with a grave expression.
“From now on, you will call me Stone-King.”
“What is this, another thing that’ll get you pelted with stones?”
“It is my new name. Stone King. Born in Atlanta, Georgia, United States...”
I muttered as I felt a headache coming on.
“Should I just kill him? I’m seriously about to.”
“Would you kill a citizen of the United States?”
“Who’s an American citizen, you lunatic?”
“Perhaps not right now, but I can soon obtain United States citizenship.”
“You should write a web novel for KakaoPage instead. What kind of idiot comes up with that bullshit?”
Magic Johnson shyly raised one hand.
“Jin, with my connections, it should be entirely poss—”
“Ah! Aah! Aaaaah!”
This was driving me insane.
I clutched my throbbing forehead and turned to Magic Johnson.
“Johnson.”
“Hmm?”
“What I asked through Team Leader Choi was for you to make him look human. That was all.”
“Of course. That was your request. But I heard our friend here desperately wanted this.”
All of this had begun shortly after I first regained consciousness, at the Skeleton King’s insistence.
He had loudly complained about how long he was expected to remain trapped inside the cramped Inventory.
His position was that he deserved an appropriate reward in light of his major contributions during the battle. From Team Leader Choi’s perspective and mine, that was a perfectly reasonable demand.
*He protected Team Leader Choi and Xiao Shen during the battle with Lei Fei, and we managed to defeat the Arch Lich thanks to him.*
I had already been thinking about how to repay the Skeleton King.
Besides, giving him human form would make many things easier.
He would no longer need to hide, and he could sign a contract with the Peace Guild so that both sides could benefit.
But...
“For starters, this isn’t the East Asian appearance I asked for. There may be a lot more foreigners in Korea these days, but he’ll still stand out. Especially looking like this.”
Before Magic Johnson could answer, the Skeleton King cut in stiffly.
“I asked him to change it.”
“What? Why?”
“I saw it on the Internet. Handsome white men do well everywhere in the world.”
“...And what exactly are you planning to do with that?”
“I wish to date.”
“Oh, God.”
Magic Johnson patted my shoulder as I groaned.
“It’s all right, Jin.”

“What do you mean, it’s all right? Do you have any idea how terrifying social media is these days? What if netizens dig up his identity and discover that he wasn’t born in Atlanta, Georgia, United States, but is actually a native of the Demon Realm? Does that make any sense? Why did you agree to a request like that?”
“I wanted to try making a face that suited my tastes.”
“What?”
“That face is my ideal type.”
*Oh, for fuck’s sake...*
I was still at a loss for words when the final blow snapped what remained of my patience.
“Do you feel wronged? Ugly as hell.”
“You son of a bitch!”
Crack!
I launched myself forward and drove my fist into the crown of his head.
The Skeleton King let out a strangled groan. He may have bitten his tongue, because bright red blood spurted from the corner of his mouth.
*Red blood? Is that part of the illusion magic too? He really did an incredible job recreating—*
No, that wasn’t the point.
“Die! Die!”
“Ghk! Guhk!”
The moment two burly men started rolling around, the suite became a disaster zone.
A desk caught in the chaos collapsed with a splintering crack, and the stack of documents Magic Johnson had been examining came cascading down over my face.
“W-Wait! Vile human! I cannot see!”
“I’m going to teach you some manners today...!”
Then, in the next instant, I froze.
Among the sheets of paper obscuring my vision, I saw a set of strange yet familiar symbols.
*This is...*
I left the Skeleton King where he was and rose from my seat, dazedly picking up a sheet of paper printed with the symbols.
*Sichuan.*
There was no mistake.
It was the exact pattern I had seen in Sichuan—not the modern Chinese province, but Sichuan in Murim.

chapters.title: Chapter 430
paragraphs: My eyelids began to tremble before I even realized it.
*Why is this here...?*
I remembered it clearly.

Immediately after the Sichuan Blood Tragedy—after the Western Heaven Demon Lord had nearly killed me several times—I had followed the Sect Leaders of the Qingcheng and Emei Sects to a cave in an unnamed cliff.
The space hidden behind the Mystic Gate Formation had been vast, with an enormous formation carved into its center.
The same formation filled with strange patterns and symbols that was now printed in color on the paper in my hand.
But... could the thing the Sect Leaders of Qingcheng and Emei had named the Moving Formation even be called a formation anymore?
I hurriedly thrust the paper toward Magic Johnson.
“Johnson. This—what is this?”
“Huh? What?”
“Why is this here...? No, where the hell did you get it?”
Taken aback by my sudden reaction, Magic Johnson answered with a bewildered expression.
“It’s a magic circle discovered in the city the Arch Lich used as its base.”
“A magic circle?”
“Yes, a magic circle. I was already in the middle of researching it... What’s wrong, Jin? Have you seen it somewhere before?”
“Are there more?”
“Of course. Every sheet of paper I was looking at before you came in is related to it.”
“What?”
Then everything piled on the desk had been related to it?
I looked at the dozens of sheets of paper scattered across the floor.
“Excuse me for a moment.”
“Jin? Jin?”
“Has he finally gone mad? How tragic, you vile and ugly human.”
I ignored Magic Johnson’s flustered calls and the Skeleton King’s nonsense.
My lips pressed firmly together, I rapidly skimmed through the stack of printouts.
Each sheet bore a different set of patterns and symbols. By the time I had examined them all, I had realized one thing.
*This is...*
There was no mistake. The strange patterns and symbols were identical to the ones I had seen in Murim, only arranged and oriented differently.
And if I assembled all these sheets like pieces of a puzzle, they would form one enormous magic circle.
*What the hell is going on?*
I felt as though someone had smashed me in the back of the head with a sledgehammer.
I stared silently at the papers for a long time before finally speaking.
“You said this was discovered at the Arch Lich’s base, right?”
Magic Johnson had a cigar between his lips by then. He blew out a cloud of smoke before answering.
“That’s right. I didn’t know anything like this existed at first, but apparently it was discovered shortly after the investigation team went in. The coalition forces sent it to me on the second day.”
“They sent it to you?”
“They wanted my opinion. They couldn’t figure out exactly what the magic circle did, either. They probably contacted the other two as well.”
The other two were probably the Grand Mages besides Magic Johnson. They were the greatest mages alive and true experts in the field.
Which meant this magic circle was something entirely new—something that had never been seen before.
“So, has your research turned up anything?”
“Nothing conclusive yet, but I have a general idea of the magic circle’s purpose.”
“Its purpose?”
“Yes. Fortunately, I have a friend who knows quite a bit about that sort of thing.”
I was just about to ask who he meant when an arrogant voice cut in.
“That would be this very body. The universe’s most insanely handsome man, born in Atlanta, Georgia, United States. Known as Stone-King.”
Right. How had I forgotten about this bastard?
He was a native of the Demon Realm and a Named Monster to boot, so he was bound to know something.
I pressed the Skeleton King for answers as he continued spouting nonsense.
“Cut the bullshit and tell me what you know.”
“Call me Mr. King from now on, and I shall consider it.”
“Mr. King, my ass. You kumquat-looking bastard.”
“Fucking Korean.”
“You son of a bitch.”
“Whoa, whoa!”
When I raised my hand, the Skeleton King instinctively scurried backward and shouted in alarm.
“All right! I said all right!”
“Talk, asshole.”
The Skeleton King regarded me warily before speaking.
“It appears to be a magic circle for absorbing life force.”
“Absorbing life force?”
“Indeed. It seems the Arch Lich used it to absorb other humans’ energy and amass power. With all that magical power at its disposal, it could control countless legions of monsters and open Gates.”
China was a vast continent.
Even after suffering staggering casualties during the Great Cataclysm, it was still home to one-fifth of the world’s population.
And approximately eighty million people lived in Sichuan Province alone—according to the official statistics, at least.
The monster wave had caused millions of casualties. Add those who had yet to be officially counted, and the number would rise to truly staggering proportions.
*And a great many of them must have been sacrificed to provide magical power. Considering the scale of what that bastard did, it all adds up.*
I bit down hard on my lip and asked the Skeleton King again.
“Are you sure?”
“It is merely my personal inference. I cannot guarantee it.”
“Why not?”
The Skeleton King clicked his tongue.
“Vile human. Can you determine the meaning of magic circles used by other humans simply by looking at them?”
“That’s...”
“Of course you cannot. This body is no different. I can raise and command soldiers according to the abilities granted to me, but I cannot wield dark magic like this.”
Damn it. He was completely right.
Just as Hunters and monsters were classified according to their respective traits, the Skeleton King only possessed the abilities specific to him.
His answer wasn’t what I had hoped for, and I could feel the strength draining out of me. But one important question remained.
“Then how did you guess that it was a life-force absorption magic circle? Can only monsters recognize patterns and symbols like these?”
If the Skeleton King understood these strange patterns and symbols—if he could teach me what they meant—I might finally be able to identify the formation I had seen in Murim.
I looked at him expectantly, only for his answer to dash my hopes a moment later.
“I do not know what those things mean. I could guess what the magic circle was for only because I’m undead.”
The Skeleton King pointed at Magic Johnson and continued.

“When I first saw it on paper, I could not tell what it was. But when I visited the site with that human I’m grateful to, I sensed it clearly. The stench of countless deaths hung over the place—more deaths than even I could begin to estimate. That was when I realized what it was.”
I could not hide my disappointment.
If neither Magic Johnson, a Grand Mage, nor the Skeleton King, a Named Monster, could understand them, then deciphering those patterns and symbols anytime soon would be practically impossible.
*Damn it.*
What the hell was going on?

The formation carved into the center of the cave. The patterns and symbols that had appeared in the magic circle discovered this time. The bizarre phenomena I had witnessed during my battle with the Blood Lord and the Western Heaven Demon Lord...
I desperately tried to deny the ominous thought that flashed through my mind.
*That can’t be. It’s impossible.*
Was this a coincidence? Or was it fate?
And if it was fate, what did this connection that had appeared out of nowhere mean?
After pacing silently around the suite for a long time, I abruptly spoke.
“I need to see it for myself.”
“Huh?”
“Hmm?”
“Johnson. I can visit the site that bastard went to, right?”
Magic Johnson thought for a moment, then nodded.
“It’s classified, but you should be able to get in, Jin. However, only the two of us can be seen. We’ll have to carry our friend in an extradimensional pocket, just like last time.”
“That’s fine. Let’s leave right away.”
“All right, let’s do that. You seem to know something too, Jin.”
Just as Magic Johnson and I were about to leave, the Skeleton King cut in with a dignified voice.
“I apologize for interrupting, humans, but this body has pressing business. You two may go without me.”
“The woman at the hotel’s front desk is exceptionally beautiful. Though concealed beneath human skin, the curves of the skeleton within are exquisite.”
I quietly asked,
“So?”
“What do you mean, ‘so’? I am informing you that I shall be spending the night out. Now, I must go arrange a date with the beauty... But, vile human.”
“What?”
“May I ask why you suddenly took out a spear?”
“Ah, this?”
I casually waved White Flame, which I had somehow already drawn from my Inventory.
“It’s nothing. I was going to stab you when you turned around.”
“I see.”
“Exactly.”
“Why aren’t you leaving? The employees will be getting off work soon. You should hurry over and ask her to dinner.”
The Skeleton King hesitated, an awkward smile tugging at his lips.
“Now that I think about it, I suppose I can take my time trying to win her over.”
“Wow, then you’ve got some free time. In that case...”
I smiled brightly and pulled out one of the extradimensional pockets I had acquired to conceal the existence of my Inventory from other people.
“Get in, asshole.”
“...Okay.”
The Skeleton King answered dejectedly and slipped inside the extradimensional pocket.
The moment I saw the magic circle with my own eyes, I understood what the Skeleton King had meant.
Or perhaps it only seemed that way because I had heard his explanation immediately beforehand.
Either way, the sight overwhelmed me, and a single word rose unbidden to my mind.
*Death.*
The enormous dark magic circle dwarfed the one I had seen in the cave.
Although its magical power had been cut off and it had lost its original function, even the traces of death left behind by the countless lives it had once claimed had not disappeared.
And... that was all I could sense.
“Jin. What do you think? Do you have any idea what it is?”
“No. None at all.”
The patterns and symbols, arranged in an incomprehensible order, remained impossible to decipher.
Just as it had in Murim, the System remained silent. After wandering around the site for hours without learning anything, I had no choice but to turn back.
“Mr. Johnson, Jin. We’ve prepared an escort to ensure you encounter no inconvenience on your way back...”
“We’re fine.”
“Yes, sir. Then I hope we meet again.”
We left the head of security and his guards behind after they snapped off razor-sharp salutes.
Once he had made sure no one was nearby, Magic Johnson quietly moved his lips.
“Jin. You knew something, didn’t you?”
“...A dream. I think I saw something similar in a dream.”
“Hmm.”
“Johnson. Can I look around by myself for a while?”
“Of course. How long do you think you’ll be?”
“I’ll be back soon.”
I began walking slowly through the ruins.
Although it was well past midnight, the city was as bright as noon, and countless people and machines were working to clear the wreckage.
The same work was probably underway in every city caught up in the war.
*It must be the same in Sichuan.*
China’s Sichuan and Murim’s Sichuan belonged to entirely different worlds. Murim was not the modern world’s past, nor was the modern world Murim’s future.
But now a connection had appeared between those utterly different worlds—and it was not the first.
*The capsule.*
Everything surrounding me had begun with the junk capsule I had picked up at a recycling center.
*How? Why? For what reason?*
More questions crowded my mind with every step, leaving my thoughts in complete disarray.
“Phew.”
At my deep sigh, the Skeleton King—whom I had quietly moved from the extradimensional pocket into my Inventory—asked,
“Are you all right, vile human?”
“Are you worried about me now?”
“No. If you are all right, let us hurry back to the hotel. Johnson told me a few days ago that there is a club nearby with a great crowd.”
*Give me back my touching moment, you lunatic.*
I considered telling him that the club Johnson had mentioned was a gay bar, but held my tongue.
“Forget it. What did I expect from you?”
“So, when are we going back?”
“I’m going, asshole. I said I’m going!”
At that exact moment—
“Where are you so desperate to go? Hell?”
At the sound of the voice—harder and colder than ever before—I slowly turned around.
Without realizing it, I must have ventured deep into the ruins. Beyond the relatively dark ruins, a familiar figure was making his way through a collapsed building toward me.
“Hell is where your old man went. If I die, I’m going to heaven.”
The eyes of Go Jun—Lee Jungryong’s Disciple and Head of Security—turned ice-cold.

chapters.title: Chapter 431
paragraphs: “Vile human. Who is that human?”
*So there is one. A human with no sense of fear.*
I muttered to myself and slowly looked around.
The desolate outskirts were far from the center, abandoned by everyone. Even the light illuminating the city as brightly as day had yet to reach this place.
And from among the ruins, a single person came walking out, casting a shadow.
“We must be bound by fate somehow. We keep running into each other.”
Go Jun answered my greeting in a cold voice.
“Not fate. An ill-fated bond.”
“Then what do you call meeting in a place like this? Coincidence?”
His answer was as sharp as a blade.
“Inevitability.”
“Clear enough. So have you been following me around like a stray dog since earlier?”
“When did you notice?”
“Since the Stone Age, you bastard. You stared at me so much that I thought you were going to bore holes in my face.”
I had sensed someone secretly watching me as soon as I left the Magic Formation site.
It was an unpleasant, clinging gaze, completely different from the curiosity and admiration everyone else directed at me.
And under the current circumstances, very few people would be openly hostile toward me.
“It was either you or those Crown Prince Party Chinese bastards. But they’re too busy cleaning up the shit they left everywhere... So the answer was obvious, wasn’t it?”
The words had clearly hit the mark, but Go Jun showed no surprise whatsoever.
“As expected. So you did notice.”
“As expected?”
“I thought you would. Otherwise, you wouldn’t have left Magic Johnson behind and come all the way out here alone.”
*Well, look at this bastard.*
Only then did I understand why Go Jun wasn’t surprised. He had deliberately sent me a signal—a signal to follow him.
This wasn’t surveillance or a lure. This was exactly the situation both Go Jun and I had wanted.
Of course, the outcome would be nothing like what he expected.
“There’s something I want to ask.”
Go Jun didn’t wait for an answer. He stared straight at me and continued.
“Was it you?”
It was a short, simple question, but the meaning behind it was unmistakable. I tilted my head and innocently asked,
“What was?”
“You know.”
“You don’t actually think I killed Uncle Jungryong, do you?”
The moment he heard Lee Jungryong’s name, Go Jun’s eyes shook violently. Without waiting for his answer, I covered my mouth with both hands.
“My God. How could you think something so horrible? Are you serious?”
“Enough of that disgusting act. Do you think I’m asking because I don’t know?”
“Then why ask? Didn’t you watch the press conference?”
“I did. You spouted nothing but lies and bullshit from beginning to end.”
Drip. Drip.
Drops of blood fell from the fist he had clenched so tightly that it had turned white. Go Jun glared at me with eyes burning with rage.
“There are only two people here—you and me. Tell me the truth with your own lips.”
“Vile human! How dare you leave out this Atlanta-born Stone King!”
That made one more monster present.
More precisely, there were two people and one monster. Though I wasn’t sure whether the Skeleton King could still be called a monster.
“Hmm.”
I scratched the back of my head as I studied Go Jun, then said,
“That’s right. I killed him.”

“Lee Jungryong and Wu Heixing. I took care of both of them. Those lunatics had cooked up a ridiculous scenario. They planned to kill me without laying a finger on the Arch Lich. And the result... Well, you know how that turned out.”
Suspecting the truth and hearing it confirmed were two entirely different things.
Even if he had already guessed what happened, hearing the answer directly from his enemy’s mouth was another matter altogether.
I drove the final nail into the coffin for Go Jun, whose body was trembling violently.
“What else was I supposed to do with bastards like that? I bought them both tickets to the United States. Uncle Jungryong even got first class.”
“You... You dared do that to him...!”
Whoosh!
Killing intent erupted from Go Jun’s entire body, freezing the air around us.
I stared at the fingers twitching toward his sword hilt, then spoke abruptly.
“What are you doing?”
Go Jun’s eyes flew wide open. At the same time, the killing intent swirling around us vanished without a trace.
No—it had been crushed beneath the wave of qi pouring from me.
The balance of power shifted in an instant, and I slowly stepped forward.

“You’ve improved by leaps and bounds since the last time I saw you. If you think about it, you’re far better than Wu Heixing. Just what I’d expect from the Disciple Lee Jungryong trained at his side.”
Step.
Step.
With each step I took, Go Jun’s face grew paler.
The gap between our powers was overwhelming. A rabbit could not defeat a tiger. The moment he made even the slightest movement to draw his sword, my teeth would sink into his neck.
“You should check where you’re lying down before you stretch out your legs. Why would you settle into your own grave?”
Bang!
Compressed air exploded from the tip of the finger I had raised leisurely.
With a sharp crack, a stream of Finger Qi shot toward Go Jun, who stood frozen like a stone statue. Then—
Clang!
It sent the sword strapped to his waist flying far into the distance.
Go Jun’s rigid expression twisted, his eyes still wide. I let out a short laugh.
“What? Did you think I was going to kill you?”
“If you want to die that badly, be more discreet next time—and come prepared to actually die. Don’t set some half-assed trap like you did today.”
My hand shot out like lightning. Go Jun had no time to react.
Bang!
The three streams of Finger Qi I fired pierced somewhere beyond the thick darkness. A moment later—
Thud-thud-thud!
Three unconscious figures in black dropped out of thin air in the distance.

They were all high-level Hunters trained in stealth and concealed by various kinds of magic, but none of them could escape my Qi Sense, which had grown even sharper after the opening of my Middle Dantian.
“What, were you filming me on the sly? You fucking hidden-camera creep.”
Tap. Tap.
Clicking my tongue, I tapped Go Jun on the cheek. A voice full of spite slipped between his clenched teeth.
“Do you think you people will get away with this?”
“You people?”
“We—the Ares Guild—will not fall. We will definitely avenge that person’s death...”
Smack!
A tooth flew out in a spray of blood. I seized Go Jun by the collar and slapped him again.
Smack!
Once more.
Smack!
And again.
Smack!
Inner-Family Heavy Hand.
Instead of tearing through his bones and flesh, the internal energy carried in my palm burrowed into Go Jun and rattled his brain.
He staggered like a drunk, unable to keep his balance. I grabbed him by the throat.
“Remember what I’m about to say. Remember it clearly.”
A bloody foam burst out with his groan and splattered across my face. An unfamiliar man was reflected in his unfocused eyes, his expression numb as he continued speaking.
“You started this, but I’ll be the one to finish it.”
In the end, the modern world was also ruled by the logic of power.

Hunters possessed superhuman abilities, while others wielded equivalent authority. They made rules to suit themselves and broke them whenever they pleased. No matter what they did, no one ever showed them a yellow card or a red card.
When Lee Jungryong cut off Uncle Kkeokjeong’s arm to keep him in check, people like them had considered it only natural.
But—
“You shouldn’t have done that.”
A new referee had stepped onto the field, so the rules had to change.
And the new rules were very simple.
I pressed Go Jun’s Mute Acupoint and muttered,
“An eye for an eye. A tooth for a tooth.”
I twisted both his arms and pulled with all my strength, as though wringing out laundry.
Crack-crack-crack!
With a sickening tear of flesh, both arms came free from his body.
An enormous amount of blood poured out, and the whites of his bulging eyes showed. A silent scream spilled from his mouth, its Mute Acupoint sealed.
“It’s not over yet.”
I shoved my fingers into the ragged stumps of his arms. The Scorching Yang Qi in my hand seared his flesh, inflicting even greater pain. I pinned down his writhing body and grabbed him by the ankles.
“This won’t be enough for someone like you.”
Crack!
My Strength could reduce even a thousand-geun boulder to powder. The bones in both his legs shattered at once, breaking into hundreds of fragments.
His body thrashed soundlessly.
As Go Jun lost consciousness from the unimaginable pain, I poured internal energy into him.
Once the light returned to his fading eyes, I hammered my fist into his shattered legs.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
By the time I finally stopped punching, what lay sprawled across the ground was no longer a human being but a large lump of meat.
The faint breath leaking from his nose and mouth was the only proof that he remained alive.
The Skeleton King, who had watched everything from inside my Inventory, spoke in a trembling voice.
“Human.”
I answered dryly.
“What?”
“N-No. It’s just...”
His voice trailed off, but I already knew what he wanted to say.
“Yeah. It’s cruel.”
“But it was necessary.”
The helplessness of being unable to do anything. Pain so unbearable that death seemed a hundred—even a thousand—times preferable.
And the fear that I could do the same thing to them anytime I wanted.
I needed to plant all of that in my enemy’s heart and carve it into his bones.
Of course, there was another option that would leave the fewest loose ends.
*Death.*
My fingertips twitched before I realized it.
With just a little more force—only a tiny bit—I could kill Go Jun.
It was the perfect opportunity to eliminate even the slightest possibility.
But...
*The timing isn’t right.*
Doubts surrounding the truth never disappeared completely.
Conspiracy theories claimed that humanity had never landed on the moon, or that countless famous figures recorded as dead were actually still alive. This was no different.

If Lee Jungryong disappeared, followed by Wu Heixing and then Go Jun—and it came to light that I had “coincidentally” been here at exactly the right time—the rumors surrounding me would cease to be mere conspiracy theories.
So this was where I had to stop.
Now, after showing him the overwhelming gap between our powers and planting the fear of me deep inside him.
“I’ll say this one last time.”
Go Jun’s body flinched. In a voice lower and more emotionless than ever, I bit out every word.
“Let it end with Lee Jungryong alone.”
My breath, hot as lava, brushed against him, and his prone body convulsed.
Like a rabbit feeling a tiger’s teeth sink into its neck.
“Hide your teeth. Sheathe your claws. If you do that... nothing will happen.”
If he had set out to kill, he should have been prepared to die.
Lee Jungryong had been my greatest enemy and obstacle. In the end, he had paid the price for what he had done.
What I was offering now was a chance to make peace.
No—a demand.
And Go Jun had only one choice left.
His head moved in the faintest nod.
I stared into his eyes, drenched in fear and dread, then pressed his Sleep Acupoint. After taking several high-grade potions from my Inventory, I poured them over his body.
Hissssss.
I watched his wounds rapidly heal, then suddenly turned my head.
“So... that’s more or less what happened.”

sentences.text: “Vile human.
Who is that human?”
*So there is one.
A human with no sense of fear.*
I muttered to myself and slowly looked around.
The desolate outskirts were far from the center, abandoned by everyone.
Even the light illuminating the city as brightly as day had yet to reach this place.
And from among the ruins, a single person came walking out, casting a shadow.
“We must be bound by fate somehow.
We keep running into each other.”
Go Jun answered my greeting in a cold voice.
“Not fate.
An ill-fated bond.”
“Then what do you call meeting in a place like this?
Coincidence?”
His answer was as sharp as a blade.
“Inevitability.”
“Clear enough.
So have you been following me around like a stray dog since earlier?”
“When did you notice?”
“Since the Stone Age, you bastard.
You stared at me so much that I thought you were going to bore holes in my face.”
I had sensed someone secretly watching me as soon as I left the Magic Formation site.
It was an unpleasant, clinging gaze, completely different from the curiosity and admiration everyone else directed at me.
And under the current circumstances, very few people would be openly hostile toward me.
“It was either you or those Crown Prince Party Chinese bastards.
But they’re too busy cleaning up the shit they left everywhere...
So the answer was obvious, wasn’t it?”
The words had clearly hit the mark, but Go Jun showed no surprise whatsoever.
“As expected.
So you did notice.”
“As expected?”
“I thought you would.
Otherwise, you wouldn’t have left Magic Johnson behind and come all the way out here alone.”
*Well, look at this bastard.*
Only then did I understand why Go Jun wasn’t surprised.
He had deliberately sent me a signal—a signal to follow him.
This wasn’t surveillance or a lure.
This was exactly the situation both Go Jun and I had wanted.
Of course, the outcome would be nothing like what he expected.
“There’s something I want to ask.”
Go Jun didn’t wait for an answer.
He stared straight at me and continued.
“Was it you?”
It was a short, simple question, but the meaning behind it was unmistakable.
I tilted my head and innocently asked,
“What was?”
“You know.”
“You don’t actually think I killed Uncle Jungryong, do you?”
The moment he heard Lee Jungryong’s name, Go Jun’s eyes shook violently.
Without waiting for his answer, I covered my mouth with both hands.
“My God.
How could you think something so horrible?
Are you serious?”
“Enough of that disgusting act.
Do you think I’m asking because I don’t know?”
“Then why ask?
Didn’t you watch the press conference?”
“I did.
You spouted nothing but lies and bullshit from beginning to end.”
Drip.
Drip.
Drops of blood fell from the fist he had clenched so tightly that it had turned white.
Go Jun glared at me with eyes burning with rage.
“There are only two people here—you and me.
Tell me the truth with your own lips.”
“Vile human!
How dare you leave out this Atlanta-born Stone King!”
That made one more monster present.
More precisely, there were two people and one monster.
Though I wasn’t sure whether the Skeleton King could still be called a monster.
“Hmm.”
I scratched the back of my head as I studied Go Jun, then said,
“That’s right.
I killed him.”
“Lee Jungryong and Wu Heixing.
I took care of both of them.
Those lunatics had cooked up a ridiculous scenario.
They planned to kill me without laying a finger on the Arch Lich.
And the result...
Well, you know how that turned out.”
Suspecting the truth and hearing it confirmed were two entirely different things.
Even if he had already guessed what happened, hearing the answer directly from his enemy’s mouth was another matter altogether.
I drove the final nail into the coffin for Go Jun, whose body was trembling violently.
“What else was I supposed to do with bastards like that?
I bought them both tickets to the United States.
Uncle Jungryong even got first class.”
“You...
You dared do that to him...!”
Whoosh!
Killing intent erupted from Go Jun’s entire body, freezing the air around us.
I stared at the fingers twitching toward his sword hilt, then spoke abruptly.
“What are you doing?”
Go Jun’s eyes flew wide open.
At the same time, the killing intent swirling around us vanished without a trace.
No—it had been crushed beneath the wave of qi pouring from me.
The balance of power shifted in an instant, and I slowly stepped forward.
“You’ve improved by leaps and bounds since the last time I saw you.
If you think about it, you’re far better than Wu Heixing.
Just what I’d expect from the Disciple Lee Jungryong trained at his side.”
Step.
Step.
With each step I took, Go Jun’s face grew paler.
The gap between our powers was overwhelming.
A rabbit could not defeat a tiger.
The moment he made even the slightest movement to draw his sword, my teeth would sink into his neck.
“You should check where you’re lying down before you stretch out your legs.
Why would you settle into your own grave?”
Bang!
Compressed air exploded from the tip of the finger I had raised leisurely.
With a sharp crack, a stream of Finger Qi shot toward Go Jun, who stood frozen like a stone statue.
Then—
Clang!
It sent the sword strapped to his waist flying far into the distance.
Go Jun’s rigid expression twisted, his eyes still wide.
I let out a short laugh.
“What?
Did you think I was going to kill you?”
“If you want to die that badly, be more discreet next time—and come prepared to actually die.
Don’t set some half-assed trap like you did today.”
My hand shot out like lightning.
Go Jun had no time to react.
Bang!
The three streams of Finger Qi I fired pierced somewhere beyond the thick darkness.
A moment later—
Thud-thud-thud!
Three unconscious figures in black dropped out of thin air in the distance.

They were all high-level Hunters trained in stealth and concealed by various kinds of magic, but none of them could escape my Qi Sense, which had grown even sharper after the opening of my Middle Dantian.
“What, were you filming me on the sly?
You fucking hidden-camera creep.”
Tap.
Tap.
Clicking my tongue, I tapped Go Jun on the cheek.
A voice full of spite slipped between his clenched teeth.
“Do you think you people will get away with this?”
“You people?”
“We—the Ares Guild—will not fall.
We will definitely avenge that person’s death...”
Smack!
A tooth flew out in a spray of blood.
I seized Go Jun by the collar and slapped him again.
Smack!
Once more.
Smack!
And again.
Smack!
Inner-Family Heavy Hand.
Instead of tearing through his bones and flesh, the internal energy carried in my palm burrowed into Go Jun and rattled his brain.
He staggered like a drunk, unable to keep his balance.
I grabbed him by the throat.
“Remember what I’m about to say.
Remember it clearly.”
A bloody foam burst out with his groan and splattered across my face.
An unfamiliar man was reflected in his unfocused eyes, his expression numb as he continued speaking.
“You started this, but I’ll be the one to finish it.”
In the end, the modern world was also ruled by the logic of power.
Hunters possessed superhuman abilities, while others wielded equivalent authority.
They made rules to suit themselves and broke them whenever they pleased.
No matter what they did, no one ever showed them a yellow card or a red card.
When Lee Jungryong cut off Uncle Kkeokjeong’s arm to keep him in check, people like them had considered it only natural.
But—
“You shouldn’t have done that.”
A new referee had stepped onto the field, so the rules had to change.
And the new rules were very simple.
I pressed Go Jun’s Mute Acupoint and muttered,
“An eye for an eye.
A tooth for a tooth.”
I twisted both his arms and pulled with all my strength, as though wringing out laundry.
Crack-crack-crack!
With a sickening tear of flesh, both arms came free from his body.
An enormous amount of blood poured out, and the whites of his bulging eyes showed.
A silent scream spilled from his mouth, its Mute Acupoint sealed.
“It’s not over yet.”
I shoved my fingers into the ragged stumps of his arms.
The Scorching Yang Qi in my hand seared his flesh, inflicting even greater pain.
I pinned down his writhing body and grabbed him by the ankles.
“This won’t be enough for someone like you.”
Crack!
My Strength could reduce even a thousand-geun boulder to powder.
The bones in both his legs shattered at once, breaking into hundreds of fragments.
His body thrashed soundlessly.
As Go Jun lost consciousness from the unimaginable pain, I poured internal energy into him.
Once the light returned to his fading eyes, I hammered my fist into his shattered legs.
Boom!
Boom!
Boom!
By the time I finally stopped punching, what lay sprawled across the ground was no longer a human being but a large lump of meat.
The faint breath leaking from his nose and mouth was the only proof that he remained alive.
The Skeleton King, who had watched everything from inside my Inventory, spoke in a trembling voice.
“Human.”
I answered dryly.
“What?”
“N-No.
It’s just...”
His voice trailed off, but I already knew what he wanted to say.
“Yeah.
It’s cruel.”
“But it was necessary.”
The helplessness of being unable to do anything.
Pain so unbearable that death seemed a hundred—even a thousand—times preferable.
And the fear that I could do the same thing to them anytime I wanted.
I needed to plant all of that in my enemy’s heart and carve it into his bones.
Of course, there was another option that would leave the fewest loose ends.
*Death.*
My fingertips twitched before I realized it.
With just a little more force—only a tiny bit—I could kill Go Jun.
It was the perfect opportunity to eliminate even the slightest possibility.
But...
*The timing isn’t right.*
Doubts surrounding the truth never disappeared completely.
Conspiracy theories claimed that humanity had never landed on the moon, or that countless famous figures recorded as dead were actually still alive.
This was no different.

If Lee Jungryong disappeared, followed by Wu Heixing and then Go Jun—and it came to light that I had “coincidentally” been here at exactly the right time—the rumors surrounding me would cease to be mere conspiracy theories.
So this was where I had to stop.
Now, after showing him the overwhelming gap between our powers and planting the fear of me deep inside him.
“I’ll say this one last time.”
Go Jun’s body flinched.
In a voice lower and more emotionless than ever, I bit out every word.
“Let it end with Lee Jungryong alone.”
My breath, hot as lava, brushed against him, and his prone body convulsed.
Like a rabbit feeling a tiger’s teeth sink into its neck.
“Hide your teeth.
Sheathe your claws.
If you do that... nothing will happen.”
If he had set out to kill, he should have been prepared to die.
Lee Jungryong had been my greatest enemy and obstacle.
In the end, he had paid the price for what he had done.
What I was offering now was a chance to make peace.
No—a demand.
And Go Jun had only one choice left.
His head moved in the faintest nod.
I stared into his eyes, drenched in fear and dread, then pressed his Sleep Acupoint.
After taking several high-grade potions from my Inventory, I poured them over his body.
Hissssss.
I watched his wounds rapidly heal, then suddenly turned my head.
“So... that’s more or less what happened.”
At that moment, a layer of space peeled away, revealing a huge Black man.
Magic Johnson regarded me with a complicated expression before speaking.
“I think there’s a lot we need to talk about.”
“I was thinking the same thing.”
As we spoke, the Skeleton King muttered quietly.
“What about the club?”
*That’s a gay bar, dumbass.*

chapters.title: Chapter 432
paragraphs: Magic Johnson was a good man.
Whether on the battlefield or in civilian life, he was always the same.
No matter the situation, he remained cheerful and never lost his smile. He had shown particular kindness to Team Leader Choi and me, even secretly handling the matter of the Skeleton King for us.
But there was no trace of playfulness or laughter in the way Magic Johnson looked at me now.
He stared at me in silence, a jumble of emotions in his eyes, before suddenly speaking.
“How much of it is true?”
“All of it. From beginning to end. Everything you saw and heard.”
I put particular emphasis on the word *everything*. Magic Johnson wasn’t dense enough to miss what I meant.
“...So you knew from the beginning.”
“As you know, I’m pretty sensitive.”
“And you didn’t care?”
“I didn’t expect you to follow me. But then I thought this might not be such a bad thing.”
“I was curious. Part of me was worried, too. It was obvious you knew something about that mysterious pattern, and just as obvious that you were hiding it.”
Before we parted, when Magic Johnson had asked about the Magic Formation, I had made the excuse that I thought I had seen something similar in a dream.
Of course, I hadn’t expected him to believe me. It had been a roundabout way of telling him not to ask about it for now.
“So I followed you, just in case...”
Magic Johnson trailed off and surveyed the blood-soaked surroundings.
“Looks like I shouldn’t have bothered.”

Two S-rank Hunters—each practically the face of his own country—had died in this momentous incident. One of them had even been a comrade who had once fought alongside Magic Johnson on the same battlefield.
Some truths were uncomfortable to know.
For Magic Johnson, this must have been one of them.
“Do you regret it?”
“A little. Maybe I would’ve been better off not knowing.”
Magic Johnson let out a quiet sigh and looked me straight in the eye.
“Jin. Why are you telling me all this?”
“Who knows?”
“You were the only one who knew the truth. If you wanted to, you could have covered it up. The same goes for him.”
I glanced at the unconscious Go Jun and shook my head.

“This wasn’t something I could hide just by keeping quiet. No matter how much I denied it, that bastard would never have believed me. Lee Jungryong and Go Jun were both ticking time bombs—dangerous enough to threaten my people.”
“Jin. You... were their enemy. You have been for a long time.”
“Yes. If you can’t eliminate an enemy, you have to make them so afraid of you that they’ll never dare look your way again. A bomb with its detonator removed can’t explode.”
“Then what about me? Why did you tell me?”
“You already know. In a situation like this, there are only two kinds of people you can choose.”
I continued slowly, enunciating each word.
“Enemies. Or friends.”
“I thought you would believe me, Johnson. Because you’re my friend.”
Magic Johnson let out a low groan and stared at me, countless emotions mingling in his eyes.
“Being friends doesn’t mean believing everything the other person says, Jin.”
“But you believed me. You didn’t doubt me once during our entire conversation.”
“Help me. Help me protect my people and build my strength.”
For some time now, I had felt everything around me beginning to change.
In Murim, Dark Heaven had begun to stir. In the modern world, the Arch Lich—a Named Monster unlike any that had come before it—had slaughtered millions and brought catastrophe in its wake.
Then there were the mysterious patterns and symbols that had appeared in both worlds.
Or perhaps they were something that could be called *dark magic*.
*Could all of this really be a coincidence?*
Everything that happened in the world was connected by invisible links. If I didn’t want it all to topple like a row of dominoes, I had to prepare.
And to do that, I desperately needed an ally.
“Johnson.”
“...Damn it.”
Magic Johnson remained silent for a moment before letting out a deep sigh.
“You know something?”
“That day—if you hadn’t asked me to teleport you straight into the monster army, I might have doubted you.”
That one remark was as good as an agreement.
My face lit up, and Magic Johnson couldn’t help but laugh.
“Damn it. It’s too late to turn back now. First, let’s clean this place up before the patrol arrives.”
He waved a hand, and the blood splattered everywhere vanished without a trace.
After cleaning the area in an instant with Clean magic, Magic Johnson frowned at Go Jun’s fallen body.
“He’s the problem... I’d like to erase his memories entirely, but given the circumstances, that would be difficult. What a pain.”
“Huh?”
My ears perked up.
I suddenly remembered how the Ares Guild’s mages had used memory-manipulation magic on the Myeongdong Guild members who had been present when I stormed their Guild.
“You can do that?”
“It would obviously be difficult, but not impossible. The stronger the target’s will and the more extensive the memories that need to be altered, the harder it becomes.”
“Oh.”
“He seems quite strong. In the worst case, we could fail and leave behind evidence that someone attempted to manipulate his mind.”
Go Jun might not look it now, but he was strong enough to qualify as an S-rank Hunter.
Unlike Wu Heixing, he was also fairly strong-willed, so trying it could be a needless gamble.
“Leaving evidence would be a problem.”
“Yes. If it were discovered, there’d be no avoiding punishment. Mental-manipulation magic is a serious felony.”
Yet Lee Jungryong and the Ares Guild had done such things without the slightest hesitation.
Even if someone noticed, they wouldn’t dare question it. Everyone knew how much power and influence they possessed.
“Still, if we tried and succeeded...”
“Under federal law, the minimum sentence would be one hundred years in prison without parole. Want to try?”
I answered without taking a breath.
“No.”
“Good boy. Wise decision.”
A minimum of one hundred years without parole?
If I got caught, I’d rot in prison without a chance. Even if I escaped, I’d spend the rest of my life as an internationally wanted fugitive.
I might even end up with a ten-billion-beri bounty on my head, living as a pirate on Somalia’s Grand Line like some manga character.
The thought alone was horrifying...
“What a shame. If this were Korea, it might be worth trying.”
“Korea? Why?”
“If you spread enough money around and hired a former chief prosecutor who could benefit from *jeongwan yewu*, you probably wouldn’t get much of a sentence.”
“Jeongwan yewu? What’s that?”
“It’s a thing. Ah, if you said you’d done it while drunk after downing about five bottles of soju, you might even get a suspended sentence.”
Magic Johnson laughed loudly as if he had heard an incredible joke.
“Don’t be ridiculous, Jin. What kind of country would allow that?”
“You’re serious? My God.”
In any case, memory-manipulation magic was off the table.
Leaving Go Jun where he lay, I walked away. The three A-rank Hunters he had concealed nearby were frozen like statues, their Paralysis Acupoints struck by the Finger Qi I had fired at them.
“You saw everything, right?”
The three men looked up at me with terror-filled eyes.
Sometimes watching someone else suffer inspired even greater fear than experiencing it yourself.
Unable to move so much as a finger, they had watched Go Jun get brutally and thoroughly crushed. They looked half out of their minds.
“I remember all three of your faces. Getting your personal information is only a matter of time.”
It was the same method the powerful had always used.
If I couldn’t kill them, I had to use that method to instill fear in them. I had to make sure they never dared bare their teeth at me again.
“If we meet like this again... I’ll kill you.”
Whoosh!
The killing intent that erupted from me sliced through the air and crushed everything around us.
After reining in my qi, I slowly swept my gaze over their corpse-pale faces, then thrust out a hand.
Crack-crack-crack!
“Ghk!”
“Hah, huff...”
Finally released from the Pressure-Point Strike, the men gasped for breath. Tears pooled in their bloodshot eyes, while saliva and vomit streamed from their open mouths.
“I’ll give you ten seconds. Take that bastard and get lost.”
There was no question who *that bastard* meant.
Before I had even finished speaking, the three men scrambled to their feet and rushed toward Go Jun.
They hoisted their still-unconscious superior onto one man’s back and fled with lightning speed.
I called one final warning after them.
“Erase everything that happened today from your memories. And think carefully about which ship you need to board if you want to stay alive.”
The Ares Guild was a massive, sturdy ship.
But its great captain, Cheon Taemin, had vanished without a trace long ago. Now Lee Jungryong, the man who had taken the helm after him, had also met his death.
The ship that had once seemed destined to sail the seas forever was beginning to list.
A captain couldn’t abandon his ship, but the sailors hired to serve aboard it were different.
If they wanted, they could find a new ship and a new shipowner.
*That should be enough for them to understand.*
The three men hesitated briefly at my words, then disappeared into the darkness.
They offered no answer or visible reaction, but I knew one thing.
They would never forget what I had said.

They would turn it over in their minds dozens—hundreds—of times before passing it on to their fellow Guild members. Then, little by little, water would begin seeping into the bottom of the enormous ship called the Ares Guild.
“Ooh, wicked human. Ooooooh.”
“This is what you call strategy, you idiot.”
“How can someone so stupid be this underhanded and cunning?!”
“...You son of a bitch.”
He wasn’t wrong, but it still pissed me the fuck off.
Let’s just say that after several years as a Hunter, I had picked up a few things through experience.

Magic Gems were now the essential power source of cutting-edge civilization. Naturally, that drew enormous amounts of capital. Capital attracted people, and wherever people gathered, all kinds of things were bound to happen.
*I’ve put the bait out with what I know... If I wait, someone will bite.*
Just as a sect’s standing in Murim was determined by the martial artists it possessed, a modern Guild’s standing was determined by the caliber of its Hunters.
And Go Jun could never fill the void Lee Jungryong had left behind.
Just as Lee Jungryong had never been able to fill the void left by Cheon Taemin.
It was only a matter of time before the fish spotted another tempting lure beyond that empty space and began swimming away.
“You certainly don’t hesitate. Are you planning to go to war with the Ares Guild?”
I shrugged at Magic Johnson’s question.
“It’s not like I couldn’t, but we should keep up appearances.”
“Appearances, huh?”
“The Peace Guild is going to grow enormously from now on. It has me, and Team Leader Choi is attracting plenty of media attention too.”
“Oh, I heard about that. Apparently Choi’s been making quite a name for himself lately.”
The global media spotlight was focused on me, but the more I avoided the press, the more attention shifted toward Team Leader Choi.
He belonged to the same Peace Guild as I did and was one of the very few people allowed to visit my hospital room.
On top of that, he had distinguished himself during this monster wave and was handsome enough to put celebrities to shame.
*And his greatest secret still hasn’t been revealed.*
If the truth—that he was Cheon Taemin’s own flesh and blood—ever became public, the media would undoubtedly go into a frenzy.
“Anyway, it’s only a matter of time before the Peace Guild takes off. Meanwhile, the Ares Guild’s influence will shrink by the day.”
“Hmm. I can certainly see that happening.”
Magic Johnson nodded, then suddenly spoke.
“But, Jin.”
“Yes?”
“What exactly do you know about the Magic Formation—”
“Oh, right. The club!”
“Huh?”
“You said you were going to a club with the Skeleton King.”
“Wait, wait, Jin!”
“Golgoli! Let’s go to the club!”
“Yes! Raise your ribs and scream!”
Listening to the Skeleton King spout nonsense, I hurried away.
Then, as I gazed up at the faint moonlight, a thought suddenly occurred to me.
*I should go back soon.*
The time was approaching.
The time to return to another world—to Murim.
