I might even end up with a ten-billion-beri bounty on my head, living as a pirate on Somalia’s Grand Line like some manga character.
The thought alone was horrifying...
“What a shame.
If this were Korea, it might be worth trying.”
“Korea?
Why?”
“If you spread enough money around and hired a former chief prosecutor who could benefit from *jeongwan yewu*, you probably wouldn’t get much of a sentence.”
“Jeongwan yewu?
What’s that?”
“It’s a thing.
Ah, if you said you’d done it while drunk after downing about five bottles of soju, you might even get a suspended sentence.”
Magic Johnson laughed loudly as if he had heard an incredible joke.
“Don’t be ridiculous, Jin.
What kind of country would allow that?”
“You’re serious?
My God.”
In any case, memory-manipulation magic was off the table.
Leaving Go Jun where he lay, I walked away.
The three A-rank Hunters he had concealed nearby were frozen like statues, their Paralysis Acupoints struck by the Finger Qi I had fired at them.
“You saw everything, right?”
The three men looked up at me with terror-filled eyes.
Sometimes watching someone else suffer inspired even greater fear than experiencing it yourself.
Unable to move so much as a finger, they had watched Go Jun get brutally and thoroughly crushed.
They looked half out of their minds.
“I remember all three of your faces.
Getting your personal information is only a matter of time.”
It was the same method the powerful had always used.
If I couldn’t kill them, I had to use that method to instill fear in them.
I had to make sure they never dared bare their teeth at me again.
“If we meet like this again...
I’ll kill you.”
Whoosh!
The killing intent that erupted from me sliced through the air and crushed everything around us.
After reining in my qi, I slowly swept my gaze over their corpse-pale faces, then thrust out a hand.
Crack-crack-crack!
“Ghk!”
“Hah, huff...”
Finally released from the Pressure-Point Strike, the men gasped for breath.
Tears pooled in their bloodshot eyes, while saliva and vomit streamed from their open mouths.
“I’ll give you ten seconds.
Take that bastard and get lost.”
There was no question who *that bastard* meant.
Before I had even finished speaking, the three men scrambled to their feet and rushed toward Go Jun.
They hoisted their still-unconscious superior onto one man’s back and fled with lightning speed.
I called one final warning after them.
“Erase everything that happened today from your memories.
And think carefully about which ship you need to board if you want to stay alive.”
The Ares Guild was a massive, sturdy ship.
But its great captain, Cheon Taemin, had vanished without a trace long ago.
Now Lee Jungryong, the man who had taken the helm after him, had also met his death.
The ship that had once seemed destined to sail the seas forever was beginning to list.
A captain couldn’t abandon his ship, but the sailors hired to serve aboard it were different.
If they wanted, they could find a new ship and a new shipowner.
*That should be enough for them to understand.*
The three men hesitated briefly at my words, then disappeared into the darkness.
They offered no answer or visible reaction, but I knew one thing.
They would never forget what I had said.
They would turn it over in their minds dozens—hundreds—of times before passing it on to their fellow Guild members.
Then, little by little, water would begin seeping into the bottom of the enormous ship called the Ares Guild.
“Ooh, wicked human.
Ooooooh.”
“This is what you call strategy, you idiot.”
“How can someone so stupid be this underhanded and cunning?!”
“...You son of a bitch.”
He wasn’t wrong, but it still pissed me the fuck off.
Let’s just say that after several years as a Hunter, I had picked up a few things through experience.
Magic Gems were now the essential power source of cutting-edge civilization.
Naturally, that drew enormous amounts of capital.
Capital attracted people, and wherever people gathered, all kinds of things were bound to happen.
*I’ve put the bait out with what I know...
If I wait, someone will bite.*
Just as a sect’s standing in Murim was determined by the martial artists it possessed, a modern Guild’s standing was determined by the caliber of its Hunters.
And Go Jun could never fill the void Lee Jungryong had left behind.
Just as Lee Jungryong had never been able to fill the void left by Cheon Taemin.
It was only a matter of time before the fish spotted another tempting lure beyond that empty space and began swimming away.
“You certainly don’t hesitate.
Are you planning to go to war with the Ares Guild?”
I shrugged at Magic Johnson’s question.
“It’s not like I couldn’t, but we should keep up appearances.”
“Appearances, huh?”
“The Peace Guild is going to grow enormously from now on.
It has me, and Team Leader Choi is attracting plenty of media attention too.”
“Oh, I heard about that.
Apparently Choi’s been making quite a name for himself lately.”
The global media spotlight was focused on me, but the more I avoided the press, the more attention shifted toward Team Leader Choi.
He belonged to the same Peace Guild as I did and was one of the very few people allowed to visit my hospital room.
On top of that, he had distinguished himself during this monster wave and was handsome enough to put celebrities to shame.
*And his greatest secret still hasn’t been revealed.*
If the truth—that he was Cheon Taemin’s own flesh and blood—ever became public, the media would undoubtedly go into a frenzy.
“Anyway, it’s only a matter of time before the Peace Guild takes off.
Meanwhile, the Ares Guild’s influence will shrink by the day.”
“Hmm.
I can certainly see that happening.”
Magic Johnson nodded, then suddenly spoke.
“But, Jin.”
“Yes?”
“What exactly do you know about the Magic Formation—”
“Oh, right.
The club!”
“Huh?”
“You said you were going to a club with the Skeleton King.”
“Wait, wait, Jin!”
“Golgoli!
Let’s go to the club!”
“Yes!
Raise your ribs and scream!”
Listening to the Skeleton King spout nonsense, I hurried away.
Then, as I gazed up at the faint moonlight, a thought suddenly occurred to me.
*I should go back soon.*
The time was approaching.
The time to return to another world—to Murim.

paragraphs: On a state-of-the-art hologram TV, a respectable-looking middle-aged news anchor spoke.

“Twenty days have passed since the monster wave in Sichuan Province—the tragedy dubbed the ‘Small Cataclysm’—finally came to an end. Across the continent, the cries of suffering people fill the air. CCTV correspondent Zhang Weijia is at the scene.”
As soon as he finished speaking, the screen changed.
Amid ruins reduced to rubble and ash, a young reporter in protective gear faced the camera and began to speak.

“Large-scale recovery efforts are currently underway throughout Sichuan Province. Aid continues to arrive from countries around the world, but the scars left by the war are nothing short of horrific.”
The camera slowly panned across the area.
The young reporter dispatched to cover the story was far from the only person there. Countless people of different countries, languages, and nationalities filled the ruins.
“Lift on three! One, two!”
“Hup!”
*Thud-thud-thud. Boom!*
There were places that heavy machinery could not enter.
Burly Hunters lifted chunks of stone and concrete instead of weapons, while mages cast detection magic without rest in search of possible survivors.
“How does it look?”
“There don’t seem to be any survivors within a hundred-meter radius. Let’s move a little and try again...”
“Here! We’ve got a survivor reading over here! Hurry!”
Whenever a severely injured survivor was rescued, healers rushed in and showered them with potions and healing magic.
When a child who had reached the brink of death finally drew a steady breath, the people around them exchanged deeply moved smiles.
But the joy lasted only a moment.
The reporter’s next words brought the cruel reality crashing back.

“According to government authorities, the number of dead and injured identified so far has reached four million. Property damage amounts to 2.3 trillion yuan. This is the greatest loss suffered since the Great Cataclysm—dozens of times greater than the damage caused by the Great Sichuan Earthquake.”
In barely a month, millions had died or been injured, and an astronomical amount of money had vanished.
Even more frightening was the fact that all of this was merely the damage tallied *so far*.
Considering everything from the plunging stock market to the damage this incident had inflicted on various industries, China would suffer badly in the days ahead.
The Chinese people were consumed by grief and fury at the news, directing the arrows of a billion people’s anger in a single direction.
The young reporter at the scene was no exception. His voice seethed with indignation as he continued.

“This monster wave was like a natural disaster beyond human power to stop. But if everyone had joined forces to prepare for the disaster and respond swiftly, the situation would have been very different. Chairman Xiao Yang has offered a profound apology and released the transcript of last month’s meeting.”
Its contents were shocking.

The transcript of the Communist Party’s highest committee meeting, previously hidden from the public, laid bare the bitter clash between Chairman Xiao Yang’s faction, which had urged them to seek immediate assistance from other countries, and the Crown Prince Party, which had argued that they should rally the power of Zhonghua and fight with the spirit of chivalry.
One person stood out above all the rest.
The star of the transcript was an old politician who had lost everything following the loss of his only son, Wu Heixing.

“Committee Member Wu Xueming, Premier of the State Council and a member of the Central Politburo Standing Committee, has spent more than fifty years in politics. It has now been revealed that he committed countless acts of corruption while leading the Crown Prince Party, the country’s largest political faction.”
Had the outcome been favorable, none of this would have happened.

But the power of Zhonghua and the spirit of chivalry he had gone on about during the meeting at the beginning of the Small Cataclysm had sounded like nothing but bullshit even to those steeped in Zhonghua ideology. In the end, they had become the laughingstock of the entire world.
Then it came to light that his past corruption involving the military had led to incidents in which tanks broke down and helicopters crashed. Wu Xueming found himself driven to the edge of a cliff.
And Chairman Xiao Yang, a seasoned politician, did not let the perfect opportunity slip by.

“Committee Member Wu Xueming used his guanxi with prominent figures in the military, political, and business worlds to embezzle astronomical sums of money. We are currently investigating every circumstance connected to this incident.”
In truth, the large-scale purge had already begun.

Of the seven standing committee members who formed the Communist Party’s highest echelon, the leading figures of the Crown Prince Party—including Wu Xueming—had been summoned one after another. A sweeping reorganization of the military had also taken place.
The media merely pointed its cameras where the government directed and recited whatever the government chose to show.
Several more investigations and trials still lay ahead, but everyone knew they would be nothing more than formalities.
“Comrades of the people, they will pay the price their crimes deserve. That is justice—”
“Hey, mister.”
Someone abruptly cut off the young reporter’s furious outcry, delivered in complete disregard of his duty as a journalist. His mind went blank.
*What kind of lunatic interrupts a live broadcast...?*
This was a colossal broadcasting disaster.
The staff at the scene, the main anchor at the broadcasting station’s desk, and even the director watching TV in his office all stared openmouthed.
But the man responsible for the entire mess could not have been calmer.
If anything, he sounded annoyed as he addressed the reporter.
“Move aside. It’s fine that you’re covering the story, but you’re getting in the way.”
“Pardon?”
“Did someone stuff your ears with stinky tofu? I’m telling you to go film somewhere else instead of blocking the way in the middle of an active work site.”
The young reporter’s face turned as white as paper. He stammered and glanced around.
The staff were terrified by the colossal broadcasting disaster unfolding before them, while the nearby Hunters looked as if someone had finally said exactly what they were thinking.
After a brief struggle, the reporter managed to shake off his panic. He forced a smile and addressed the man.
“I-I’m sorry. It seems we made a mistake.”
“To hell with sorry... Ugh, my throat.”
*Khhk—ptooey.*
Covered in dust from head to toe, the man spat out a wad of black phlegm and continued.
“It’s only a mistake if you didn’t know. I saw you slip the person in charge some money to get in here, so don’t give me that.”
“E-Excuse me! What exactly are you implying?”
“What do you mean, implying? I saw the whole thing. Wanna bet your balls on it?”
At that moment, the cameraman watching the entire scene unfold at point-blank range felt his own balls tremble.
*We’re fucked.*
His employer, CCTV, was China’s largest broadcasting station and one of the five biggest in the world.
And now, during the nine-o’clock evening news broadcast watched by tens of millions of people, someone was proposing a bet involving his balls.
The young reporter was already begging the man with the expression of someone whose balls had been cut off.
“S-Sir, please...”
“Hey, kid. Move while I’m asking nicely.”
“This is a broadcast. So please watch your language...”
“Wow, you really don’t listen. There’s a survivor underneath where you’re standing, so move.”
“What?!”
The reporter and every member of the staff leaped back as if they had been burned.
Only then did the man nod.
He strode over to a massive pile of concrete and placed a hand on it.
“That’s better. Now stay back and don’t get in the way. You’ll get hurt.”
*Whoosh! Boom!*
There was no need to find anyone to help him.
A chunk of concrete that had taken several Hunters to move flew like a pebble, while rock and ground split apart like cheesecake whenever the man’s hand blurred.
*Papapapapak!*
It was over in the blink of an eye. Before a cup of instant noodles could have finished cooking, the man emerged from the deep pit into which he had vanished.
In his arms was a tiny old woman.
“What... What is this...?”
The broadcasting staff stood speechless at the astonishing sight until the Hunters rushing over pushed them aside.
When a healer in a pure-white robe hurried forward with a potion, the man waved him off.
“Not yet. She’s too weak to handle a potion right now.”
“W-Wait. You look like a close-combat Hunter, but this is my field of expertise...”
“Hmm. I don’t think so.”
The man answered calmly and placed a hand against the old woman’s back.
Warmth radiated from him strongly enough to be felt several meters away, and a faint trace of color returned to the old woman’s pallid face.
“Move her somewhere warm first. Keep her body temperature up with magic. Once she regains consciousness, you should be able to use a potion or healing magic.”
The healer stared back and forth between the old woman and the man, dumbfounded.
“T-Thank you, sir.”
“No need to thank me for doing the obvious, and no need for the ‘sir.’ Let’s leave it at that. And... hmm.”
The man hesitated briefly before continuing in a low, subdued voice.
“She’s the last one. In this area.”
Those who understood what he meant let out low groans.
They included not only the Hunters but the broadcasting staff as well. Strangely, although they accepted his claim, they could not hide their bewilderment.
*Why?*

All they had to do was glance around to see hundreds of Hunters using magic and cutting-edge equipment to search for survivors. It was only natural to trust them over the man standing before them. They should have dismissed his words as nonsense, and yet...
*Somehow, I believe him.*
Why?
After the astonishing scene they had just witnessed, all thought of a *broadcasting disaster* vanished from their minds.
Two other thoughts surfaced in its place.
*No way. Could it be?*
“That’s only my personal opinion. So please don’t give up until the very end.”
The cameraman raised the camera he had unknowingly let droop toward the ground.
Then he called out to the man, who had bowed his head slightly and was about to turn away.
“C-Could you be Mr. Jin?”
His question spoke for everyone present.
The man was so thoroughly covered in dust that they could barely make out his features.
But what he had shown them in that brief moment had clearly reminded them of one person...
“No.”
The answer came without even a breath’s hesitation. The cameraman asked again.
“Y-You’re not?”
“You mean Jin Taekyung? I appreciate the mistake, but why would he be here? According to the news, he hasn’t shown hide nor hair of himself. Who knows what he’s doing?”
That was true. Jin Taekyung was a hero who had not shown his face once since the press conference.
It seemed absurd that they had suspected him based on nothing more than a vague feeling.
Just as the cameraman sighed, the young reporter suddenly spoke.
“Then may I ask you one question?”
“No. Take care.”
“What do you think of the claim that Mr. Jin is descended from Chen Lin, the Ming Dynasty general who fought in the Imjin War?”
At that moment, the man walking away spun around like lightning.
“Why does everyone have to be someone’s descendant? Then, for fuck’s sake, is Asmodeus descended from Einstein? Even bullshit should make some kind of sense...”
A silence fell as if the world itself had stopped.
The man—Jin Taekyung—looked at the people staring blankly at him and opened his mouth.
“You all know I was joking, right?”
“I was just passing by and stopped in for a moment.”
“Please edit this out. And cut the part about the balls too.”
The reporter, finally recovering from the shock, barely managed to squeeze out his voice.
“It’s live, sir.”
“Oh.”
Jin Taekyung nodded, his expression devastated, then asked again.
“Live? You’re not joking? It’s actually live?”
“Yes.”
“Then how much of that did you broadcast...?”
“I’m sorry, but from the beginning to the end...”
“Any idea what the ratings are?”
“I just checked the messages. They say we’ve broken through thirty percent.”
“Oh. I see.”
Jin Taekyung fell silent for a moment, then started walking away.
The young reporter, whose life had just turned around as a colossal broadcasting disaster transformed into a sensational exclusive, called after him desperately.
“S-Sir! Where are you going?”
The answer came back, drained of all energy.
“Home.”
He was telling the truth.
A formation of dozens of aircraft swept across the sky and landed on the vast expanse of freshly cleared ground.
It was the aircraft formation that would take him back to Korea while he was briefly going to another world.

The young reporter, whose life had just turned around as a colossal broadcasting disaster transformed into a sensational exclusive, called after him desperately.
“S-Sir!
Where are you going?”
The answer came back, drained of all energy.
“Home.”
He was telling the truth.
A formation of dozens of aircraft swept across the sky and landed on the vast expanse of freshly cleared ground.
It was the aircraft formation that would take him back to Korea while he was briefly going to another world.

paragraphs: “Have you looked in a mirror?”
That was the first thing Team Leader Choi, the first person off the aircraft, said to me.
I’d already guessed I looked rough, considering the people around me hadn’t recognized me, but was I really that much of a mess?
“No. Is it bad?”
“Yes. Bad enough that even your family couldn’t recognize you, Mr. Jin.”
“Other people, maybe, but Mom would recognize me. She went through labor to give birth to me.”
“We watched the news together on the flight here. During your interview, she asked who that filthy-looking man was and why he kept snapping at everyone.”
“...Seriously?”
I looked over Team Leader Choi’s shoulder.
Mom poked her head through the open doorway of the private jet and spoke in a voice as tiny as an ant.
“Sorry, son.”
She vanished as soon as she said it, and a slim face appeared in her place. It was Hayeon, her skin glowing as if she’d spent the past several days eating and sleeping to her heart’s content.
“I recognized you right away! I’m the only one who did, right?”
“Who are you? I’m an only child.”
“What the heck?”
Letting Hayeon’s words go in one ear and out the other, I asked Team Leader Choi, “That brat talked the most trash about me, didn’t she?”
“Yes. She was having a wonderful time egging your mother on.”
Yep. She was definitely my sister.
Hayeon must have overheard us, because she immediately pulled her head back inside. She wasn’t just good at studying—she was quick on the uptake, too.
“It’s nice to see such a harmonious family.”
“If we became twice as harmonious, someone would disappear from the family register.”
Team Leader Choi replied with a straight face.
“That would still be better. I don’t have any family. Except for my maternal grandfather, and I don’t even know where he is.”
“...Why are you doing this to me?”
“It was a joke.”
“Please use your turn signal before swerving into my lane like that.”
Team Leader Choi chuckled at my grumbling and extended a hand.
At a brief activation word, an Item imbued with Clean magic flashed brightly.
A cool breeze made of mana swept over me, blowing away all the dust and grime at once.
“Thanks. Much better.”
“Don’t mention it. You’ve certainly kept busy to the very end. You vanished without warning on the day of your departure, which put us in a rather difficult position.”
“You’re making it sound worse than it was. I was planning to be back on time.”
Team Leader Choi stared at me without a word. I scratched the back of my head and continued as if I were making an excuse.
“I just stopped by on the off chance.”
“Mr. Jin.”
“I know what you’re going to say.”
“Even if you do, this still needs to be said.”
Team Leader Choi looked me in the eye and spoke with deliberate clarity.
“You can’t save everyone. Mr. Jin, you... did your best.”
I smiled bitterly.
I had witnessed many deaths, both in the modern world and in Murim.
Sometimes I had been a spectator, far removed from what was happening. Other times, I had been at the heart of it.
And whenever it was all over, I always found myself asking the same question.
Just as I did now.
*Was that really the best I could do?*
The best.
The greatest and finest one could achieve after devoting every ounce of sincerity and strength.
Those two words frightened me more than anything, because there was no fixed standard for them.
Whether you had done your best was something only you could decide.
But there would always be regrets. Even if they amounted to no more than a few crumbs, as long as they remained buried deep in your heart, you couldn’t truly say you had done your best.
Because doing your best meant having no regrets at all.
“Nice weather today.”
I looked up at the sky and muttered for no particular reason, then grinned at Team Leader Choi.
“Let’s call it second-best. I’ll feel better that way.”
“How you see yourself and how others see you are two different things. To us, it was the best—and more.”
That wasn’t Team Leader Choi’s voice.
I had already sensed his presence, so I turned without surprise.
The owner of the aged voice addressed me with a gentle smile.
“So... you are leaving after all, Mr. Jin.”
I smiled back at Chairman Xiao Yang.
“The hotel rates were higher than I expected.”
“They are merchants, are they not? It is only natural to charge for the services they provide.”
“I might’ve stayed if they’d offered me a discount, but I think they were overcharging me because I’m a foreigner.”
“Oh dear. So that happened. Shall this old man give them a stern talking-to and persuade you to stay a little longer?”
“The bus has already left. It would be rude to chase it down the road and ask the driver to open the door.”
“Then I suppose I have no choice but to let you go. Ha ha.”
As if any hotel would be crazy enough to charge me—let alone overcharge me—in a situation like this.
We traded light jokes while reaffirming each other’s intentions, then clasped hands.
“You have given us more help than I could ever dare measure.”
His voice and gaze were sincere.
The people who had accompanied the Chairman also bowed respectfully to me.
Several familiar faces stood among them, including Xiao Shen and Wei Fenghu, the Minister of National Defense.
I gave them a slight nod and answered with a joke.
“I only did what I had to do. More importantly, it wasn’t volunteer work. You know that, right?”
“Ha ha. Of course.”
I had momentarily forgotten, but the bounty on the Arch Lich’s head had been an astounding fifty trillion won.
It was such an astronomical sum that even the compensation I’d receive for fighting in a month-long war would look like pocket change beside it.
I had never imagined possessing that much money in my life, and it still didn’t feel real.
*Fifty trillion won.*
Only half a year ago, I’d been eating seven-thousand-won bowls of bone hangover soup to save money, then cooking ramen afterward because one bowl wasn’t enough to fill me up.
Maybe that was why I felt more dazed than happy.
“Um, by the way...”
Chairman Xiao Yang raised his eyebrows.
“Are you really going to pay me?”
The instant the words left my mouth, Team Leader Choi firmly stepped on my foot. Chairman Xiao Yang’s wrinkled eyes curved into a gentle smile.
“Why? Do you not wish to receive it?”
“No! Of course I do!”
My vehement reply sent a ripple of laughter through the crowd.
Chairman Xiao Yang laughed heartily and patted me on the shoulder.
“Did I not say so? It is only natural to pay a fair price for work performed.”
They said China was the Middle Kingdom because it was too large to be a small nation and too narrow-minded to be a Great Nation, but this old man sure was generous.
I scratched my chin awkwardly.

There was nothing wrong with receiving payment under the contract, but accepting a bounty of fifty trillion won amid such devastation made me feel like a thief rummaging through someone else’s storehouse.
“If money’s tight, you can pay me in installments.”
“If you are worried about rebuilding the damage, that is something our country must handle. Your bounty is being processed quickly, Mr. Jin, so it will be paid officially soon.”
Chairman Xiao Yang leaned closer and whispered in my ear.
“When I plowed the fields and pulled out the rotten stalks, piles of gold came tumbling out. So there is no need for you to feel uncomfortable, Mr. Jin.”
It took me a moment to realize he was talking about the Crown Prince Party.
According to the news, the assets seized so far already amounted to hundreds of trillions of won.
And that was before they had even touched Wu Xueming, the faction’s de facto leader, or the rest of its leadership.
*Now that’s some corruption.*
A country’s landmass must be proportional to the size of its people’s nerve.
Still, they had ended up penniless and behind bars, so justice had been served to some extent.
Feeling considerably lighter, I answered, “Then I’ll accept it gratefully.”
“What are you saying? Thanks to you, we were able to prevent an even greater catastrophe. On behalf of all the people who could not be here today, I offer you my thanks once again, Mr. Jin.”
Before I could stop them, Chairman Xiao Yang and his attendants bowed respectfully.
The people gathered here were the major officials who moved an entire nation.
They were, in essence, the body and head of China itself.
As I stood there flustered, a familiar voice reached my ear.
“Should I get down on my knees, too?”
“Faye Chen.”
She approached with a playful expression and poked me in the cheek.
“You worked hard, young man.”
“Not at all. Everyone...”
“Of course everyone worked hard. But if you hadn’t defeated the Arch Lich, we wouldn’t have this peace. I’m sure everyone feels the same way. Except for that obnoxious prince, of course.”
Prince Felix, dressed in a dazzling formal uniform with a snow-white cloak draped over his shoulders, gave an irritated cough and stared at me.
“What?”
“I pay my respects to you, Korean commoner.”
“...I appreciate it, but could you leave out the last few words?”
“I pay my respects to you, Korean commoner.”
“Are you doing this on purpose?”
“I am sincere.”
“I’m sure you are, you bastard. I really am a commoner.”
“That is not what I meant.”
Prince Felix suddenly extended a hand.
But unlike usual, he didn’t offer me the back of his own hand. Instead, he seized mine and pulled it toward him.
Then, while I stood there dumbfounded, he kissed the back of my hand and stepped away.
*What the fuck?*
Faye Chen burst out laughing at my speechless expression. Prince Felix calmly said what he had to say.
“I have shown you my respect. It shall never happen again, so treasure this honor for generations to come. Until we meet again.”
With that final remark, delivered without the slightest change in expression, Prince Felix swept away with his attendants.
Magic Johnson, who had watched the entire scene, smacked his lips.
“Charming.”
“...That’s your type?”
“Respect my preferences.”
“He has a spouse.”
“That is why I am restraining myself.”
We should never let him visit a Korean convenience store. The moment he took a bite of tuna mayo, the world would be hit by an unprecedented upheaval.
As I shook my head, Team Leader Choi spoke quietly.
“Mr. Jin. It’s time to leave.”
The words weren’t meant only for me, but for everyone gathered there.
I nodded and said my final farewells.
I made sure not to leave out Xiao Shen and Wei Fenghu, with whom I’d spent so much time.
“Take care.”
“We’ll definitely meet again, hyung.”
Xiao Shen, who was only in his early twenties, rubbed his reddened eyes with his sleeve before continuing.
“I’ll become an outstanding Hunter like you, hyung, and rise to lead the public security forces that protect everyone.”
“You’re still young, but you’re already blinded by the desire for power. That job must be brutal.”
“I’m ashamed to admit it, but I’ve decided to accept my grandfather’s help.”

“Good. He’ll have plenty of advice for you, so listen carefully and carve every word into your bones. I don’t know what kind of man he is, but I’m sure everything he tells you will be wise and helpful...”
My words were cut off by something Xiao Shen said.
“You know him too, hyung.”
“Huh? Know what?”
“My grandfather.”
“What are you talking about? The only grandfathers I know are Butler Kim from my Guild and the owner of the real-estate office outside my goshiwon.”
Chairman Xiao Yang cut in with a laugh.
“Ha ha. This old man is here as well, you know.”
“Oh, come on. Nice joke...”
Wait a minute.
The corners of my eyes began to twitch.
*Xiao Yang. Xiao Shen. Xiao, Xiao?*
I’d dismissed it because Xiao was a common surname in China, like Kim or Park in Korea, but now that I looked at them, their faces were strangely similar too.
“Don’t tell me...”
“Yes. That’s right.”
“Even you are no different, Mr. Jin. Everyone reacts the same way.”
“...I think I’m going to be sick.”
“Hyung?”
“Mr. Jin?”
What kind of novel was this?
*The Younger Friend I Met in China Turned Out to Be the Chinese Chairman’s Grandson.*
Even the title sounded ridiculous.
Why was everyone I met born with a silver spoon in their mouth?
After a brief bout of panic, I finally managed to force out my voice.
“Oh. I see.”
“I am grateful to you not only as Chairman, but also as a grandfather reunited with his grandson. It is a debt this old man could never repay in a lifetime.”
“Ah... No need to rush.”
Apparently, I had saved the Chinese Chairman’s grandson without even realizing it.
Still dazed, I exchanged final farewells with grandfather and grandson. Then my gaze fell on someone else.
*Wei Fenghu.*
I wasn’t imagining the emptiness in his smile.
Unlike his superior, he had lost someone of his own blood whom he loved.
We looked at each other in silence for a moment, then spoke at the same time.
“Goodbye.”
“Take care, Mr. Jin. You have truly worked hard.”
It was a brief exchange, but it was enough.
“Well, then.”
I gave everyone a slight bow and followed Team Leader Choi onto the waiting aircraft.

Mom looked me over with an expression that was equal parts anxious and delighted. Meanwhile, Hayeon had taken advantage of the distraction to sip champagne. When our eyes met, she gave me a sheepish smile.
“Oppa, want a glass?”
“What do you mean, a glass? You’re a minor. Hey, take that away from her.”
The Skeleton King, already in human form and seated nearby, ignored me completely. He muttered in a gloomy voice.
“It won’t stand... I’m a eunuch...”
Team Leader Choi, seated beside him, offered a few words of consolation.
“Keep your chin up. Next time, I’ll ask Mr. Johnson to do something about it.”
“R-Really?”
I nearly smacked him, but a quiet laugh escaped me instead.
At last, I felt as if I were back where I belonged.
My beloved family, whom I love more than anyone, along with my colleagues and friends.
Even though we were inside a chartered plane rather than a house, I felt an indescribable sense of comfort.
*Yes. This is enough.*
“We will now begin takeoff. Passengers in the cabin, please...”
An announcement rang out, and the aircraft rose toward the sky under the escort of the flight formation.
After we had spent a long while laughing, talking, and sharing stories, I sensed that the time had come.
I watched everyone sleeping soundly from the fatigue that had built up, then lay back in my plush seat.
*Login.*
Ding.
With the familiar notification, darkness covered my vision, and I set off.
Toward another world and another group of people waiting for me far away.

chapters.title: Chapter 435
paragraphs: Night had fallen deep enough to swallow even the last glow of sunset. A boy sat at the bow, staring into the black river, when he abruptly spoke.
“What brings you here?”
“I thought I’d have a drink while gazing at the Yangtze. Didn’t realize someone had beaten me to the spot.”
Behind the boy, an old man barely five feet tall appeared like a ghost, without so much as a whisper. He shook the gourd in his hand and grinned.
“Well? Want some?”
“Excessive drinking is harmful to the body. You should abstain.”
“Don’t be like that. Have a drink with me. The atmosphere is nice.”
“It would be even better if I were alone.”
“What a mouth on such a green little brat. An elder’s been talking to you all this time, and you haven’t even bothered to look at him.”
The boy frowned. Dark clouds gathered over his handsome face—a face bright enough to evoke a clear blue sky—and lightning flashed across it.
Then, instead of his usual clear voice, a low, sunken voice slipped between his lips.
“That’s enough.”
A pale-blue gleam shone from his eyes in the darkness.
There was no trace left of Mungyeong, the bright and cheerful young medical apprentice.
In his place stood the peerless martial artist known as the Slaughter Saint, a savage beast baring its claws.
But he wasn’t the only monster aboard.
“Oh, how frightening.”

The old man curled up the corners of his mouth without a care in the world, standing before an aura powerful enough to freeze even an ordinary Peak master stiff as a statue. Then Fire King Jeok Cheongang tossed him the gourd.
“Drop the little-brat act. It doesn’t suit you. Wet your throat.”
Mungyeong caught the gourd as it drifted lazily toward him and answered in a dry voice.
“Not interested.”
“What, are you still too young to drink?”
“I quit. A long time ago.”
“Must’ve been when you started playing medical apprentice.”
“...Don’t you sleep?”
“You get less sleep when you’re old. Like someone I know.”

Mungyeong shook his head slightly. Taciturn by nature and unaccustomed to showing emotion, he had always found Jeok Cheongang difficult to talk to. If he didn’t want to deal with the man, his best option was to leave.
“You going?”
“That’s none of your business.”
“What about the liquor?”
Mungyeong tossed the gourd into the river. The rolling waters of the Yangtze swallowed it in an instant.
“I finished it.”
“...If you didn’t want it, you could’ve at least given it back. What a nasty old man.”
Mungyeong’s gaze sharpened as he walked past Jeok Cheongang.
The Slaughter Saint no longer existed. Now he was merely an ordinary young medical apprentice, the sort one might find anywhere.
“Your tongue is too loose.”
“There aren’t any ears listening, so what does it matter? Besides, after coming all this way, why bother hiding your identity?”
Mungyeong did not answer.
No—he couldn’t.
Why had he done it?
Had it been nothing more than a momentary impulse?
Even the cold reason that had never wavered through countless acts of killing could not explain it.
“I see. You still haven’t found the answer yourself.”
Mungyeong remained silent for a moment before replying.
“We’re merely traveling together.”
“I understand. That was how it started for me too. Then I met one bizarre bastard, and he completely ruined my later years.”
Mungyeong had a good idea who this “bizarre bastard” was, and he could think of no better description.
He had encountered every manner of person and incident in the turbulent martial world, yet that bastard was unlike anyone he had ever seen.
“Jin Taekyung.”
“So you do know him. Well, how could you not?”
“He’s an unusual one. He’s reached an impressive realm for his age.”
The corner of Jeok Cheongang’s mouth twitched.

“Ahem. Impressive, my ass. He’s just lucky. In terms of pure martial talent, he can’t compare to the Sword Saint’s Disciple. The kid doesn’t seem to realize it yet, but he’s already completed all the preparations necessary to open his Middle Dantian.”
Mungyeong recalled the young man who had spent the entire journey performing tricks with a snake.
He also remembered the sight of that same young man at the Sichuan Tang Clan, scattering dazzling Sword Force despite being barely past twenty.
“That boy was impressive too. No—he did seem impressively insane. In terms of talent alone, he’s definitely a step above Jin Taekyung.”
“What!”
“Ah.”
Mungyeong stared at Jeok Cheongang for a moment, then clicked his tongue.
“You certainly dote on your Disciple.”
“Disciple?”
Jeok Cheongang paused before clearing his throat.
“Ahem. Well. He might be my Disciple, or he might not...”
“What kind of nonsense is that?”
“No, well... The circumstances are somewhat complicated. You see, what happened was...”
Mungyeong suddenly felt a headache coming on.
It had been only a few days since an unheard-of group called Dark Heaven had dyed Sichuan red with blood.
His thoughts were tangled enough already. Listening to a story about this bizarre master and disciple threatened to give him seasickness he had never suffered before.
“If you have no further business with me, I’ll be leaving. I hope nothing like this happens again.”
Mungyeong tossed out the words and started toward the cabin.
“Thank you. For saving the kid.”
“I mean it.”
Mungyeong did not answer. He opened the cabin door and went inside. Jeok Cheongang grumbled behind him about what a prickly old man he was, but Mungyeong ignored him and sat on a hard wooden berth.
On the berth a few paces away, a passenger who had claimed the spot long ago was fast asleep.
Mungyeong stared at the motionless Jin Taekyung and thought,
*He really is a bizarre one.*
Perhaps that was why even the way he slept was strange. At first, his breathing had been so faint that Mungyeong wondered whether he had used the Turtle Breath Technique.
And that wasn’t all. Jin Taekyung possessed a Heavenly Martial Physique, a constitution that appeared perhaps once every few hundred years.
Jeok Cheongang had even made the unbelievable claim that Jin Taekyung’s body was steadily becoming more perfect.
*Absurd.*
Why was the Heavenly Martial Physique called the Heavenly Martial Physique?
Because it was the most perfect body for learning martial arts—a martial constitution bestowed by heaven itself.
The word *perfect* meant there was nothing to add and nothing to take away. Jeok Cheongang had surely misjudged the matter because his eyes were clouded by his foolish affection for his Disciple.
*Still, there’s no denying he’s an impressive bastard. Or should that be bastards?*
Cheongpung lay asleep on the berth right beside Jin Taekyung, drool running from his mouth.
His lips moved as if he were eating. On closer inspection, Mungyeong discovered that Cheongpung was sucking on the head of the snake he always carried beside him and mumbling in his sleep.
“Dumplings, roast duck, and mooncakes too, please...”
“Lots and lots, please...”
What in the world had happened while Mungyeong was away?
Mungyeong looked back and forth between Jin Taekyung and Cheongpung with an awkward expression.
*These are the ones destined to illuminate the future of Murim?*
Even in Mungyeong’s eyes, the pair had already gone far beyond the level of mere young prodigies.
They were peerless geniuses who had broken through the wall into Supreme Peak despite being barely past twenty.
If either of them opened their Middle Dantian before turning thirty, then...
*This is...*
Mungyeong’s eyes twitched as he studied Jin Taekyung and Cheongpung more closely.
*When? No, how?*
He sprang to his feet like lightning and hurriedly took Jin Taekyung’s pulse.

The instant he sent internal energy through the Mingmen acupoint, an utterly unbelievable reality unfolded before him. His thoughts ground to a halt, leaving only one fact circling endlessly through his mind.
*His Middle Dantian... is open?*
Even the Unshakable Mind he had cultivated over many years failed him.
And just as Mungyeong stared blankly into space, a voice spoke.
“What are you doing?”
Mungyeong lowered his gaze and found a pair of eyes looking up at him.
Jin Taekyung’s gaze moved from Mungyeong’s hand against the Mingmen acupoint on his back to the other hand resting against his chest, directly over his Middle Dantian.
Then he opened his mouth.
“What the fuck?”
Mungyeong answered with complete sincerity.
“It’s a misunderstanding.”
“More like, ‘Oh yeah.’”
“Calm down and listen to me...”
Jin Taekyung responded to his sincerity with a shout loud enough to wake everyone aboard the swift ship.
“Old Master!”
*Boom!*
The cabin door exploded into ash, revealing Fire King Jeok Cheongang.
In the dead of night, the peaceful silence of the Yangtze was shattered.

Mu Song, known as Ship-Fire Boy, was the Disciple of the Seafaring King—the Alliance Leader of the Yangtze River Channel League—and the Stronghold Lord of Water Dragon Stronghold, which ruled the rivers of Sichuan. He cried out with a face as though the sky had fallen.
“No! My swift ship!”
I quietly looked away, while the Slaughter Saint—no, Mungyeong—suddenly announced that he had medicine to prepare and left.
Jeok Cheongang, who had burned one of Mu Song’s swift ships to ashes, patted him on the shoulder.
“It’s fine. You can always build another ship.”
“No! Noooo!”
“Come now, I said it’s fine. With enough people and gold, a ship can be thrown together in no time.”

“It isn’t that simple! That wasn’t an ordinary ship. It was a special swift ship that only our Yangtze River Channel League can build! To make another, we’d have to contact headquarters, bring in craftsmen, and pour a thousand gold into it...”
Mu Song’s furious voice gradually faded.
Jeok Cheongang was watching him with an ominous smile.
Scorching Yang Qi already blazed around his fist.
“You’d pour a thousand gold into it, and then what?”
Mu Song closed his mouth.
He was clearly weighing whether to pour a thousand gold into rebuilding the swift ship or pour his own blood into the Yangtze.
In the end, it came down to money or his life. The choice wasn’t difficult.
“...I was about to say that even after pouring a thousand gold into it, we’d still have money left over, Great Hero Jeok.”
“Right? Business is good around here, isn’t it?”

Mu Song’s ferocious face twisted. The sight would have made ordinary people piss themselves down to their innards, but despite appearances, that was his smile. As befitted a pure-blooded river bandit, he simply had a vicious face.
Despite his size, he rubbed his palms together ingratiatingly.
“Oh, don’t even ask. We’d rob more if there were anything left to take.”
“Yes, yes. Good to hear. Since it came to mind, let me say this: don’t rob people too much. It’s none of my business, but they need to make a living too.”
“Yes, yes.”
“I apologize again for this incident. I made a small mistake while training.”
“Of course. Such things happen. Were you hurt anywhere?”
“No. But my qi has felt weak lately. It would be nice to have something to chew on...”
“We recently acquired a few fine specimens of He Shou Wu. It seems they’ve finally found their rightful owner.”
“The owner is you. This old man is merely a guest. Ha ha. Still, if you insist on giving them to me, I’ll gratefully accept.”
Jeok Cheongang patted Mu Song’s shoulder a few more times, then turned and scowled at me.
“Damn it. Why did you cause such a commotion in the middle of the night?”
I answered calmly.
“Imagine waking up and finding some man touching your chest and back.”
“I’d burn him down to bone ash.”
“Yes. That’s what happened. How was I supposed to think straight in that situation? Besides, you smashed everything to pieces before I could stop you.”
The result had been fiery.
True to his title as the Slaughter Saint, Mungyeong had evaded Jeok Cheongang’s attacks with ghostlike movements, while the Flame Divine Palm’s searing heat had set the swift ship ablaze.
Jeok Cheongang frowned and muttered,
“I thought that bastard hadn’t kicked his old habits.”
“Well, they say a habit formed at three lasts until eighty.”
“He passed eighty a long time ago, didn’t he?”
“Then let’s say a habit formed at three lasts until a hundred.”
Mungyeong, who had been rushing around checking on everyone who had fallen into the water, whispered as he passed us.
“If you don’t want to die, shut your mouth.”
Instead of shutting my mouth, I shouted loudly enough for everyone to hear.
“Mungyeong, what did you say?”
“Yes, yes?”
“No. Didn’t you just say something to me?”
“That couldn’t... possibly be. You must have misheard me.”
“Right?”
“Yes, yes.”
“Then keep doing your work. Thanks for your hard work.”
“Thank... you.”
This was what happened when you committed too hard to the bit.
Anyway, it sure was a spectacle immediately after coming back.
*This is Murim.*
I shook my head as I gazed out over the Yangtze stretching endlessly into the distance.

chapters.title: Chapter 436
paragraphs: The Yangtze.
As its name suggested, the Yangtze was immense. In terms of length especially, few rivers on the continent could compare.
It crossed five provinces in all—Sichuan, Chongqing, Hubei, Anhui, and finally Jiangsu. As a vital hub of waterborne transportation, it would occupy a large portion of our journey.
“Our current plan is to follow one of the Yangtze’s tributaries to Hubei, then disembark and continue overland to Henan.”
After finishing his brief explanation, Jin Wikyung slowly looked over the group, including me.
“Does anyone have any questions?”
Whoosh!
The instant he finished speaking, one hand shot into the air.

Judging by how fast it went up, its owner could have been a model student bursting with academic enthusiasm. In reality, the hand belonged to a Supreme Peak master notorious throughout Murim as a thug on a national scale.
“There’s something this old man has been wondering for a while.”
“I’m all ears, Great Hero Jeok.”
“So what you’re saying is...”
Jeok Cheongang continued with a deeply sour expression.
“It sounds like you’re telling us to grow old and die on this damn Yangtze. Am I mistaken?”
That was the Fire King for you. He really knew how to bring the heat.
Jin Wikyung swallowed hard at Jeok Cheongang’s way of speaking, which came crashing forward like an eight-ton truck with a broken steering wheel.
“How could that be, Great Hero Jeok? This is simply the itinerary decided upon at the meeting.”
“A meeting? What kind of lunatics came up with this schedule? Even at the fastest pace, it’ll take seven days and nights just to reach Hubei!”
“At the top, we have Great Hero Sword Saint Mae Jonghak, and beneath him, the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families...”
“That’s enough. I don’t need to hear any more.”
“Pardon?”

“The Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families are all idiots with nothing but shit in their heads, so forget about them. I’ll explain things properly to Mae Jonghak myself. Change the itinerary while there’s still time. Staring at water all day is going to give me qi deviation.”
In short, he was telling them to do their worst.
It was the kind of unreasonable demand only Jeok Cheongang could get away with. Not a single person here dared object to him.
*Ah. There was one person who could.*
Jeok Cheongang must have had the same thought, because he subtly turned his head.
His gaze met Mungyeong’s in midair.
Mungyeong looked back at him with an expression that clearly said *pathetic*.
Jeok Cheongang stared at him, then tossed out a single remark.
“Hey. What are you looking at me like that for?”
“You little punk, you’re still wet behind the ears. I ought to poke your eyes out and squeeze all the ink from them.”
He was openly laying into him now.
Mungyeong’s fist trembled.
As someone who knew his true identity, I found the sight chilling. To everyone else, however, it looked entirely different.
Hyuk Mujin and Gung Gibang, who had been languishing from the aftereffects of sampling the Yangtze, spoke in faint, faltering voices.
“Why are you picking on the boy? Just look at Mungyeong shaking. He’s such a gentle soul...”
“I may eat stray yellow dogs, but Mungyeong couldn’t kill an ant.”
He probably killed people during the time it took to kill an ant.
I had heard that more than a thousand people were *officially* known to have died at the hands of the Slaughter Saint.
Even if he went around smearing Madecassol healing ointment on his sword, he still wasn’t the sort of person anyone could call gentle.
“You lot... No. Forget it. Just keep living like that.”
Jeok Cheongang looked ready to say something, but let out a deep sigh instead. Then he abruptly turned toward me.
“Why are you saying nothing?”
“About what?”
“What else? Do you really want to keep floating around on this miserable water?”
“Oh, that.”
I scratched my chin and thought for a moment before answering.
“I don’t mind it.”
“What!”
“Little Brother!”
Jeok Cheongang and Jin Wikyung’s reactions were polar opposites. But I hadn’t said it to help Jin Wikyung. I meant it.
“There must be a reason the people in charge decided on this route. Besides, the scenery is nice.”
This was a world without environmental pollution. At dawn, a hazy mist blanketed the river, and the sight of the clear water stretching endlessly into the distance made my chest feel wide open.
When Jeok Cheongang had been unconscious, none of it had moved me at all, but...
In any case, I needed to set aside my impatience for a while and take the time to reflect and collect myself.
*And there are things I need to investigate.*
The mysterious patterns and symbols discovered in both worlds.

I had to find out whether my suspicions about them were correct. To do that, I had a lot to take care of while going back and forth between Murim and the modern world. If we traveled overland, the time available for that would be drastically reduced.
I tried to gently coax Jeok Cheongang around.
“It’s only a difference of a few days. Old Master—no, Master, you need to think about your health too. It hasn’t been long since you pushed yourself so hard.”
“What do you mean, pushed myself? Do you think this old man is on his deathbed?”
“Then what? Are you sixteen and in the prime of youth? A fresh-faced eighteen-year-old?”
“You little bastard!”
The instant Jeok Cheongang’s eyes flared, I hurriedly spoke.
“Martial arts! I need instruction in martial arts!”
The hand that had risen as though to smack me stopped in midair.
I didn’t miss the opening and continued.
“I’ve gained some insight recently. If we travel overland, there won’t be enough time for you to teach me.”
“Instruction...”
“There are parts I could never understand on my own, no matter how hard I rack my brain—even if I died and came back to life.”
“Is that true?”
“Yes. It’s precious instruction that only one person in all the world can give me—my master.”
Jeok Cheongang narrowed his eyes.
“If we use our movement techniques to the fullest overland, we could reach Henan several days earlier.”
“What does that have to do with receiving instruction?”

“It has everything to do with it. Didn’t you say before that you thought Sword Saint Mae Jonghak might be stronger than this old man? By your logic, shouldn’t you reach Henan as quickly as possible and ask the Sword Saint?”
I had tossed that out to tease him, but he actually remembered it.
I pretended not to know what he was talking about.
“You must have heard me wrong. Was I drunk out of my mind that day?”
“What a load of drunken bullshit.”
“To me, Master, you’re always the best.”
“Is that so?”
Jeok Cheongang glanced sideways at Mungyeong before asking,
“Then how do I compare to the Slaughter Saint?”
“What?”
“The Slaughter Saint. The one among the Three Saints whom no one can match when it comes to killing people. How do I compare to him?”
I could feel the people around me waiting with interest for my answer.
And I could also feel someone discreetly leaking killing intent.
*Ah, fuck it. I don’t know.*
I swallowed hard and opened my mouth.
“He’s a total fucking pushover.”
“Hm. Perhaps this boy knows what he’s talking about.”
“I know my martial arts, don’t I? I can size someone up at a glance.”
“Ahem. Did you grease your tongue? You’re showering me with flattery when you never do anything of the sort. Do you think this old man will fall for such a shallow trick?”
“...Then why are you smiling?”
Was he Murim’s Joker?
Jeok Cheongang’s grin had stretched all the way to his ears, but he immediately schooled his expression. He couldn’t quite hide the corners of his mouth twitching as he fought back a smile.
“When did I smile?”
“You didn’t. Anyway, let’s just keep going like this.”
Jeok Cheongang already knew that I had opened my Middle Dantian. He considered it for a moment, then smacked his lips.
“Damn it. Even so, I hate water. Looks like this old man will be suffering in his twilight years.”
Had he been a Fire Pokémon in his previous life?
At this point, maybe he should change his sobriquet from the Fire King to Charizard.
“What’s with that disrespectful look?”
“Me? When?”
“Forget it. It isn’t the first or second time, anyway. It was my mistake for expecting manners from an uncouth little brat like you.”
Jeok Cheongang clicked his tongue and turned toward Jin Wikyung.
“You heard everything, didn’t you?”
“Yes. We will see to it that you suffer no inconvenience.”
“So what are you planning to do after taking this miserable Yangtze to Hubei? There must be a reason worth enduring all this trouble.”
“We have an important matter to attend to.”
“An important matter?”
“Would it be all right if I told you later?”
Jeok Cheongang narrowed his eyes, but that was all.
If Jin Wikyung was speaking that way, it meant the matter was confidential—something better discussed with fewer ears around.
Jeok Cheongang might not care what other people thought, but that didn’t mean he was oblivious.
“Understood. Then are we finished here?”
Jin Wikyung politely clasped his hands.
“Thank you for your hard work.”
But one person was dissatisfied with the outcome of this brief meeting.
“W-wait a moment. Are you saying you intend to take our Water Dragon Stronghold’s swift ship all the way to Hubei?”
Jin Wikyung was about to answer the ship’s owner, Mu Song, when Jeok Cheongang stepped between them.
“Is there a problem?”
“G-Great Hero Jeok, Hubei is much too far. Even with a favorable wind, it will take more than seven days and nights...”
“You can’t leave the stronghold empty for that long?”
“Yes, yes! Exactly!”
“A body is no good if the torso and limbs are intact but the head is missing. That would be a problem.”
“Does that mean...?”
“Go as far as Sichuan.”
Mu Song’s face brightened.
“Thank you!”
“Leave the ship behind.”
“What?”
“Do you expect this old man to continue in a skiff? We can find sailors along the way. Leave this swift ship or whatever it’s called, then go back.”
Mu Song fell silent for a moment before managing to speak.
“Well...”
“What?”
“Now that I think about it, it would be better for my subordinates and me to escort you and see to your every need.”
“Good heavens, there’s really no need. I already feel bad about burning one of your ships. I’m not sure whether I should impose upon you like this.”
“...Please don’t set anything else on fire.”
“That depends on how you behave.”
Was this the tyranny of a major corporation?
In all my life, this was the first time I had ever felt sorry for a river bandit.
Mu Song clasped his hands and withdrew with a sorrowful expression. Cheongpung quietly approached him and held out the dumpling in his hand.
Just how much had he stuffed down his throat in the meantime? Both cheeks were already on the verge of bursting.
“’Ave one.”
“...Are you telling me to eat it? Are you giving it to me?”
“Yeah!”
Feeling the warmth of human kindness for the first time in ages, Mu Song’s eyes grew misty.
“Thank you, Young Hero Cheongpung.”
Then he stuffed the cold dumpling into his mouth in one bite.
Cheongpung swallowed what he had been chewing and smiled brightly.
“Tasty, right?”
“It truly is. It’s the best dumpling I’ve had lately. I’ll have to get some from you now and then.”
“That was the last one.”
“What? You gave me the last dumpling? Young Hero Cheongpung, you...”
“My grandpa told me that when you have something good, you should share it with other people.”
Considering how much he had eaten by himself until now, it sounded like complete bullshit. But Mu Song didn’t know that, and he was deeply moved.
“Thank you, Young Hero Cheongpung. We’ve barely even spoken, yet you’ve gone out of your way to do this for me. I didn’t know that... Sniff.”
Mu Song’s gratitude did not last long.
“My grandpa told me something else too. Whoever eats the last dumpling has to buy the next batch!”

“If we travel for one more day, we’ll reach a place called Guang’an. The dumplings sold in the market there are really good. When I traveled around the world for a year, I stayed there for a whole month because of those dumplings. Ah, no, that’s not what I meant. Grandpa said we absolutely had to stop there! He said whoever ate the last dumpling had to buy a whole bunch more!”
What a terrifying little bastard.
Now he was even selling out his grandfather to get more dumplings.
Gung Gibang, who had been watching the scene, muttered that Cheongpung would make an excellent Beggars’ Sect disciple.
Mu Song, now doomed to stop at the famous dumpling shop in Guang’an, answered with every last scrap of trust in humanity drained from his face.
“Understood.”
“Yay! Grandpa will be happy!”
Was that even human?
I was still horrified by the bottomless depths of his character when—
“You don’t look well. May I examine you for a moment?”
Fucking pushover—no, Mungyeong was looking at me with concern.
He had a large acupuncture needle hidden in one hand, pressed right against my waist.
“Uh, no. No, I’m fine. I’m not feeling—”
“You don’t look well. May I examine you for a moment?”
“I’m really fi—”
“You don’t look well. May I examine you for a moment?”
It was humiliating, but I think I just pissed myself a little.

paragraphs: As its name suggested, a swift ship was built with speed as its top priority.
If an ordinary warship was a heavyweight, then a swift ship was closer to a welterweight.
Naturally, its hull wasn’t particularly large, which meant there weren’t many places aboard where you could avoid everyone else’s eyes.
“Oh, dear.”
“Great Hero Jin. What brings you here?”
Two river bandits who had been slacking off at the stern under the pretense of standing guard recognized me and bowed obsequiously.
I nodded gravely and opened my mouth.
“Save me...”
At that moment, something sharp poked me right in the Mingmen acupoint at the small of my back.
“Save—stay alert as you go.”
“What?”
“I said, stay alert as you go. I need to discuss something with this fellow for a moment.”
“Oh, I see.”
*No. Don’t agree. Please be suspicious.*
I continued speaking while shooting an urgent sidelong glance at Mungyeong, who was pressed against my side.
“Be sure to take care on your way! If anyone asks about me, tell them I’m with Mungyeong!”
“Uh, understood.”
“No, not ‘understood.’ Oh, right! My master! If my master comes looking for me...”
“I don’t think that’s likely.”
Mungyeong cut me off with an innocent smile.

“It seems there’s something urgent to discuss with Great Hero Jin Wikyung. In any case, we’ve only come to see a patient for a moment, so please don’t concern yourself with us. Go on and rest in the cabin. I’ll let you know afterward.”
“Works for us.”
Nothing was sweeter than authorized slacking in the middle of a boring guard shift.
The river bandits smiled and left, delighted to lounge in the cool shade. As for the Sound Transmission I was preparing to send as a last resort, a single sentence from Mungyeong stopped me cold.
“You seem to have three or four lives.”
“You have two choices. Answer every question this old man asks from now on, or, if you’d rather not, quietly keep your mouth shut.”
I asked, just in case.
“What happens if I choose the second option?”
“You’ll go to Hubei.”
“That doesn’t sound too ba—”
Mungyeong calmly continued before I could finish.
“You’ll drift all the way to Hubei while sunk at the bottom of the Yangtze. Quietly.”
“...I thought you said you’d stopped killing.”
“That depends on this old man’s will. It’s none of your concern.”
*What the fuck? It isn’t like he’s trying to quit smoking...*
Dumbfounded, I protested again.
“You’re the Divine Physician. Are you really threatening to kill me?”
“I’m the former Divine Physician. I passed that name on to my Disciple long ago. So? What’s your answer?”
I glared at Mungyeong.
“Do you really think I’ll give in to a threat like this?”
“Of course.”
“You read me perfectly. I’ll answer every question with the utmost sincerity.”
Mungyeong seemed momentarily at a loss for words. After a long silence, he finally spoke.
“I’ve seen all kinds, but never anyone as strange as you.”
“From everyone else’s perspective, I’d say we’re both equally strange. Send a messenger-pigeon survey to everyone in Murim and ask which one of us is the bigger freak.”
“Freak?”
“My tongue slipped. Sorry.”
The aura Mungyeong let loose made every hair on my body stand on end.
He silently watched me swallow hard, then tossed out a single phrase.
“Middle Dantian.”
“Huh?”
“Until a few days ago—no, until half a day ago—your Middle Dantian was closed. What trick did you use to accomplish such a great feat overnight?”
*So this was why he’d called me aside.*
*I knew he’d noticed.*
The hierarchy of martial realms was perfectly vertical.
It was like sitting in a lofty place and looking down upon everything beneath you.
The Fire King and the Slaughter Saint were peerless masters who had climbed the highest peaks in the rugged mountain range known as Murim.
Both had opened their Middle Dantians long before a person named Jin Taekyung had even been born into Murim. Of course they had noticed the change in me.
The problem was...
*What am I supposed to tell him?*

It wasn’t as though I had farted in my sleep and somehow opened my Middle Dantian. Other people could attain that kind of enlightenment only through grueling training or while hovering between life and death.
I hesitated, then spotted the large acupuncture needle in Mungyeong’s hand and hurriedly answered.
“It just happened.”
“What?”
“It just opened.”
“...And you expect me to believe that?”
*Obviously not.*
So I threw in a cliché straight out of a martial arts novel.
“Actually, I did have a strange dream.”
I glanced around and lowered my voice. Mungyeong’s brow furrowed.
“A dream?”
“Yes. A white-haired old man who looked incredibly ancient suddenly started swinging a sword at me without warning. I didn’t even realize it was a dream, so I focused on dodging first.”
It didn’t matter whether it was a spear, a sword, or a back-scratcher. This was a world overrun with all kinds of superstition.
A white-haired old man with the air of an immortal appearing in my dream was enough to pique anyone’s curiosity.
Sure enough, Mungyeong asked withreader waiting for the next update.
“And then?”

“I summoned every last ounce of strength I had and fought back, but I was no match for him. No matter how I attacked, he dodged without a care. And whenever I tried to get away, he glided up to me like a ghost and slashed me with his sword. Swish, slash—ugh! You know what I mean?”
“You didn’t realize it was a dream?”

“I didn’t have time to realize anything. Besides, the pain felt incredibly real. Before I knew it, he’d cut me hundreds of times. I thought, *So this is how I die.* But then I noticed I hadn’t shed a single drop of blood. That was when I realized it was a dream.”
“Continue.”
“But it was driving me insane. He kept cutting me, and it hurt like hell. Even after I realized it was a dream, I couldn’t wake up.”
“Yes. Exactly.”
Mungyeong flinched as if he’d been cut himself.
*This guy gives surprisingly good reactions.*
Having reconfirmedreader hidden behind the terrifying name of Slaughter Saint, I continued without hesitation.
“I don’t even know how much time passed. Days? Months? I lost all sense of time as he cut me over and over and I kept swinging back. Then, all of a sudden, I felt something strange.”
“Explain it in detail. What was it like?”
This part, at least, I could describe in detail and tell him the truth. It was something I had personally experienced during my battle with the Arch Lich.
An ordinary person might have dismissed my explanation as vague, airy nonsense, but after listening, Mungyeong quietly muttered, “Enlightenment. You gained a fortuitous encounter.”
“Whoa, I’ve got goose bumps. He said something similar.”
“He left you a message?”
“Yes. He looked at me and smiled for the first time, then said that this fortuitous encounter was a blessing he was bestowing upon me and that I should devote myself even more fully to my training.”
“Was that all?”
“Huh?”
“Did he say anything else?”
“Uh, well...”
*Hold on. I didn’t plan for this.*
I’d squeezed this entire story out of my brain on the spot, and I’d already used everything I had prepared.
But Mungyeong was demanding another installment, and I had nothing left in reserve.
The problem was, Mungyeong wasn’t an ordinary reader.
He was the Slaughter Saint.
*What happens if I end it here?*
What else? I’d sink to the bottom of the Yangtze and drift all the way to Hubei.
As Mungyeong’s eyes narrowed, I hurriedly opened my mouth.
“He did say one more thing.”
“What did he say?”
“Well, that is...”
*Fuck it. I don’t know.*
I swallowed dryly and cautiously spoke.
“You have to suffer to be a Murim man.”
“What?”
“He really said that. Those exact words. Then he climbed onto his sword and flew off...”
“I can sense profound wisdom in those words.”
“Huh?”
I let out a stupefied sound while keeping a wary eye on the large needle in Mungyeong’s hand.
*What the hell is he talking about now?*
When I raised my head, I saw Mungyeong murmuring under his breath and nodding slightly as though he were groaning.
After muttering something unintelligible, he suddenly spoke.
“It was Lü Yan.”
“I know about stomach cancer and lung cancer, but... are you sick somewhere?”
“...You don’t know Lü Yan?”
Mungyeong looked at me as though I were insane, then continued.
“Lü Yan. His courtesy name was Dongbin, and his Taoist name was Chunyangzi. He attained his own Dao and reached the realm of an immortal. People called him the Sword Immortal.”
“Wait. You mean Lü Dongbin?”
“You finally understand.”

I might not have known Lü Yan, but I knew Sword Immortal Lü Dongbin. Along with Jang Samfeng of Wudang and Bodhidharma of Shaolin Temple, he was one of the three perennial fixtures of martial arts novels.
Mungyeong continued, his expression deadly serious.
“The old man you saw in your dream must have been Lü Dongbin. He vanished by riding his sword at the end, so he must have been the Sword Immortal.”
“Uh... I suppose so.”
I’d only made that part up because it sounded cool, but somehow it had turned into this.
I knew from novels that there was an immortal named Lü Dongbin, but this was the first I’d heard of him being a master of sword-riding arts.
*Talk about making the facts fit the theory.*
That was exactly what was happening.
Having decided that the old man from my dream—or rather, my story—was Lü Dongbin, Mungyeong was now fitting everything together with absolute seriousness without even realizing it.
“Did his beard reach down to his chest?”
“Yes.”
“How tall was he?”
“He was short.”
“Boy! I’m asking how short!”
“Oh, just short. I was being cut to pieces the entire time. When was I supposed to study his height?”
Mungyeong nodded and let most of my answers pass, but there was one dangerously close call.
“What did he carry besides the sword?”
“Let me think... His scabbard.”
“Do you want to die? Of course he had that. Was there nothing else?”
“...I think that was all.”
The light in Mungyeong’s eyes darkened.
“Lü Dongbin did not carry only a sword. He always held a Taoist fly-whisk in his right hand.”
“Have you been lying to this old man all along?”
It was a life-or-death crisis.

I had no idea why a man known as the Sword Immortal would walk around carrying a fly-whisk, but my top priority was avoiding Mungyeong’s suspicions. Without letting a single change cross my face, I answered.
“Everything I said was true.”
“Then why does your description contradict Lü Dongbin’s usual appearance?”
“He must have left his fly-whisk behind today.”
“What kind of bullshi—”
“No, wait. Have you ever seen Lü Dongbin?”
“I have.”
*Fuck, I’m the one who saw him. What are you going to do about it?*
Seizing the advantage, I bore down on Mungyeong while he was momentarily at a loss for words.
“And did I ever say he was Lü Dongbin? I thought he was just some old man. You were the one who called him Lü Dongbin first.”
“You?”

“That isn’t the point. That’s what happened, isn’t it? Honestly, I don’t care whether he was Lü Dongbin or Kim Dongbin. I met some unidentified old man in a dream and gained a fortuitous encounter. That’s all. But you’re hounding me like I’ve committed some terrible crime, so I really... Ha.”
“Can you see the tears in my eyes? I don’t want to act like this as a grown man, but this is so unfair I’m actually crying.”
The truth was, I was scared.
That, combined with the self-loathing of having to invent lies under threat despite committing no crime, eventually sent a tear rolling down my cheek.
*Is this what life is?*
I had wet myself below earlier, and now I was wetting myself above.
It had started as an act, but somehow it had become real. Bewilderment flashed across Mungyeong’s nearly expressionless face.
“You little bastard. What trick are you pulling?”
“Ugh, there you go again. I’m done. I quit. I answered all your questions, so I’m leaving.”
“You’re leaving?”
“I don’t care anymore. Do whatever you want. Kill me, spare me, use Impure World Reincarnation on me—whatever.”
Just as I was about to take a step, someone appeared while scattering a powerful aura.
“What the hell is this dogshit?”
The gazes of the Fire King and the Slaughter Saint collided in midair.

sentences.text: As its name suggested, a swift ship was built with speed as its top priority.
If an ordinary warship was a heavyweight, then a swift ship was closer to a welterweight.
Naturally, its hull wasn’t particularly large, which meant there weren’t many places aboard where you could avoid everyone else’s eyes.

Two river bandits who had been slacking off at the stern under the pretense of standing guard recognized me and bowed obsequiously.
I nodded gravely and opened my mouth.

At that moment, something sharp poked me right in the Mingmen acupoint at the small of my back.
“Save—stay alert as you go.”
“What?”

I need to discuss something with this fellow for a moment.”
“Oh, I see.”

Don’t agree.
Please be suspicious.*

“Be sure to take care on your way!

“Uh, understood.”
“No, not ‘understood.’ Oh, right!
My master!
If my master comes looking for me...”
“I don’t think that’s likely.”

In any case, we’ve only come to see a patient for a moment, so please don’t concern yourself with us.
Go on and rest in the cabin.
I’ll let you know afterward.”
“Works for us.”
Nothing was sweeter than authorized slacking in the middle of a boring guard shift.
The river bandits smiled and left, delighted to lounge in the cool shade.

“You seem to have three or four lives.”
“You have two choices.
Answer every question this old man asks from now on, or, if you’d rather not, quietly keep your mouth shut.”
I asked, just in case.

“You’ll go to Hubei.”

Quietly.”

It’s none of your concern.”
*What the fuck?

What’s your answer?”
I glared at Mungyeong.
“Do you really think I’ll give in to a threat like this?”
“Of course.”
“You read me perfectly.
I’ll answer every question with the utmost sincerity.”
Mungyeong seemed momentarily at a loss for words.
After a long silence, he finally spoke.
“I’ve seen all kinds, but never anyone as strange as you.”
“From everyone else’s perspective, I’d say we’re both equally strange.
Send a messenger-pigeon survey to everyone in Murim and ask which one of us is the bigger freak.”
“Freak?”
“My tongue slipped.
Sorry.”
The aura Mungyeong let loose made every hair on my body stand on end.
He silently watched me swallow hard, then tossed out a single phrase.
“Middle Dantian.”
“Huh?”
“Until a few days ago—no, until half a day ago—your Middle Dantian was closed.
What trick did you use to accomplish such a great feat overnight?”
*So this was why he’d called me aside.*
*I knew he’d noticed.*
The hierarchy of martial realms was perfectly vertical.
It was like sitting in a lofty place and looking down upon everything beneath you.
The Fire King and the Slaughter Saint were peerless masters who had climbed the highest peaks in the rugged mountain range known as Murim.
Both had opened their Middle Dantians long before a person named Jin Taekyung had even been born into Murim.
Of course they had noticed the change in me.
The problem was...
*What am I supposed to tell him?*
It wasn’t as though I had farted in my sleep and somehow opened my Middle Dantian.
Other people could attain that kind of enlightenment only through grueling training or while hovering between life and death.
I hesitated, then spotted the large acupuncture needle in Mungyeong’s hand and hurriedly answered.
“It just happened.”
“What?”
“It just opened.”
“...And you expect me to believe that?”
*Obviously not.*
So I threw in a cliché straight out of a martial arts novel.
“Actually, I did have a strange dream.”
I glanced around and lowered my voice.
Mungyeong’s brow furrowed.
“A dream?”
“Yes.
A white-haired old man who looked incredibly ancient suddenly started swinging a sword at me without warning.
I didn’t even realize it was a dream, so I focused on dodging first.”
It didn’t matter whether it was a spear, a sword, or a back-scratcher.
This was a world overrun with all kinds of superstition.
A white-haired old man with the air of an immortal appearing in my dream was enough to pique anyone’s curiosity.
Sure enough, Mungyeong asked withreader waiting for the next update.
“And then?”
“I summoned every last ounce of strength I had and fought back, but I was no match for him.
No matter how I attacked, he dodged without a care.
And whenever I tried to get away, he glided up to me like a ghost and slashed me with his sword.
Swish, slash—ugh!
You know what I mean?”
“You didn’t realize it was a dream?”
“I didn’t have time to realize anything.
Besides, the pain felt incredibly real.
Before I knew it, he’d cut me hundreds of times.
I thought, *So this is how I die.* But then I noticed I hadn’t shed a single drop of blood.
That was when I realized it was a dream.”
“Continue.”
“But it was driving me insane.
He kept cutting me, and it hurt like hell.
Even after I realized it was a dream, I couldn’t wake up.”
“Yes.
Exactly.”
Mungyeong flinched as if he’d been cut himself.
*This guy gives surprisingly good reactions.*
