chapters.title: Chapter 438
paragraphs: Jeok Cheongang’s eyes blazed as he glared at Mungyeong.
“How dare you threaten someone else’s dis, dis... Disciple Taekyung while this old man was away?”
“...What the hell is ‘Disciple Taekyung’?”
My tears dried up at once as I muttered in disbelief. Jeok Cheongang roared.
“Quiet!”
Mungyeong and I answered at the same time.
“You’re louder, Old Master. You’re practically shouting ‘Disciple Taekyung’ from the center of the world.”
“Judging by that voice, you’ll live another ten years.”
*Did he roast a train smokestack in an air fryer and eat it?*
It was a good thing Mungyeong had used his internal energy to raise a qi barrier and keep the sound from escaping. Otherwise, people would have gathered around us long ago.
Jeok Cheongang’s face flushed bright red. Mungyeong quietly clicked his tongue.
“We merely had a brief conversation. What would this old man gain from threatening such a young pup?”
Jeok Cheongang turned toward me.
“You answer me. Is what that old man said true?”
“It’s true that we only talked, but he said I’d sink to the bottom of the Yangtze if he didn’t like my answer.”
At my tattling, Mungyeong shamelessly added,
“Of course, I did frighten him a little.”
“Would you look at this damned old man! You think you’ll get away with pulling something like this?”
“Calm yourself. I merely had something to ask him about his Middle Dantian.”
Jeok Cheongang had leaned forward as though he were about to charge, but he stopped dead.
“Middle Dantian?”
“Yes. Surely you didn’t fail to notice.”
“Opening one’s Middle Dantian in such a short time is impossible. Even heavenly fortune cannot explain it.”
Jeok Cheongang looked back and forth between Mungyeong and me, then let out a short laugh.
“So it was nothing.”
“...What?”
“So you’re trying to say that the boy learned demonic martial arts or something?”
“That...”
“I’ll put it simply. No.”
Mungyeong was left speechless by Jeok Cheongang’s calm, utterly confident response. Jeok Cheongang crooked a finger at me.
“What are you waiting for? Come here.”
“Huh?”
“You asked me to oversee your training, didn’t you? We’re starting now.”
“Oh. Right.”
The situation moved on so smoothly that even I was caught off guard. As though he had read my thoughts, Jeok Cheongang asked,
“I am curious, though. How exactly did you open your Middle Dantian?”
“Uh, well. I had a dream, and there was this old man with a sword...”
“Did you meet the Sword Immortal Lü Dongbin?”
“...Well, judging by what that guy over there said, maybe.”
“You gained a fortuitous encounter. It seems the heavens are helping you. Things beyond human understanding do happen in this world from time to time.”
Jeok Cheongang was looking at me, but his answer was directed at Mungyeong.
After tossing out that remark for Mungyeong to hear, Jeok Cheongang suddenly swung his wrinkled hand.
*Smack!*
“Ow! Why did you hit me?”
“You irritated me, so I felt like hitting you. Got a problem with that?”
“What if I do?”
“Then you can take another hit.”
*Whack!*
“Aaagh!”
“You blockheaded brat. Quit whining. Stop fooling around and follow me.”
*Can I really just leave like this?*
I glanced at Mungyeong, who stood there wearing an unreadable expression. A thunderous shout immediately crashed down on me.
“And yet, you brat!”
“Okay, okay, I get it. Please stop shouting.”
“Dragging your feet like this, do you even intend to train?”
I turned my back on Mungyeong and followed close behind Jeok Cheongang, whispering,
“But aren’t you going to ask anything else?”
Jeok Cheongang answered gruffly without turning around.
“About what?”
“No, I mean... the Middle Dantian...”
“Stop talking nonsense and follow me. From now on, don’t go anywhere near that old man.”
“Yes, sir.”
That was exactly what I wanted. I wasn’t some Mermaid Princess of the Yangtze, and I had absolutely no intention of getting on his bad side and drifting all the way to Hubei with the fish.
“If I catch you in a situation like this again, I’ll teach you a lesson. Understand?”
“...I’m the victim here. Why are you blaming me?”
“Quiet. I was about to smash everything to pieces earlier, but I held myself back.”
“Come to think of it, you really did show restraint.”
“Would the ship have survived if I hadn’t?”
“True. We should take Senior Mu Song’s circumstances into consideration. Did you see his face when the swift ship caught fire?”
Jeok Cheongang whipped his head around and frowned.
“What kind of nonsense are you talking about? Why should this old man care about those river bandits’ circumstances?”
“Huh?”
“If we lose another ship here, we’ll have to move everyone aboard to a different one. All that extra weight would slow us down.”
“Think before you speak. We need to get off this wretched Yangtze as quickly as possible. It’s damp, it rocks, and it never seems to end.”
*What a lovely personality.*
I watched the Fire Pokémon walk away, shuddering from head to toe, when a thought suddenly occurred to me.
*If we burn everything down, couldn’t we travel by land?*
I decided not to say it. Jeok Cheongang was more than capable of actually doing it.
I did my best to ignore Mungyeong’s prickling gaze on the back of my head as I followed Jeok Cheongang.
The swift ship cut through the water without slowing.

Every vessel that saw the flag of the Yangtze River Channel League flying high above the deck hurriedly cleared a path. Even the government warships with their cozy ties to the League were no exception.

The river bandits knew the lower Yangtze and its waterways like the backs of their hands. Following Mu Song’s orders, they pulled hard on their oars, while the sails billowed wide in the wind blowing from far away.
Like the churning waters of the Yangtze, the hours of that day rushed past.
And...
Just as he had the previous night, Mungyeong sat at the bow and gazed out at the Yangtze shrouded in darkness. When his uninvited guest arrived again, he spoke in a low voice.
“You’re later than I expected.”
“It took time to find the liquor that fellow Mu Song—or whatever his name is—had hidden away. He fought tooth and nail to keep it from me until the very end.”
Jeok Cheongang perched on the railing and broke the seal on a small jar he had taken out as carefully as though it were a treasured family heirloom.
A fragrant aroma of liquor immediately spread through the air, cracking Mungyeong’s usually impassive expression.
“Jiannan Chun?”
“Of course. When you come to Sichuan, you drink Jiannan Chun. This is what makes the trip worthwhile.”
“That doesn’t seem like ordinary Jiannan Chun.”

“According to that fellow, it was a gift from his Master. A man as eminent as the Seafaring King wouldn’t have given his Disciple ordinary liquor... Thanks to him, this old man’s tongue is enjoying a rare treat.”
Jeok Cheongang lifted the jar to his mouth and gulped down the liquor, then smacked his lips.
“Damn, that’s good. Want a drink?”
Mungyeong stared intently at the jar of Jiannan Chun, then shook his head.
“...I believe I told you I quit drinking a long time ago.”
“You took too long to answer. For an old man known as the greatest assassin in history, you make your thoughts awfully easy to read.”
“That still makes me better than an old man who carries on like a reckless brat at his age.”
“What did you say?”
“Enough nonsense. Let’s get to the point. You have something to say to me, don’t you?”
Jeok Cheongang’s visit the previous day had been unexpected. Today was different.
Several shichen earlier, Jeok Cheongang had used Sound Transmission to tell Mungyeong that he would come. Mungyeong had been waiting for him.
“You’re impatient. That isn’t very assassin-like, either.”
“I’m a medical apprentice, not an assassin.”
“Then call yourself a life-taker.”
“Disciple and Master alike. Your words and actions are exactly the same.”
Ignoring Mungyeong’s frown, Jeok Cheongang took another drink and wiped his mouth with his sleeve before answering.
“Our words and actions may resemble each other, but we’re worlds apart. That brat is a monster who has strayed beyond all common sense.”
Mungyeong nodded silently.

He couldn’t disagree with the word *monster*. Reaching the Supreme Peak realm just after passing the age of twenty was astonishing enough, but Jin Taekyung had taken another step before he had even caught his breath.
*When did he reach the Supreme Peak realm?*
Mungyeong searched his memories of the distant past.
He had been younger then—sharper and quieter than he was now. He had devoted his heart and soul entirely to martial arts.

Sometimes covertly and sometimes through direct confrontation, he had accumulated experience through countless real battles. At last, he had set foot in that exalted realm said to admit only the chosen.
*I was in my mid-thirties.*
Even Mungyeong, hailed as the greatest assassin in history and known as the Slaughter Saint, had not reached the Supreme Peak realm until after turning thirty.
He had opened his Middle Dantian several years later, when he was nearing forty.
Yet Jin Taekyung had left his mark on Murim’s long history when he was barely past twenty.
In Mungyeong’s estimation, this could only be the work of demonic, heterodox arts—and an unparalleled demonic martial art at that.
“I have a feeling this conversation will take a while.”
“No, it’ll be over quickly. This old man doesn’t have much to say.”
Mungyeong’s gaze darkened at Jeok Cheongang’s answer.
“Why not?”
“What can I say about something I’ve never seen or heard of? There’s nothing to do but accept it.”
“Surely you don’t believe that nonsense about the Sword Immortal Lü Dongbin appearing in his dream and granting him enlightenment.”
“It may have happened, or it may not have. But even if it’s true, it wouldn’t be all that surprising. Heh heh.”
“Fire King!”
The thunderous cry struck the qi barrier surrounding the two men and reverberated with a deep hum.
But the anger that flashed across Mungyeong’s face vanished without a trace at Jeok Cheongang’s next words.
“Two years.”
“...What did you say?”

“It took that brat only two years to break through the wall of the Supreme Peak realm and open his Middle Dantian. If this old man were Lü Dongbin, I would have come to him in person instead of appearing in a dream, saying, ‘What an incredible fellow there is in the lower world.’”
Mungyeong first questioned his own ears, then Jeok Cheongang’s state of mind.
But the small old man before him continued speaking, his eyes clearer than Mungyeong had ever seen them.
“Don’t doubt him. When you face that brat, erase everything you’ve seen and heard throughout your life from your mind. Do you understand what I mean?”
“Taekyung. That boy and the Sword Saint’s Disciple are Divine Dragons in the truest sense. No one has ever seen one. All anyone can do is imagine what they must be like.”
*Whoosh.*
White foam splashed against the bow. A long time passed before Mungyeong broke the silence.
“I can’t believe it.”
“I didn’t tell you to believe it. I only told you to accept it.”
“Every part of that is impossible.”
“There’s one truth this old man learned while growing older for no good reason. You can’t control another person’s heart.”
Jeok Cheongang had learned that only after sending his first Disciple away.
And only after he met a young man by chance and, one day, truly accepted him into his heart did he realize something else.
The pain that throbbed whenever he remembered that day had grown faint.
“You’ll understand if you keep watching him. Just as I did.”
Mungyeong silently watched Jeok Cheongang’s back as he rose from the railing and ambled away. Then he suddenly spoke.
“What is that brat doing right now?”
“Taekyung?”
Jeok Cheongang turned his head and laughed heartily beneath the moonlight.
“He’s sleeping like the dead.”
If training at Fire Gate Cavern had been a marathon, this was a sprint relay.
During the little over a week it would take to reach Hubei, I had decided to travel back and forth between the modern world and Murim, juggling two lives.
*Ding.*
**System Logout** complete!
I opened my eyes to the familiar chime. I was inside the private jet bound for Korea.
I saw people sleeping soundly from all the fatigue they had accumulated, along with one monster staring at me with his eyes wide open.
“What are you looking at, you punk?”
The Skeleton King answered.
“So that was it. Hmm. Do all humans sleep like the dead, just like you?”
“I’m special.”
“Not weird?”
*Whack!*
This bastard really went out of his way to get hit.

sentences.text: Jeok Cheongang’s eyes blazed as he glared at Mungyeong.
“How dare you threaten someone else’s dis, dis...
Disciple Taekyung while this old man was away?”
“...What the hell is ‘Disciple Taekyung’?”
My tears dried up at once as I muttered in disbelief.
Jeok Cheongang roared.
“Quiet!”
Mungyeong and I answered at the same time.
“You’re louder, Old Master.
You’re practically shouting ‘Disciple Taekyung’ from the center of the world.”
“Judging by that voice, you’ll live another ten years.”
*Did he roast a train smokestack in an air fryer and eat it?*
It was a good thing Mungyeong had used his internal energy to raise a qi barrier and keep the sound from escaping.
Otherwise, people would have gathered around us long ago.
Jeok Cheongang’s face flushed bright red.
Mungyeong quietly clicked his tongue.
“We merely had a brief conversation.
What would this old man gain from threatening such a young pup?”
Jeok Cheongang turned toward me.
“You answer me.
Is what that old man said true?”
“It’s true that we only talked, but he said I’d sink to the bottom of the Yangtze if he didn’t like my answer.”
At my tattling, Mungyeong shamelessly added,
“Of course, I did frighten him a little.”
“Would you look at this damned old man!
You think you’ll get away with pulling something like this?”
“Calm yourself.
I merely had something to ask him about his Middle Dantian.”
Jeok Cheongang had leaned forward as though he were about to charge, but he stopped dead.
“Middle Dantian?”
“Yes.
Surely you didn’t fail to notice.”
“Opening one’s Middle Dantian in such a short time is impossible.
Even heavenly fortune cannot explain it.”
Jeok Cheongang looked back and forth between Mungyeong and me, then let out a short laugh.
“So it was nothing.”
“...What?”
“So you’re trying to say that the boy learned demonic martial arts or something?”
“That...”
“I’ll put it simply.
No.”
Mungyeong was left speechless by Jeok Cheongang’s calm, utterly confident response.
Jeok Cheongang crooked a finger at me.
“What are you waiting for?
Come here.”
“Huh?”
“You asked me to oversee your training, didn’t you?
We’re starting now.”
“Oh.
Right.”
The situation moved on so smoothly that even I was caught off guard.
As though he had read my thoughts, Jeok Cheongang asked,
“I am curious, though.
How exactly did you open your Middle Dantian?”
“Uh, well.
I had a dream, and there was this old man with a sword...”
“Did you meet the Sword Immortal Lü Dongbin?”
“...Well, judging by what that guy over there said, maybe.”
“You gained a fortuitous encounter.
It seems the heavens are helping you.
Things beyond human understanding do happen in this world from time to time.”
Jeok Cheongang was looking at me, but his answer was directed at Mungyeong.
After tossing out that remark for Mungyeong to hear, Jeok Cheongang suddenly swung his wrinkled hand.
*Smack!*
“Ow!
Why did you hit me?”
“You irritated me, so I felt like hitting you.
Got a problem with that?”
“What if I do?”
“Then you can take another hit.”
*Whack!*
“Aaagh!”
“You blockheaded brat.
Quit whining.
Stop fooling around and follow me.”
*Can I really just leave like this?*
I glanced at Mungyeong, who stood there wearing an unreadable expression.
A thunderous shout immediately crashed down on me.
“And yet, you brat!”
“Okay, okay, I get it.
Please stop shouting.”
“Dragging your feet like this, do you even intend to train?”
I turned my back on Mungyeong and followed close behind Jeok Cheongang, whispering,
“But aren’t you going to ask anything else?”
Jeok Cheongang answered gruffly without turning around.
“About what?”
“No, I mean... the Middle Dantian...”
“Stop talking nonsense and follow me.
From now on, don’t go anywhere near that old man.”
“Yes, sir.”
That was exactly what I wanted.
I wasn’t some Mermaid Princess of the Yangtze, and I had absolutely no intention of getting on his bad side and drifting all the way to Hubei with the fish.
“If I catch you in a situation like this again, I’ll teach you a lesson.
Understand?”
“...I’m the victim here.
Why are you blaming me?”
“Quiet.
I was about to smash everything to pieces earlier, but I held myself back.”
“Come to think of it, you really did show restraint.”
“Would the ship have survived if I hadn’t?”
“True.
We should take Senior Mu Song’s circumstances into consideration.
Did you see his face when the swift ship caught fire?”
Jeok Cheongang whipped his head around and frowned.
“What kind of nonsense are you talking about?
Why should this old man care about those river bandits’ circumstances?”
“Huh?”
“If we lose another ship here, we’ll have to move everyone aboard to a different one.
All that extra weight would slow us down.”
“Think before you speak.
We need to get off this wretched Yangtze as quickly as possible.
It’s damp, it rocks, and it never seems to end.”
*What a lovely personality.*
I watched the Fire Pokémon walk away, shuddering from head to toe, when a thought suddenly occurred to me.
*If we burn everything down, couldn’t we travel by land?*
I decided not to say it.
Jeok Cheongang was more than capable of actually doing it.
I did my best to ignore Mungyeong’s prickling gaze on the back of my head as I followed Jeok Cheongang.
The swift ship cut through the water without slowing.
Every vessel that saw the flag of the Yangtze River Channel League flying high above the deck hurriedly cleared a path.
Even the government warships with their cozy ties to the League were no exception.
The river bandits knew the lower Yangtze and its waterways like the backs of their hands.
Following Mu Song’s orders, they pulled hard on their oars, while the sails billowed wide in the wind blowing from far away.
Like the churning waters of the Yangtze, the hours of that day rushed past.
And...
Just as he had the previous night, Mungyeong sat at the bow and gazed out at the Yangtze shrouded in darkness.
When his uninvited guest arrived again, he spoke in a low voice.
“You’re later than I expected.”
“It took time to find the liquor that fellow Mu Song—or whatever his name is—had hidden away.
He fought tooth and nail to keep it from me until the very end.”
Jeok Cheongang perched on the railing and broke the seal on a small jar he had taken out as carefully as though it were a treasured family heirloom.
A fragrant aroma of liquor immediately spread through the air, cracking Mungyeong’s usually impassive expression.
“Jiannan Chun?”
“Of course.
When you come to Sichuan, you drink Jiannan Chun.
This is what makes the trip worthwhile.”
“That doesn’t seem like ordinary Jiannan Chun.”
“According to that fellow, it was a gift from his Master.
A man as eminent as the Seafaring King wouldn’t have given his Disciple ordinary liquor...
Thanks to him, this old man’s tongue is enjoying a rare treat.”
Jeok Cheongang lifted the jar to his mouth and gulped down the liquor, then smacked his lips.
“Damn, that’s good.
Want a drink?”
Mungyeong stared intently at the jar of Jiannan Chun, then shook his head.
“...I believe I told you I quit drinking a long time ago.”
“You took too long to answer.
For an old man known as the greatest assassin in history, you make your thoughts awfully easy to read.”
“That still makes me better than an old man who carries on like a reckless brat at his age.”
“What did you say?”
“Enough nonsense.
Let’s get to the point.
You have something to say to me, don’t you?”
Jeok Cheongang’s visit the previous day had been unexpected.
Today was different.
Several shichen earlier, Jeok Cheongang had used Sound Transmission to tell Mungyeong that he would come.
Mungyeong had been waiting for him.
“You’re impatient.
That isn’t very assassin-like, either.”
“I’m a medical apprentice, not an assassin.”
“Then call yourself a life-taker.”
“Disciple and Master alike.
Your words and actions are exactly the same.”
Ignoring Mungyeong’s frown, Jeok Cheongang took another drink and wiped his mouth with his sleeve before answering.
“Our words and actions may resemble each other, but we’re worlds apart.
That brat is a monster who has strayed beyond all common sense.”
Mungyeong nodded silently.
He couldn’t disagree with the word *monster*.
Reaching the Supreme Peak realm just after passing the age of twenty was astonishing enough, but Jin Taekyung had taken another step before he had even caught his breath.
*When did he reach the Supreme Peak realm?*
Mungyeong searched his memories of the distant past.
He had been younger then—sharper and quieter than he was now.
He had devoted his heart and soul entirely to martial arts.
Sometimes covertly and sometimes through direct confrontation, he had accumulated experience through countless real battles.
At last, he had set foot in that exalted realm said to admit only the chosen.
*I was in my mid-thirties.*
Even Mungyeong, hailed as the greatest assassin in history and known as the Slaughter Saint, had not reached the Supreme Peak realm until after turning thirty.

“What can I say about something I’ve never seen or heard of?

“Surely you don’t believe that nonsense about the Sword Immortal Lü Dongbin appearing in his dream and granting him enlightenment.”

Heh heh.”

chapters.title: Chapter 439
paragraphs: *Smack!*
The blow caught the Skeleton King square in the forehead, sending him staggering.
But only for a moment. He lowered his head, which had snapped back from the impact, into its proper position and grinned smugly.
“Heh heh. That barely tickled.”
“Oh, right. Your disguise is so convincing that I forgot for a second.”
There was no way an undead monster—already dead, whether it had a soul or not—could feel pain. Magic Johnson really had done one hell of a job with his full-body plastic surgery.
As I clicked my tongue softly, the Skeleton King shrugged.
“You must not place this king on the same level as a weak human.”
“Of course I don’t. You’re an undead monster.”
“An undead monster? This king is Stone-King, born and raised in Atlanta, Georgia, in the United States!”
“Hey, hey!”
What the hell was wrong with this lunatic? Why was he suddenly shouting?
I hurriedly raised my internal energy to block the sound, then sighed in relief when I saw that everyone was still sleeping soundly.
“You can’t even speak English properly.”
“I learned several things on the internet. They said communication would pose no problem as long as I knew two phrases.”
“Go ahead, then.”
Mr. Stone-King, a proud native of Atlanta, Georgia, United States, opened his mouth.
“How are you. I’m fine, thank you. And you?”
“...You’re Korean, aren’t you, you bastard?”
He had a Hollywood face, but his skill and pronunciation were purely homegrown Korean.
As I shook my head in disbelief, the Skeleton King asked with a shocked expression,
“Is this king’s English truly that terrible?”
“Yeah. So let’s just say you’re half Korean. It’s not like anyone’s going to care about your background anyway.”
“Then I was adopted by a family in Atlanta, Georgia...”
“No, for fuck’s sake. Did you hide honey in Atlanta or something? Is every treasure in the world supposed to be there?”
“But it sounds impressive, does it not? I read on the internet that white men are popular with women all over the world. Besides, this king is handsome.”
“What good is that when you can’t even get it up?”
Rendered speechless, the Skeleton King pointed at me with a trembling finger.
“How could you say something so cruel?”
“I can say worse, so stop talking nonsense. If you don’t want people finding out you’re a monster, wear this.”
The Skeleton King accepted the object I summoned from my Inventory and tilted his head, his anger forgotten.
“Vile human, what is this?”
“A gift from Magic Johnson. He said it took a while because he had to have it flown in from the United States on short notice.”
“That gracious human? A ring for me?”
The Skeleton King stared gravely at the ring I had given him.
“Is this perhaps what humans call a proposal?”
“What the hell are you talking about, you lunatic? It’s just a ring enchanted with translation magic.”
“Hmm. I appreciate the gift, but it looks rather crude. It does not sparkle like a diamond, either. It is unbefitting of a king’s dignity.”
“Magic Johnson commissioned a Grand Mage he knows to make it specially, so its performance is top-class. It’s probably worth whatever price they care to name.”
“Now that I look again, I can sense its noble dignity. It will uphold my royal authority nicely.”
What an irritating bastard.
There was no doubt about it. He had become far stronger—and far crazier—than he had been as the Skeleton Warlord.
Regardless, he slipped the ring onto his middle finger with a satisfied expression, then pulled a smartphone from the lining of his suit.
That, too, was an expensive, cutting-edge smartphone with a Magic Gem built into it, another gift from Magic Johnson.
“What are you doing?”
“This king must personally express his gratitude to the gracious human.”
“You’ve got better manners than I expected. Are you going to text him?”
“Vile human.”
“Huh?”
The Skeleton King looked at me as though I were pathetic.
“Who sends texts in this day and age? Naturally, one uses social media.”
“...Uh, sure.”
“We already follow each other. I have also learned how to send direct messages.”
I stared at the Skeleton King’s phone, my mouth falling open.
Holy shit. It was real. An undead monster with a social media account. Did this app not even require identity verification?
But something else was even more surprising.
“...You have five thousand followers?”
“State the number accurately. It is 5,134. A record achieved in less than a week.”
“What the hell? Is this fake?”
“Is being handsome not the greatest advantage? I merely used this king’s face as my profile picture, and countless requests to follow one another came pouring in from around the world. Heh heh.”
The Skeleton King answered with an arrogant look and began sending a message to Magic Johnson.
└ Good human. I'm fine thank you. and you?
After checking the message, I let out a small sigh.
“Don’t send messages to anyone else.”
“Why not?”
“If I say don’t, then don’t, you bastard.”
So much for Atlanta, Georgia.
Calling himself a native of Atlanta District, Georgia City, Gyeonggi Province, would have sounded more believable.
Apparently, even translation magic couldn’t save English so painfully Korean that it made my head spin.
“At this rate, even the Akabutakchi tribe, who have preserved their traditions in the Amazon rainforest for hundreds of years, won’t believe you’re American.”
“Hmm. I do not know exactly what you mean, but the oddly specific nature of it makes me even angrier.”
“Just do as I say. If your identity gets exposed, it won’t end with a little trouble.”
No matter how good my public image was right now, if the Skeleton King’s identity became known, we would clearly have to brace ourselves for considerable repercussions.
I turned my head.
“Isn’t that right, Team Leader Choi?”
In the seat diagonally beside us, Team Leader Choi had been awake by himself for several minutes. He answered,
“I was already considering the matter of the Skeleton King—”
“Stone-King. Call me Mr. King.”
The Skeleton King cut him off firmly. Team Leader Choi stared at him for a moment, then continued with a sigh.
“In any case, we are considering every possibility regarding Mr. King’s future arrangements. For now, it would be best to avoid exposure to the press and other media.”
“I refuse. I will proudly reveal myself to the world.”
“Really? Team Leader Choi, what are the penalties for entering the country illegally?”
Team Leader Choi answered at once.
“Deportation, without question. He would also have to expect a fine or imprisonment.”
“What about entering illegally from the Demon Realm?”
“It has never happened before, but instead of the police, a large-scale raid team would be dispatched.”
“You heard him.”
The Skeleton King’s eyes swiveled back and forth in silence before he finally spoke.
“...It cannot be helped. The world is not yet prepared to accept this king, so I shall exercise restraint for a while.”
“That’s what you should do. Unless you want to spend the rest of your life lying low in my Inventory.”
“A-All right.”
The biggest headache was dealt with.
Now there was the second headache... and this one I had no choice but to face head-on.
Not because I lacked alternatives, but because doing so would help with my plans going forward.
*It’s a pain, but it can’t be helped.*
I quietly tapped the armrest, lost in thought, then abruptly spoke.
“What’s the atmosphere like back home right now?”
Team Leader Choi gave me a terse, emphatic answer.
“It’s insane.”
“...That bad?”

“When someone passes the judicial exam, banners go up in their neighborhood and at their alma mater, and the local newspaper runs a short article. More than fifteen hundred people pass that exam every year. How much more attention do you think you would receive, Mr. Jin Taekyung?”
With that perfectly apt comparison, Team Leader Choi clicked in midair.
The holographic screen built into the seat filled with countless online articles.
[At Last, He Has Returned.]
[Who Is Jin Taekyung? Chairman Xiao Yang Bows His Head on Behalf of the Chinese People. The Reverent Farewell of S-Rank Hunters...]
[The Young Hero Who Fought to Rescue Survivors Until the Very End Finally Returns to the Arms of His Homeland.]

It wasn’t just the Korean media. China, where the incident had taken place, and countries around the world were flooding the internet with article after article about my return and what I would do next.
I had known this was coming and expected it, but I still couldn’t help gaping when I saw a photograph attached to an online article posted five minutes earlier.
“Wait. Are all those people actually human?”
“They aren’t monsters, so they probably are.”
“Holy shit...”
The photograph showed a crowd packed into Incheon Airport without so much as a gap between them.
Thousands? No, tens of thousands.
As I stared blankly at the screen, Team Leader Choi continued.
“Traffic throughout the surrounding area has come to a standstill, and a car parade is being prepared under military and police control.”
“What? A car parade?”
“Did I not tell you?”
“You mentioned it in passing, so I thought you were joking. I mean... isn’t this a bit much?”
Team Leader Choi shook his head firmly.
“It has to be this much. You are the new S-rank Hunter representing Korea.”
“Even so, this is excessive. At this rate, the President will show up too.”
“Ah, I really did fail to mention that.”
“What?”
“He is coming. The Blue House contacted us first this morning. I meant to tell you on the plane, but I dozed off and forgot.”
For a moment, my thoughts ground to a halt.
Tens of thousands of people waiting for me at Incheon Airport. Paralyzed roads and a spectacular car parade. And now the President was coming too.
I sat there speechless, then finally forced the words out.
“...Really? You’re not joking?”
“Yes. They want to shake your hand, stand with you at the photo line, and take a picture together.”
“Team Leader Choi, I don’t know anything about politics. If I get tangled up in something and it goes wrong, I’ll be completely screwed.”
“I know how you feel, Mr. Jin Taekyung. That is why I tried to turn them down politely, but they seemed quite determined. It was not easy.”
“You still should have refused. Even if I belong to Peace Guild, how could you make that decision on your own?”
No matter how much we trusted each other or how little time there had been, this was something he should have consulted me about.
At the sight of my rigid expression, Team Leader Choi lowered his head apologetically.
“I’m sorry. They offered several favorable conditions, including tax breaks, so I thought it would benefit you as well.”
“Forget that. Call them right now and tell them it’s off... Wait. Tax breaks?”
“Yes. You know the bounty that was placed on the Arch Lich. If the Chinese government pays it to you, then under Korean law, it would count as foreign-source income for a Korean resident...”
“Wait. So how much tax would I have to pay in total?”

“I cannot say for certain, but it would be several trillion won. The bounty alone is fifty trillion won. Even if we simplify things and assume only ten percent is deducted, it would still be an enormous amount. Of course, the amount left over would be much larger.”
“...That’s true.”
“Once again, I apologize for failing to get your approval. I will tell the Blue House that this is no longer happening.”
I nodded, my expression hard.
“Team Leader. This must never happen again.”
Right. I was about to get my hands on tens of trillions of won. Even if I paid every cent of tax I owed, I would still be incredibly wealthy.
No matter how insignificant the conditions they were offering might be, I couldn’t get involved with politicians just to save a little on taxes. That was something I needed to avoid.
*A few trillion won? I can just pay it and be done with it.*
I cast my worries aside and leaned back against the soft seat.
*Pop! Pop-pop-pop!*
At Incheon Airport, hundreds of cameras flashed at once.
At the photo line set up under strict security, two men whose professions could not have been more different shook hands with broad smiles.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung. You’ve truly been through a lot.”
“Oh, not at all. You’ve been busy lately too, haven’t you, Mr. President?”
As the Skeleton King watched the scene, he thought,
*What a vile human.*
The thought applied just as much to Team Leader Choi, who was smiling contentedly as though everything had gone according to plan.

“A gift from Magic Johnson.
He said it took a while because he had to have it flown in from the United States on short notice.”
“That gracious human?
A ring for me?”
The Skeleton King stared gravely at the ring I had given him.
“Is this perhaps what humans call a proposal?”
“What the hell are you talking about, you lunatic?
It’s just a ring enchanted with translation magic.”
“Hmm.
I appreciate the gift, but it looks rather crude.
It does not sparkle like a diamond, either.
It is unbefitting of a king’s dignity.”
“Magic Johnson commissioned a Grand Mage he knows to make it specially, so its performance is top-class.
It’s probably worth whatever price they care to name.”
“Now that I look again, I can sense its noble dignity.
It will uphold my royal authority nicely.”
What an irritating bastard.
There was no doubt about it.
He had become far stronger—and far crazier—than he had been as the Skeleton Warlord.
Regardless, he slipped the ring onto his middle finger with a satisfied expression, then pulled a smartphone from the lining of his suit.
That, too, was an expensive, cutting-edge smartphone with a Magic Gem built into it, another gift from Magic Johnson.
“What are you doing?”
“This king must personally express his gratitude to the gracious human.”
“You’ve got better manners than I expected.
Are you going to text him?”
“Vile human.”
“Huh?”
The Skeleton King looked at me as though I were pathetic.
“Who sends texts in this day and age?
Naturally, one uses social media.”
“...Uh, sure.”
“We already follow each other.
I have also learned how to send direct messages.”
I stared at the Skeleton King’s phone, my mouth falling open.
Holy shit.
It was real.
An undead monster with a social media account.
Did this app not even require identity verification?
But something else was even more surprising.
“...You have five thousand followers?”
“State the number accurately.
It is 5,134.
A record achieved in less than a week.”
“What the hell?
Is this fake?”
“Is being handsome not the greatest advantage?
I merely used this king’s face as my profile picture, and countless requests to follow one another came pouring in from around the world.
Heh heh.”
The Skeleton King answered with an arrogant look and began sending a message to Magic Johnson.
└ Good human.
I'm fine thank you. and you?
After checking the message, I let out a small sigh.
“Don’t send messages to anyone else.”
“Why not?”
“If I say don’t, then don’t, you bastard.”
So much for Atlanta, Georgia.
Calling himself a native of Atlanta District, Georgia City, Gyeonggi Province, would have sounded more believable.
Apparently, even translation magic couldn’t save English so painfully Korean that it made my head spin.
“At this rate, even the Akabutakchi tribe, who have preserved their traditions in the Amazon rainforest for hundreds of years, won’t believe you’re American.”
“Hmm.
I do not know exactly what you mean, but the oddly specific nature of it makes me even angrier.”
“Just do as I say.
If your identity gets exposed, it won’t end with a little trouble.”
No matter how good my public image was right now, if the Skeleton King’s identity became known, we would clearly have to brace ourselves for considerable repercussions.
I turned my head.
“Isn’t that right, Team Leader Choi?”
In the seat diagonally beside us, Team Leader Choi had been awake by himself for several minutes.
He answered,
“I was already considering the matter of the Skeleton King—”
“Stone-King.
Call me Mr.
King.”
The Skeleton King cut him off firmly.
Team Leader Choi stared at him for a moment, then continued with a sigh.
“In any case, we are considering every possibility regarding Mr.
King’s future arrangements.
For now, it would be best to avoid exposure to the press and other media.”
“I refuse.
I will proudly reveal myself to the world.”
“Really?
Team Leader Choi, what are the penalties for entering the country illegally?”
Team Leader Choi answered at once.
“Deportation, without question.
He would also have to expect a fine or imprisonment.”
“What about entering illegally from the Demon Realm?”
“It has never happened before, but instead of the police, a large-scale raid team would be dispatched.”
“You heard him.”
The Skeleton King’s eyes swiveled back and forth in silence before he finally spoke.
“...It cannot be helped.
The world is not yet prepared to accept this king, so I shall exercise restraint for a while.”
“That’s what you should do.
Unless you want to spend the rest of your life lying low in my Inventory.”
“A-All right.”
The biggest headache was dealt with.
Now there was the second headache... and this one I had no choice but to face head-on.
Not because I lacked alternatives, but because doing so would help with my plans going forward.
*It’s a pain, but it can’t be helped.*
I quietly tapped the armrest, lost in thought, then abruptly spoke.
“What’s the atmosphere like back home right now?”
Team Leader Choi gave me a terse, emphatic answer.
“It’s insane.”
“...That bad?”
“When someone passes the judicial exam, banners go up in their neighborhood and at their alma mater, and the local newspaper runs a short article.
More than fifteen hundred people pass that exam every year.
How much more attention do you think you would receive, Mr.
Jin Taekyung?”
With that perfectly apt comparison, Team Leader Choi clicked in midair.
The holographic screen built into the seat filled with countless online articles.
[At Last, He Has Returned.]
[Who Is Jin Taekyung?
Chairman Xiao Yang Bows His Head on Behalf of the Chinese People.
The Reverent Farewell of S-Rank Hunters...]
[The Young Hero Who Fought to Rescue Survivors Until the Very End Finally Returns to the Arms of His Homeland.]
It wasn’t just the Korean media.
China, where the incident had taken place, and countries around the world were flooding the internet with article after article about my return and what I would do next.
I had known this was coming and expected it, but I still couldn’t help gaping when I saw a photograph attached to an online article posted five minutes earlier.
“Wait.
Are all those people actually human?”
“They aren’t monsters, so they probably are.”
“Holy shit...”
The photograph showed a crowd packed into Incheon Airport without so much as a gap between them.
Thousands?
No, tens of thousands.
As I stared blankly at the screen, Team Leader Choi continued.
“Traffic throughout the surrounding area has come to a standstill, and a car parade is being prepared under military and police control.”
“What?
A car parade?”
“Did I not tell you?”
“You mentioned it in passing, so I thought you were joking.
I mean... isn’t this a bit much?”
Team Leader Choi shook his head firmly.
“It has to be this much.
You are the new S-rank Hunter representing Korea.”
“Even so, this is excessive.
At this rate, the President will show up too.”
“Ah, I really did fail to mention that.”
“What?”
“He is coming.
The Blue House contacted us first this morning.
I meant to tell you on the plane, but I dozed off and forgot.”
For a moment, my thoughts ground to a halt.
Tens of thousands of people waiting for me at Incheon Airport.
Paralyzed roads and a spectacular car parade.
And now the President was coming too.
I sat there speechless, then finally forced the words out.
“...Really?
You’re not joking?”
“Yes.
They want to shake your hand, stand with you at the photo line, and take a picture together.”
“Team Leader Choi, I don’t know anything about politics.
If I get tangled up in something and it goes wrong, I’ll be completely screwed.”
“I know how you feel, Mr.
Jin Taekyung.
That is why I tried to turn them down politely, but they seemed quite determined.
It was not easy.”
“You still should have refused.
Even if I belong to Peace Guild, how could you make that decision on your own?”
No matter how much we trusted each other or how little time there had been, this was something he should have consulted me about.
At the sight of my rigid expression, Team Leader Choi lowered his head apologetically.
“I’m sorry.
They offered several favorable conditions, including tax breaks, so I thought it would benefit you as well.”
“Forget that.
Call them right now and tell them it’s off...
Wait.
Tax breaks?”
“Yes.
You know the bounty that was placed on the Arch Lich.
If the Chinese government pays it to you, then under Korean law, it would count as foreign-source income for a Korean resident...”
“Wait.
So how much tax would I have to pay in total?”
“I cannot say for certain, but it would be several trillion won.
The bounty alone is fifty trillion won.
Even if we simplify things and assume only ten percent is deducted, it would still be an enormous amount.
Of course, the amount left over would be much larger.”
“...That’s true.”
“Once again, I apologize for failing to get your approval.
I will tell the Blue House that this is no longer happening.”
I nodded, my expression hard.
“Team Leader.
This must never happen again.”
Right.
I was about to get my hands on tens of trillions of won.
Even if I paid every cent of tax I owed, I would still be incredibly wealthy.
No matter how insignificant the conditions they were offering might be, I couldn’t get involved with politicians just to save a little on taxes.
That was something I needed to avoid.
*A few trillion won?
I can just pay it and be done with it.*
I cast my worries aside and leaned back against the soft seat.
*Pop!
Pop-pop-pop!*
At Incheon Airport, hundreds of cameras flashed at once.
At the photo line set up under strict security, two men whose professions could not have been more different shook hands with broad smiles.
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung.
You’ve truly been through a lot.”
“Oh, not at all.
You’ve been busy lately too, haven’t you, Mr.
President?”
As the Skeleton King watched the scene, he thought,
*What a vile human.*
The thought applied just as much to Team Leader Choi, who was smiling contentedly as though everything had gone according to plan.

chapters.title: Chapter 440
paragraphs: The day Jin Taekyung’s private jet landed at Incheon International Airport, cameras from around the world turned toward Korea.

Countless flashes erupted without pause, bright enough to make people forget the sun was already setting. Despite the midwinter cold, hundreds of thousands packed the surrounding area and greeted the returning hero with thunderous cheers.
And at the center of it all stood one man, staring blankly at the welcome that had far exceeded anything he’d imagined.
“...What the hell is all this, goddammit?”
His voice was no louder than an ant’s, but the world’s media outlets had brought their best equipment. They didn’t miss the young hero’s offhand remark.
“What the sibu-leol?”
“Que veut-elle dire par là?”
“Was meint sie damit?”
Korean profanity was famously diverse—so much so that even translation devices struggled with it.

The Western reporters hesitated, unable to grasp the full-bodied meaning of *sibu-leol*, but the Korean reporters, who had mastered all manner of wildly inventive curses since their school days, moved like lightning.
“An article! Get it online now! We have to be first!”
“W-With this?”
“You idiot, don’t you know that everything Jin Taekyung does is breaking news right now? Stop wasting time. Get a shot of his mouth as he swears, grab the audio, and upload it immediately!”
“Yes, Senior! But, Senior... won’t this cause trouble?”
“Trouble? What trouble?”
“If it looks like we’re attacking Jin Taekyung, there could be a backlash. You know, something like *Jin Taekyung Profanity Controversy*...”
The veteran reporter scowled at his junior.
*Was that kid in his second year now, or his third? After working in the field this long, he should’ve learned to think, but he was still hopelessly slow on the uptake.*
The veteran barely held back a curse when he remembered that the idiot in front of him was the bureau chief’s nephew.
“Hey. Reporter Hong.”
“Yes.”
“Jin Taekyung is allowed to swear.”
“What?”
“When a politician or celebrity swears in public in this country, they become the worst person alive. But when Jin Taekyung does it, people nearly die of happiness. Understand?”
“Yes, yes, Senior!”
Only then did the junior nod. The veteran let out a deep sigh and looked at his smartphone.
The chatroom for the live stream currently airing on iTube, the world’s largest video-sharing website, was already going berserk.

Broadcast networks, cable channels, and general programming channels were all showing the scene. On top of that, viewers around the world were watching through iTube’s live stream.
With untold numbers watching, the massive limousine bus carrying Jin Taekyung and his companions began to move.

└ Wow, this is insane. There are so many people that the cameras can’t even fit them all in the frame ᄃᄃ; └ This is bigger than the Olympics. How many drones are there, anyway? └ A lot, I guess? └ I know that much... └ I got goose bumps the moment the bus started moving. My chest actually swelled up. Is this for real?
The limousine bus carrying Jin Taekyung and his companions moved at ten kilometers per hour through a wall of people.
Brilliant fireworks exploded without pause, and flower petals scattered by the crowd whirled through the air on the wind.
At first, Jin Taekyung watched the scene with an awkwardly stiff expression. Before long, however, he smiled and waved at the crowd.
*They’re people who like me.*
Six months ago, Jin Taekyung had been no more than a grain of sand on a beach.
An F-rank Hunter who could be found anywhere, ignored by everyone and swept away whenever a wave rolled in.
He had never once imagined that a day like this would come.
*All I ever dreamed of was retiring without dying...*

He had gained so much. He’d been forced to walk a thorny path with death on every side, but the fruit hanging along the way had been sweet. Power beyond his wildest imagination, enormous wealth, and even fame.
And...
“You’ve worked hard, my son.”
“I’m really proud of you too, Mr. Jin Taekyung, but these flashes are so bright I can barely see your face. How long are those reporters planning to keep this up?”
His family, who had always been with him.
His mother’s warm hand stroking his back made his throat tighten, while the sight of his sister scrunching up her face against the flashes drew a quiet laugh from him.
“Mom worked harder than I did. You too, Sis.”
“I know. Mom and Oppa worked harder.”
“I thought you were barely human, but you do have a shred of conscience after all.”
“Wow, listen to him.”
“Smile, you idiot. Do you have any idea how many cameras are filming us right now?”
With that joking remark, Jin Taekyung pulled them both into a hug. Then he met a pair of eyes watching him from behind his family.
“You’ve truly been through a lot, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“You too, Team Leader Choi. I’m just a big, dumb brute. Without you, I really would’ve had a hard time.”
“I only did what I had to do. And I’ll continue to do the same.”
“You’re saying something scary with a smile.”
“You know this isn’t the end.”
He knew.
That was why his resolve hardened even further.
Jin Taekyung had made it this far across a perilous field of thorns. He couldn’t allow his precious family and friends to walk the same path.
Even if his feet became covered in blood and he collapsed from the pain, he would protect them from the threats drawing ever closer.
Sometimes they would join forces. And even if it meant sacrificing himself...
“I’ll be counting on you for a long time to come.”
Team Leader Choi stared at the hand Jin Taekyung held out. Then a deep dimple appeared beside his mouth.
“Yes. Always.”
Just as the two firmly clasped hands, a grumbling voice rang out inside Jin Taekyung’s head.
*You’re all having a grand old time.*
*Are you still sulking?*
*Who is sulking?! Does this body, reborn as a great king, look as though it would feel such a petty human emotion?*
*You’re definitely sulking.*
*I am not!*
The attention seeker—no, the Skeleton King—who had been forced by circumstances to hide in the Inventory had been sulking bitterly for quite a while.
Jin Taekyung smiled faintly and spoke inwardly.
*Hey.*
*Do not speak to me!*
*Thanks for everything so far. I’m counting on you from here on out, too.*
*H-Hmm.*
The Skeleton King cleared his throat and continued hesitantly.
*Since you put it that way, I shall consider it.*
*Consider what?*
*Staying with you, you vile human.*
*Oh, you don’t need to consider that.*
*What?*

*You’re joining Peace Guild no matter what. I’ve already had the contract drawn up, so go put your thumbprint on it. No, wait. Your fingerprints won’t show up in a records check, so I guess you’ll have to stamp it with your skull.*
*What is this?! Is this not a free and democratic country?!*
*Nope. I’m going to work you like a slave and suck out every last drop, right down to your marrow.*
*Release this body immediately! Turn the car around!*
Unable to hold it in any longer, Jin Taekyung burst out laughing and leaned toward the driver’s seat.
“Could we head straight to the next destination?”
“Pardon?”
The startled driver stammered out a reply.
“That’s different from the instructions we received beforehand.”
“Can’t we?”
“I’m sorry, but we can’t.”
“We really can’t?”
“I’m afraid not...”
“Seriously, truly, we can’t?”
The driver answered in a voice halfway to surrender.
“...I think we might be able to.”
“Then please take us to Peace Guild’s guild house.”
The driver relayed the request to his superior. After it passed through several levels of reporting, the higher-ups were bewildered but readily agreed.
And the roughly three thousand drones followed the seemingly endless car parade.
The limousine bus carrying Jin Taekyung and his companions eventually stopped in front of Peace Guild’s guild house.
Every moment of their meeting with the Guild members waiting there was captured on camera and broadcast around the world.
Even after midnight passed and the long-awaited Christmas Eve arrived, the fervor showed no sign of dying down.
If anything, people seemed to compete to feed fresh wood and wind to the fading flames.
The name Jin Taekyung was everywhere, and for someone still suffering from severe aftereffects, it was unbearable torment.
“This morning, the United States’ S-rank Hunter Magic Johnson announced through his official social-media account that he is pursuing some kind of agreement with Peace Guild—”
*Bang!*
The announcer’s face vanished from the holographic television. The man who had smashed the machine screamed.
“Jin Taekyung, Jin Taekyung, Jin Taekyung!”
*Bang! Crash!*
His eyes were bloodshot. Powerful qi shot from his wildly swinging fists, smashing everything around him and reducing it to dust.
That name was more hateful than any other.
At the same time, it belonged to the man who had shown him a fear he could never forget.
“Aaaaaaaagh!”
Just as Go Jun howled amid the devastated room, a faint sound of movement reached him, followed by a cautious voice.
“T-Team Leader.”

An F-rank Hunter who could be found anywhere, ignored by everyone and swept away whenever a wave rolled in.
He had never once imagined that a day like this would come.
*All I ever dreamed of was retiring without dying...*
He had gained so much.
He’d been forced to walk a thorny path with death on every side, but the fruit hanging along the way had been sweet.
Power beyond his wildest imagination, enormous wealth, and even fame.
And...
“You’ve worked hard, my son.”
“I’m really proud of you too, Mr.
Jin Taekyung, but these flashes are so bright I can barely see your face.
How long are those reporters planning to keep this up?”
His family, who had always been with him.
His mother’s warm hand stroking his back made his throat tighten, while the sight of his sister scrunching up her face against the flashes drew a quiet laugh from him.
“Mom worked harder than I did.
You too, Sis.”
“I know.
Mom and Oppa worked harder.”
“I thought you were barely human, but you do have a shred of conscience after all.”
“Wow, listen to him.”
“Smile, you idiot.
Do you have any idea how many cameras are filming us right now?”
With that joking remark, Jin Taekyung pulled them both into a hug.
Then he met a pair of eyes watching him from behind his family.
“You’ve truly been through a lot, Mr.
Jin Taekyung.”
“You too, Team Leader Choi.
I’m just a big, dumb brute.
Without you, I really would’ve had a hard time.”
“I only did what I had to do.
And I’ll continue to do the same.”
“You’re saying something scary with a smile.”
“You know this isn’t the end.”
He knew.
That was why his resolve hardened even further.
Jin Taekyung had made it this far across a perilous field of thorns.
He couldn’t allow his precious family and friends to walk the same path.
Even if his feet became covered in blood and he collapsed from the pain, he would protect them from the threats drawing ever closer.
Sometimes they would join forces.
And even if it meant sacrificing himself...
“I’ll be counting on you for a long time to come.”
Team Leader Choi stared at the hand Jin Taekyung held out.
Then a deep dimple appeared beside his mouth.
“Yes.
Always.”
Just as the two firmly clasped hands, a grumbling voice rang out inside Jin Taekyung’s head.
*You’re all having a grand old time.*
*Are you still sulking?*
*Who is sulking?!
Does this body, reborn as a great king, look as though it would feel such a petty human emotion?*
*You’re definitely sulking.*
*I am not!*
The attention seeker—no, the Skeleton King—who had been forced by circumstances to hide in the Inventory had been sulking bitterly for quite a while.
Jin Taekyung smiled faintly and spoke inwardly.
*Hey.*
*Do not speak to me!*
*Thanks for everything so far.
I’m counting on you from here on out, too.*
*H-Hmm.*
The Skeleton King cleared his throat and continued hesitantly.
*Since you put it that way, I shall consider it.*
*Consider what?*
*Staying with you, you vile human.*
*Oh, you don’t need to consider that.*
*What?*
*You’re joining Peace Guild no matter what.
I’ve already had the contract drawn up, so go put your thumbprint on it.
No, wait.
Your fingerprints won’t show up in a records check, so I guess you’ll have to stamp it with your skull.*
*What is this?!
Is this not a free and democratic country?!*
*Nope.
I’m going to work you like a slave and suck out every last drop, right down to your marrow.*
*Release this body immediately!
Turn the car around!*
Unable to hold it in any longer, Jin Taekyung burst out laughing and leaned toward the driver’s seat.
“Could we head straight to the next destination?”
“Pardon?”
The startled driver stammered out a reply.
“That’s different from the instructions we received beforehand.”
“Can’t we?”
“I’m sorry, but we can’t.”
“We really can’t?”
“I’m afraid not...”
“Seriously, truly, we can’t?”
The driver answered in a voice halfway to surrender.
“...I think we might be able to.”
“Then please take us to Peace Guild’s guild house.”
The driver relayed the request to his superior.
After it passed through several levels of reporting, the higher-ups were bewildered but readily agreed.
And the roughly three thousand drones followed the seemingly endless car parade.
The limousine bus carrying Jin Taekyung and his companions eventually stopped in front of Peace Guild’s guild house.
Every moment of their meeting with the Guild members waiting there was captured on camera and broadcast around the world.
Even after midnight passed and the long-awaited Christmas Eve arrived, the fervor showed no sign of dying down.
If anything, people seemed to compete to feed fresh wood and wind to the fading flames.
The name Jin Taekyung was everywhere, and for someone still suffering from severe aftereffects, it was unbearable torment.
“This morning, the United States’ S-rank Hunter Magic Johnson announced through his official social-media account that he is pursuing some kind of agreement with Peace Guild—”
*Bang!*
The announcer’s face vanished from the holographic television.
The man who had smashed the machine screamed.
“Jin Taekyung, Jin Taekyung, Jin Taekyung!”
*Bang!
Crash!*
His eyes were bloodshot.
Powerful qi shot from his wildly swinging fists, smashing everything around him and reducing it to dust.
That name was more hateful than any other.
At the same time, it belonged to the man who had shown him a fear he could never forget.
“Aaaaaaaagh!”
Just as Go Jun howled amid the devastated room, a faint sound of movement reached him, followed by a cautious voice.
“T-Team Leader.”

chapters.title: Chapter 441
paragraphs: “T-Team Leader. May I come in for a moment?”
The voice was taut with tension.
Go Jun glared at the door with bloodshot eyes and thrust out a hand.
*Crack!*
A tremendous force tore through the air, ripping apart the iron door and crumpling it like a sheet of paper.
The security-team employee who witnessed the incredible sight from a few feet away swallowed a startled breath.
“Gasp.”
“I told you not to let anyone approach.”
The moment he met Go Jun’s blazing red eyes, a chill ran down his spine.

He had heard his colleagues talk about the extreme change in their direct superior, who had always been as precise and cold as a machine. But facing him like this, the team member’s voice trembled with fear despite himself.
“I-It’s just that... there’s something I need to report...”
“Put it off.”
His voice was low, as though dragged up from the depths of an abyss.
The team member would have loved to do exactly that. But if it had been anything trivial, they would never have drawn lots to decide who had to deliver the report.
He swallowed hard and summoned his courage.
“The head of the investigation team contacted us urgently. He said they found a strange object they couldn’t identify...”
Go Jun, who had been about to turn away, came to an abrupt stop.
“A strange object?”
“Yes, Team Leader.”
“Could it be—”
“No, sir.”
Afraid Go Jun’s anger might turn on him, the team member hurriedly continued.
“We checked. None of the late Vice Guild Master’s belongings have been found yet.”
“Are you sure?”
“Yes. We’re constantly monitoring the team members dispatched to the site in case they try to pocket anything. There’s no doubt.”
“And?”
“Pardon?”
“There’s only one report I need from those bastards. A report saying they found what I need.”
Go Jun’s eyes darkened.
Even now, with the Crown Prince Party—closely tied to Ares Guild—on the decline, the Guild’s influence and power remained intact.
The person in charge could change. The government could be replaced. But the greed that lived in every human heart would never disappear.
Even the straightest bamboo bent beneath enough weight. Go Jun had created that weight with tens of billions of won.
The head of the investigation team managing the city that had once been the Arch Lich’s stronghold, along with the senior officials under him, had proved no different.
“Tell those bastards to find it, no matter what it takes. Until then, I don’t want to hear from them again.”
There was no such thing as a favor in this world without a price. Go Jun had bought them with a fortune, and if they failed to deliver what he wanted, he intended to retaliate accordingly.
That was how important the object was.
Not merely because it was a keepsake of the Master he had followed like a father. It could also become a powerful weapon—one capable of driving someone into a corner with no escape.
*A holographic recorder.*
Lee Jungryong had been the true master of the immensely influential Ares Guild. In case the unexpected ever happened, he had always carried a miniature holographic recorder on his person.
The day he died at Jin Taekyung’s hands had been no exception.
*All the evidence is in there. If I can find it, then afterward...*
At that moment, the fire in Go Jun’s eyes wavered violently.
*Afterward... what am I supposed to do?*
Before he knew it, the face of one man—someone he hated beyond measure and feared even more—flashed before his eyes.
*...Jin Taekyung.*
Merely thinking the name made his heart plummet and his hands and feet tremble.
The indifferent gaze that had looked down at him beneath the faint moonlight and the dry voice that had accompanied it clouded his eyes and ears like an apparition.
*I’ll say this one last time.*
The voice had burrowed into Go Jun’s ears while he screamed in unimaginable agony.
*Let it end with Lee Jungryong. Hide your teeth and put away your claws. If you do that... nothing will happen.*

Every bone in his body had been crushed like matchsticks, and his raw flesh had been torn away as though wrung from his body. Without even getting the chance to wield his weapon properly, he had been left thrashing in an endless swamp of pain.
Lee Jungryong had been an insurmountable wall and a Master Go Jun revered.
Jin Taekyung was something no one had ever seen before.
No. He was like...
“A monster.”
The single word that escaped Go Jun without his realizing it was steeped in all the emotions and fear he felt.
Then he came to his senses and understood.
His hatred for Jin Taekyung was nothing compared to his terror.

Jin Taekyung’s existence was fear itself, branded forever into Go Jun’s soul like a mark burned into flesh. At the same time, it was another name for the perfect helplessness he had felt for the first time in his life.
“T-Team Leader?”
Go Jun did not answer. Teeth clenched, he lowered his head and stared at his trembling hands.
*What the fuck is this...*
*Crunch.*
He bit his lip until it bled, then raised his head. Ignoring the team member’s bewildered stare at the sight of his frightened superior, he spoke.
“Tell the head of the investigation team to bring me that damned strange object. I don’t know what it is, but I should at least see it for myself.”
“But a moment ago, you said—Ah, understood.”
Realizing his mistake, the team member hurriedly bowed and left the room.
Only after walking a considerable distance down the corridor did he finally release the breath he had been holding. He gestured to the hotel employees waiting nearby.
“Wait here for a while. Go in once he’s calmed down. And the new room is ready, right?”
The Chinese hotel employees nodded calmly.
This was not the first time Go Jun had gone on a rampage. It had already happened several times over the past week.
But what did that matter?
Until a few days ago, the hotel had belonged to a local notable in Sichuan Province. Once Ares Guild bought it, the Koreans before them became their new employers.
And excellent employers they were, lavishing the staff with extra pay in exchange for their silence.
“I’m tired of repeating myself. We all know the situation, so let’s do our jobs properly.”
The team member tossed them a thick envelope, wiped the sweat from his brow, and walked away.

Being unable to leave this godforsaken land of China was bad enough. What troubled him even more was the unstable condition of the man poised to succeed Lee Jungryong as the new captain of Ares Guild.
*Could that rumor really have been true?*
He recalled the story quietly circulating within the security team.
And the unease stirring within him.
*The treatment is incredible, but if Team Leader stays like that from now on...*
There would be no problem if Go Jun remained the head of security. The enormous warship called the Ares Guild was not so fragile that one mistake by a helmsman could make it capsize.
But if the man at the helm became its new captain, that was a different story.
*Damn it. I’ve never had to worry about this before.*
The team member muttered to himself and pulled a smartphone from inside his suit jacket. It was a work phone that left no records and could not be traced.
After a long series of rings, someone answered.
“Ah, Mr. Park. I’ve been waiting for your call.”
“I’ll get straight to the point. Our team leader wants to see the object you mentioned for himself.”
“In person?”
“Yes. In person. Our team leader wants to avoid public attention as much as possible right now, so you understand what I’m saying, don’t you?”
The head of the investigation team cleared his throat on the other end of the call.
“Ahem. That may be difficult. Since this is the Arch Lich’s former stronghold, there are foreign personnel dispatched by the United Nations as well, and security is tighter than you might think...”
“Name your price. But there can’t be a single mistake.”
A short while later, the team member ended the call and clicked his tongue.
“Greedy bastards. Money is all they care about. Then again, I guess that works in our favor.”
The world did not change easily. Before overwhelming wealth and power, the word *impossible* lost all meaning.
Since joining Ares Guild’s security team, he had witnessed the impossible being made possible countless times.
And that fortresslike power would naturally be inherited by one man.
*Team Leader Go Jun.*
The new captain of Ares Guild.
He himself was merely one of countless rowers, but Go Jun was different. As his thoughts reached that point, he found himself wondering about the one man Go Jun feared so much.
*Jin Taekyung.*
No one could silence people completely.
The rumor had begun when three Hunters who had secretly left with Go Jun one day a week earlier started talking.
For now, only a tiny handful within the security team—Go Jun’s closest associates—knew the truth. But soon enough, it would spread like an epidemic.
*If it’s true... Haa. Things have gotten seriously complicated.*
The team member took a deep breath and focused.
From now on, he would have countless decisions to agonize over. Should he stay aboard his current ship or leave for another?
If he wanted to avoid becoming anyone’s enemy, his only choice was to leave the field entirely.
*I need to keep my head on straight. Yeah.*
Right now, his first priority was retrieving the object the head of the investigation team had smuggled out.
As he headed toward the agreed meeting place, he suddenly found himself envying Jin Taekyung.
*Damn. If I had fifty trillion won like that bastard, I’d move straight to Europe and live like royalty.*
He was wealthy himself and owned several buildings, but human greed was not so easily satisfied.
Once someone owned an expensive foreign car, they wanted a luxury yacht and a helicopter. Then they wanted a private jet of their own.
The team member smacked his lips in envy.
*I wonder what Jin Taekyung is doing right now. Throwing a party on a luxury yacht with Playboy models?*
Well-tanned bronze muscles rippled beneath the blazing sunlight.
Their identity was that of beautiful model women from around the world who had gathered to enjoy a yacht party with me...
“One, two!”
“Heave-ho!”
...or not.
They belonged to the river bandits of the Water Dragon Stronghold.
I watched the musclebound monsters bustling around the deck with a mournful gaze.
*A yacht party, my ass.*
I had only ever seen that kind of thing online, and I intended to keep it that way.
Reality wasn’t a boat party with beautiful women. It was staring out at the Yangtze from a deck packed with musclebound river bandits doing boat PT.
No. There was one more thing.
*Whoosh!*
I had to dodge the finger flicks our boisterous Old Master, Fire King Jeok Cheongang, sent flying whenever he got bored.
“Well, look at you. Dodging, are we?”

“...Isn’t dodging them the whole point of this training? You said I needed to maintain a mind like a clear mirror and still water while heightening my senses so I could get used to my Middle Dantian.”
Jeok Cheongang answered without a shred of shame.
“That one was meant to hit you. How dare you look away during training?”
“I was looking away with both eyes.”
“Why, you little... Want me to gouge them out for you?”
Eyes blazing, Jeok Cheongang crooked his fingers like claws and continued.
“Do you think this training is easy? Even when you concentrate fully, you can barely dodge them.”
“Fine, fine. I understand. I said I understand.”
Grumbling, I closed my eyes.
Then, a moment later, I quietly opened them again.
“What?”
“Didn’t I just dodge that perfectly even while looking away?”
“Oh. You did, didn’t you?”
What the hell was this?
Jeok Cheongang pressed his lips tightly together beneath my incredulous stare, then abruptly exploded.
“Not like that! Do it like that brat! Like him!”
He pointed at a young man sitting cross-legged without so much as twitching.
For some reason, Cheongpung had been forced to join me in training.

“Look at that brat. He may be a little strange most of the time, but when it matters, he does everything perfectly. His posture hasn’t wavered, and his breathing remains long, light, and steady. An unwavering mind and posture, no matter what happens around him. That is what it means to possess a mind like a clear mirror and still water.”
After showering Cheongpung with praise without pausing for breath, Jeok Cheongang pointed at him again.
“Watch carefully how he dodges. Now, when I send a finger flick...”
*Whoosh! Thud!*
The finger flick struck Cheongpung squarely in the temple, and his eyes flew open.
He looked around through eyes still heavy with sleep, then rubbed his head when the pain finally seemed to register.
“Ow. That hurts...”
Then he returned to dreamland faster than light.
I stared at Jeok Cheongang.
“Clear as a mirror? What?”
“A clear mirror... Forget it. You and that brat both. To hell with all of it!”
The Yangtze was peaceful today, too.
