Even Cheongpung dropped the candied fruit he had been bringing to his mouth.
*Am I dreaming?*
I was seriously considering the question when Jeok Cheongang continued with a warm smile.
“Come to think of it, this old man has never seen such a large and magnificent library in his life.
Would it be all right if I looked around for a while?”
Zhuge Gyun answered with a dazed expression.
“Of course.”
“Even if I burn it down?”
“...Pardon?”
“It was a joke, you little punk.
Ho-ho.
How could I burn everything in sight when I’m here as a guest?”
Jeok Cheongang laughed heartily, then added,
“Knocking over a bookshelf by accident would be another matter.”
In the next instant, Jeok Cheongang shot upward like a streak of light.
At the same time, a palm strike carrying the tremendous force of ten thousand geun slammed into the nearest bookshelf.
Boom!
It happened before anyone could stop him.
I stared at the scene unfolding before me, my mouth hanging open.
*Oh, fuck.*
Rumble...
The bookshelf, which looked to be at least three zhang tall, began to tilt.
And there were hundreds of them.
In the blink of an eye, the countless shelves packed together at regular intervals became one enormous row of dominoes.
“W-wait, wait, wait, wait!”
Crash!
Rumble-rumble-rumble!
The deafening roar swallowed Zhuge Gyun’s scream.
As every bookshelf came crashing down, years of accumulated dust erupted into the air and filled the library in a dense cloud.
No, I wasn’t even sure it could still be called a library.
A graveyard of books would have been more appropriate.
It might even have become one person’s grave.
“Fatherrrr!”
Jeok Cheongang patted the wailing Zhuge Gyun on the shoulder.
“You’re the new Family Head of the Zhuge Clan now.”
“Nooo!”
Whack!
Jeok Cheongang smacked him on the back of the head and gave him an incredulous look.
“You really can’t take a joke, can you?
Can’t you see your father over there, alive and well?”
Jeok Cheongang was telling the truth.
A couple of coughs came from within the thick cloud of dust, and a slender figure emerged, waving one hand as he walked toward us.
“Well, now.
Cough.
I’m sorry I couldn’t come out to greet you sooner.
There have been an unusual number of matters requiring my attention lately.
Cough.”
“At least you know.
What an ill-mannered brat.”
Jeok Cheongang answered curtly and flicked his sleeve.
Whoosh!
Compressed air burst outward, scattering the dust cloud.
At last, the man came fully into view.
“Ha.
Seeing you like this makes me realize how much time has passed.
Do you remember this old man?”
A clear voice answered.
“Of course.
It was the fifth Mid-Autumn Festival after my birth.
Senior ate two plates of roast duck and drank five jars of Yeoahong, then fought a duel with Great Hero Peng as the gathering drew to a close and ended up with a bloody nose.”
“What?
That Thunderbolt Saber King bastard was there too?
We even fought?”
“Yes.
Great Hero Peng laughed loudly and struck the table, spilling wine on Senior’s knee.
It was a minor disagreement.”
“That sounds like a major incident where it wouldn’t have been strange for someone to die.”
Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet laugh before continuing.
“Quite a few years have passed, but that incredible head of yours is still as sharp as ever.
All right, enough nonsense.
Come here.
You have guests waiting for you.”
“I was planning to greet them regardless.”
Though the middle-aged man was covered in dust, it couldn’t conceal his refined appearance.
He was the youngest Sect Leader of any prestigious great family or sect I had met so far.
His eyes, unusually clear and radiant, turned toward us.
“My apologies for keeping such honored guests waiting.
I am Zhuge Feng.”
It was a remarkably plain greeting for the Family Head of the Zhuge Clan, the foremost great family in Hubei Province and one of the central pillars of the orthodox faction.
Then, before anyone could respond, Zhuge Feng continued.
The moment I heard his next words, I suddenly understood why his sobriquet was Crouching Dragon Guest.
“Time is as precious as gold, and I have no desire to take anyone else’s gold.
Only those who wish to remain need stay.
Oh, and I’ve always believed people should make themselves comfortable when they talk, so please don’t take this the wrong way.”
I wondered what he meant until Zhuge Feng promptly flopped onto his side, paying no attention to the dust coating the floor.
A laugh escaped me.
“Sure, why not?
This is comfortable.”
I lay down at an angle and propped my chin on one hand.
The corners of his eyes curved like crescent moons.
Though everyone looked dumbfounded, they sat down one by one and listened to Zhuge Feng.
Mu Song tried to leave, saying he had to visit a Yangtze River Channel League stronghold in Hubei, but one remark from Zhuge Feng stopped him in his tracks.
“I won’t stop you if you wish to leave, but what I am about to say concerns you deeply as well, Ship-Fire Boy Mu Song.”
Mu Song hesitated, then remained behind.
Surprisingly, Mungyeong, who had seemed the most likely to leave first, stayed quietly where he was.
Then again, with everyone else remaining, leaving alone might have drawn even more attention.
The Zhuge Clan’s intelligence network had already informed Zhuge Feng that this young medical apprentice was the Divine Physician’s Disciple.
He gave Mungyeong a curious look, but soon turned away and began to speak.
“It was exactly one month ago.
I was in the library, reading the *Records of the Grand Historian* for the eighty-fifth time, when I heard the news.”
The Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families were the leading powers of their respective provinces.
With roots stretching back anywhere from a hundred years to several centuries, each possessed a dense intelligence network that allowed them to know their territory like the palm of their hand.
The Zhuge Clan was no exception.
“The Sea Serpent Society had disappeared.”
“The Sea Serpent Society?
What’s that, Benefactor?”
“I don’t know either.”
Unlike the bewildered Cheongpung and me, everyone else’s eyes widened.
Mu Song’s reaction stood out more than anyone else’s.
“Th-the Sea Serpent Society?”
“Yes, the very one you know.
The association formed by the countless fishermen and boatmen of Hubei Province.”
Ah.
Now I understood.
I had never heard of the Sea Serpent Society, but I could guess what kind of organization it was.
To put it simply and dispense with all the old-fashioned explanations, it was a sort of professional association.
Just as each region had a Hunter Association, Hubei Province had—or rather, used to have—an association of fishermen called the Sea Serpent Society.
And this was unquestionably good news, at least for Mu Song.
The faint smile tugging at the corners of his mouth was proof enough.
“I cannot say what the Zhuge Clan thinks of this, but as someone devoted to the League, I welcome the news.
The Sea Serpent Society caused my Master no end of trouble.”
“I thought you would feel that way.
At least within Hubei Province, it was the only organization capable of standing against the Yangtze River Channel League.”
Tributaries of the Yangtze ran throughout Hubei Province like a spiderweb.
No matter how powerful the Yangtze River Channel League was, it must have been vastly outnumbered by the people who made their living from fishing.
Though Hubei was outside the Sichuan territory under his responsibility, Mu Song laughed heartily at the news that one powerful rival had disappeared.
“But how did they end up disbanding?
Did they happen to smuggle salt or something...?”
Zhuge Feng shook his head.
“Of course not.
Even if they had been smuggling salt, the Sea Serpent Society would never have handled it so carelessly.
And if they had been caught, a fleet dispatched by order of the Son of Heaven would already be filling the Yangtze throughout Hubei.”
“Then was it an internal conflict?”
“I don’t think you properly understood what I said.”
His clear, transparent eyes fixed on Mu Song.
As he faced Mu Song’s confusion, Zhuge Feng continued slowly.
“The Sea Serpent Society disappeared.
Someone crushed it utterly.”
“The night before I received that report, a banquet was held to celebrate the Society Head’s eightieth birthday.
Forty-five shipowners who had sworn loyalty to him and roughly a thousand members of the Sea Serpent Society attended.
They drank until past midnight and launched dozens of pleasure boats onto the waters of Red Cliffs.
And that was the last of it.”
The next morning, an old boatman who rose at dawn found the waters of Red Cliffs choked with corpses and the wreckage of brutally shattered boats.
The Society Head and the organization’s core members, including dozens of shipowners, had all met their deaths at Red Cliffs.
The Sea Serpent Society had lost both its head and its body.
Nothing can move without either.
The Sea Serpent Society, which had stood shoulder to shoulder with the Yangtze River Channel League and wielded power throughout Hubei Province for decades, disappeared just like that.
“H-how could such a thing happen...?”
“It is strange that you, of all people, knew nothing about it.”
Zhuge Feng stared steadily at the speechless Mu Song.
“Do you know who moved first after the incident at Red Cliffs became known?
The authorities?
The Sea Serpent Society members who were lucky enough to survive?
No.
It was the Yangtze River Channel League.
They invaded the Sea Serpent Society’s territory and took control of the Yangtze with astonishing speed.”
“...Great Hero Zhuge.”
Mu Song’s face hardened.
Like the rest of us, he seemed to have finally realized why he had needed to remain.
“Are you saying you suspect me?
The League?”
“Of course I didn’t.
The Great Hero Hwang of Donghu Stronghold whom I know is not such a foolish man.
He is different from the other foolish, violent Stronghold Lords.”
Zhuge Feng brushed the dust from his shoulder and smiled faintly at Mu Song.
“That was certainly what I thought—until the Dongting Fisherman, who had publicly condemned the Yangtze River Channel League, disappeared three days ago.”
At that moment, unrest spread through the group, and a familiar notification rang in my ears.
Ding.

chapters.title: Chapter 446
paragraphs: Ding.
**System** A Quest has been generated.
A familiar System notification.
Immediately afterward, a translucent holographic window visible only to me appeared in midair.

**System Quest Another Chaos** An ominous air hangs over the once-peaceful Hubei Province. The clear waters of the Yangtze have been dyed red with blood, the once-mighty Sea Serpent Society has fallen amid countless deaths, and the Dongting Fisherman, who publicly condemned the Yangtze River Channel League, has disappeared. If someone uncovers the truth behind these events and finds the culprit, the chaos will subside. **Grade:** Peak **Restriction:** Jin Taekyung **Mission:** Uncover the truth behind the events *(Incomplete) Reward:** ??? **Failure:** The chaos in Hubei Province will worsen, and further incidents will occur Will you accept the Quest? Y / N
*A Quest...*
I slowly looked around.
Mu Song sat with his lips pressed tightly together, while Crouching Dragon Guest Zhuge Feng stared at him with a cold smile.
Jeok Cheongang frowned as he watched the two of them, and Mungyeong sat expressionlessly.
And finally... there was Jin Wikyung, calmly observing the entire situation.
*So he did know.*

According to Zhuge Feng, the Sea Serpent Society Head and a thousand of his men had been buried beneath the waters of Red Cliffs a fortnight ago. Jin Wikyung must have heard about it on his way to Sichuan.
*And adding Hubei to our return route means the leadership in Henan approved it too.*
Now that the bloody incidents in Shaolin and Sichuan had exposed Dark Heaven’s existence to the entire world, the series of events unfolding in Hubei could not be taken lightly.
If this was Dark Heaven’s scheme, we had to stop it.
And if the Yangtze River Channel League had taken advantage of the chaos caused by Dark Heaven to carry out some plot of its own, they had to be punished as an example to others.
Jin Wikyung had not come here as the Lesser Family Head or acting Family Head of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.
He had come as an inspector for the new Murim Alliance that would soon be formed.
What that meant was simple.
*I have to stand with Jin Wikyung too.*
Besides, the Quest carried no penalty. There was little point in asking whether I would accept when I was already in the same boat as him.
I muttered inwardly.
*Yes.*
Ding.
**System Quest accepted! - Quest **Another Chaos** has been registered in the Quest Window! Quest information may be updated depending on the situation.
I wasn’t sure what else there was to update.

Judging by Zhuge Feng’s words and the atmosphere I had sensed on the way to the Zhuge Clan, all of Hubei Province had already branded the Yangtze River Channel League as the culprit and was pointing fingers at them.
But...
“Are you certain the Yangtze River Channel League is responsible?”
Personally, I didn’t think we could jump to conclusions just yet.
My question broke the heavy silence. Crouching Dragon Guest Zhuge Feng smiled faintly.
“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung. You seem to have many questions about this matter.”
“I can’t say I don’t.”
“Go ahead, provided we do not waste each other’s valuable time.”
“First, I would like to ask whether there is any evidence.”
“Evidence?”

“Yes. All you have is circumstantial evidence, don’t you? At the very least, shouldn’t there be a witness who saw the Yangtze River Channel League attack the Sea Serpent Society on the night of the incident at Red Cliffs?”
“A witness. What else?”
“You still haven’t determined what happened to the Dongting Fisherman, who publicly condemned the Yangtze River Channel League.”
“Continue.”
I glanced at Jeok Cheongang before going on.
“According to what I once heard from the old—no, from my Master, the Dongting Fisherman was a Supreme Peak master who belonged to neither the orthodox nor the unorthodox faction.”
“Correct. The Dongting Fisherman spent his entire life near Dongting Lake and built friendships with renowned figures from all walks of life.”
The Dongting Fisherman was well known even in Murim, where strange and extraordinary figures were hardly rare.

It was unusual enough that he had never joined either the orthodox or unorthodox faction and had spent his entire life near Dongting Lake. But the formidable martial arts he performed with the single fishing rod he always carried were also famous throughout Murim.
“I couldn’t understand how a Supreme Peak master like the Dongting Fisherman could disappear without anyone noticing.”
“What about it do you find difficult to understand?”

“If someone killed the Dongting Fisherman, his opponent must have been a master of equal or greater skill. When two Supreme Peak masters really go at it, all hell breaks loose. There’s no way no one would notice.”
“You certainly speak plainly. Continue.”
“And this might be disrespectful to Senior Mu Song.”
Mu Song, who had regained some of his composure after I stepped in, nodded.
“Speak. I don’t mind.”
“Really?”
“Of course.”
“Well, if you say so.”
I spoke cautiously.
“Honestly, does the Yangtze River Channel League have a master of that caliber? From what I’ve seen, it sure didn’t seem like it.”
What? You said you didn’t mind. You told me to speak.
Mu Song looked considerably less fine than before, so I quietly amended my statement.
“Ah, of course, I’m only talking about Hubei. I respect the Seafaring King. I even enjoyed the drama—no, anyway, I’m a huge fan.”
“Actually, when I was little, I dreamed of becoming a river bandit. The Grand Line! The great Yangtze!”
All right. My fault.
Why did I feel guilty when I was technically trying to help him?
Zhuge Feng rescued me from the crisis with a single sentence.
“There is a master of that caliber.”
“What? There is? You’re not lying? Seriously?”
Leaving Mu Song looking dejected once again, Zhuge Feng continued slowly.
“Yangtze One Saber Hwang Chung.”
“Yangtze One Saber. Yangtze One Saber...”
The sobriquet sounded vaguely familiar, but the name itself was new to me. Surely he wasn’t the Hwang Chung from *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*.
*He does seem to be the Uncle Hwang Mu Song mentioned when we first arrived in Hubei.*
As I tilted my head at the unfamiliar name, Jeok Cheongang cut in sharply.
“Yangtze One Saber? That bastard who’s the Seafaring King’s sworn brother?”
“Yes. I imagine you know him as well, Senior.”

“I crossed paths with him once during the Great Faction War. He was calm and clever for a river bandit. I remember thinking the young fellow had a decent personality and considerable martial talent... It seems he finally crossed the wall.”
“If he had not helped the Seafaring King, the Yangtze River Channel League as it exists today would not be here.”
“You call that something worth saying? Without someone to keep him in check, how could the Seafaring King, that foul-tempered bastard, have ruled the Yangtze?”
Wow. That was practically spitting in his face.
Mu Song’s lips twitched as though he had something to say after hearing his Master insulted right in front of him, but Jeok Cheongang silenced him with a single fierce glare.
I seized the opening and quickly spoke up.
“Then are you saying Yangtze One Saber killed the Dongting Fisherman?”
Zhuge Feng considered the question for a moment, then nodded.
“Most likely.”
“Most likely?”
“Nothing has been proven. We have no certainty, only suspicions and circumstantial evidence. But many witnesses can testify to where the Dongting Fisherman went before he disappeared.”
“And where was that?”
Zhuge Feng looked at Mu Song and continued slowly.
“Donghu Stronghold. He headed for the headquarters of Donghu Stronghold, where Yangtze One Saber, Great Hero Hwang Chung, serves as Stronghold Lord. And he was never seen again.”
“That’s impossible!”
Those words had not come from me.
Mu Song shot to his feet, the veins standing out on his neck as he shouted.
“Uncle Hwang would never do such a thing!”
He, too, was one of the disciples who had inherited the Seafaring King’s ultimate technique.
The qi pressure radiating from Mu Song, who had reached the upper limits of the Peak realm, stirred the dust settled around us.
Zhuge Feng covered his mouth with his sleeve, gave a small cough, and answered calmly.
“Why do you say that?”

“You know as well as I do, Family Head! During the Great Faction War, Uncle Hwang persuaded my Master to side with the orthodox faction. He is also one of the moderates within our League! There is no possibility that a man like him would destroy the Sea Serpent Society in this manner and kill the Dongting Fisherman!”
“‘No possibility’? What an empty and meaningless thing to say. Circumstances change, and so do people. A wise man such as myself deduces the outcome from the circumstances.”
Zhuge Feng remained so composed that Mu Song’s anger seemed almost pointless.
“I will say this plainly: I am not convinced that the Yangtze River Channel League is behind this. But every circumstance points to your League.”

“Why? Because once the Sea Serpent Society, which opposed our League for so many years, disappeared, our brothers moved in to fill the void? Or because the Dongting Fisherman happened to disappear on his way to visit Uncle Hwang?”
“Both.”
“Did you even ask our brothers what happened?”
“Not yet.”
“Then why—!”
Just as Mu Song was about to shout, Zhuge Feng’s quiet voice pierced the ears of everyone in the room, including me.
“If no one from the Yangtze River Channel League has shown themselves, whom could I possibly ask?”
“A full month has passed. Did you think our family, Wudang, and the authorities had done nothing all this time and were simply casting baseless suspicion upon the Yangtze River Channel League?”
Silence settled over the room.
Everyone stared wordlessly at Zhuge Feng and Mu Song.
Unlike Mu Song, who had frozen like a statue, Zhuge Feng continued smoothly.
“Two days after the incident at Red Cliffs, Dangyang Stronghold and Honghu Stronghold—which had swiftly seized the Sea Serpent Society’s territory—vanished without a trace. Every last person.”
“...Then what about Donghu Stronghold?”

“Someone once told me that Donghu Stronghold was a natural fortress built on the water. I tried to see for myself, and they were right. Now that even the Sea Serpent Society’s core boatmen have all been drowned, we could not enter Donghu Stronghold by crossing the waters of Tianling Falls.”
The mysterious grandeur of nature sometimes refused all human intrusion.
The Tianling Falls Zhuge Feng mentioned were clearly the passage to Donghu Stronghold, one that only a tiny number of boatmen could navigate.
Someone counted among the finest boatmen in the Yangtze River Channel League or the Sea Serpent Society—or someone who had spent his entire life on the Yangtze in Hubei...
The Dongting Fisherman must have been one of them.

“The Dongting Fisherman and the late Sea Serpent Society Head were close friends. Enraged by his friend’s death, he publicly condemned your League, launched a boat, and crossed Tianling Falls—the very same Tianling Falls where we have sunk dozens of ships over the past month.”
Zhuge Feng abruptly rose and began walking at a leisurely pace.
He clicked his tongue softly at the fallen bookshelf, then rummaged through the towering piles of books as he continued.
“But did you know this? Although we failed to cross Tianling Falls, the Yangtze, after accepting dozens of ships as tribute, tossed us a gift as if out of generosity.”
Scrape. Crash!
A precariously balanced stack of books came tumbling down, sending dust billowing into the air.
Covered in pale dust, Zhuge Feng adjusted his cap and straightened.
Something dark and battered lay in his hand.
“That’s...”
“Your guess is correct, Successor Beggar.”
Zhuge Feng nodded at Gung Gibang’s murmur.
“The Black Bamboo Fishing Rod. The Dongting Fisherman’s signature weapon, the only one of its kind in all Murim.”
“Well then, Ship-Fire Boy Mu Song.”
Zhuge Feng slowly raised the broken Black Bamboo Fishing Rod.
He pointed it at the wide-eyed Mu Song as though about to run him through.
“You will take the lead and guide us beyond Tianling Falls to Donghu Stronghold. I intend to see with my own two eyes exactly what happened there.”

Zhuge Feng remained so composed that Mu Song’s anger seemed almost pointless.
“I will say this plainly: I am not convinced that the Yangtze River Channel League is behind this.
But every circumstance points to your League.”
“Why?
Because once the Sea Serpent Society, which opposed our League for so many years, disappeared, our brothers moved in to fill the void?
Or because the Dongting Fisherman happened to disappear on his way to visit Uncle Hwang?”
“Both.”
“Did you even ask our brothers what happened?”
“Not yet.”
“Then why—!”
Just as Mu Song was about to shout, Zhuge Feng’s quiet voice pierced the ears of everyone in the room, including me.
“If no one from the Yangtze River Channel League has shown themselves, whom could I possibly ask?”
“A full month has passed.
Did you think our family, Wudang, and the authorities had done nothing all this time and were simply casting baseless suspicion upon the Yangtze River Channel League?”
Silence settled over the room.
Everyone stared wordlessly at Zhuge Feng and Mu Song.
Unlike Mu Song, who had frozen like a statue, Zhuge Feng continued smoothly.
“Two days after the incident at Red Cliffs, Dangyang Stronghold and Honghu Stronghold—which had swiftly seized the Sea Serpent Society’s territory—vanished without a trace.
Every last person.”
“...Then what about Donghu Stronghold?”
“Someone once told me that Donghu Stronghold was a natural fortress built on the water.
I tried to see for myself, and they were right.
Now that even the Sea Serpent Society’s core boatmen have all been drowned, we could not enter Donghu Stronghold by crossing the waters of Tianling Falls.”
The mysterious grandeur of nature sometimes refused all human intrusion.
The Tianling Falls Zhuge Feng mentioned were clearly the passage to Donghu Stronghold, one that only a tiny number of boatmen could navigate.
Someone counted among the finest boatmen in the Yangtze River Channel League or the Sea Serpent Society—or someone who had spent his entire life on the Yangtze in Hubei...
The Dongting Fisherman must have been one of them.
“The Dongting Fisherman and the late Sea Serpent Society Head were close friends.
Enraged by his friend’s death, he publicly condemned your League, launched a boat, and crossed Tianling Falls—the very same Tianling Falls where we have sunk dozens of ships over the past month.”
Zhuge Feng abruptly rose and began walking at a leisurely pace.
He clicked his tongue softly at the fallen bookshelf, then rummaged through the towering piles of books as he continued.
“But did you know this?
Although we failed to cross Tianling Falls, the Yangtze, after accepting dozens of ships as tribute, tossed us a gift as if out of generosity.”
Scrape.
Crash!
A precariously balanced stack of books came tumbling down, sending dust billowing into the air.
Covered in pale dust, Zhuge Feng adjusted his cap and straightened.
Something dark and battered lay in his hand.
“That’s...”
“Your guess is correct, Successor Beggar.”
Zhuge Feng nodded at Gung Gibang’s murmur.
“The Black Bamboo Fishing Rod.
The Dongting Fisherman’s signature weapon, the only one of its kind in all Murim.”
“Well then, Ship-Fire Boy Mu Song.”
Zhuge Feng slowly raised the broken Black Bamboo Fishing Rod.
He pointed it at the wide-eyed Mu Song as though about to run him through.
“You will take the lead and guide us beyond Tianling Falls to Donghu Stronghold.
I intend to see with my own two eyes exactly what happened there.”

chapters.title: Chapter 447
paragraphs: Whoosh.
Silence hung over the swift ship as it cut rapidly through the current.
The river pirates of Water Dragon Stronghold rowed like machines, their mouths clamped shut, while Mu Song stared straight ahead with a rigid expression.
*What a fantastic atmosphere.*
I clicked my tongue inwardly and looked around.
Four swift ships were currently bound for Donghu Stronghold.
But the mood aboard them was worlds apart from when we had been sailing toward Hubei.
The unfamiliar faces now filling the ships were the reason.
*The Zhuge Clan. And Wudang.*
Disciples of the two prestigious factions that divided Hubei Province between them filled all four vessels.
One glance was enough to tell that they were elites, handpicked in preparation for possible bloodshed. Every last one of them was an exceptional martial artist.
And at their center stood two men.
“The wind seems unusually strong today, Family Head Zhuge.”
Zhuge Feng answered the old Daoist in an untroubled voice.
“You need not worry. If the wind is blowing like this, things will actually be easier for us.”
“Why is that? I understand dozens of ships have already sunk in winds weaker than this.”

“The boatmen’s skill is one factor, but the swift ships that symbolize the Yangtze River Channel League are in a class of their own. Rather than being swept away by strong winds, they can catch the wind and surge forward with even greater force.”
“I have heard some talk about swift ships as well... but I do not know the details, as my experience is limited. I have spent my entire life in Murim, yet it feels as though I have wasted it.”
“You have spent all that time at Wudang’s headquarters, so it is only natural that you would not know. But... may I ask what became of the matter you mentioned last time?”

“Our Sect Leader is personally working on it together with the disciples of our main sect. As for me, I was sent here instead, since all I was doing was sitting around and consuming the sect’s grain.”
“Doing nothing but consuming grain? With Perfected Being Hyeongong joining us, this junior feels as though he has gained an army of thousands.”
Zhuge Feng was not merely being polite. He meant every word.
Perfected Being Hyeongong.
That was the Daoist name of the old man in the heavily patched robe, with a single worn Pine-Pattern Ancient Sword hanging at his waist.
Neither his position within Wudang nor his generational seniority in Murim was inferior to Zhuge Feng’s.
If anything, he stood equal to Zhuge Feng—or even above him.

Unlike Zhuge Feng, who had yet to turn sixty, Perfected Being Hyeongong was a master of the previous generation who had distinguished himself during the Great Faction War. He was also the current Wudang Sect Leader’s Junior Brother.
*And one of the Supreme Peak masters Wudang is so proud of.*
Perfected Being Hyeongong was the swordsman said to have reached the ultimate stage of Wudang’s greatest technique, the Taiji Wisdom Sword.
Even as Family Head of the Zhuge Clan, Zhuge Feng spoke to him with marked respect in front of everyone. That alone showed the regard he had for Hyeongong.
Of course, there was one exception to all this.
“That little punk has grown.”
At the words of Jeok Cheongang—Murim’s own Bodhidharma-tier old-timer—I muttered in disbelief.
“He sure has. He’s grown so much his beard turned white.”
“How old was he the last time I saw him? Thirty? Hah. Time certainly flies. Those soft-fuzzed little brats have all become Sect Leaders and Elders.”
“Soft fuzz? At thirty, wouldn’t he have had a full bush down there?”
Jeok Cheongang glared at me with fire in his eyes.
“Judging by the way you keep nitpicking my every word, you must want every hair below your waist plucked out.”
“No, why would you say something like that?”
I had absolutely no desire to receive a Fire King Zilean waxing on the deck of a swift ship.
I waved my hands at the speed of light, then stole a sidelong glance at Jeok Cheongang.
“Since we’re on the subject, may I ask your venerable age?”
“Venerable?”
Even under normal circumstances, Jeok Cheongang treated being called old as another way of asking him to kill you. I awkwardly tried again.
“...Then, your age?”
“My age?”
Seriously, what more did he want? The man was over a hundred.
I asked with all the exasperation I could muster.
“Cheongang, how old are you?”
Whack!
Right. I knew that would happen.
Jeok Cheongang smacked the back of my head like a bolt of lightning, then answered in a bored voice.
“I stopped counting after I passed one hundred.”
“So how long ago was the last time you counted?”
“Five thousand years ago. Satisfied?”
Cheongpung, who had been dangling from the nearby bow, dropped his jaw.
“Wow! Five thousand years old!”
“...Does that little punk not know how to doubt anything?”
“...That’s just how he is. Anyway, you look unbelievably young for your age.”
Jeok Cheongang stared hard at me.
“Would you like to know more?”
“Of course not.”
Honestly, I did want to know, but judging by his expression, this was something I was better off not knowing.
He was sensitive about his age at the best of times. Worse, being aboard a swift ship racing over rougher currents and through stronger winds than ever seemed to be causing him tremendous stress.
“When the hell is this goddamned piece of wood going to stop?”
Right then, as though it had heard his complaint, the goddamned piece of wood sped up even more.
Whoooosh!
A column of water shot high into the air, and the once-steady hull began rocking from side to side.
Cheongpung cheered at the sudden violent motion like a child visiting an amusement park on Children’s Day.

Hyuk Mujin and Gung Gibang, who still had not recovered from their little dip in the Yangtze, let out ear-splitting screams. Mungyeong alone remained perfectly balanced, but when he noticed everyone looking at him, he tactfully grabbed the railing.
And Jeok Cheongang...
“Uhh! Uhhhhhhhh!”
He was panicking so badly that no one would have guessed his title was the Fire King.
Good heavens, look at those bulging eyes. He could be used in a Gangnam plastic surgeon’s subway advertisement as a successful double-eyelid surgery case.
Dodging the water splashing into my face, I shouted at Mu Song.
“Senior! Could you slow down a little—”
“That will be difficult.”
Mu Song cut me off sharply.
Like a man born and raised on the Yangtze, he stood tall as though his feet were planted on level ground. He raised one hand and pointed ahead.
“Can you see it?”
See what?
I narrowed my eyes and stared where he was pointing.
I drew up my internal energy and focused it into my eyes. My dramatically enhanced vision pierced the dense fog blanketing the churning river.
*That’s...*
I saw it.
A passage so narrow that even swift ships, among the sleekest of all vessels, could barely squeeze through two abreast.
And directly before it, a violent whirlpool twisting like a blade.
Whoooosh! Crack!

A massive log that had drifted in from parts unknown was caught in the whirlpool, which stretched more than a hundred zhang in radius. Unable to withstand the crushing water pressure, it snapped apart.
Some of the splintered pieces were flung away and smashed into a huge rock standing behind the whirlpool like a gatekeeper, shattering into fragments.
*A whirlpool like that in a river? Not the sea, but a river?*
The sight was as wondrous as it was chilling.
And everyone aboard the swift ships knew the identity of that monstrous whirlpool.
“Tianling Falls!”
Someone shouted the words like a scream.
That was right. This was Tianling Falls.
A work of nature that had transformed Donghu Stronghold of the Yangtze River Channel League into a natural fortress—and a monster that had swallowed countless lives and ships over the centuries.
Looking as though he might suffocate at any moment, Jeok Cheongang declared, “Turn the ship around. I would rather fight the Great Faction War all over again than cross that.”
Gung Gibang and Hyuk Mujin spoke next, their faces suggesting they had already suffocated.
“Senior Mu Song. Please save us. I would rather beg in a beggars’ den.”
“Captain, thank you for everything. I’m done with Murim. I want to go home and sell silk.”
“...It looks like your soul will be sold before the silk.”
Not that I wasn’t scared myself.
Watching that enormous whirlpool rush toward us made me feel like an ant tumbling into an antlion’s pit.
*Fuck. We’re going to smash against that rock and get blown to pieces, then get sucked straight down like someone flushed a toilet.*
Before the terror of nature itself, even the System and Supreme Peak martial arts seemed useless.
If someone dropped me into the middle of the Yangtze, I was confident I could somehow swim to shore. But if I got caught in a whirlpool like that...
Then I really was finished.
“Whew. Whew.”
As I took deep breaths, a thick hand settled on my shoulder.
“My youngest.”
Even as a fairly tall man myself, I had to tilt my head back to look up at the giant beside me. Jin Wikyung spoke with a calm expression.
“Do not worry about a thing.”
His composure alone made me want to call him Eldest Brother.

Putting aside Jeok Cheongang, who had a pathological hatred of water, even I had reached the Supreme Peak realm and was still feeling my blood run cold. Yet Jin Wikyung, whose martial arts were far below ours, did not waver in the slightest.
*So this is why he’s my eldest brother. Why he’s the Lesser Family Head.*
“Eldest Brother...”
“Yes.”
Jin Wikyung smiled faintly and nodded.
“Even in death, the bond between our brothers will last forever.”
“What?”
“I can see our deceased parents hovering before my eyes. It is as though they are beckoning to us from Tianling Falls.”
“...Isn’t Father still alive?”
“We lost contact with him again a long time ago. Let us simply consider him dead.”
*Eldest brother, my ass. He’s just a big bastard.*
And while he was at it, he had declared our perfectly alive father dead just because the man had dumped the family responsibilities on him and run away.
*Shit...*
I looked around. Most of the people aboard were already half out of their minds, surrendering their bodies to the beat of Mother Nature.
With my last shred of hope, I looked at Mu Song.
“Senior Mu Song.”
“I’m sorry, but it is too late to stop.”
Whoooosh! Crack!
“Oh, fuck. He’s right.”
Mu Song nodded, his expression grim.
“Hold on tight. My men and I will do our best as well.”
“What? What do you mean, do your best?”

“Do you think every province has its own Tianling Falls? I have only crossed it three or four times, when I came to Hubei to visit Uncle Hwang. We have no choice but to trust in the League’s swift ships and the skills we have honed over the years.”
“W-wait. So you’re saying... you’re a Tianling Falls newbie?”
“I do not know why you are suddenly bringing up Liu Bei, but of course I am unfamiliar with it. Ever since leaving headquarters and becoming a Stronghold Lord, I have spent all my time in Sichuan.”
He had a point.
A fucking punchable point.
Half out of my mind, I barely squeezed out my voice.
“You’ve got to be kidding me. Why are you only telling us something this important now?”
“Great Hero Zhuge told me not to tell anyone else.”
What?
My head snapped around at lightning speed. The disciples of both factions stood rigid with tension, and at their center was one man.
Zhuge Feng met my gaze and laughed heartily as the rising spray pelted his face.
“A wise man leads his allies, while a strategist deceives even his allies! Now that we have all climbed onto the tiger’s back, let us ride it to the bitter end!”
Was this really happening?
Every last one of us was left speechless.
Jeok Cheongang, meanwhile, lost his mind.
“That fucking son of a bitch...!”
It was one of the greatest fits of rage I had ever witnessed.
But just as Jeok Cheongang rolled his eyes back until only the whites showed and prepared to charge—
“Everyone, hold on tight!”
At Mu Song’s urgent shout, the whirlpool of Tianling Falls opened its maw wide and slammed into the swift ship.
KRA-KOOOOM!

chapters.title: Chapter 448
paragraphs: A Supreme Peak master could perform feats straight out of an old folktale—erasing several zhang of distance in a single step, leaping upward by stepping on empty air, and bringing down a cliff with one punch.
But...
“Hold on ti—aaaaah!”
KRA-KOOOOM!
We were not on solid ground, but in the middle of the Yangtze, a river as vast as the open sea.
Before a massive whirlpool hundreds of zhang across, the swift ship carrying me was no more than a tiny leaf.
BOOM!
“Whoa, whoa, whoaaaa!”
“Aaaaargh!”
The tremendous pressure of the water slammed into the swift ship’s side. The racing vessel was hurled into the air and began to tilt.
As the world slowly turned upside down, Jin Wikyung clung to my torso as though I were a life jacket and screamed.
“Mother! I’m coming!”
“Where do you think you’re going? Let go!”
“Father! If you’re watching, tell me the answer!”
*What fucking answer? There isn’t one.*
But the bigger problem was that Jin Wikyung was not alone. Gung Gibang, Hyuk Mujin, and even the disciples of the Zhuge Clan and Wudang had all been driven half out of their minds.
The only ones who had managed to keep their composure were the Supreme Peak masters, myself included.
“Uhh! Uhhhhh! Water! Wateeer!”
Correction. There was one exception.
I grabbed Jeok Cheongang, who was screaming at the top of his lungs with his eyes squeezed shut, and thrust my free hand into the air with all my strength.
*Flame Divine Palm!*
BOOM!
Compressed air exploded outward on a wave of powerful internal energy.
Part of the blade-like whirlpool scattered, and the vessel, which had been plunging upside down toward the river, barely managed to right itself.
But it was far too soon to feel relieved.
A second and then a third whirlpool were bearing down on the falling swift ship.
*I can’t do this alone. At a time like this...*
A thought flashed through my mind like lightning, and I shouted a single name.
“Cheongpung!”
“Yes!”
Cheongpung nodded as though he understood perfectly and flung both arms into the air.
“Kiya-hoo!”
“Not ‘kiya-hoo,’ you lunatic! Do what I did!”
“Ah. Yes, Benefactor!”
Cheongpung had been enjoying the Wolmido Disco Pang Pang all by himself, but now he snapped both sleeves.
The Taeeul Miri Palm, one of Huashan’s proudest techniques, transformed into dozens of flower petals that lashed through the air.
BOOM-BOOM-BOOM!
It could not match the destructive power of the Flame Divine Palm, but in a situation like this, the Taeeul Miri Palm’s far wider range made it ideal.
When the blade-like currents of Tianling Falls faltered, the disciples of the Zhuge Clan and Wudang seemed to recover the senses that had briefly abandoned them.
“Ha-ha-ha! The tiger is running wild! Disciples of our family, unleash the Great Heavenly Star Divine Palm!”
Crouching Dragon Guest Zhuge Feng issued the order as he swept the feather fan in his hand.
Though he had yet to cross the wall into the Supreme Peak realm, his mastery of fan techniques alone was said to rival that of a Supreme Peak master.
WHOOOOSH!
A breeze stirred along the fan’s ribs, then swelled into a mighty wind that held back the whirlpool.
A towering surge rose like a triangular wave, threatening to swallow the swift ship, only to be stopped by the wind.
At that moment—
SWISH!
A streak of light shot from Perfected Being Hyeongong’s waist and swept through the air.
Taiji Wisdom Sword.

The streak of light flashed through everything in its path, cleaving space and slicing through the wind. The wall of water raised by Tianling Falls seemed to split apart for an instant, then shattered completely.
SPLAAASH!
Spray burst in every direction.
Drenched in an enormous volume of cold water, Jeok Cheongang’s eyes flew open like a man waking from sleep.
Then he glared at the whirlpool, flames streaming from his eyes, and roared.
“You wet, smelly, filthy things!”
He wasn’t exactly wrong, but why did he sound so pathetic?
Contrary to what I thought, however, the internal energy erupting from Jeok Cheongang’s sleeves was overwhelmingly powerful.
“Get the hell out of here!”
FWOOOSH—KRA-KOOOOM!
Several jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi burst forth at once.
The moisture filling the air evaporated, and the tremendous recoil sent the swift ship shooting forward like an arrow.
“Kiya-hoo!”
“Cheongpung, you lunatic!”
“Oh. Sorry, Benefactor!”
BOOM-BOOM-BOOM!
Palm forces erupted without pause as we fought to protect the vessel, while Tianling Falls sought to sink the uninvited guests who had trespassed upon its domain.
Mu Song gritted his teeth hard enough to draw blood, the veins bulging in his neck.
“Hard to port! Turn together!”
“Aaaaargh!”
BANG!
Amid the chaos, the young medical apprentice blended in by screaming with everyone else while secretly firing off a palm force. Only Jeok Cheongang, Cheongpung, and I knew what he had done.
“One, two!”
“Now! Row with every last bit of strength you have!”
SPLAAASH!
Their efforts paid off.
The four swift ships carrying hundreds of passengers drove onward through the whirlpools, farther and farther ahead.
The moment we cleared Tianling Falls, the exhausted passengers sprawled across the decks without the slightest concern for appearances.
But there was an exception to everything.
His eyes red around the edges, Jeok Cheongang stared at the waters of the Yangtze, now calm as though nothing had happened. Then he abruptly spoke.
“As the current Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan, I hereby declare that, as of this time tomorrow, the Zhuge Clan shall be our sect’s public enemy.”
“Every bastard bearing the Zhuge name should be seized and thrown into that godforsaken Tianling Falls. Any objections?”
“What if I have one?”
“I’ll throw you in with them.”
“Then I have no objections.”
“Good. Seize that goddamn bastard at once and bring him before me.”
At the end of Jeok Cheongang’s blazing gaze was a swift ship following several dozen zhang behind us. Zhuge Feng sat at its bow, waving his feather fan.
“Ha-ha, Senior! Please set aside your anger!”
“...Are you laughing?”
Even I wanted to kill him.
Bringing down a cliff would have been easier. Just imagine being sucked into a whirlpool in the middle of the vast Yangtze, with nowhere to flee.

People tossed around names like Stepping on Empty Air and Rising on Duckweed, Crossing Water as though they were simple tricks, but both techniques consumed tremendous amounts of internal energy. Rescuing several hundred people would have been unthinkable.
*What the hell is something like that doing in a river? It isn’t even the sea.*
There was a reason it was called Tianling Falls.
Then again, if it had merely been a rough stretch of water, the Zhuge Clan and Wudang would have stormed Donghu Stronghold long ago.
Even as I thought this, Jeok Cheongang’s fury continued racing toward its peak.
“Turn the ship around at once! Zhuge Feng, Crouching Dragon Guest—whatever that bastard calls himself, this old man will break both his legs today and leave him bedridden for the rest of his life!”
“Calm down. Please calm down.”

“Do I look like I can calm down right now? I already hate water, and now I’ve suffered through this because we came to some godforsaken place! The man who claims to have crossed it several times can’t even find the right channel and just stands there groaning! At this point, are you a river bandit or a ferryman to the afterlife?”
At the sight of Jeok Cheongang raging like a madman, Mu Song, who had been lying spread-eagled on the deck, flinched and pushed himself upright.
“P-please calm yourself, Great Hero. I never dreamed Tianling Falls would be this bad, either.”
“You’ve been here several times and didn’t know? If you don’t know, does your life as a river bandit end here? Should I end your life here, too?”
“T-that’s not it. The currents of Tianling Falls have grown abnormally strong compared to before...”
“Grown stronger? What kind of bullshit is that? It has barely rained this year, and you dare try to deceive this old man with sweet talk that will be exposed at once?”
“I-I’m telling the truth! How could I dare lie to the Fire King?”
*Hmm.*
Mu Song had a point. Who would dare lie to Fire King Jeok Cheongang?
If he caught you lying, losing a hand would be the least of your worries. Your whole body would end up roasted medium-rare.
*Still, can the current really get that much stronger when there hasn’t been much rain?*
Forget it. I wasn’t a meteorologist or an ecosystem researcher. Thinking about it would get me nowhere.
I clicked my tongue softly and addressed Jeok Cheongang, who had not stopped berating Mu Song.
“Old Master.”

“When we return, do your job properly. If you make this old man suffer through something like that again, I’ll storm the headquarters of the Yangtze River Channel League, burn every ship to ashes, and throw that Seafaring King bastard into Tianling Falls along with the Zhuge Clan bastards... What is it? Tell me later.”
“That’s not it. I think we’ve arrived.”
“What!”
Tap-tap-tap-tap!
He moved at Quick Attack speed.
Jeok Cheongang flung Mu Song aside, crossed the swift ship in a single step, and stared straight ahead with his eyes wide open.
Soon, an emotional exclamation spilled from his lips.
“Oh. Ohhh!”
Anyone watching him might have thought he had discovered a treasure island, but what appeared beyond the thick fog was simply an island.
It was neither small like the islands scattered along Korea’s Han River nor deserted, without any sign of human habitation.
“That over there... Could it be...?”
At Hyuk Mujin’s murmur, Gung Gibang nodded beside him.
“It’s a ferry landing. Looks like we came to the right place.”
The existence of a ferry landing where ships could dock meant, in other words, that people lived there—or that the island was frequently used as a stopover.
And everyone present already knew who had established their home in a place that could only be reached by crossing that insane Tianling Falls.
“Wow, Donghu Stronghold!”
Cheongpung’s shout broke the silence of the Yangtze and rang out across the water.
Jin Wikyung spoke, his expression stiff.
“By now, Donghu Stronghold must know we have arrived. It would be wise to prepare for any unforeseen developments.”
No one needed to ask what he meant.

If Donghu Stronghold really was responsible for the two incidents that had occurred over the past fifteen days, just as the circumstances revealed so far suggested... then a clash of martial force might take place, in accordance with the laws of Murim.
“Stronghold Lord. We did not come here to spill blood. I trust you understand what I mean.”
Mu Song had remained silent until now. He met Jin Wikyung’s gaze and answered.
“My subordinates and I took the lead in coming here to prove our League brothers’ innocence. If you persecute us without even hearing the full circumstances...”
“I can promise you that will not happen. Wudang and the Zhuge Clan have already guaranteed as much, and everyone present, myself included, will serve as a witness.”
After a brief hesitation, Mu Song gave a small nod.
“...I will trust you.”
Perhaps Mu Song was the person here most desperate to prevent bloodshed.

No matter how skilled the river bandits of Donghu Stronghold might be, and no matter how powerful their leader, Yangtze One Saber Hwang Chung, was as a Supreme Peak master, they could not withstand our current force.

Even if some utterly incomprehensible disaster—a genuine one-in-ten-thousand chance—sent everyone here to the bottom of the Yangtze, the Yangtze River Channel League would then have to face the whole of Murim. If the Nine Sects and One Gang joined forces with the Five Great Families, the League would vanish without a trace.
“Raise the flag high and let them know we are here.”
The river bandits of Water Dragon Stronghold immediately carried out their lord’s order.
Soon, the flag of the Yangtze River Channel League fluttered above the four swift ships, and seven low drumbeats echoed beyond the fog.
And then...
Nothing happened.
The Yangtze, the fog, and the quietly flowing water remained unchanged.
The only things that changed were the question on Jin Wikyung’s face and the wavering in Mu Song’s eyes.
“Stronghold Lord. What is happening?”
“I’m not sure, either. We definitely sent the signal, so a reply should have come...”
At that very moment—
“I’m afraid that will be difficult.”
Everyone turned toward the sudden voice.
Countless gazes fell upon the young medical apprentice whom no one had paid any attention to until now.
He continued in a clear, composed voice.
“It seems something has happened.”
“What do you mean...!”
Mu Song’s shout died unfinished.
The young medical apprentice, Mungyeong, raised a finger and pointed.
Something previously concealed by the fog and aquatic plants had floated into view.
It was someone’s corpse.

chapters.title: Chapter 449
paragraphs: From the moment they crossed the unnaturally powerful current of Tianling Falls and entered the territory of Donghu Stronghold, Ship-Fire Boy Mu Song’s heart had been beating faster and faster.
*Uncle Hwang. I’ve come.*
Hwang Chung, the Yangtze One Saber and Lord of Donghu Stronghold, was like a master to Mu Song. No—perhaps he was even more than that.
Mu Song’s true master, the Seafaring King, was not an affectionate man, and their relationship was as dry and barren as sand.
When Mu Song was young, it had been Hwang Chung’s warm advice and consideration that allowed him to endure his master’s harsh scolding and grueling training.
*I believe in you, Uncle. You’re not the kind of man who would do such a thing.*
Hwang Chung was more serious and thoughtful than anyone else in the Yangtze River Channel League.
There was no way a man like him would make the worst possible move by eliminating the Sea Serpent Society and the Dongting Fisherman in such a manner.
It was because of his unshakable faith in Hwang Chung that Mu Song had chosen to come here in person.
But despite that faith, his unease continued to swell with every passing moment.
*Why is it so quiet?*
The Hwang Chung he knew, the Yangtze One Saber, was thorough and cautious in everything he did. He would never neglect the stronghold’s defenses simply because Tianling Falls protected it.
Donghu Stronghold was a natural fortress built on the Yangtze.
If unauthorized intruders crossed Tianling Falls, they would soon see a gorge several hundred zhang long, along with countless arrowheads waiting to greet them from above.
But...
*We’re already right in front of it. Why hasn’t there been any reply?*
Even after they raised the Yangtze River Channel League’s flag and beat the drums to signal their arrival, the surroundings remained as quiet as before.
Mu Song’s heart hammered against his ribs as he stared at the island shrouded in thick fog.
*Something has gone wrong.*
The thought flashed through his mind.
It was not long before his vague unease took shape.
“It seems something has happened.”
“What do you mean...!”
Mu Song turned toward the young medical apprentice Mungyeong, but the rest of his words died in his throat. He swallowed hard.
A moment later, alarm spread like wildfire among the people aboard the ships.
“Th-that’s...”
“A corpse! It’s a corpse!”
Everyone present was a martial artist accustomed to blood and death. They had seen enough corpses to be sick of them, but this time was different.

This was Donghu Stronghold. With the Sea Serpent Society’s key figures wiped out and the Dongting Fisherman all but confirmed dead, there should have been no one in Hubei Province capable of crossing the now even fiercer Tianling Falls to reach this place.
And yet a corpse had appeared out of nowhere.
Amid the commotion, Mu Song forced out a strained command.
“...Pull it aboard at once. We need to identify it.”
“Y-yes, sir!”
Before the river bandits of Water Dragon Stronghold could move, someone strode forward.
“Stand back.”
Fire King Jeok Cheongang had been raging only moments ago. Now he spoke in a low, somber voice as he extended one hand.
Powerful internal energy shot across the distance and seized the corpse submerged in the water.
Whoosh—thud!
The body landed heavily on the deck of the swift ship.
Half of its upper body was gone, and its face was bloated. Mu Song’s eyes widened the moment he saw it.
“This man...”
“Do you know him?”
Jin Taekyung strode over, and Mu Song nodded dazedly.
“Little Tide Demon Wang Pil. Uncle Hwang’s right-hand man and the Deputy Stronghold Lord of Donghu Stronghold.”
Donghu Stronghold ruled the Yangtze in Hubei Province. Naturally, the name and sobriquet of its Deputy Stronghold Lord—and the right-hand man of Yangtze One Saber Hwang Chung—were widely known.
Ignoring the sighs that escaped at the name Little Tide Demon, Jin Taekyung stared at Mu Song with a stiff expression.
“The Deputy Stronghold Lord? Are you certain?”
“Without a doubt. The body is badly damaged, but not enough to keep me from recognizing his face.”
“...Damn it.”
Jin Taekyung’s expression hardened. So did the faces of everyone who understood what this meant.

The death of even an ordinary river bandit would have been ominous enough. But this was the Deputy Stronghold Lord of Donghu Stronghold, a Supreme Peak master of the Yangtze River Channel League whose name was renowned throughout Hubei Murim.
What this sequence of events meant was obvious.
*Something has happened at Donghu Stronghold.*
Jin Taekyung was the first to act on the thought that had flashed through all their minds.
Whoosh!
He crossed the deck at blinding speed, reached the stern of the swift ship, and thrust both arms out with all his strength.
Boom! Booooom!
The Scorching Yang Qi carried by the Flame Divine Palm evaporated the river water and propelled the swift ship forward.
Only then did the others recover from their shock and begin moving after him.
“Boatmen, return to your positions and take up the oars! Every second counts!”
“Tell the other ships! Send the signal at once!”
Boom, boom, boooom!
Urgent shouts and drumbeats shattered the silence.
Amid the chaos, Mu Song raised his head, his heart pounding harder and louder than the drums echoing around him.
And then—
He saw it.
No—all of them saw it.
Beyond the fog parting before the bow of the swift ship lay a shattered ferry landing and countless corpses filling the river.
“What the fuck...!”
The curse burst from my mouth at full volume before I could stop it. But no one gave me a disapproving look or blamed me.
Maybe they were too overwhelmed to care. Or maybe I had simply said what they all wanted to say.
That was how horrific the scene before us was.
“This is a hellscape.”
“...How could this happen?”
Jeok Cheongang muttered in a grim, subdued voice, while the usually cheerful Cheongpung looked around with trembling eyes.
Everywhere he looked, there were collapsed houses and corpses.
The bodies we had seen around the ferry landing were only a fraction of the dead scattered across the island.
“C-Captain. Over there...”
“I know.”
I forced myself to ignore Hyuk Mujin, who was calling to me in a trembling voice.
I had already seen what he was pointing at. My teeth clenched before I even realized it.
*Children and commoners who never learned martial arts.*
Donghu Stronghold was not inhabited solely by river bandits.
They had brought their families and relatives to this safe, natural fortress, and the people who gathered here had formed a village of their own.
And...
*They’re all dead.*
Children who looked as though they had only just been weaned. Frail old people and women. Even the hundreds of river bandits who should have risked their lives to protect them.
Every single one of them was dead.

That was the conclusion my companions and I had reached after searching every corner of the island for more than half a day, along with the martial artists of Wudang and the Zhuge Clan and the river bandits of Water Dragon Stronghold under Mu Song.
And among those countless dead was one particular person.
“Uncle Hwang!”
Mu Song’s beastlike roar echoed from far away. Gung Gibang muttered in a heavy voice.
“Looks like he finally found him.”
Some people said that no human life was more valuable than another.
But that was not true. There was a difference in weight. A person’s death weighed differently depending on who they had been in life and what relationship they had shared with you.
For Mu Song, at least, Yangtze One Saber Hwang Chung must have been such a person.
“The Family Head has ordered me to bring you to him at once.”
At the words of the Zhuge Clan martial artist who came hurrying toward us, Jin Wikyung nodded.
“This concerns Great Hero Hwang, I presume.”
“Yes. Great Hero Hwang’s body was just found. However...”
“Let’s go. We’ll hear the rest directly from the Family Head.”
We set off without another word.
Not to mourn Hwang Chung’s death, but because even in death, the Yangtze One Saber was important enough to demand our immediate attention.
Jeok Cheongang was the only one among us who had known him, but grief was not the reason his expression had hardened, either.
“What do you think?”
The sudden Sound Transmission slipped into my ear. I slowed my steps and answered.
“The same as you, Old Master.”
“You know what this old man is thinking?”
“You’re thinking the same thing I am.”
“I feel an urge to use the Flame Divine Palm.”
“I’ve needed to piss for a while, too, but I’ve been holding it in. You should hold it in as well, Old Master. I’m still organizing my thoughts.”
I calmly laid out what I had been considering over the past half a day.

“Donghu Stronghold is a natural fortress that can only be reached by crossing Tianling Falls. I don’t know every detail of the situation here, but no ordinary force could dream of defeating the Supreme Peak master Hwang Chung and the river bandits under his command.”
“Even a mongrel has the advantage in its own yard. To face men who have spent their entire lives on the Yangtze, you would need overwhelming strength.”
Jeok Cheongang’s Sound Transmission continued.

“The Yangtze One Saber in particular is a veritable water ghost. During the Great Faction War, he won overwhelming victories against the Demonic Cult in every battle fought on water. To wipe out Donghu Stronghold, the attackers would have needed at least twice its strength.”
*Twice the strength of Donghu Stronghold...*
I had only realized it after coming here, but Donghu Stronghold was on a scale utterly incomparable to the other water strongholds.
The number of bodies discovered so far had already surpassed a thousand. In terms of size alone, it would not have been an exaggeration to call it a faction in its own right.
*Mu Song said something like that before, too. Donghu Stronghold is the strongest water stronghold in the Yangtze River Channel League after its headquarters.*
One look around was enough to understand why.

Everything had been shattered and destroyed, but this one water stronghold had once maintained a fleet of some fifty ships and built a settlement filled with houses that would not have looked out of place in a bustling city.

It might not have compared to prestigious great factions such as the Nine Sects and One Gang or the Five Great Families, but the river bandits under the Yangtze One Saber must have been formidable elites in their own right.
And very few groups could deploy twice that much force against Donghu Stronghold.
No—only a handful.
“If we’re talking about places capable of mobilizing that many men and ships...”
“As far as this old man knows, there are only four in Hubei Province. One of them is already as good as gone.”
“Wudang, the Zhuge Clan, the government, and the Sea Serpent Society. Correct?”

“Correct. But most of the Sea Serpent Society are fishermen and boatmen who banded together for their livelihoods, so they have far too few masters. Wudang and the Zhuge Clan have the strength, but neither has any reason or justification to attack Donghu Stronghold.”
“The government is the same.”

“Of course. Even a child knows that Murim and the authorities maintain a relationship of mutual noninterference. Even if the Son of Heaven had issued an imperial edict to subjugate the stronghold, it could never have been carried out this secretly, hidden from the eyes of the entire realm.”
Murim was a tree rooted deep within the forest of the world.
It had grown too tall to prune, and anyone who tried to chop it down carelessly risked damaging the blade of their own ax instead.
That was one of the reasons Murim had endured even though the owner of the forest had changed many times.
A towering tree that even the Son of Heaven, the woodcutter, could not easily raise his ax against.
That was Murim. The countless branches and leaves that had sprung from this great tree had grown by joining forces—and, at times, by breaking one another.
The Yangtze River Channel League was one of the thicker branches.

If all the water strongholds scattered across the realm were gathered in one place, they would be a major force in their own right, and the number of masters among them would not fall far behind the Nine Sects and One Gang or the Five Great Families.
And now that very branch of the Yangtze River Channel League had been broken.
By someone whose identity remained unknown.
“Do you think the culprit is one of those four? Wudang, the Zhuge Clan, the authorities, or the Sea Serpent Society?”
“This waterway sees hundreds of ships pass through every day. Mobilizing enough force to cross Tianling Falls while avoiding all those eyes would be... extremely difficult.”
“It might have been extremely easy.”
I finally let out the words that had been hovering on the tip of my tongue.
“If it was Dark Heaven.”

“They had no need to load hundreds or thousands of men onto ships and cross Tianling Falls. If a warp—no, if the formation they call a Moving Formation is hidden somewhere around here, that would explain everything.”
Dark Heaven had already proved it could be done in Shaolin and Sichuan.
If my guess was correct, it would also fully explain how they had gone unnoticed by the countless eyes traveling along the Yangtze.
Jeok Cheongang remained silent for a while before letting out a low groan.
“So this old man isn’t the only one who thinks so.”
“In a situation like this, we can’t rule out Dark Heaven. It stinks too damn much.”
“But why the Yangtze River Channel League?”
“I don’t know.”
I continued as I watched the familiar faces slowly approaching from the distance.
“That’s what we need to find out now.”

*Something has gone wrong.*
The thought flashed through his mind.

“It seems something has happened.”

He swallowed hard.

This was Donghu Stronghold.

Fire King Jeok Cheongang had been raging only moments ago.

Powerful internal energy shot across the distance and seized the corpse submerged in the water.
Whoosh—thud!
The body landed heavily on the deck of the swift ship.
Half of its upper body was gone, and its face was bloated.
Mu Song’s eyes widened the moment he saw it.
“This man...”
“Do you know him?”
Jin Taekyung strode over, and Mu Song nodded dazedly.
“Little Tide Demon Wang Pil.
Uncle Hwang’s right-hand man and the Deputy Stronghold Lord of Donghu Stronghold.”
Donghu Stronghold ruled the Yangtze in Hubei Province.
Naturally, the name and sobriquet of its Deputy Stronghold Lord—and the right-hand man of Yangtze One Saber Hwang Chung—were widely known.
Ignoring the sighs that escaped at the name Little Tide Demon, Jin Taekyung stared at Mu Song with a stiff expression.
“The Deputy Stronghold Lord?
Are you certain?”
“Without a doubt.
The body is badly damaged, but not enough to keep me from recognizing his face.”
“...Damn it.”
Jin Taekyung’s expression hardened.
So did the faces of everyone who understood what this meant.
The death of even an ordinary river bandit would have been ominous enough.
But this was the Deputy Stronghold Lord of Donghu Stronghold, a Supreme Peak master of the Yangtze River Channel League whose name was renowned throughout Hubei Murim.
What this sequence of events meant was obvious.
*Something has happened at Donghu Stronghold.*
Jin Taekyung was the first to act on the thought that had flashed through all their minds.
Whoosh!
He crossed the deck at blinding speed, reached the stern of the swift ship, and thrust both arms out with all his strength.
Boom!
Booooom!
The Scorching Yang Qi carried by the Flame Divine Palm evaporated the river water and propelled the swift ship forward.
Only then did the others recover from their shock and begin moving after him.
“Boatmen, return to your positions and take up the oars!
Every second counts!”
“Tell the other ships!
Send the signal at once!”
Boom, boom, boooom!
Urgent shouts and drumbeats shattered the silence.
Amid the chaos, Mu Song raised his head, his heart pounding harder and louder than the drums echoing around him.
And then—
He saw it.
No—all of them saw it.
Beyond the fog parting before the bow of the swift ship lay a shattered ferry landing and countless corpses filling the river.
“What the fuck...!”
The curse burst from my mouth at full volume before I could stop it.
But no one gave me a disapproving look or blamed me.
Maybe they were too overwhelmed to care.
Or maybe I had simply said what they all wanted to say.
That was how horrific the scene before us was.
“This is a hellscape.”
“...How could this happen?”
Jeok Cheongang muttered in a grim, subdued voice, while the usually cheerful Cheongpung looked around with trembling eyes.
Everywhere he looked, there were collapsed houses and corpses.
The bodies we had seen around the ferry landing were only a fraction of the dead scattered across the island.
“C-Captain.
Over there...”
“I know.”
I forced myself to ignore Hyuk Mujin, who was calling to me in a trembling voice.
I had already seen what he was pointing at.
My teeth clenched before I even realized it.
*Children and commoners who never learned martial arts.*
Donghu Stronghold was not inhabited solely by river bandits.
They had brought their families and relatives to this safe, natural fortress, and the people who gathered here had formed a village of their own.
And...
*They’re all dead.*
Children who looked as though they had only just been weaned.
Frail old people and women.
Even the hundreds of river bandits who should have risked their lives to protect them.
Every single one of them was dead.

That was the conclusion my companions and I had reached after searching every corner of the island for more than half a day, along with the martial artists of Wudang and the Zhuge Clan and the river bandits of Water Dragon Stronghold under Mu Song.
